explanation: Desirous of reaching Laṅkā in order to discover Sītā, Hanumān takes a leap from a peak of Mount Mahendra and honouring with the touch of his hand Mount Maināka, which rose from the bottom of the sea to provide rest on its peak to Hanumān, encounters Surasā (mother of Nāgas), sent by the gods in the form of an ogress, who was waiting for Hanumān with her mouth open to devour him. He enters her belly assuming a minute form and comes out without killing her. Further, he is met by another ogress, Siṃhikā by name, standing with her mouth wide open to gulp Hanumān. He enters her mouth after assuming a minute form and comes out after splitting her belly open and killing her. Then contracting his body into a minute form again in order to preclude the attention of the ogres, he descends on a mountain peak outside Laṅkā

shloka_text:
ततो रावणनीतायाः सीतायाः शत्रुकर्षणः ।
इयेष पदमन्वेष्टुं चारणाचरिते पथि ॥ १ ॥
explanation: In order to discover the whereabouts of Sītā, who had been taken away by Rāvaṇa, Hanumān, the scourge of his foes, wished to course through the heavens, the path of the Cāraṇas or celestial bards. (1)

shloka_text:
दुष्करं निष्प्रतिद्वन्द्वं चिकीर्षन् कर्म वानरः ।
समुदग्रशिरोग्रीवो गवां पतिरिवाबभौ ॥ २ ॥
explanation: With his head and neck exalted, Hanumān, the monkey chief, who sought to accomplish without any other support a feat, which was difficult for others to perform, looked like a well-built bull. (2)

shloka_text:
अथ वैदूर्यवर्णेषु शाद्वलेषु महाबलः ।
धीरः सलिलकल्पेषु विचचार यथासुखम् ॥ ३ ॥
द्विजान् वित्रासयन् धीमानुरसा पादपान् हरन् ।
मृगांश्च सुबहून् निघ्नन् प्रवृद्ध इव केसरी ॥ ४ ॥
explanation: 26 * VĀLMĪKI-RĀMĀYAṆA * Scaring away the birds, nay, pulverizing the trees with his breast and crushing very many deer and other wild animals under his feet, the brave and wise Hanumān, who was endowed with extraordinary might, trod at ease, in the meantime, like a full-grown lion on the swards possessing the hue of a cat's-eye gem and stretching evenly like a sheet of green water. (3-4)

shloka_text:
नीललोहितमाञ्जिष्ठपद्मवर्णैः सितासितैः।
स्वभावसिद्धैर्विमलैर्धातुभिः समलंकृतम् ॥ ५ ॥
कामरूपिभिराविष्टमभीक्षणं सपरिच्छदैः।
यक्षकिंनरगन्धर्वैर्देवकल्पैः सपन्नगैः ॥ ६ ॥
स तस्य गिरिवर्यस्य तले नागवरायुते।
तिष्ठन् कपिवरस्तत्र हृदे नाग इवाबभौ ॥ ७ ॥
explanation: Stopping short at the well-known foot of that jewel among mountains—which was crowded with lordly elephants, was rendered most charming by spotless natural minerals of purple, rosy, ruby-like and white and black hues and was constantly visited by Yakṣas (a class of demigods ruled over by Kubera, the god of riches), Kinnaras (a class of semi-divine beings credited with a human figure and the head of a horse or with a horse's body and a human head), Gandharvas (celestial musicians), and Nāgas (serpent-demons believed to have a human face with serpent-like lower extremities), who very nearly resembled the gods, were capable of changing their form at will and were accompanied by their retinue—Hanumān, the foremost of monkeys, looked like a large-bodied elephant standing in a pool. (5—7)

shloka_text:
स सूर्याय महेन्द्राय पवनाय स्वयम्भुवे।
भूतेभ्यश्चाञ्जलिं कृत्वा चकार गमने मतिम् ॥ ८ ॥
explanation: Joining his palms by way of salutation to the sun-god, the mighty Indra (the ruler of gods), the wind-god (his own procreant), Brahmā (the self-born) and the genii (the attendants of Lord Śiva), he made up his mind to depart. (8)

shloka_text:
अञ्जलिं प्राङ्मुखं कुर्वन् पवनायात्मयोनये।
ततो हि ववृधे गन्तुं दक्षिणो दक्षिणां दिशम् ॥ ९ ॥
explanation: Joining his palms towards the east in salutation to the wind-god, his procreant, the proficient Hanumān then actually grew in size in order to proceed to the southern quarter. (9)

shloka_text:
प्लवगप्रवरैर्दृष्टः प्लवने कृतनिश्चयः।
ववृधे रामवृद्ध्यर्थं समुद्र इव पर्वसु ॥ १० ॥
explanation: Gazed on with wonder and love by foremost of the monkeys and having resolved to take a leap, he swelled in size further for the purpose of Śrī Rāma as the sea swells on the full-moon days. (10)

shloka_text:
निष्प्रमाणशरीरः सँल्लिलङ्घयिषुरर्णवम्।
बाहुभ्यां पीडयामास चरणाभ्यां च पर्वतम् ॥ ११ ॥
explanation: Wishing to leap across the sea, his body having grown immensely, Hanumān pressed the mountain with his hands and feet. (11)

shloka_text:
स चचालाचलश्चाशु मुहूर्तं कपिपीडितः।
तरुणां पुष्पिताग्राणां सर्वं पुष्पमशातयत् ॥ १२ ॥
explanation: Pressed by Hanumān, the aforesaid mountain forthwith shook awhile and caused all the flowers of the trees standing on it to fall, the ends of their branches being laden with blossom. (12)

shloka_text:
तेन पादपमुक्तेन पुष्पौघेण सुगन्धिना।
सर्वतः संवृतः शैलो बभौ पुष्पमयो यथा ॥ १३ ॥
explanation: Covered on all sides with that fragrant shower of flowers, discharged by the trees, the mountain appeared as though it were all flowers. (13)

shloka_text:
तेन चोत्तमवीर्येण पीड्यमानः स पर्वतः।
सलिलं सम्प्रसुस्वाव मदमत्त इव द्विपः ॥ १४ ॥
explanation: Nay, while being pressed by Hanumān, who was endowed with surpassing might, the said mountain spurted water profusely even as an elephant in rut would exude ichor in abundance. (14)

shloka_text:
पीड्यमानस्तु बलिना महेन्द्रस्तेन पर्वतः ।
रीतीनिर्वर्तयामास काञ्चनाञ्जनराजतीः ॥ १५ ॥
explanation: Being pressed by that mighty monkey, the Mahendra mountain for its part let loose streams possessing the hues of gold, antimony and silver, flowing, as they did, through beds containing the ore of these metals. (15)

shloka_text:
मुमोच च शिलाः शैलो विशालाः समनःशिलाः ।
मध्यमेनाचिषा जुष्टो धूमराजीरिवानलः ॥ १६ ॥
explanation: The mountain also discharged from its flanks massive boulders containing realgar even as a fire burning with a mild flame would release columns of smoke. (16)

shloka_text:
हरिणा पीड्यमानेन पीड्यमानानि सर्वतः ।
गुहाविष्टानि सत्त्वानि विनेदुर्विकृतैः स्वरैः ॥ १७ ॥
explanation: Being tormented by the squeezing, the mountain, which was being hard pressed by Hanumān, the creatures took to caverns and shrieked in unnatural tones. (17)

shloka_text:
स महान् सत्त्वसन्नादः शैलपीडानिमित्तजः ।
पृथिवीं पूरयामास दिशश्चोपवनानि च ॥ १८ ॥
explanation: That loud clamour of the creatures inhabiting the mountain, occasioned by the circumstance of pressure exerted on the mountain by Hanumān, filled the earth as well as the four quarters and the groves. (18)

shloka_text:
शिरोभिः पृथुभिर्नागा व्यक्तस्वस्तिकलक्षणैः ।
वमन्तः पावकं घोरं ददंशुर्दशनैः शिलाः ॥ १९ ॥
explanation: Vomiting a terrible fire through their large heads (mouths,) which revealed the marks of Swastika on them, snakes bit the rocks with their fangs. (19)

shloka_text:
तास्तदा सविषैर्दष्टाः कुपितैस्तैर्महाशिलाः ।
जञ्वलुः पावकोहीसा बिभिदुश्च सहस्रधा ॥ २० ॥
explanation: Bitten by those venomous serpents provoked to anger, the aforesaid huge rocks burst into flames as though lighted by fire, and got split up into thousands of fragments. (20)

shloka_text:
यानि त्वौषधजालानि तस्मिञ्जातानि पर्वते ।
विषघ्रान्यपि नागानां न शोकुः शमितुं विषम् ॥ २१ ॥
explanation: Even the bunches of medicinal herbs, capable of counteracting poison, which had sprung up on that mountain, could not neutralize the poison of the snakes. (21)

shloka_text:
भिद्यतेऽयं गिरिर्भूतैरिति मत्वा तपस्विनः ।
त्रस्ता विद्याधरास्तस्मादुत्पेतुः स्त्रीगणैः सह ॥ २२ ॥
explanation: Alarmed to think that the mountain in question was being riven by genii, ascetics practising austerities on it as well as the Vidyādharas enjoying life there with the hosts of their womenfolk rose in the air from that mountain. (22)

shloka_text:
पानभूमिगतं हित्वा हैममासवभाजनम् ।
पात्राणि च महाहाणि करकांश्च हिरण्मयान् ॥ २३ ॥
लेह्यानुच्चाववान् भक्ष्यान् मांसानि विविधानि च ।
आर्षभाणि च चर्माणि खड्गांश्च कनकत्सरून् ॥ २४ ॥
कृतकण्ठगुणाः क्षीबा रक्तमाल्यानुलेपनाः ।
रक्ताक्षाः पुष्कराक्षाश्च गगनं प्रतिपेदिरे ॥ २५ ॥
explanation: Leaving their gold jug of wine lying in the liquor-house as well as their precious utensils and gold vases for carrying water as also sauces of every description capable of being licked and articles of food that could be easily gulped, fruit pulps of various kinds, shields made of the hides of oxen and swords with gold hilts, the intoxicated Vidyādharas with reddish lotus-like eyes, who had put garlands around their neck, and were decorated with red flowers and daubed with red sandal-paste, rose to the heavens. (23—25)

shloka_text:
हारनूपुरकेयूरपारिहार्यधराः स्त्रियः ।
विस्मिताः सस्मितास्तस्थुराकाशे रमणैः सह ॥ २६ ॥
explanation: Wearing pearl necklaces, anklets, armlets and bangles, the Vidyādhara women stood astonished and full of smiles with their husbands in the airspace. (26)

shloka_text:
दर्शयन्तो महाविद्यां विद्याधरमहर्षयः ।
सहितास्तस्थुराकाशे वीक्षांचक्रुश्च पर्वतम् ॥ २७ ॥
explanation: Revealing their great skill in the form of 28 * VĀLMĪKI-RĀMĀYAṆA * capability to remain standing in the airspace, which had obviously been acquired through some magical spell, the Vidyādharas, who looked like eminent sages, stood in a body in the airspace and gazed down on the mountain. (27)

shloka_text:
शुश्रुवुश्च तदा शब्दमृषीणां भावितात्मनाम्।
चारणानां च सिद्धानां स्थितानां विमलेऽम्बरे ॥ २८ ॥
explanation: Nay, they heard at that time the following observation of the pure-minded Ṛṣis (seers of Vedic Mantras), Cāraṇas (celestial bards) and Siddhas (a class of demigods endowed with mystic powers from their very birth) standing like them in the cloudless sky: (28)

shloka_text:
एष पर्वतसंकाशो हनुमान् मारुतात्मजः।
तितीर्षति महावेगः समुद्रं वरुणालयम् ॥ २९ ॥
explanation: “Looking like a mountain in size and possessed of extraordinary vigour, the yonder Hanumān, son of the wind-god, seeks to leap across the sea, the abode of Varuṇa, the god of water. (29)

shloka_text:
रामार्थं वानरार्थं च चिकीर्षन् कर्म दुष्करम्।
समुद्रस्य परं पारं दुष्प्रापं प्रासुमिच्छति ॥ ३० ॥
explanation: “Eager to perform for the cause of Śrī Rāma and the monkeys, a feat which is hard to accomplish, he seeks to touch the other (opposite) shore of the sea, which is difficult to reach.” (30)

shloka_text:
इति विद्याधरा वाचः श्रुत्वा तेषां तपस्विनाम्।
तमप्रमेयं ददृशुः पर्वते वानरर्षभम् ॥ ३१ ॥
explanation: Hearing the aforesaid remarks of those ascetics, the Vidyādharas espied on the mountain-like Hanumān, the foremost of monkeys, whose strength was beyond measure. (31)

shloka_text:
दुधुवे च स रोमाणि चकम्पे चानलोपमः।
ननादं च महानादं सुमहानिव तोयदः ॥ ३२ ॥
explanation: Nay, looking like a flame, Hanumān shook the hair on his body and quivered and loudly thundered like a huge cloud. (32)

shloka_text:
आनुपूर्व्यां च वृत्तं तल्लाङ्गुलं रोमभिश्चतम्।
उत्पतिष्यन् विचिक्षेप पाक्षराज इवोरगम् ॥ ३३ ॥
explanation: While about to spring up, he stretched out his prominent tail which was thickly set with hair and had been successively rolled up in a circle—as Garuḍa, the king of birds, would jolt a snake. (33)

shloka_text:
तस्य लाङ्गुलमाविद्धमतिवेगस्य पृष्ठतः।
ददृशे गरुडेनेव ह्रियमाणो महोरगः ॥ ३४ ॥
explanation: Curled at his back, the tail of Hanumān, who was full of great vigour, looked like a huge serpent being borne away by Garuḍa. (34)

shloka_text:
बाहू संस्तम्भयामास महापरिघसंनिभौ।
आससाद कपिः कट्यां चरणौ संचुकोच च ॥ ३५ ॥
explanation: Hanumān firmly fixed on the mountain his arms, which resembled a pair of huge iron clubs, and crouched at the waist and also contracted his feet. (35)

shloka_text:
संहृत्य च भुजौ श्रीमांस्तथैव च शिरोधराम्।
तेजः सत्त्वं तथा वीर्यमाविवेश स वीर्यवान् ॥ ३६ ॥
explanation: Nay, drawing in his arms and likewise his neck too, the glorious and powerful Hanumān summoned all his energy, courage and virility. (36)

shloka_text:
मार्गमालोकयन् दूरादूर्ध्वप्रणिहितेक्षणः।
रुरोध हृदये प्राणानाकाशमवलोकयन् ॥ ३७ ॥
explanation: Having cast his eyes upwards in order to survey the long distance he had to cover, he held his breath in the heart while looking into the sky. (37)

shloka_text:
पद्म्यां दृढमवस्थानं कृत्वा स कपिकुञ्जरः।
निकुच्य कर्णौ हनुमानुत्पतिष्यन् महाबलः ॥ ३८ ॥
वानरान् वानरश्रेष्ठ इदं वचनमब्रवीत्।
यथा राघवनिर्मुक्तः शरः श्वसनविक्रमः ॥ ३९ ॥
गच्छेत् तद्वद्गमिष्यामि लंकां रावणपालिताम्।
नहि द्रक्ष्यामि यदि तां लंकायां जनकात्मजाम् ॥ ४० ॥
अनेनैव हि वेगेन गमिष्यामि सुरालयम्।
यदि वा त्रिदिवे सीतां न द्रक्ष्यामि कृतश्रमः ॥ ४१ ॥
बद्ध्वा राक्षसराजानमानयिष्यामि रावणम्।
सर्वथा कृतकार्योऽहमेष्यामि सह सीतया ॥ ४२ ॥
explanation: Having firmly established himself with his feet, and contracting his ears, while * SUNDARAKĀṆḌA * 29 about to leap, Hanumān, that elephant among the monkeys, nay, the foremost of monkeys, who was endowed with extraordinary might, addressed the following words to the monkeys: “Even as an arrow shot by Śrī Rāma, a scion of Raghu, would fly with the speed of the wind, I too would, likewise, course to Laṅkā, which is guarded by Rāvaṇa. If, however, I don’t find Sītā, the daughter of Janaka, in Laṅkā, I shall certainly proceed with the same speed to heaven, the abode of gods. If I don’t find Sītā in heaven even after exerting myself much, I shall bring Rāvaṇa, the ruler of ogres, in chains. At all events I shall return successful with Sītā. Or, else I shall bring Laṅkā with Rāvaṇa after uprooting it.” (38—42)

shloka_text:
आनयिष्यामि वा लंकां समुत्पाट्य सरावणाम्।
एवमुक्त्वा तु हनुमान् वानरो वानरोत्तमः ॥ ४३ ॥
उत्पाताथ वेगेन वेगवानविचारयन्।
सुपर्णमिव चात्मानं मेने स कपिकुञ्जरः ॥ ४४ ॥
explanation: Saying so, Hanumān, the foremost of monkeys, for his part, who was full of vigour, sprang up in the sky with impetuosity, unmindful of the exertion. Nay, that elephant among the monkeys accounted himself a compeer of Garuḍa. (43-44)

shloka_text:
समुत्पतति वेगात् तु वेगात् ते नगरोहिणः।
संहृत्य विटपान् सर्वान् समुत्पेतुः समन्ततः ॥ ४५ ॥
explanation: Drawing together all their boughs even while Hanumān sprang up in the sky with vehemence, the aforesaid trees growing on the mountain flew with force on all sides. (45)

shloka_text:
स मत्तकोयष्टिभकान् पादपान् पुष्पशालिनः।
उद्गहन्नुरुवेगेन जगाम विमलेऽम्बरे ॥ ४६ ॥
explanation: Bearing aloft in his great onrush the trees charming with flowers and with lapwings in heat perched on them, Hanumān coursed through the cloudless sky. (46)

shloka_text:
ऊरुवेगोथिता वृक्षा मुहूर्तं कपिमन्वयुः।
प्रस्थितं दीर्घमध्वानं स्वबन्धुमिव बान्धवाः ॥ ४७ ॥
explanation: Swept away by the force of his thighs, the trees followed the monkey for a while like relatives accompanying their near and dear ones set out on a long journey. (47)

shloka_text:
तमूरुवेगोन्मथिताः सालाश्चान्ये नगोत्तमाः।
अनुजग्मुर्हनुमन्तं सैन्या इव महीपतिम् ॥ ४८ ॥
explanation: Uprooted by the impetus of his thighs, sal and other excellent trees followed Hanumān even as troops would follow a king. (48)

shloka_text:
सुपुष्पिताग्रैर्बहुभिः पादपैरन्वितः कपिः।
हनुमान् पर्वताकारो बभूवाद्भुतदर्शनः ॥ ४९ ॥
explanation: Followed by numerous trees with their extremities laden with blossoms, Hanumān, who looked like a mountain in size, presented a weird appearance. (49)

shloka_text:
सारवन्तोऽथ ये वृक्षा न्यमर्जल्लवणाम्भसि।
भयादिव महेन्द्रस्य पर्वता वरुणालये ॥ ५० ॥
explanation: Trees, which were solid, forthwith sank into the brackish sea even as mountains in the hoary past took a plunge into the ocean (the abode of Varuṇa) in fear of the mighty Indra. (50)

shloka_text:
स नानाकुसुमैः कीर्णः कपिः साङ्कुरकोरकैः।
शुशुभे मेघसंकाशः खद्योतैरिव पर्वतः ॥ ५१ ॥
explanation: Covered with flowers of every kind, dropped from the trees that followed him, including shoots and buds, the aforesaid Hanumān, who resembled a cloud, shone brightly as a mountain with fireflies. (51)

shloka_text:
विमुक्तास्तस्य वेगेन मुक्त्वा पुष्पाणि ते द्रुमाः।
व्यवशीर्यन्त सलिले निवृत्ताः सुहृदो यथा ॥ ५२ ॥
explanation: Shedding their blossom when receded by his impetus, the said trees dropped into the water of the sea like near and dear ones returned after escorting their relative up to the margin of water. (52)

shloka_text:
लघुत्वेनोपपन्नं तद् विचित्रं सागरेऽपतत्।
द्रुमाणां विविधं पुष्पं कपिवायुसमीरितम्।
ताराचितमिवाकाशं प्रबभौ स महार्णवः ॥ ५३ ॥
explanation: Swept away by the wind set in motion 30 * VĀLMĪKI-RĀMĀYAṆA * by Hanumān dashing forward across the sky, the blossom on the trees, consisting of every variety, dropped on the ocean and presented a curious sight while floating, endowed as they were with lightness of weight. Carpeted with them, that vast sea looked charming like the star-spangled sky. (53)

shloka_text:
पुष्पौषेण सुगन्धेन नानावर्णेन वानरः।
बभौ मेघ इवोद्यन् वै विद्युदृणविभूषितः ॥ ५४ ॥
explanation: Covered with a shower of fragrant flowers of various tints, Hanumān actually looked charming like a rising cloud streaked with flashes of lightning. (54)

shloka_text:
तस्य वेगसमुद्भूतैः पुष्पैस्तोयमदृश्यत।
ताराभिरिव रामाभिरुदिताभिरिवाम्बरम् ॥ ५५ ॥
explanation: Overspread with flowers scattered by his impetus, the sea-water resembled the firmament spangled with lovely stars just risen. (55)

shloka_text:
तस्याम्बरगतौ बाहू ददृशाते प्रसारितौ।
पर्वताग्राद् विनिष्कान्तौ पञ्चास्याविव पन्नगौ ॥ ५६ ॥
explanation: His two arms outstretched in space looked like a pair of five-hooded serpents risen from a mountain-top. (56)

shloka_text:
पिबन्निव बभौ चापि सोर्मिजालं महार्णवम्।
पिपासुरिव चाकाशं ददृशे स महाकपिः ॥ ५७ ॥
explanation: Nay, while looking downward the mighty Hanumān appeared as though drinking up the vast sea alongwith the mass of its waves; and looking upwards, he appeared keen to imbibe the sky. (57)

shloka_text:
तस्य विद्युत्प्रभाकारे वायुमार्गानुसारिणः।
नयने विप्रकाशेते पर्वतस्थाविवानलौ ॥ ५८ ॥
explanation: The eyes of Hanumān, who was following the course of the wind, blazed like a pair of fires burning on a mountain, flashing as they did like lightning. (58)

shloka_text:
पिङ्गे पिङ्गाक्षमुख्यस्य बृहती परिमण्डले।
चक्षुषी सम्प्रकाशेते चन्द्रसूर्याविव स्थितौ ॥ ५९ ॥
explanation: Nay, the reddish-brown large round eyes of Hanumān, the foremost of monkeys, shed their bright light like the moon and the sun shining together. (59)

shloka_text:
मुखं नासिकया तस्य ताम्रया ताम्रमाबभौ।
संध्यया समभिस्मृष्टं यथा स्यात् सूर्यमण्डलम् ॥ ६० ॥
explanation: Due to the reflection of his coppery nose, his countenance looked red as the solar orb embraced by dusk. (60)

shloka_text:
लाङ्गुलं च समाविद्धं प्लवमानस्य शोभते।
अम्बरे वायुपुत्रस्य शक्रध्वज इवोच्छ्रितम् ॥ ६१ ॥
explanation: Moreover, the coiled tail of Hanumān, son of the wind-god, darting across the sky looked charming like a tall banner hoisted (on the twelfth day of the bright half of Bhādrapada) in honour of Indra, the ruler of gods. (61)

shloka_text:
लाङ्गुलचक्रो हनुमान् शुक्लदंष्ट्रोऽनिलात्मजः।
व्यरोचत महाप्राज्ञः परिवेषीव भास्करः ॥ ६२ ॥
explanation: With his curled tail and white teeth, the highly intelligent Hanumān, an offspring of the wind-god, shone brightly as the sun encircled by a misty halo. (62)

shloka_text:
स्फिग्देशेनातिताम्रेण रराज स महाकपिः।
महता दारितेनेव गिरिगैरिकधातुना ॥ ६३ ॥
explanation: With his deep-red rump, that mighty Hanumān looked splendid like a mountain with a large deposit of red chalk rent asunder. (63)

shloka_text:
तस्य वानरसिंहस्य प्लवमानस्य सागरम्।
कक्षान्तरगतो वायुर्जीमृत इव गर्जति ॥ ६४ ॥
explanation: The wind passing through the arm-pits of that leonine Hanumān, bounding over the sea, thundered like a cloud. (64)

shloka_text:
खे यथा निपतत्युल्का उत्तरान्ताद् विनिःसृता।
दृश्यते सानुबन्धा च तथा स कपिकुञ्जरः ॥ ६५ ॥
explanation: That elephant among the monkeys was seen darting much in the same way as a meteor risen from the upper part of the northern quarter shoots alongwith its tail-like extremity. (65)

shloka_text:
पतत्पतङ्गसंकाशो व्यायतः शुशुभे कपिः।
प्रवृद्ध इव मातङ्गः कक्ष्यया बध्यमानया ॥ ६६ ॥
explanation: The enormous monkey, Hanumān, who resembled the moving sun, looked charming with his tail entwined round his waist as a fully developed elephant with a girth tied round its waist. (66)

shloka_text:
उपरिष्टाच्छरीरणं चायया चावगाढया।
सागरे मारुताविष्टा नौरिवासीत् तदा कपिः ॥ ६७ ॥
explanation: Coursing above with his body and with his reflection immersed in water, Hanumān looked at that time like a vessel propelled by the wind above and sailing on the sea below. (67)

shloka_text:
यं यं देशं समुद्रस्य जगाम स महाकपिः।
स तु तस्याङ्गवेगेन सोन्माद इव लक्ष्यते ॥ ६८ ॥
explanation: Whichever part of the sea that enormous Hanumān passed over, it looked actually riotous, as it were, due to the impetus of his body and terrific speed. (68)

shloka_text:
सागरस्योर्मिजालानामुरसा शैलवर्षणाम्।
अभिध्वंस्तु महावेगः पुप्लुवे स महाकपिः ॥ ६९ ॥
explanation: Full of extraordinary vehemence, that huge monkey, Hanumān, dashed forward actually smashing with his breast the rows of waves of the sea, rising as high as mountains. (69)

shloka_text:
कपिवातश्च बलवान् मेघवातश्च निर्गतः।
सागरं भीमनिर्हृदं कम्पयामासतुर्भृशम् ॥ ७० ॥
explanation: The mighty wind generated by the impetus of Hanumān as well as the wind set in motion by clouds, when adrift, violently agitated the sea, which began to roar terribly. (70)

shloka_text:
विकर्षन्नृर्मिजालानि बृहन्ति लवणाम्भसि।
पुप्लुवे कपिशार्दूलो विकिरन्निव रोदसी ॥ ७१ ॥
explanation: Forcibly drawing series of huge billows in the salt sea, Hanumān, a tiger among monkeys, sped along agitating the earth and heaven both, as it were. (71)

shloka_text:
मेरुमन्दरसंकाशानुद्रतान् सुमहर्णवे।
अत्यक्रामन्महावेगस्तरङ्गान् गणयन्निव ॥ ७२ ॥
explanation: Hanumān, who was rushing alongwith great speed, moved on counting, as it were, the billows resembling Mounts Meru and Mandara in size, raised in the vast sea. (72)

shloka_text:
तस्य वेगसमुद्घुष्टं जलं सजलदं तदा।
अम्बरस्थं विबभ्राजे शरदभ्रमिवाततम् ॥ ७३ ॥
explanation: The water raised by his onrush and hanging in the air alongwith clouds looked exceptionally charming at that time like an outstretched mass of autumnal clouds. (73)

shloka_text:
तिमिनक्रङ्गषाः कूर्मा दृश्यन्ते विवृतास्तदा।
वस्त्रापकर्षणेनेव शरीराणि शरीरिणाम् ॥ ७४ ॥
explanation: Exposed at that time on account of the sea-water being raised by the onrush of Hanumān, whales, crocodiles, alligators and turtles became visible even like the limbs of men uncovered by drawing the covering off. (74)

shloka_text:
क्रममाणं समीक्ष्याथ भुजगाः सागरंगमाः।
व्योमि तं कपिशार्दूलं सुपर्णमिव मेनिरे ॥ ७५ ॥
explanation: Keenly observing that tiger among the monkeys coursing through space, the serpents moving in the sea forthwith took him to be Garuḍa endowed with lovely wings. (75)

shloka_text:
दशयोजनविस्तीर्णां त्रिंशद्योजनमायता।
छाया वानरसिंहस्य जवे चारुतराभवत् ॥ ७६ ॥
explanation: The shadow of that lion among monkeys, Hanumān, which was ten Yojanas (or eighty miles) wide and thirty Yojanas (or two hundred forty miles) long, appeared lovelier due to the rapidity of his movement. (76)

shloka_text:
श्वेताभ्रधनराजीव वायुपुत्रानुगामिनी।
तस्य सा शुशुभे छाया पतिता लवणाम्भसि ॥ ७७ ॥
explanation: Falling on the salt sea and following Hanumān, an offspring of the wind-god, that 32 * VĀLMĪKI-RĀMĀYAṆA * shadow of his looked charming like a row of clouds sailing in the white sky. (77)

shloka_text:
शुशुभे स महातेजा महाकायो महाकपिः।
वायुमार्गे निरालम्बे पक्षवानिव पर्वतः ॥ ७८ ॥
explanation: On his aerial path, where he had nothing to rest upon, that great monkey of vast proportions, who was endowed with extraordinary energy, appeared lovely like a winged mountain. (78)

shloka_text:
येनासौ याति बलवान् वेगेन कपिकुञ्जरः।
तेन मार्गेण सहसा द्रोणीकृत् इवार्णवः ॥ ७९ ॥
explanation: The sea below the path by which that mighty elephant-like monkey, Hanumān, moved with speed, got suddenly transformed into a trough, as it were. (79)

shloka_text:
आपाते पक्षिसङ्घानां पक्षिराज इव व्रजन्।
हनुमान् मेघजालानि प्रकर्षन् मारुतो यथा ॥ ८० ॥
explanation: Coursing through the path of birds like Garuḍa, the king of winged creatures, Hanumān appeared like the wind drawing away clouds with force. (80)

shloka_text:
पाण्डुरारुणवर्णानि नीलमञ्जिष्ठकानि च।
कपिनाऽऽकृष्यमाणानि महाभ्राणि चकाशिरे ॥ ८१ ॥
explanation: Being drawn by Hanumān, big clouds, which were either white or reddish in colour or blue or madder-coloured, looked charming; (81)

shloka_text:
प्रविशन्नभ्रजालानि निष्पतश्च पुनः पुनः।
प्रच्छन्नश्च प्रकाशश्च चन्द्रमा इव दृश्यते ॥ ८२ ॥
explanation: Repeatedly entering into the masses of clouds and then emerging, he looked like the hidden and the visible moon, respectively. (82)

shloka_text:
प्लवमानं तु तं दृष्ट्वा प्लवगं त्वरितं तदा।
ववृषुस्तत्र पुष्पाणि देवगन्धर्वचारणाः ॥ ८३ ॥
explanation: Seeing the aforesaid Hanumān bounding apace at that time, gods, Gandharvas (celestial songsters) and Dānavas (demons) rained flowers on him. (83)

shloka_text:
तताप नहि तं सूर्यः प्लवन्तं वानरेश्वरम्।
सिषेवे च तदा वायू रामकार्यार्थसिद्धये ॥ ८४ ॥
explanation: The sun did not actually scorch Hanumān, the ruler of monkeys, who was travelling for the sake of accomplishing his object in the shape of Śrī Rāma's task viz., the quest of Sītā; while the wind-god ministered to him by fanning him with a delightful breeze in order to refresh him. (84)

shloka_text:
ऋषयस्तुष्टुवुश्चैनं प्लवमानं विहायसा।
जगुश्च देवगन्धर्वाः प्रशंसन्तो वनौकसम् ॥ ८५ ॥
explanation: Nay, Ṛṣis (seers of Vedic Mantras) extolled Hanumān coursing through airspace; while gods and Gandharvas sang praises in order to sustain him in his arduous journey. (85)

shloka_text:
नागाश्च तुष्टुवुर्यक्षा रक्षांसि विविधानि च।
प्रेक्ष्य सर्वे कपिवरं सहसा विगतकलमम् ॥ ८६ ॥
explanation: Observing Hanumān, the foremost of monkeys, with a smile on his lips and entirely free from languor, Nāgas (semi-divine beings having the face of a man and the tail of a serpent, and inhabiting Pātāla) and Yakṣas (a class of demigods) as well as ogres of all classes—all lauded him. (86)

shloka_text:
तस्मिन् प्लवगशार्दूले प्लवमाने हनूमति।
इक्ष्वाकुकुलमानार्थी चिन्तयामास सागरः ॥ ८७ ॥
explanation: While Hanumān, that tiger among monkeys, was moving along through airspace, the deity presiding over oceans, who sought to do honour to the lineage of Ikṣwāku, to which Śrī Rāma had the honour to belong, reflected as follows : (87)

shloka_text:
साहाय्यं वानरेन्द्रस्य यदि नाहं हनूमतः।
करिष्यामि भविष्यामि सर्ववाच्यो विवक्षताम् ॥ ८८ ॥
explanation: 'If I do not lend assistance to Hanumān, a leader of monkeys, I shall incur the obloquy of all among those gifted with speech. (88)

shloka_text:
अहमिक्ष्वाकुनाथेन सगरेण विवर्धितः।
इक्ष्वाकुसचिवश्चायं तन्नार्हत्यवसादितुम् ॥ ८९ ॥
explanation: * SUNDARAKĀṆḌA * 33 ‘I was greatly extended by King Sagara, the protector of Ikṣwāku’s race, while Hanumān is helping Śrī Rāma, a descendant of Ikṣwāku. He must not, therefore, come to grief in this journey. (89)

shloka_text:
तथा मया विधातव्यं विश्रमेत यथा कपिः ।
शेषं च मयि विश्रान्तः सुखी सोऽतितरिष्यति ॥ ९० ॥
explanation: ‘I should so arrange that Hanumān may rest awhile. Having rested awhile on me, I am sure he will leap across the rest of the sea with ease.’ (90)

shloka_text:
इति कृत्वा मतिं साध्वीं समुद्रश्छन्नमभसि ।
हिरण्यनाभं मैनाकमुवाच गिरिसत्तमम् ॥ ९१ ॥
explanation: Having made this righteous resolve, the god presiding over the oceans spoke as follows to Maināka, the foremost of mountains, consisting mainly of gold and submerged in water : (91)

shloka_text:
त्वमिहासुरसङ्गानां देवराज्ञा महात्मना ।
पातालनिलयानां हि परिघः संनिवेशितः ॥ ९२ ॥
explanation: “You have actually been established here by the high-souled Indra, the ruler of gods, by way of a barrier against the intrusion into the terrestrial region of the hordes of demons inhabiting Pātāla, the nethermost subterranean region. (92)

shloka_text:
त्वमेषां ज्ञातवीर्याणां पुनरेवोत्पत्तिष्वताम् ।
पातालस्याप्रमेयस्य द्वारमावृत्य तिष्ठसि ॥ ९३ ॥
explanation: “You stand here blocking the entrance of the immeasurable Pātāla against the aforesaid demons, whose valour is well known and who are prone to come up to the surface of this earth once more. (93)

shloka_text:
तिर्यगूर्ध्वमधश्चैव शक्तिस्ते शैल वर्धितुम् ।
तस्मात् संचोदयामि त्वामुत्तिष्ठ गिरिसत्तम ॥ ९४ ॥
explanation: “The capacity to grow from side to side (horizontally) as also upwards and downwards (vertically) is there in you, O mountain! I, therefore, command you as follows: please swell upwards, O jewel among mountains! (94)

shloka_text:
स एष कपिशार्दूलस्त्वामुप्येति वीर्यवान् ।
हनुमान् रामकार्यार्थी भीमकर्मा खमाप्लुतः ॥ ९५ ॥
explanation: “Here is the powerful Hanumān of terrific deeds, a veritable tiger among monkeys, who has already sprung in the sky, seeking, as he does, to achieve the purpose of Śrī Rāma, passing over you. (95)

shloka_text:
अस्य साह्यं मया कार्यमिक्ष्वाकुकुलवर्तिनः ।
मम इक्ष्वाकवः पूज्याः परं पूज्यतमास्तव ॥ ९६ ॥
explanation: “Assistance must be rendered by me to Hanumān, who is a servant of the House of Ikṣwāku. The Ikṣwākus are worthy of adoration to me and are by far the highest object of veneration to you. (96)

shloka_text:
कुरु साचिव्यमस्माकं न नः कार्यमतिक्रमेत् ।
कर्तव्यमकृतं कार्यं सतां मन्यमुदीरयेत् ॥ ९७ ॥
explanation: “Therefore, please render assistance to us. Our plan should not be allowed to miscarry through default. A duty which needs must be performed is likely to rouse the anger of the virtuous if not scrupulously discharged. (97)

shloka_text:
सलिलादूर्ध्वमुत्तिष्ठ तिष्ठत्वेष कपिस्त्वयि ।
अस्माकमतिथिश्चैव पूज्यश्च प्लवतां वरः ॥ ९८ ॥
explanation: “Therefore, rise up from the water. Let Hanumān stand on you. Hanumān, the foremost of monkeys, is our unexpected guest and worthy of our adoration, too. (98)

shloka_text:
चामीकरमहानाभ देवगन्धर्वसेवित ।
हनुमाँस्त्वयि विश्रान्तस्ततः शेषं गमिष्यति ॥ ९९ ॥
explanation: “Having rested on you, O mountain with a lofty peak of gold and frequented by gods and Gandharvas, Hanumān will then cover the remaining distance. (99)

shloka_text:
काकुत्स्थस्यानुशंस्यं च मैथिल्याश्च विवासनम् ।
श्रमं च प्लवगेन्द्रस्य समीक्ष्योत्थातुमर्हसि ॥ १०० ॥
explanation: “Nay, fully considering the soft-heartedness of Śrī Rāma, a scion of Kakutstha, as well as of Sītā, a princess of Mithilā, living perforce in an alien land, as 34 * VĀLMĪKI-RĀMĀYAṆA * also the exertion of Hanumān, a leader of monkeys, you ought to rise up.” (100)

shloka_text:
हिरण्यगर्भो मैनाको निशम्य लवणाम्भसः।
उत्पपात जलात् तूर्णं महादुमलतावृतः ॥ १०१ ॥
explanation: Hearing the aforesaid words of Varuṇa, the deity presiding over the salty sea, Mount Maināka, which contained deposits of gold in its bowels and was covered by large trees and creepers, instantly emerged from under the water. (101)

shloka_text:
स सागरजलं भित्त्वा बभूवात्युच्छ्रुतस्तदा।
यथा जलधरं भित्त्वा दीसरशिमर्दिवाकरः ॥ १०२ ॥
explanation: Dividing the sea-water, Maināka rose very high at that moment even as the sun with its brilliant rays would, tearing the veil of a cloud. (102)

shloka_text:
स महात्मा मुहूर्तेन पर्वतः सलिलावृतः।
दर्शयामास शृङ्गाणि सागरेण नियोजितः ॥ १०३ ॥
explanation: Enjoined by the deity presiding over the ocean, the aforesaid mountain of vast proportions, which had heretofore been covered with water, revealed its peaks in an instant. (103)

shloka_text:
शातकुम्भमयैः शृङ्गैः सकिंनरमहोरगैः।
आदित्योदयसंकाशैरुल्लिखद्भिरिवाम्बरम् ॥ १०४ ॥
explanation: The mountain looked charming with its peaks of gold, which were inhabited by Kinnaras (a class of demigods with a human figure and the head of a horse) and huge serpents, and shimmered like the sun at dawn, and which were scraping the skies, as it were. (104)

shloka_text:
तस्य जाम्बूनदैः शृङ्गैः पर्वतस्य समुत्थितैः।
आकाशं शस्त्रसंकाशमभवत् काञ्चनप्रभम् ॥ १०५ ॥
explanation: Due to the towering peaks of that mountain, consisting of gold, the blue sky which shone like a sword, now shed the lustre of gold. (105)

shloka_text:
जातरूपमयैः शृङ्गैर्भ्राजमानैर्महाप्रभैः।
आदित्यशतसंकाशः सोऽभवद् गिरिसत्तमः ॥ १०६ ॥
explanation: With its shining peaks of gold, emitting a dazzling splendour, that jewel among mountains shone brightly like a hundred suns. (106)

shloka_text:
समुत्थितमसङ्गेन हनुमानग्रतः स्थितम्।
मध्ये लवणतोयस्य विघ्नोऽयमिति निश्चितः ॥ १०७ ॥
explanation: Hanumān positively considered the mountain, which instantly stood very high before him in the midst of the salty sea, to be a stumbling block in his journey. (107)

shloka_text:
स तमुच्छ्रुतमत्यर्थं महावेगो महाकपिः।
उरसा पातयामास जीमूतमिव मारुतः ॥ १०८ ॥
explanation: Hanumān, the mighty monkey, who was possessed of great impetuosity, felled with his breast the exceedingly lofty mountain even as the wind would strike down a cloud. (108)

shloka_text:
स तदासादितस्तेन कपिना पर्वतोत्तमः।
बुद्ध्वा तस्य हरेर्वेगं जहर्षं च ननाद च ॥ १०९ ॥
explanation: Worsted on that occasion by the aforesaid Hanumān and recognizing his impetuosity, Maināka, the foremost of mountains, felt rejoiced and roared too. (109)

shloka_text:
तमाकाशगतं वीरमाकाशे समुपस्थितः।
प्रीतो हृष्टमना वाक्यमब्रवीत् पर्वतः कपिम् ॥ ११० ॥
मानुषं धारयन् रूपमात्मनः शिखरे स्थितः।
दुष्करं कृतवान् कर्म त्वमिदं वानरोत्तम ॥ १११ ॥
explanation: Assuming the form of a human being and standing on his own summit, the mountain, which stood very high once more in the sky, glad at heart, lovingly spoke as follows to Hanumān, the heroic monkey, who still remained in the sky: “You have undertaken this task, which is hard to accomplish, O jewel among monkeys! (110-111)

shloka_text:
निपत्य मम शृङ्गेषु सुखं विश्रम्य गम्यताम्।
राघवस्य कुले जातैरुदधिः परिवर्धितः ॥ ११२ ॥
explanation: “Alighting on my peaks and having comfortably rested awhile, resume your journey with renewed vigour. The ocean * SUNDARAKĀṆḌA * 35 was extended by the sons of Sagara, who were born in the ancestry of Śrī Rāma. (112)

shloka_text:
स त्वां रामहिते युक्तं प्रत्यर्चयति सागरः।
कृते च प्रतिकर्तव्यमेष धर्मः सनातनः ॥ ११३ ॥
explanation: “The deity presiding over the said sea seeks to offer respect to you, who are engaged in the service of Śrī Rāma. And service must be rendered in return for a service: such is the eternal law. (113)

shloka_text:
सोऽयं तत्प्रतिकारार्थी त्वतः सम्मानमहंति।
त्वन्निमित्तमनेनाहं बहुमानात् प्रचोदितः ॥ ११४ ॥
explanation: “Hence, seeking to repay that obligation of his benefactors, the sons of Sagara, this Ocean merits attention in the shape of willingness to accept his hospitality by you. I have, therefore, been very politely charged by him in the following words to honour you: (114)

shloka_text:
योजनानां शतं चापि कपिरेष खमाप्लुतः।
तव सानुषु विश्रान्तः शेषं प्रक्रमतामिति ॥ ११५ ॥
explanation: “Hanumān has taken a leap in the sky with a view to covering a distance of even a hundred Yojanas (or eight hundred miles). Having rested awhile on your peaks, he may cover the remaining distance.” (115)

shloka_text:
तिष्ठ त्वं हरिशार्दूल मयि विश्रम्य गम्यताम्।
तदिदं गन्धवत् स्वादु कन्दमूलफलं बहु ॥ ११६ ॥
explanation: “Therefore, tarry, O tiger among monkeys, and proceed further after reposing on me for some time. Here are abundant bulbs, roots and fruits, both fragrant and luscious. (116)

shloka_text:
तदास्वाद्य हरिश्रेष्ठ विश्रान्तोऽथ गमिष्यसि।
अस्माकमपि सम्बन्धः कपिमुख्य त्वयास्ति वै।
प्रख्यातस्त्रिषु लोकेषु महागुणपरिग्रहः ॥ ११७ ॥
explanation: “Having relished them, O jewel among monkeys, and reposed for a short while, you should then proceed on your course. Indeed we too have some relation with you, O jewel among monkeys! You are a repository of great virtues and are widely known in all the three worlds. (117)

shloka_text:
वेगवन्तः प्लवन्तो ये प्लवगा मारुतात्मज।
तेषां मुख्यतमं मन्ये त्वामहं कपिकुञ्जर ॥ ११८ ॥
explanation: “I account you the most prominent among monkeys, who are given to leaping and full of vigour, O elephant among monkeys! (118)

shloka_text:
अतिथिः किल पूजार्हः प्राकृतोऽपि विजानता।
धर्मं जिज्ञासमानेन किं पुनर्यादृशो भवान् ॥ ११९ ॥
explanation: “Even an ordinary newcomer is surely deserving of adoration at the hands of a discerning man who is keen to know his duty, much more so an individual such as you. (119)

shloka_text:
त्वं हि देववरिष्ठस्य मारुतस्य महात्मनः।
पुत्रस्तस्यैव वेगेन सदृशः कपिकुञ्जर ॥ १२० ॥
explanation: “Indeed, you are a son of the high-souled wind-god, the most pre-eminent among gods, and the only one equal to him in speed, O elephant among monkeys! (120)

shloka_text:
पूजिते त्वयि धर्मज्ञे पूजां प्राप्नोति मारुतः।
तस्मात् त्वं पूजनीयो मे शृणु चाप्यत्र कारणम् ॥ १२१ ॥
explanation: “On your being adored, a knower as you are of what is right, the wind-god will have received my homage. You are worthy of adoration to me for that reason. Know one further reason for my adoring the wind-god through you : (121)

shloka_text:
पूर्वं कृतयुगे तात पर्वताः पक्षिणोऽभवन्।
तेऽपि जग्मुर्दिशः सर्वा गरुडा इव वेगिनः ॥ १२२ ॥
explanation: “Formerly, in Satyayuga, O dear one, mountains were endowed with wings. Full of speed they too used to range all the four quarters even like so many Garudas. (122)

shloka_text:
ततस्तेषु प्रयातेषु देवसङ्घाः सहर्षिभिः।
भूतानि च भयं जग्मुस्तेषां पतनशङ्कया ॥ १२३ ॥
explanation: “Therefore, when they moved with speed to and fro, hosts of gods with Ṛṣis (seers of 36 * VĀLMĪKI-RĀMĀYAṆA * Vedic Mantras) and spirits too fell a prey to panic, seized as they were with the apprehension of their falling. (123)

shloka_text:
ततः क्रुद्धः सहस्राक्षः पर्वतानां शतक्रतुः।
पक्षांश्चिच्छेद वत्रेण ततः शतसहस्रशः ॥ १२४ ॥
explanation: “Provoked to anger by their fear, Indra (who is presupposed to have performed a hundred Aśwamedha sacrifices in his previous existences as a condition precedent for attaining that position) thereupon lopped off with his thunderbolt the wings of mountains in hundreds of thousands. (124)

shloka_text:
स मामुपगतः क्रुद्धो वत्रमुद्यम्य देवराट्।
ततोऽहं सहसा क्षिप्तः श्वसनेन महात्मना ॥ १२५ ॥
अस्मिन्त्लवणतोये च प्रक्षिप्तः प्लवगोत्तम।
गुप्तपक्षः समग्रश्च तव पित्राभिरक्षितः ॥ १२६ ॥
explanation: “Lifting up his thunderbolt in anger, the aforesaid Indra, the ruler of gods, approached me too; I, however, was thereupon suddenly tossed into the sky by the high-souled wind-god and then violently cast into this salty sea. In this way my wings were preserved; nay, I was saved with all my being by your father, O jewel among monkeys! (125-126)

shloka_text:
ततोऽहं मानयामि त्वां मान्योऽसि मम मारुते।
त्वया ममेष सम्बन्धः कपिमुख्य महागुणः ॥ १२७ ॥
explanation: “Therefore, do I esteem you and you are worthy of honour to me, O son of the wind-god! This bond of mine with you in the shape of your being my benefactor's son is full of great potentialities, O leader of monkeys! (127)

shloka_text:
अस्मिन्त्वेनोते कार्ये सागरस्य ममैव च।
प्रीतिं प्रीतमनाः कर्तुं त्वमर्हसि महामते ॥ १२८ ॥
explanation: “This long awaited and welcome opportunity of repaying my debt to your father having thus fortunately arrived, you ought to oblige the deity presiding over the ocean as well as myself with a glad heart, O highly talented Hanumān! (128)

shloka_text:
श्रमं मोक्षय पूजां च गृहाण हरिसत्तम।
प्रीतिं च मम मान्यस्य प्रीतोऽस्मि तव दर्शनात् ॥ १२९ ॥
explanation: “Therefore, pray, relieve your fatigue and accept my hospitality as well as my affection, O jewel among the monkeys! I am pleased to see you, worthy of honour as you are to me.” (129)

shloka_text:
एवमुक्तः कपिश्रेष्ठस्तं नगोत्तममब्रवीत्।
प्रीतोऽस्मि कृतमातिथ्यं मन्युरेषोऽपनीयताम् ॥ १३० ॥
explanation: Spoken to as above by Maināka, Hanumān, the foremost of monkeys, replied as follows to the aforesaid jewel among mountains: “I am pleased with you and homage has been done by you in the form of kind words. Let this sad thought that your hospitality has not been accepted by me be banished from your mind. (130)

shloka_text:
त्वरते कार्यकालो मे अहश्चाप्यतिवर्तते।
प्रतिज्ञा च मया दत्ता न स्थातव्यमिहान्तरा ॥ १३१ ॥
explanation: “The time allotted to my duty of leaping across the sea and tracing out Sītā is hastening me. The day too is passing. Nay, plighted word has been given by me to my fellow monkeys to the effect that I would not tarry here midway.” (131)

shloka_text:
इत्युक्त्वा पाणिना शैलमालभ्य हरिपुङ्गवः।
जगामाकाशमाविश्य वीर्यवान् प्रहसन्निव ॥ १३२ ॥
explanation: Saying so and touching the mountain with his hand as a token of respect and friendship, nay, rising to the skies, the valiant Hanumān, the foremost of monkeys, sped on as though heartily laughing. (132)

shloka_text:
स पर्वतसमुद्राभ्यां बहुमानादवेक्षितः।
पूजितश्चोपपन्नाभिराशीर्भिरभिनन्दितः ॥ १३३ ॥
explanation: He was on that occasion regarded with great esteem, adored and cheered with suitable benedictions by the deities presiding over the mountain and the ocean both. (133)

shloka_text:
अथोर्ध्वं दूरमागत्य हित्वा शैलमहाणवौ।
पितुः पन्थानमासाद्य जगाम विमलेऽम्बरे ॥ १३४ ॥
explanation: Then, rising high, nay, leaving the mountain as well as the ocean, far below and reaching the path of the wind (i.e., his * SUNDARAKĀṆḌA * 37 father), Hanumān coursed through the cloudless sky. (134)

shloka_text:
भूयश्चोर्ध्वं गतिं प्राप्य गिरिं तमवलोकयन्।
वायुसूनिर्गालम्बो जगाम कपिकुञ्जरः ॥ १३५ ॥
explanation: Rising still higher and looking on the mountain below, Hanumān, a son of the wind-god, an elephant among the monkeys, moved on unsupported in the sky. (135)

shloka_text:
तद् द्वितीयं हनुमतो दृष्ट्वा कर्म सुदुष्करम्।
प्रशशंसुः सुराः सर्वे सिद्धाश्च परमर्षयः ॥ १३६ ॥
explanation: Seeing the aforesaid second feat of Hanumān, viz., refusal on his part to seize the golden opportunity offered to him by Mount Maināka to rest on its peaks, which was most difficult to accomplish, the gods, and the Siddhas as well as the greatest Ṛṣis—all lauded him. (136)

shloka_text:
देवताश्चाभवन् हृष्टास्तत्रस्थास्तस्य कर्मणा।
काञ्चनस्य सुनाभस्य सहस्राक्षश्च वासवः ॥ १३७ ॥
explanation: The gods, who happened to be on the mountain (at that time in order to see what the mountain intended to do by rising up), nay, Indra, the thousand-eyed god, too, all were pleased with the act of offering hospitality and foothold to Hanumān by that golden mountain with beautiful slopes. (137)

shloka_text:
उवाच वचनं धीमान् परितोषात् सगददम्।
सुनाभं पर्वतश्रेष्ठं स्वयमेव शचीपतिः ॥ १३८ ॥
explanation: The sagacious Indra (the spouse of Śaci) on his own initiative addressed the following words in faltering tones through intense gratification to Maināka, the foremost of mountains, distinguished by charming slopes : (138)

shloka_text:
हिरण्यनाभ शैलेन्द्र परितुष्टोऽस्मि ते भृशम्।
अभयं ते प्रयच्छामि गच्छ सौम्य यथासुखम् ॥ १३९ ॥
explanation: "I am extremely pleased with you, O lord of mountains with peaks of gold! I grant you immunity from all fear of being shorn of your wings by me. Therefore, proceed according to your pleasure, O gentle one! (139)

shloka_text:
साह्यं कृतं ते सुमहद् विश्रान्तस्य हनुमतः।
क्रमतो योजनशतं निर्भयस्य भये सति ॥ १४० ॥
explanation: "Exceedingly valuable assistance has been rendered by you to Hanumān, who is fearlessly attempting to leap over a distance of hundred Yojanas (or eight hundred miles), even though there is every risk of his getting exhausted in the course of his journey and falling down, and who has had the mental satisfaction of having rested. (140)

shloka_text:
रामस्यैष हितायैव याति दाशरथेः कपिः।
सत्क्रियां कुर्वता शक्त्या तोषितोऽस्मि दृढं त्वया ॥ १४१ ॥
explanation: "This monkey is journeying only for the benefit of Śrī Rāma, son of Daśaratha. And I have been highly gratified by you through a good turn done to Hanumān according to your capacity." (141)

shloka_text:
स तत् प्रहर्षमलभद् विपुलं पर्वतोत्तमः।
देवतानां पतिं दृष्ट्वा परितुष्टं शतक्रतुम् ॥ १४२ ॥
explanation: Seeing Indra, the ruler of gods, highly gratified, Maināka, the foremost of mountains, derived deep and abundant joy. (142)

shloka_text:
स वै दत्तवरः शैलो बभूवावस्थितस्तदा।
हनुमांश्च मुहूर्तेन व्यतिचक्राम सागरम् ॥ १४३ ॥
explanation: Having been granted, as above, by Indra the boon of security, the aforesaid mountain then stood rooted as before, below the surface of sea-water; while Hanumān shortly sped over the sea. (143)

shloka_text:
ततो देवाः सगन्धर्वाः सिद्धाश्च परमर्षयः।
अब्रुवन् सूर्यसंकाशां सुरसां नागमातरम् ॥ १४४ ॥
explanation: Thereupon the gods, Siddhas and the most eminent Ṛṣis with Gandharvas approached and spoke as follows to Surasā, mother of the Nāgas, who shone brightly like the sun : (144)

shloka_text:
अयं वातात्मजः श्रीमान् प्लवते सागरोपरि।
हनुमान् नाम तस्य त्वं मुहूर्तं विघ्नमाचर ॥ १४५ ॥
राक्षसं रूपमास्थाय सुघोरं पर्वतोपमम्।
दंष्ट्राकरालं पिङ्गाक्षं वक्त्रं कृत्वा नभःस्पृशम् ॥ १४६ ॥
explanation: 38 * VĀLMĪKI-RĀMĀYAṆA * “This glorious son of the wind-god, Hanumān by name, is leaping across the sea. Assuming the exceedingly hideous form of an ogress, gigantic as a mountain, and revealing a head looking fearful with its tusks and red-brown eyes and reaching up to the sky, pray, you interrupt him awhile. (145-146)

shloka_text:
बलमिच्छामहे ज्ञातुं भूयश्चास्य पराक्रमम्।
त्वां विजेष्यत्युपायेन विषादं वा गमिष्यति ॥ १४७ ॥
explanation: “We seek to ascertain his strength and more so his prowess whether he will conquer you with expediency or give way to despondency.” (147)

shloka_text:
एवमुक्ता तु सा देवी दैवतैरभिसत्कृता।
समुद्रमध्ये सुरसा बिभ्रती राक्षसं वपुः ॥ १४८ ॥
विकृतं च विरूपं च सर्वस्य च भयावहम्।
प्लवमानं हनूमन्तमावृत्येदमुवाच ह ॥ १४९ ॥
explanation: Assuming in mid-sea, when spoken to and honoured by the gods, the form of an ogress, which was deformed and ugly too, nay, inspiring fear to all and encompassing Hanumān, who was leaping forward, Surasā for her part spoke to him, they say, as follows : (148-149)

shloka_text:
मम भक्ष्यः प्रदिष्टस्त्वमीश्वरैर्वानरर्षभ।
अहं त्वां भक्षयिष्यामि प्रविशेदं ममाननम् ॥ १५० ॥
explanation: “You have been destined by the lords of the universe to serve as my food, O, jewel among the monkeys ! I shall accordingly eat you up; pray ! enter for good this mouth of mine. (150)

shloka_text:
वर एष पुरा दत्तो मम धात्रेति सत्वरा।
व्यादाय वक्त्रं विपुलं स्थिता सा मारुतेः पुरः ॥ १५१ ॥
explanation: “A boon to this effect that I shall be able to catch up and devour whosoever comes up before me was granted in my favour by the creator, Brahmā.” Opening her vast mouth with these words, she speedily stood up before Hanumān, son of the wind-god. (151)

shloka_text:
एवमुक्तः सुरसया प्रहृष्टवदनोऽब्रवीत्।
रामो दाशरथिर्नाम प्रविष्टो दण्डकावनम्।
लक्ष्मणेन सह भ्रात्रा वैदेह्या चापि भार्यया ॥ १५२ ॥
explanation: Accosted thus by Surasā, Hanumān with his face lit up with excessive joy, replied as follows: “A son of Emperor Daśaratha, Śrī Rāma by name, entered deep into the Daṇḍaka forest with his younger brother, Laksmana, as well as his consort, Sītā, a princess of the Videha territory. (152)

shloka_text:
अन्यकार्यविषक्तस्य बद्धवैरस्य राक्षसैः।
तस्य सीता हता भार्या रावणेन यशस्विनी ॥ १५३ ॥
explanation: “Sītā, the illustrious consort of Śrī Rāma, was carried off by Rāvaṇa while Śrī Rāma was engaged in chasing and killing the demon, Marica, since the ogres bore deep-rooted enmity to him. (153)

shloka_text:
अथवा मैथिलीं दृष्ट्वा रामं चाक्लिष्टकारिणम्।
आगमिष्यामि ते वक्त्रं सत्यं प्रतिशृणोमि ते ॥ १५५ ॥
explanation: “Or, if you are bent on devouring me at all costs, I promise you in good faith: having seen Sītā, a princess of Mithilā, as well as reporting to Śrī Rāma, who is unwearied in action, I shall seek your mouth.” (155)

shloka_text:
एवमुक्ता हनुमता सुरसा कामरूपिणी।
अब्रवीन्नातिवर्तेन्मां कश्चिदेष वरो मम ॥ १५६ ॥
explanation: Spoken to as aforesaid, Surasā, who was capable of assuming any form at will, rejoined : “None dare elude me: such is the boon granted in my favour.” (156)

shloka_text:
तं प्रयान्तं समुद्रीक्ष्य सुरसा वाक्यमब्रवीत्।
बलं जिज्ञासमाना सा नागमाता हनूमतः ॥ १५७ ॥
explanation: Perceiving him on the journey nevertheless, that mother of the Nāgas, * SUNDARAKĀṆḌA * 39 Surasā, who was keen to ascertain the strength of Hanumān, said: (157)

shloka_text:
निविश्य वदनं मेऽद्य गन्तव्यं वानरोत्तम।
वर एष पुरा दत्तो मम धात्रेति सत्वरा ॥ १५८ ॥
व्यादाय विपुलं वक्त्रं स्थिता सा मारुतेः पुरः।
एवमुक्तः सुरसया क्रुद्धो वानरपुंगवः ॥ १५९ ॥
अब्रवीत् कुरु वै वक्त्रं येन मां विषहिष्यसि।
इत्युक्त्वा सुरसां क्रुद्धो दशयोजनमायताम् ॥ १६० ॥
दशयोजनविस्तारो हनुमानभवत् तदा।
तं दृष्ट्वा मेघसंकाशं दशयोजनमायतम्।
चकार सुरसाप्यास्यं विंशद् योजनमायतम् ॥ १६१ ॥
explanation: “You must proceed only after entering my mouth for once today, O jewel among the monkeys! Such is the boon granted in my favour by the creator, Brahmā, in the past.” Saying so and opening her enormous mouth, she hastily stood in front of Hanumān, son of the wind-god. Provoked to anger when spoken to in these words by Surasā, Hanumān, the foremost of monkeys, said, “Extend your mouth so that you may be able to sustain me.” Saying so to Surasā, whose mouth was ten Yojanas (or eighty miles) wide, Hanumān then angrily assumed a height of ten Yojanas. Seeing him ten Yojanas high and resembling a cloud, Surasā too made her mouth twenty Yojanas (or one hundred and sixty, miles) wide. (158—161)

shloka_text:
हनुमांस्तु ततः क्रुद्धस्त्रिंशद् योजनमायतः।
चकार सुरसा वक्त्रं चत्वारिंशत् तथोच्छ्रुतम् ॥ १६२ ॥
explanation: Enraged at this, Hanumān for his part became thirty Yojanas (or two hundred and forty miles) high. Surasā, likewise, made her mouth forty Yojanas (or three hundred and twenty miles) wide. (162)

shloka_text:
बभूव हनुमान् वीरः पञ्चाशद् योजनोच्छ्रुतः।
चकार सुरसा वक्त्रं षष्टिं योजनमुच्छ्रुतम् ॥ १६३ ॥
explanation: Thereupon the gallant Hanumān became fifty Yojanas (or four hundred miles) high, while Surasā made her mouth sixty Yojanas (or four hundred and eighty miles) wide. (163)

shloka_text:
तदैव हनुमान् वीरः सप्ततिं योजनोच्छ्रुतः।
चकार सुरसा वक्त्रमशीतिं योजनोच्छ्रुतम् ॥ १६४ ॥
explanation: That very moment the valiant Hanumān became seventy Yojanas (or five hundred and sixty miles) high and Surasā too made her mouth eighty Yojanas (or six hundred and forty miles) wide. (164)

shloka_text:
हनुमाननलप्रख्यो नवतिं योजनोच्छ्रुतः।
चकार सुरसा वक्त्रं शतयोजनमायतम् ॥ १६५ ॥
explanation: Hanumān, who was blazing like fire, thereupon became ninety Yojanas (or seven hundred and twenty miles) high and Surasā widened her mouth to a hundred Yojanas (or eight hundred miles). (165)

shloka_text:
तद् दृष्ट्वा व्यादितं त्वास्यं वायुपुत्रः स बुद्धिमान्।
दीर्घजिह्वं सुरसया सुभीमं नरकोपमम् ॥ १६६ ॥
स संक्षिप्यात्मनः कायं जीमूत इव मारुतिः।
तस्मिन् मुहूर्ते हनुमान् बभूवाङ्गुष्ठमात्रकः ॥ १६७ ॥
explanation: Seeing the aforesaid mouth opened by Surasā, which with its long tongue was extremely terrible to look at and was a replica of hell, and contracting his body like a cloud, Hanumān, son of the wind-god, was reduced to the breadth of a thumb the same moment. (166-167)

shloka_text:
सोऽभिपद्याथ तद्वक्त्रं निष्पत्य च महाबलः।
अन्तरिक्षे स्थितः श्रीमानिदं वचनमब्रवीत् ॥ १६८ ॥
explanation: Having entered her mouth and coming out forthwith, the glorious Hanumān, who was endowed with extraordinary might, spoke to her as follows standing in airspace : (168)

shloka_text:
प्रविष्टोऽस्मि हि ते वक्त्रं दाक्षायणि नमोऽस्तु ते।
गमिष्ये यत्र वैदेही सत्यश्चासीद् वरस्तव ॥ १६९ ॥
explanation: “Indeed, I have entered your mouth and the boon granted to you has been honoured. * Verses 162 to 165 above have been rejected as interpolated by some commentators. The author of the commentary known by the name of “Rāmāyaṇa-Śiromaṇi” has, however commented on them and we have therefore incorporated them into the text. 40 * VĀLMĪKI-RĀMĀYAṆA * My salutation be to you, O daughter of Dakṣa ! I shall now move to the place where Sītā, a princess of the Videha territory, is.” (169)

shloka_text:
तं दृष्ट्वा वदनान्मुक्तं चन्द्रं राहुमुखादिव ।
अब्रवीत् सुरसा देवी स्वेन रूपेण वानरम् ॥ १७० ॥
explanation: Seeing him released from her mouth as the moon gets released from the mouth of the demon Rāhu, and appearing in her native form, the goddess Surasā said to the monkey : (170)

shloka_text:
अर्थसिद्ध्यै हरिश्रेष्ठ गच्छ सौम्य यथासुखम् ।
समानय च वैदेहीं राघवेण महात्मना ॥ १७१ ॥
explanation: “Move according to your pleasure for accomplishing your mission, O gentle Hanumān, the foremost of monkeys, and unite Sītā, a princess of the Videha territory, with the high-souled Śrī Rāma, a scion of Raghu.” (171)

shloka_text:
तत् तृतीयं हनुमतो दृष्ट्वा कर्म सुदुष्करम् ।
साधुसाध्विति भूतानि प्रशशंसुस्तदा हरिम् ॥ १७२ ॥
explanation: Witnessing this third feat of Hanumān in the shape of escaping alive from the mouth of Surasā, which was most difficult to accomplish, living beings, who were watching it, applauded the monkey on that occasion, exclaiming “Well done, excellent !” (172)

shloka_text:
स सागरमनाधृष्यमभ्येत्य वरुणालयम् ।
जगामाकाशमाविश्य वेगेन गरुडोपमः ॥ १७३ ॥
explanation: Drawing near the inviolable sea, the abode of Varuṇa, the god of water, and coursing through the air, he moved on with speed like Garuḍa. (173)

shloka_text:
सेविते वारिधाराभिः पतगैश्च निषेविते ।
चरिते कैशिकाचार्यैररावतनिषेविते ॥ १७४ ॥
सिंहकुञ्जरशार्दूलपतगोरगवाहनैः ।
विमानैः सम्पतद्भिश्च विमलैः समलंकृते ॥ १७५ ॥
वत्राशनिसमस्पर्शैः पावकैरिव शोभिते ।
कृतपुण्यैर्महाभागैः स्वर्गजिद्भिरधिष्ठिते ॥ १७६ ॥
वहता ह्व्यमत्यन्तं सेविते चित्रभानुना ।
ग्रहनक्षत्रचन्द्रार्कतारागणविभूषिते ॥ १७७ ॥
महर्षिगणगन्धर्वनागयक्षसमाकुले ।
विविक्ते विमले विश्वे विश्वावसुनिषेविते ॥ १७८ ॥
देवराजगजाक्रान्ते चन्द्रसूर्यपथे शिवे ।
विताने जीवलोकस्य वितते ब्रह्मनिर्मिते ॥ १७९ ॥
बहुशः सेविते वीरैर्विद्याधरगणैर्वृते ।
जगाम वायुमार्गे च गरुत्मानिव मारुतिः ॥ १८० ॥
explanation: Like Garuḍa, Hanumān, son of the wind-god, coursed through the path of the wind, which was refreshed by torrents and frequented by birds, was traversed by masters of music and dancing (Tumburu and other Gandharvas) and used by Airāvata (a celestial elephant which carries Indra on its back), and was adorned with stainless fast-moving aerial cars drawn by lions, elephants, tigers, birds and serpents; which was presided over and rendered charming by highly blessed souls, who had performed meritorious deeds in their previous lives and had accordingly won their residence in heaven, were hard to the touch like a diamond and thunderbolt and shone like fire; which was inhabited by the god of fire abundantly carrying oblations to the various gods, and was richly adorned with planets, lunar asterisks, the moon, the sun and groups of stars; which was ever thronged with hosts of eminent Ṛṣis (the seers of Vedic Mantras), Gandharvas, Nāgas and Yakṣas, and was isolated, cloudless and spacious and frequented by Viśwāvasu, the chief of Gandharvas; nay which was traversed by elephants (other than Airāvata) belonging to Indra, the ruler of gods, was the peaceful orbit of the sun and the moon, and served as an extensive canopy for the world of living beings, spread by Brahmā, the creator, and which was frequented by numerous heroes ascending to heaven by virtue of their laying down their life in a righteous cause and blocked by Vidyādharas (celestial artists). (174—180)

shloka_text:
हनुमान् मेघजालानि प्राकर्षन् मारुतो यथा ।
कालागुरुसवर्णानि रक्तपीतसितानि च ॥ १८१ ॥
explanation: * SUNDARAKĀṆḌA * 41 Like the wind, Hanumān dragged along with him masses of clouds of the same colour as Agallocam (the black aloe) as also red, yellow and white in colour. (181)

shloka_text:
कपिना कृष्यमाणानि महाभ्राणि चकाशिरे।
प्रविशन्नभ्रजालानि निष्पतश्च पुनः पुनः ॥ १८२ ॥
प्रावृषीन्दुरिवाभाति निष्पतन् प्रविशंस्तदा।
प्रदृश्यमानः सर्वत्र हनुमान् मारुतात्मजः ॥ १८३ ॥
भेजेऽम्बरं निरालम्बं पक्षयुक्त इवादिराट्।
प्लवमानं तु तं दृष्ट्वा सिंहिका नाम राक्षसी ॥ १८४ ॥
मनसा चिन्तयामास प्रवृद्धा कामरूपिणी।
अद्य दीर्घस्य कालस्य भविष्याम्यहमाशिता ॥ १८५ ॥
इदं मम महासत्त्वं चिरस्य वशमागतम्।
इति संचिन्त्य मनसा च्छायामस्य समाक्षिपत् ॥ १८६ ॥
explanation: Drawn by Hanumān, the huge clouds looked charming. Penetrating the masses of clouds and coming out again and again, he shone forth at that moment like the moon emerging from and entering into the clouds during the monsoon. Eagerly watched everywhere by all, Hanumān, son of the wind-god, sped through the supportless sky like Sumeru, the king of mountains, endowed with wings. Seeing him moving on, an ogress, Siṃhikā by name, who was able to change her form at will, and had grown out of all proportion, thought for her part within herself: “Today I shall be sated for a long time to come. After a long wait this huge creature has fallen in my grasp.” Reflecting thus in her heart, she clutched his shadow. (182—186)

shloka_text:
छायायां गृह्यमाणायां चिन्तयामास वानरः।
समाक्षिपोऽस्मि सहसा पङ्गुकृतपराक्रमः ॥ १८७ ॥
प्रतिलोमेन वातेन महानौरिव सागरे।
तिर्यगूर्ध्वमधश्चैव वीक्षमाणस्तदा कपिः ॥ १८८ ॥
ददर्श स महासत्त्वमुत्थितं लवणाम्भसि।
तद् दृष्ट्वा चिन्तयामास मारुतिर्विकृताननाम् ॥ १८९ ॥
explanation: On his shadow being seized, Hanumān thought: “Clutched by someone all of a sudden, I have been rendered powerless like a big bark retarded in its course by an adverse wind.” Looking about sideways as well as both upward and below, the said Hanumān espied a huge creature risen from the salty sea below. Seeing that female form with an ugly face, Hanumān, son of the wind-god, reflected: (187—189)

shloka_text:
कपिराज्ञा यथाख्यातं सत्त्वमद्भुतदर्शनम्।
छायाग्राहि महावीर्यं तदिदं नात्र संशयः ॥ १९० ॥
explanation: “It is the same creature of weird appearance, endowed with extraordinary prowess and capable of securing her prey by means of its shadow, which was depicted in its true colours by Sugrīva, the king of monkeys; there is no doubt about it.” (190)

shloka_text:
स तां बुद्धार्थतत्त्वेन सिंहिकां मतिमान् कपिः।
व्यवर्धत महाकायः प्रावृषीव बलाहकः ॥ १९१ ॥
explanation: Knowing her from the correctness of the description given by Sugrīva to be Siṃhikā, that sagacious Hanumān grew out of all proportions to be gigantic in form like a cloud during the rains. (191)

shloka_text:
तस्य सा कायमुद्गीक्ष्य वर्धमानं महाकपेः।
वक्त्रं प्रसारयामास पातालाम्बरसंनिभम् ॥ १९२ ॥
घनराजीव गर्जन्ती वानरं समभिद्रवत्।
स ददर्श ततस्तस्या विकृतं सुमहन्मुखम् ॥ १९३ ॥
कायमात्रं च मेधावी मर्माणि च महाकपिः।
स तस्या विकृते वक्त्रे वज्रसंहननः कपिः ॥ १९४ ॥
संक्षिप्य मुहुरात्मानं निपपात महाकपिः।
आस्ये तस्या निमज्जन्तं ददृशुः सिद्धचारणाः ॥ १९५ ॥
ग्रस्यमानं यथा चन्द्रं पूर्णं पर्वणि राहुणा।
ततस्तस्या नखैस्तीक्ष्णैर्मर्माण्युत्कृत्य वानरः ॥ १९६ ॥
उत्पपाताथ वेगेन मनःसम्पातविक्रमः।
तां तु दिष्ट्या च धृत्या च दाक्षिण्येन निपात्य सः ॥ १९७ ॥
कपिप्रवीरो वेगेन ववृधे पुनरात्मवान्।
हृतहृत्सा हनुमता पपात विधुराम्भसि।
स्वयंभुवैव हनुमान् सृष्टस्तस्या निपातने ॥ १९८ ॥
explanation: Observing the body of that mighty Hanumān growing, she distended her mouth, which resembled the space enclosed in Pātāla (the nethermost subterranean region) and, thundering like a mass of clouds, rushed towards Hanumān. That huge, intelligent 42 * VĀLMĪKI-RĀMĀYAṆA * monkey, Hanumān, then noticed her ugly enormous mouth, which was of the same dimensions as his body, as well as her vulnerable parts. Contracting his body further, that mighty monkey, Hanumān, who was hard as a diamond, fell into her hideous mouth. Siddhas and Cāraṇas beheld him disappearing into her mouth like the full moon being devoured on a full moon night by the demon Rāhu. Then, tearing out her vulnerable parts with his sharp nails, the monkey forthwith rushed out with the rapidity of thought. Having overthrown her with the help of Providence, as well as through firmness and ingenuity, Hanumān, for his part, who was the foremost hero among the monkeys and self-possessed too, rapidly grew once more in size. With her heart, the very seat of her life, torn asunder by Hanumān, she fell down dead into the water. Hanuman was created as an instrument for her destruction by Brahmā, the self-born creator himself. (192—198)

shloka_text:
तां हतां वानरेणाशु पतितां वीक्ष्य सिंहिकाम्।
भूतान्याकाशचारीणि तमूचुः प्लवगोत्तमम् ॥ १९९ ॥
explanation: Perceiving the aforesaid Siṃhikā killed in no time by Hanumān and fallen, the beings who ranged the skies said to that jewel among the monkeys : (199)

shloka_text:
भीममद्य कृतं कर्म महत्सत्त्वं त्वया हतम्।
साधयार्थमभिप्रेतमरिष्टं प्लवतां वर ॥ २०० ॥
explanation: “A terrific valiant deed has been performed by you this day in that a mighty creature has been killed by you. Now accomplish your desired object without hindrance, O jewel among the monkeys ! (200)

shloka_text:
यस्य त्वेतानि चत्वारि वानरेन्द्र यथा तव।
धृतिर्दृष्टिर्मतिर्दक्ष्यं स कर्मसु न सीदति ॥ २०१ ॥
explanation: “He in whom the following four virtues, viz., firmness, vision, understanding and skill actually exist, as in you, never fails in his undertakings.” (201)

shloka_text:
स तैः सम्पूजितः पूज्यः प्रतिपन्नप्रयोजनैः।
जगामाकाशमाविश्य पन्नगाशनवत् कपिः ॥ २०२ ॥
explanation: Bounding in the air like Garuḍa (who feeds on serpents), adored with ceremony by those beings, who were now accomplished of purpose—thanks to the gallantry of Hanumān—the aforesaid monkey, who was worthy of adoration for his exploits, sped on. (202)

shloka_text:
प्राप्तभूयिष्ठपारस्तु सर्वतः परिलोकयन्।
योजनानां शतस्यान्ते वनराजीं ददर्श सः ॥ २०३ ॥
explanation: Looking around on all sides when he had well-nigh reached the opposite shore at the end of a hundred Yojanas (or eight hundred miles), he espied a row of forest trees: (203)

shloka_text:
ददर्श च पतन्नेव विविधद्रुमभूषितम्।
द्वीपं शाखामृगश्रेष्ठो मलयोपवनानि च ॥ २०४ ॥
explanation: While yet in the airspace, Hanumān, the foremost of monkeys, also beheld an island adorned with trees of various kinds as well as groves on the Malaya mountain. (204)

shloka_text:
सागरं सागरानूपान् सागरानूपजान् द्रुमान्।
सागरस्य च पत्नीनां मुखान्यपि विलोकयत् ॥ २०५ ॥
explanation: He further saw the sea skirting the island, the watery regions bordering it, the trees growing in those regions and the mouths of rivers (consorts of the ocean) too. (205)

shloka_text:
स महामेघसंकाशं समीक्ष्यात्मानमात्मवान्।
निरुद्धन्तमिवाकाशं चकार मतिमान् मतिम् ॥ २०६ ॥
explanation: Gazing on his own person, which closely resembled a big cloud and blocked the sky, as it were, the intelligent Hanumān, who was self-possessed too, began to reflect. (206)

shloka_text:
कायवृद्धिं प्रवेगं च मम दृष्ट्वैव राक्षसाः।
मयि कौतूहलं कुर्युरिति मेने महामतिः ॥ २०७ ॥
explanation: The highly talented Hanumān felt convinced that seeing the extraordinary growth of his body and his tremendous speed itself, the ogres would be inquisitive about him. (207)

shloka_text:
ततः शरीरं संक्षिप्य तन्महीधरसंनिभम्।
पुनः प्रकृतिमापेदे वीतमोह इवात्मवान् ॥ २०८ ॥
explanation: Then, contracting his aforesaid expanded body, which closely resembled a mountain, he once more assumed his native form, even as he, who has mastered his self and is completely free from infatuation, realizes his own blissful divine nature. (208)

shloka_text:
तदूपमतिसंक्षिप्य हनुमान् प्रकृतौ स्थितः।
त्रीन् क्रमानिव विक्रम्य बलिवीर्यहरो हरिः ॥ २०९ ॥
explanation: Having considerably contracted that form of his, Hanumān returned to his natural state, even as having taken three strides in His Cosmic Form and thereby frustrated the power of Bali, the demon king, Lord Śrī Viṣṇu descended as the Divine Dwarf, returned to His former state (of a dwarf). (209)

shloka_text:
स चारुनानाविधरूपधारी
परं समासाद्य समुद्रतीरम्।
परैरशक्यं प्रतिपन्नरूपः
समीक्षितात्मा समवेक्षितार्थः ॥ २१० ॥
explanation: Having duly reached the other shore of the sea, which could not be approached by anyone else, Hanumān, who was capable of assuming various graceful forms, gazed on his own body and, fully considering his mission of tracing out Sītā, regained his native form. (210)

shloka_text:
ततः स लम्बस्य गिरेः समृद्धे
विचित्रकूटे निपपात कूटे।
सकेतकोददालकनारिकेले
महाभ्रकूटप्रतिमो महात्मा ॥ २११ ॥
explanation: Then the high-souled Hanumān, who resembled a huge mass of clouds, descended on a summit of the *Lamba* mountain, rich in fruit and blossom and covered with *Ketaka*, *Uddālaka* and coconut trees and consisting of wonderful lower peaks. (211)

shloka_text:
ततस्तु सम्प्राप्य समुद्रतीरं
समीक्ष्य लंकां गिरिवर्यमूर्ध्नि।
कपिस्तु तस्मिन् निपपात पर्वते
विधूय रूपं व्यथयन्मृगद्विजान् ॥ २१२ ॥
explanation: Duly reaching the seashore and perceiving from there Laṅkā perched on a summit of the Trikūṭa mountain, the foremost of mountains, Hanumān for his part descended on that mountain, Trikūṭa, abandoning his assumed colossal form and agitating the beasts and birds inhabiting that mountain with his gigantic monkey form. (212)

shloka_text:
स सागरं दानवपन्नगायुतं
बलेन विक्रम्य महोर्मिमालिनम्।
निपत्य तीरे च महोदधेस्तदा
ददर्श लंकाममरावतीमिव ॥ २१३ ॥
explanation: Having leapt by dint of his vigour over the sea infested with demons and reptiles and heaving with series of huge waves, and descending on the shore of the vast sea, Hanumān then saw Laṅkā standing like Amarāvati, the city of gods, the capital of Indra. (213)
Reflecting on the difficulty of penetrating into Laṅkā, which was strongly guarded by ogres, Hanumān further contracts his body and enters it at moonrise

shloka_text:
स सागरमनाधृष्यमतिक्रम्य महाबलः।
त्रिकूटस्य तटे लंकां स्थितः स्वस्थो ददर्श ह॥ १॥
explanation: Standing at ease on a slope of the Trikūṭa mountain, on having negotiated the inviolable sea, Hanumān, who was endowed with extraordinary might, surveyed Laṅkā: so the tradition goes. (1)

shloka_text:
ततः पादपमुक्तेन पुष्पवर्षेण वीर्यवान्।
अभिवृष्टस्ततस्तत्र बभौ पुष्पमयो हरिः॥ २॥
explanation: Covered all over by a shower of blossoms discharged by the trees on all sides, the powerful monkey, Hanumān, looked as if consisting of flowers only. (2)

shloka_text:
योजनानां शतं श्रीमांस्तीर्त्वाप्युत्तमविक्रमः।
अनिःश्वसन् कपिस्तत्र न ग्लानिमधिगच्छति॥ ३॥
explanation: Even on having covered a hundred Yojanas (eight hundred miles), the glorious Hanumān, who was endowed with prowess of the first magnitude, did not gasp for breath nor did he experience any fatigue. (3)

shloka_text:
शतान्यहं योजनानां क्रमेयं सुबहून्यपि।
किं पुनः सागरस्यान्तं संख्यातं शतयोजनम्॥ ४॥
explanation: He said to himself: 'I am able to journey many hundreds of miles, to say nothing of reaching the opposite shore of a sea, which has been calculated as being at a distance of a hundred Yojanas only.' (4)

shloka_text:
स तु वीर्यवतां श्रेष्ठः प्लवतामपि चोत्तमः।
जगाम वेगवाँल्लंकां लङ्घयित्वा महोदधिम्॥ ५॥
explanation: Having negotiated the vast sea, Hanumān, for his part, who was the foremost of powerful beings and a jewel among the monkeys, and was full of energy, reached Laṅkā. (5)

shloka_text:
शाद्वलानि च नीलानि गन्धवन्ति वनानि च।
मधुमन्ति च मध्येन जगाम नगवन्ति च॥ ६॥
explanation: He passed through dark green meadows and groves full of fragrance, nay, full of trees and full of honey too. (6)

shloka_text:
शैलांश्च तरुसंछन्नान् वनराजीश्च पुष्पिताः।
अभिचक्राम तेजस्वी हनूमान् प्लवगर्षभः॥ ७॥
explanation: The glorious Hanumān, the foremost of monkeys, further coursed through mountains covered with trees and groves laden with blossom. (7)

shloka_text:
स तस्मिन्नचले तिष्ठन् वनान्युपवनानि च।
स नगाग्रे स्थितां लंकां ददर्श पवनात्मजः॥ ८॥
explanation: Stationed on that mountain, he saw forests and groves. That son of the wind-god, Hanumān, also beheld Laṅkā perched on the top of the mountain. (8)

shloka_text:
सरलान् कर्णिकारांश्च खर्जूरांश्च सुपुष्पितान्।
प्रियालान् मुचुलिन्दांश्च कुटजान् केतकानपि॥ ९॥
प्रियड्डून् गन्धपूर्णांश्च नीपान् सप्तच्छदांस्तथा।
असनान् कोविदारांश्च करवीरांश्च पुष्पितान्॥ १०॥
पुष्पभारनिबद्धांश्च तथा मुकुलितानपि।
पादपान् विहगाकीर्णान् पवनाधृतमस्तकान्॥ ११॥
हंसकारण्डवाकीर्णा वापीः पद्मोत्पलावृताः।
आक्रीडान् विविधान् रम्यान् विविधांश्च जलाशयान्॥ १२॥
संततान् विविधैर्वृक्षैः सर्वर्तुफलपुष्पितैः।
उद्यानानि च रम्याणि ददर्श कपिकुञ्जरः॥ १३॥
explanation: Hanumān, an elephant among the monkeys, further saw Saralas (a species of pine trees), and Karnikaras, as also date-palms in full blossom, Priyalas and muculindas (a species of oranges), Kūtajas, also Ketakas and fragrant Priyangus (trees yielding long pepper as their fruit), Nipas (a species of * SUNDARAKĀṆḌA * 45 Kadamba trees) as well as Saptacchadas, Asanas, Kovidaras and Karaviras in blossom as also trees adorned with a load of flowers as well as those bearing buds only, and which were crowded with birds and whose crests were being shaken by the wind, ponds abounding in swans and Karandavas (a species of duck) and carpeted with lotuses and water-lilies, lovely pleasure-groves of every description and lovely ponds of various kinds overspread by trees of every species, bearing fruit and flower in all seasons as also delightful gardens. (9—13)

shloka_text:
समासाद्य च लक्ष्मीवाँल्लंकां रावणपालिताम्।
परिखाभिः सपद्याभिः सोत्पलाभिरलंकृताम् ॥ १४ ॥
सीतापहरणात् तेन रावणेन सुरक्षिताम्।
समन्ताद् विचरद्विश्व राक्षसैरुग्रधन्वभिः ॥ १५ ॥
काञ्चनेनावृतां रम्यां प्राकारेण महापुरीम्।
गृहैश्च गिरिसंकाशैः शारदाम्बुदसंनिभैः ॥ १६ ॥
पाण्डुराभिः प्रतोलीभिरुच्चाभिरभिसंवृताम्।
अङ्गालकशताकीर्णां पताकाध्वजशोभिताम् ॥ १७ ॥
तोरणैः काञ्चनैर्दिव्यैर्लतापङ्क्तिविराजितैः।
ददर्श हनुमाँल्लंकां देवो देवपुरीमिव ॥ १८ ॥
explanation: Duly arriving at the great and lovely city of Laṅkā, which was protected by Rāvaṇa, nay, was fringed with moats full of lotuses and water-lilies and was strongly guarded, ever since Sītā had been abducted and placed there, by the selfsame Rāvaṇa, as well as by other ogres armed with formidable bows ranging on every side; which was enclosed with a golden boundary wall and crowded with buildings lofty as mountains and resembling autumnal clouds; which was hemmed in with white-plastered and elevated roads, was crowded with hundreds of mansions and decorated with flags and pennons and was distinguished by wonderful golden archways adorned with rows of climbers—the glorious Hanumān surveyed Laṅkā even as a god would look at the city of gods. (14—18)

shloka_text:
गिरिमूर्ध्नि स्थितां लंकां पाण्डुरैर्भवनैः शुभैः।
ददर्श स कपिः श्रीमान् पुरीमाकाशगामिव ॥ १९ ॥
explanation: That illustrious Hanumān saw Laṅkā perched on the summit of a mountain and distinguished by its sparkling white mansions as though it were a city moving in the airspace. (19)

shloka_text:
पालितां राक्षसेन्द्रेण निर्मितां विश्वकर्मणा।
प्लवमानामिवाकाशे ददर्श हनुमान् कपिः ॥ २० ॥
explanation: Nay, Hanumān beheld the city constructed by Viśwakarmā, the architect of gods, and protected by Rāvaṇa, the king of the ogres, as though it was sailing in the sky. (20)

shloka_text:
वप्रप्राकारजघनां विपुलाम्बुवनाम्बराम्।
शतघ्नीशूलकेशान्तामङ्गालकावर्तसंकाम् ॥ २१ ॥
मनसेव कृतां लंकां निर्मितां विश्वकर्मणा।
द्वारमुत्तरमासाद्य चिन्तयामास वानरः ॥ २२ ॥
कैलासनिलयप्रख्यमालिखन्तमिवाम्बरम्।
ध्रियमाणमिवाकाशमुच्छ्रुतैर्भवतोत्तमैः ॥ २३ ॥
explanation: He further conceived Laṅkā, the city built by Viśwakarmā, as a woman evolved with his mind, with its buttress and enclosure as her hip and loins, the vast sea and the woods encircling the city for her raiment, the Śataghnis* and Śūlas (spikes) for her locks and the mansions for her earrings. Reaching the northern gate, which looked like the gateway of the city of Alakā, the capital of Kubera, the god of riches, perched on Mount Kailāśa, the abode of Lord Śiva, which scraped the sky, as it were, by means of its tall mansions and supported the firmament, as it were, on its housetops, Hanumān fell abrooding. (21—23)

shloka_text:
सम्पूर्णा राक्षसैर्घोरैर्नागैर्भोगवतीमिव।
अचिन्त्यां सुकृतां स्पष्टां कुबेराध्युषितां पुरा ॥ २४ ॥
दंष्ट्राभिर्बहुभिः शूरैः शूलपट्टिशपाणिभिः।
रक्षितां राक्षसैर्घोरैर्गुहामाशीविषैरिव ॥ २५ ॥
तस्याश्च महतीं गुमिं सागरं च निरीक्ष्य सः।
रावणं च रिपुं घोरं चिन्तयामास वानरः ॥ २६ ॥
explanation: Observing the city—which was overfull with fierce ogres as Bhogavati, the capital of Pātāla, with Nāgas—was beyond conception and well-constructed, was clearly visible and had been occupied by Kubera in the past and was guarded by numerous gallant and terrible ogres distinguished by tusks and carrying spikes and Pattisas (a kind of sharp-edged spear) in their hands, even as a cavern by venomous serpents—as well as its mighty defences, as also the sea encircling it and thinking the formidable adversary in the form of Rāvaṇa, Hanumān reflected as follows : (24—26)

shloka_text:
आगत्यापीह हरयो भविष्यन्ति निरर्थकाः।
नहि युद्धेन वै लंका शक्या जेतुं सुरैरपि ॥ २७ ॥
explanation: 'The monkeys will prove of no avail even on coming here; for Laṅkā cannot be conquered in any case through warfare even by the gods. (27)

shloka_text:
इमां त्वविषमां लंकां दुर्गां रावणपालिताम्।
प्राप्यापि सुमहाबाहुः किं करिष्यति राघवः ॥ २८ ॥
explanation: 'What will Śrī Rāma, a scion of Raghu, of highly mighty arms do even on actually reaching this Laṅkā, which is surpassingly rugged and difficult of access and is protected by Rāvaṇa? (28)

shloka_text:
अवकाशो न साम्रस्तु राक्षसेष्वभिगम्यते।
न दानस्य न भेदस्य नैव युद्धस्य दृश्यते ॥ २९ ॥
explanation: 'No possibility at all is perceived of winning over ogres through persuasion or gift nor of bringing them to their knees by sowing dissension among them nor again of reducing them to submission through warfare. (29)

shloka_text:
चतुर्णामेव हि गतिर्वानराणां तरस्विनाम्।
वालिपुत्रस्य नीलस्य मम राज्ञश्च धीमतः ॥ ३० ॥
explanation: 'Only four agile monkeys, can actually reach this place, viz., Aṅgada (the son of Vāli), Nila, the sagacious king Sugriva and myself. (30)

shloka_text:
यावज्जानामि वैदेहीं यदि जीवति वा न वा।
तत्रैव चिन्तयिष्यामि दृष्ट्वा तां जनकात्मजाम् ॥ ३१ ॥
explanation: 'Meanwhile, I shall find out whether Sītā, a princess of the Videha territory, is alive or not. Having seen that daughter of King Janaka, I shall consider other points only then.' (31)

shloka_text:
ततः स चिन्तयामास मुहूर्तं कपिकुञ्जरः।
गिरेः शृङ्गे स्थितस्तस्मिन् रामस्याभ्युदयं ततः ॥ ३२ ॥
explanation: Stationed on that mountain peak, that elephant among the monkeys, Hanumān, pondered for a while the means of discovering Sītā in which lay the welfare of Śrī Rāma. (32)

shloka_text:
अनेन रूपेण मया न शक्या रक्षसां पुरी।
प्रवेष्टुं राक्षसैर्गुमा क्रूरैर्बलसमन्वितैः ॥ ३३ ॥
explanation: He said to Himself: 'Laṅkā, the city of ogres, guarded as it is by ferocious and mighty ogres, cannot be entered by me in this form. (33)

shloka_text:
महौजसो महावीर्या बलवन्तश्च राक्षसाः।
वञ्चनीया मया सर्वे जानकीं परिमार्गता ॥ ३४ ॥
explanation: 'All the ogres, who are endowed with extraordinary energy and extraordinary prowess and are full of might, must be blindfolded by me while I continue to look about for Sītā, the daughter of Janaka. (34)

shloka_text:
लक्ष्यालक्ष्येण रूपेण रात्रौ लंकापुरी मया।
प्राप्तकालं प्रवेष्टुं मे कृत्यं साधयितुं महत् ॥ ३५ ॥
explanation: 'In order to accomplish this great task it is advisable for me to enter the city of Laṅkā during the night in a form which cannot be directly perceived, but whose existence could be inferred by its exploits.' (35)

shloka_text:
तां पुरीं तादृशीं दृष्ट्वा दुराधर्षा सुरासुरैः।
हनुमांश्चिन्तयामास विनिःश्वस्य मुहुर्मुहुः ॥ ३६ ॥
explanation: Beholding that city to be of the kind mentioned above and difficult to overcome even for gods and demons, and sighing again and again, Hanumān reflected as follows : (36)

shloka_text:
केनोपायेन पश्येयं मैथिलीं जनकात्मजाम्।
अदृष्टो राक्षसेन्द्रेण रावणेन दुरात्मना ॥ ३७ ॥
explanation: 'Through what device shall I be able to behold Sītā, daughter of King Janaka and a princess of Mithilā, myself remaining unperceived by the evil-minded Rāvaṇa, the ruler of the ogres? (37)

shloka_text:
न विनश्येत् कथं कार्यं रामस्य विदितात्मनः।
एकामेकस्तु पश्येयं रहिते जनकात्मजाम् ॥ ३८ ॥
explanation: 'How shall I be able to see the daughter of Janaka alone in secret with none else beside me, so that the cause of Śrī Rāma, the knower of the Self, may not be altogether lost? (38)

shloka_text:
भूताश्चार्था विनश्यन्ति देशकालविरोधिताः।
विकलवं दूतमासाद्य तमः सूर्योदये यथा ॥ ३९ ॥
explanation: 'Nay, even as darkness disappears at sunrise, objects which are all but accomplished are completely lost at the hands of a timid or thoughtless messenger when they are set in opposition to time and place. (39)

shloka_text:
अर्थानर्थान्तरे बुद्धिर्निश्चितापि न शोभते।
घातयन्तीह कार्याणि दूताः पण्डितमानिनः ॥ ४० ॥
explanation: 'Even a decision duly arrived at by a ruler in consultation with his ministers regarding what should be done and what should be refrained from, does not yield good results when implemented by a thoughtless messenger. Messengers fancying themselves clever, but really not so, bring to nought all undertakings on such occasions. (40)

shloka_text:
न विनश्येत् कथं कार्यं वैकलव्यं न कथं भवेत्।
लङ्घनं च समुद्रस्य कथं नु न भवेद् वृथा ॥ ४१ ॥
explanation: 'How should I act to ensure that the purpose may not be frustrated? How should I guard against thoughtlessness? And how, I wonder, should I ensure that my leaping across the sea does not go in vain? (41)

shloka_text:
मयि दृष्टे तु रक्षोभी रामस्य विदितात्मनः।
भवेद् व्यर्थमिदं कार्यं रावणानर्थमिच्छतः ॥ ४२ ॥
explanation: 'If I am detected by the ogres, this project (in the shape of my being sent to Laṅkā) of Śrī Rāma, who is a knower of the Self, and who seeks the overthrow of Rāvaṇa, will miscarry. (42)

shloka_text:
नहि शक्यं क्वचित् स्थातुमविज्ञातेन राक्षसैः।
अपि राक्षसरूपेण किमुतान्येन केनचित् ॥ ४३ ॥
explanation: 'It is not possible at this place for anyone to remain anywhere unknown by the ogres even in the disguise of an ogre, much less in any other form. (43)

shloka_text:
वायुरप्यत्र नाज्ञातश्चरेदिति मतिर्मम।
नह्यत्राविदितं किंचिद् रक्षसां भीमकर्मणाम् ॥ ४४ ॥
explanation: 'My belief is that even the wind cannot circulate here undetected. Certainly nothing here is unknown to the ogres of terrible deeds. (44)

shloka_text:
इहाहं यदि तिष्ठामि स्वेन रूपेण संवृतः।
विनाशमुपयास्यामि भर्तुर्वरश्च हास्यति ॥ ४५ ॥
explanation: 'If I remain here in my native form, I shall certainly meet with destruction and the cause of my master will suffer. (45)

shloka_text:
तदहं स्वेन रूपेण रजन्यां ह्रस्वतां गतः।
लंकामभिपतिष्यामि राघवस्यार्थसिद्धये ॥ ४६ ॥
explanation: 'Therefore, reduced to a small size, I shall penetrate into Laṅkā by night in my own form for carrying through the purpose of my master: (46)

shloka_text:
रावणस्य पुरीं रात्रौ प्रविश्य सुदुरासदाम्।
प्रविश्य भवनं सर्वं द्रक्ष्यामि जनकात्मजाम् ॥ ४७ ॥
explanation: 'Entering by night the capital of Rāvaṇa, which is most difficult of access, and penetrating through every dwelling, I shall find out Janaka's daughter.' (47)

shloka_text:
इति निश्चित्य हनुमान् सूर्यस्यास्तमयं कपिः।
आचकाङ्क्षे तदा वीरो वैदेह्या दर्शनोत्सुकः ॥ ४८ ॥
explanation: 48 * VĀLMĪKI-RĀMĀYAṆA * Having resolved thus, Hanumān, the heroic monkey, who was eager to discover Sītā, a princess of the Videha territory, then longed for the sunset. (48)

shloka_text:
सूर्ये चास्तं गते रात्रौ देहं संक्षिप्य मारुतिः ।
वृषदंशकमात्रोऽथ बभूवाद्भुतदर्शनः ॥ ४९ ॥
explanation: Nay, contracting his body at night, when the sun had actually set, the son of the wind-god assumed the size of a cat, strange to behold. (49)

shloka_text:
प्रदोषकाले हनुमांस्तूर्णमुत्पत्य वीर्यवान् ।
प्रविवेश पुरीं रम्यां प्रविभक्तमहापथाम् ॥ ५० ॥
प्रासादमालाविततां स्तम्भैः काञ्चनसंनिभैः ।
शातकुम्भनिभैर्जालैर्गन्धर्वनगरोपमाम् ॥ ५१ ॥
explanation: Springing up quickly at eventide, the powerful Hanumān proceeded to penetrate deep into the lovely city, whose highways had been symmetrically aligned, which was filled with rows of mansions, and with its golden pillars and golden lattice windows, it looked like the city of the Gandharvas. (50-51)

shloka_text:
समभौमाष्टभौमैश्च स ददर्श महापुरीम् ।
तलैः स्फटिकसंकीर्णैः कार्तस्वरविभूषितैः ॥ ५२ ॥
वैदूर्यमणिचित्रैश्च मुक्ताजालविभूषितैः ।
तैस्तैः शुशुभिरे तानि भवनान्यत्र रक्षसाम् ॥ ५३ ॥
explanation: He saw the great city from where he stood as distinguished by seven-storeyed and eight-storeyed mansions. Those dwellings of the ogres in this city shone brightly with their respective floors inlaid with crystal and gold, nay, studded with cat's-eye gems and decorated with strings of pearls. (52-53)

shloka_text:
काञ्चनानि विचित्राणि तोरणानि च रक्षसाम् ।
लंकामुद्योतयामासुः सर्वतः समलंकृताम् ॥ ५४ ॥
explanation: Wonderful archways of gold, erected by the ogres, also illumined Laṅkā, decorated on all sides. (54)

shloka_text:
अचिन्त्यामद्भुताकारां दृष्ट्वा लंकां महाकपिः ।
आसीद् विषण्णो हृष्टश्च वैदेह्या दर्शनोत्सुकः ॥ ५५ ॥
explanation: Beholding Laṅkā, which was beyond all imagination and strange to look at, Hanumān, the great monkey, felt despondent and delighted too at the prospect of finding out Sītā, eager as he was to see Sītā, a princess of the Videha territory. (55)

shloka_text:
स पाण्डुराविद्धविमानमालिनीं
महार्हजाम्बूनदजालतोरणाम् ।
यशस्विनीं रावणबाहुपालितां
क्षपाचरैर्भीमबलैः सुपालिताम् ॥ ५६ ॥
