बलिनो वीर्ययुक्तस्य भार्यात्वं किं न लिप्ससे ॥ ११ ॥
explanation: “Why don’t you acquiesce in this proposal put forward by me, O lady! charming of every limb?” Dilating her eyes, which resembled a cat’s, an ogress, Harijāta by name, then angrily spoke as follows : “You deserve to be a wife of that king of ogres by whom were vanquished all the thirty-three principal deities, viz., the twelve Ādityas, the eleven Rudras, the eight Vasus and the twin Aświnikumāras, and even Indra, the ruler of gods. Why don’t you seek the wifehood of Rāvaṇa, who is heroic and mighty, full of valour and proud of his prowess, and who never turns his back on the field of battle? (9—11)

shloka_text:
प्रियां बहुमतां भार्या त्यक्त्वा राजा महाबलः ।
सर्वासां च महाभागां त्वामुपैष्यति रावणः ॥ १२ ॥
explanation: “Renouncing his beloved wife Mandodari, who is much esteemed by all his wives and is highly blessed, Rāvaṇa will betake himself to you. (12)

shloka_text:
समृद्धं स्त्रीसहस्रेण नानारत्नोपशोभितम् ।
अन्तःपुरं तदुत्सृज्य त्वामुपैष्यति रावणः ॥ १३ ॥
explanation: “Nay, leaving alone his well-known gynaecium, enriched by thousands of women and decked with various jewels, Rāvaṇa will go to you.” (13)

shloka_text:
तस्य सर्वसमृद्धस्य रावणस्य महात्मनः।
किमर्थं राक्षसेन्द्रस्य भार्यात्वं नेच्छसेऽधमे ॥ १५ ॥
explanation: “Why don’t you solicit the wifehood of the aforesaid ruler of ogres, the high-souled Rāvaṇa, who is fully accomplished in every way, O vile woman?” (15)

shloka_text:
ततस्तां दुर्मुखी नाम राक्षसी वाक्यमब्रवीत्।
यस्य सूर्यो न तपति भीतो यस्य स मारुतः।
न वाति स्मायतापाङ्गि किं त्वं तस्य न तिष्ठसे ॥ १६ ॥
explanation: Then another ogress, Durmukhi by name, spoke as follows: “Why don’t you yield to Rāvaṇa, in fear of whom the sun does not shine brightly and the wind stops blowing terrifically, O lady with long-cornered eyes? (16)

shloka_text:
पुष्पवृष्टि च तरवो मुमुचुर्यस्य वै भयात्।
शैलाः सुन्नुवुः पानीयं जलदाश्च यदेच्छति ॥ १७ ॥
तस्य नैऋतराजस्य राजराजस्य भामिनि।
किं त्वं न कुरुषे बुद्धिं भार्यार्थे रावणस्य हि ॥ १८ ॥
explanation: “Why don’t you really make up your mind, O lovely woman, to become the wife of that Rāvaṇa, the lord of ogres and the king of kings, in fear of whom the trees rain down flowers, mountains and clouds shed their water whenever he wills? (17-18)

shloka_text:
साधु ते तत्त्वतो देवि कथितं साधु भामिनि।
गृह्णा सुस्मिते वाक्यमन्यथा न भविष्यसि ॥ १९ ॥
explanation: “Accept cheerfully, O lovely lady with sweet smiles, the advice which has been tendered to you in good spirit and in accordance with facts; or else you shall die.” (19)

Citing the examples of Śaci, Arundhatī and other devoted wives, even though threatened by the ogresses, Sītā with a stout heart boldly proclaims her resolve not to submit to anyone else other than her own husband even on pain of death. Hanumān silently watches her being menaced by the ogresses by means of harsh words and show of weapons, and weeping

shloka_text:
ततः सीतां समस्तास्ता राक्षस्यो विकृताननाः।
परुषं परुषानर्हामुचुस्तद्वाक्यमप्रियम् ॥ १ ॥
explanation: Thereupon all those ogresses of loathsome appearance addressed the following harsh and unpalatable words to Sītā, who did not merit such harsh words : (1)

shloka_text:
किं त्वमन्तःपुरे सीते सर्वभूतमनोरमे।
महाहंशयनोपेते न वासमनुमन्यसे ॥ २ ॥
explanation: “Why don’t you consent to dwell, O Sītā, in the gynaecium of Rāvaṇa, ravishing the soul of all created beings and furnished with costly couches? (2)

shloka_text:
मानुषी मानुषस्यैव भार्यात्वं बहु मन्यसे।
प्रत्याहर मनो रामान्नैवं जातु भविष्यति ॥ ३ ॥
explanation: “A human being that you are, you prize the wifehood of a human being alone. Pray, * SUNDARAKĀṆḌA * 125 withdraw your mind from Rāma; for, if you continue to love Rāma, you will never survive. (3)

shloka_text:
त्रैलोक्यवसुभोक्तारं रावणं राक्षसेश्वरम्।
भर्तारमुपसंगम्य विहरस्व यथासुखम् ॥ ४ ॥
explanation: “Approaching for union as a husband, Rāvaṇa, the lord of ogres, who enjoys the riches of all the three worlds, sport happily with him. (4)

shloka_text:
मानुषी मानुषं तं तु राममिच्छसि शोभने।
राज्याद् भ्रष्टमसिद्धार्थं विकलवन्तमनिन्दिते ॥ ५ ॥
explanation: “Merely because you are a human being, O good lady of irreproachable charm, you pant for Rāma, who has been deprived of his kingdom, whose object has not been accomplished and as such who remains ever agitated in mind !” (5)

shloka_text:
राक्षसीनां वचः श्रुत्वा सीता पद्मनिभेक्षणा।
नेत्राभ्यामश्रुपूर्णाभ्यामिदं वचनमब्रवीत् ॥ ६ ॥
explanation: Hearing the exhortation of the ogresses, Sītā of lotus-like eyes replied as follows with eyes full of tears : (6)

shloka_text:
यदिदं लोकविद्विष्टमुदाहरत संगताः।
नैतन्मनसि वाक्यं मे किल्बिषं प्रतितिष्ठति ॥ ७ ॥
explanation: “This cheap and sinful advice, which you have jointly tendered and which is repugnant in the eyes of the world, does not hold in my mind even for a moment. (7)

shloka_text:
न मानुषी राक्षसस्य भार्या भवितुमर्हति।
कामं खादत मां सर्वा न करिष्यामि वो वचः ॥ ८ ॥
explanation: “A human lady ought not to become the wife of an ogre. Devour me all if you will; I will never follow your advice. (8)

shloka_text:
दीनो वा राज्यहीनो वा यो मे भर्ता स मे गुरुः।
तं नित्यमनुरक्तास्मि यथा सूर्यं सुवर्चला ॥ ९ ॥
explanation: “Destitute or deprived of his kingdom, he who is my husband is my adorable deity. I am ever devoted to him even as Suvarcalā (consort of the sun-god) is to the sun-god. (9)

shloka_text:
अवलीनः स निर्वाक्यो हनुमान् शिशपादुमे।
सीतां संतर्जयन्तीस्ता राक्षसीरशृणोत् कपिः ॥ १४ ॥
explanation: Remaining hidden in the Aśoka tree without uttering a word, Hanumān listened to those ogresses threatening Sītā. (14)

shloka_text:
तामभिक्रम्य संरब्धा वेपमानां समन्ततः।
भृशं संलिलिहुर्दीप्तान् प्रलम्बान् दशनच्छदान् ॥ १५ ॥
explanation: Assailing on all sides Sītā, who was trembling with fear, enraged as they were, they licked their protruding and glowing lips again and again. (15)

shloka_text:
ऊचुश्च परमकृद्भाः प्रगृह्याशु परश्वधान्।
नेयमर्हति भर्तारं रावणं राक्षसाधिपम् ॥ १६ ॥
explanation: 126 * VĀLMĪKI-RĀMĀYAṆA * Nay, quickly holding up their axes, highly enraged, as they were, they said, “She does not deserve to have Rāvaṇa, the suzerain lord of ogres, for her husband.” (16)

shloka_text:
सा भर्त्स्यमाना भीमाभी राक्षसीभिर्वरांगना।
सा बाष्पमपमार्जन्ती शिंशपां तामुपागमत् ॥ १७ ॥
explanation: While that lovely lady was being overawed by the terrible ogresses, she approached that Aśoka tree, wiping away her tears. (17)

shloka_text:
ततस्तां शिंशपां सीता राक्षसीभिः समावृता।
अभिगम्य विशालाक्षी तस्थौ शोकपरिप्लुता ॥ १८ ॥
explanation: Reaching the foot of that Śimśapā tree, the large-eyed Sītā then stood overwhelmed with grief, surrounded as she was by the ogresses. (18)

shloka_text:
तां कृशां दीनवदनां मलिनाम्बरवासिनीम्।
भर्त्सयाञ्चक्रिरे भीमा राक्षस्यस्ताः समन्ततः ॥ १९ ॥
explanation: Standing around her, the hideous ogresses reproached the emaciated Sītā, who wore a wretched appearance and was clad in a soiled garment. (19)

shloka_text:
ततस्तु विनता नाम राक्षसी भीमदर्शना।
अब्रवीत् कुपिताकारा कराला निर्णतोदरी ॥ २० ॥
explanation: Thereupon a fearful and grim-visaged ogress, Vinatā by name, who wore angry looks and had a sunken belly, spoke as follows: (20)

shloka_text:
सीते पर्याप्तमेतावद् भर्तुः स्नेहः प्रदर्शितः।
सर्वत्रातिकृतं भद्रे व्यसनायोपकल्पते ॥ २१ ॥
explanation: “This much of affection which has been shown by you for your husband is enough, O Sītā! But anything carried to excess leads to adversity everywhere, O good lady! (21)

shloka_text:
परितुष्टास्मि भद्रं ते मानुषस्ते कृतो विधिः।
ममापि तु वचः पथ्यं ब्रुवन्त्याः कुरु मैथिलि ॥ २२ ॥
explanation: “I am highly pleased with you, O princess of Mithilā! May good betide you! The rule of conduct enjoined upon human beings has been followed by you. Now please also carry out the advice tendered by me, who speak only that which is wholesome to you. (22)

shloka_text:
रावणं भज भर्तारं भर्तारं सर्वरक्षसाम्।
विक्रान्तमापतन्तं च सुरेशमिव वासवम् ॥ २३ ॥
explanation: “Take for your husband Rāvaṇa, the protector of all ogres, who is valiant and possessed of a comely exterior like Indra, the ruler of gods. (23)

shloka_text:
दक्षिणं त्यागशीलं च सर्वस्य प्रियवादिनम्।
मानुषं कृपणं रामं त्यक्त्वा रावणमाश्रय ॥ २४ ॥
explanation: “Leaving the mortal and wretched Rāma, betake yourself to Rāvaṇa, who is clever and munificent and speaks kindly to all. (24)

shloka_text:
दिव्यंगरागा वैदेहि दिव्याभरणभूषिता।
अद्यप्रभृति लोकानां सर्वेषामीश्वरी भव ॥ २५ ॥
अग्रेः स्वाहा यथा देवी शची वेन्द्रस्य शोभने।
किं ते रामेण वैदेहि कृपणेन गतायुषा ॥ २६ ॥
explanation: “Using celestial cosmetics and adorned with excellent ornaments, O princess of the Videha territory, become you from this day the sovereign of all the three worlds like Swāhā, the consort of the god of fire, or like Goddess Śaci, the spouse of Indra, O charming lady! What purpose of yours will be served by the wretched Rāma, whose life has now ebbed, O princess of the Videha territory! (25-26)

shloka_text:
एतदुक्तं च मे वाक्यं यदि त्वं न करिष्यसि।
अस्मिन् मुहूर्ते सर्वास्त्वां भक्षयिष्यामहे वयम् ॥ २७ ॥
explanation: “If, on the other hand, you will not act upon this advice tendered by me, we shall all devour you at this very hour.” (27)

shloka_text:
अन्या तु विकटा नाम लम्बमानपयोधरा।
अब्रवीत् कुपिता सीतां मुष्टिमुद्यम्य तर्जती ॥ २८ ॥
explanation: Then clenching her fist and menacing Sītā, another ogress with hanging breasts, Vikaṭā by name, angrily spoke as follows: (28)

shloka_text:
बहून्यप्रतिरूपाणि वचनानि सुदुर्मते।
अनुक्रोशान्मुदुत्वाच्च सोढानि तव मैथिलि ॥ २९ ॥
explanation: * SUNDARAKĀṆḌA * 127 “Many unseemly remarks of yours, uttered with reference to Rāvaṇa, have been endured by us out of compassion and tenderness, O grossly stupid princess of Mithilā ! (29)

shloka_text:
न च नः कुरुषे वाक्यं हितं कालपुरस्कृतम् ।
आनीतासि समुद्रस्य पारमन्यैर्दुरासदम् ॥ ३० ॥
explanation: “It is a pity that you do not even then abide by our wholesome and opportune advice. You must remember that you have been transported to the other shore of the sea, which is difficult of access to others. (30)

shloka_text:
रावणान्तःपुरे घोरे प्रविष्टा चासि मैथिलि ।
रावणस्य गृहे रुद्धा अस्माभिस्त्वभिरक्षिता ॥ ३१ ॥
explanation: “Again you have found your way into the dreadful gynaecium of Rāvaṇa, O princess of Mithilā ! Nay, you have been detained in the abode of Rāvaṇa and are guarded on all sides by us. (31)

shloka_text:
न त्वां शक्तः परित्रातुमपि साक्षात् पुरंदरः ।
कुरुष्व हितवादिन्या वचनं मम मैथिलि ॥ ३२ ॥
explanation: “Not even Indra (the destroyer of strongholds) himself is capable of rescuing you. Therefore, act upon the advice of mine, who am tendering friendly counsel to you, O princess of Mithilā ! (32)

shloka_text:
अलमश्रुनिपातेन त्यज शोकमनर्थकम् ।
भज प्रीतिं प्रहर्षं च त्यजन्ती नित्यदैत्यताम् ॥ ३३ ॥
explanation: “Cease shedding tears. Give up grief, which is of no avail. Shaking off perpetual depression, embrace cheerfulness and experience excessive delight. (33)

shloka_text:
सीते राक्षसराजेन परिक्रीड यथासुखम् ।
जानीमहे यथा भीरु स्त्रीणां यौवनमध्रुवम् ॥ ३४ ॥
explanation: “Sport with Rāvaṇa happily, O Sītā, since we all know the youth of all women to be transitory, O timid lady ! (34)

shloka_text:
यावन्न ते व्यतिक्रामेत् तावत् सुखमवाप्नुहि ।
उद्यानानि च रम्याणि पर्वतोपवनानि च ॥ ३५ ॥
सह राक्षसराजेन चर त्वं मदिरेक्षणे ।
स्त्रीसहस्राणि ते देवि वशे स्थास्यन्ति सुन्दरि ॥ ३६ ॥
explanation: “Enjoy happiness as long as your youth does not pass. Nay, range you the lovely gardens as well as mountains and groves along with Rāvaṇa, the king of ogres, O lady with maddening eyes ! Thousands of women will remain at your beck and call, O charming lady ! (35-36)

shloka_text:
रावणं भज भर्तारं भर्तारं सर्वरक्षसाम् ।
उत्पाट्य वा ते हृदयं भक्षयिष्यामि मैथिलि ॥ ३७ ॥
यदि मे व्याहृतं वाक्यं न यथावत् करिष्यसि ।
ततश्चण्डोदरी नाम राक्षसी क्रूरदर्शना ॥ ३८ ॥
भ्रामयन्ती महच्छूलमिदं वचनमब्रवीत् ।
इमां हरिणशावाक्षीं त्रासोत्कम्पपयोधराम् ॥ ३९ ॥
रावणेन हतां दृष्ट्वा दौर्हदो मे महानयम् ।
यकृत्प्लीहं महत् क्रोडं हृदयं च सबन्धनम् ॥ ४० ॥
गात्राण्यपि तथा शीर्षं खादेयमिति मे मतिः ।
ततस्तु प्रघसा नाम राक्षसी वाक्यमब्रवीत् ॥ ४१ ॥
explanation: “Accept as your consort Rāvaṇa, the lord of all ogres. Tearing out your heart, on the other hand, I shall feast on it, O princess of Mithilā, if you will not duly follow the advice tendered by me.” Brandishing a huge dart, an ogress of ferocious looks, Candodari by name, then spoke as follows: “At the sight of this woman with eyes resembling those of a fawn and with her breasts shaking through fear, borne away to Laṅkā by Rāvaṇa, this great longing sprang up in my heart that I should feast on her liver and spleen, her swollen breast as well as her heart including its stem (consisting of veins and arteries), nay, all her limbs and head too. Such is my mind even now.” Then an ogress, Praghāśa by name, for her part spoke as follows : (37—41)

shloka_text:
कण्ठमस्या नृशंसायाः पीडयामः किमास्यते ।
निवेद्यतां ततो राज्ञे मानुषी सा मृतेति ह ॥ ४२ ॥
explanation: “We shall presently squeeze the neck of this heartless woman; why do we tarry? Let it then be reported to the king that the ‘human lady in question has breathed her last’, they say. (42)

shloka_text:
नात्र कश्चन संदेहः खादतेति स वक्ष्यति।
ततस्त्वजामुखी नाम राक्षसी वाक्यमब्रवीत् ॥ ४३ ॥
explanation: “Hearing this news he will say, ‘devour her’; there is no doubt about it.” Thereupon an ogress, Ajāmukhi by name, spoke as follows : (43)

shloka_text:
विशस्येमां ततः सर्वान् समान् कुरुत पिण्डकान्।
विभजाम ततः सर्वां विवादो मे न रोचते ॥ ४४ ॥
explanation: “Having hacked her, make all pieces equal then. We shall all after that divide them among ourselves. Disputation does not find favour with me. (44)

shloka_text:
पेयमानीयतां क्षिप्रं माल्यं च विविधं बहु।
ततः शूर्पणखा नाम राक्षसी वाक्यमब्रवीत् ॥ ४५ ॥
explanation: “Let drink also be brought speedily as well as many garlands of various kinds.” Then an ogress, Śūrpaṇakhā by name, spoke as follows : (45)

shloka_text:
अजामुख्या यदुक्तं वै तदेव मम रोचते।
सुरा चानीयतां क्षिप्रं सर्वशोकविनाशिनी ॥ ४६ ॥
explanation: “That alone which has been suggested by my friend, Ajāmukhi, appeals to me as well. Let wine too, which dispels all grief, be brought soon. (46)

shloka_text:
मानुषं मांसमास्वाद्य नृत्यामोऽथ निकुम्भिलाम्।
एवं निर्भर्त्स्यमाना सा सीता सुरसुतोपमा।
राक्षसीभिर्विरूपाभिर्धैर्यमुत्सृज्य रोदिति ॥ ४७ ॥
explanation: “Having enjoyed human flesh, we shall then dance in the presence of Goddess Bhadrakāli installed in the western quarter of Laṅkā (known by the name of Nikumbhila).” Losing her patience while being threatened thus by the monstrous ogresses, the said Sītā, who resembled the daughter of a god, began to cry. (47)
Unable to endure the threats of the ogresses and calling aloud Śrī Rāma and others, Sītā bursts into a wail

shloka_text:
अथ तासां वदन्तीनां परुषं दारुणं बहु।
राक्षसीनामसौम्यानां रुरोद जनकात्मजा ॥ १ ॥
explanation: In the midst of those repellent ogresses, who were uttering many such unkind and cruel remarks, the daughter of Janaka, Sītā, now fell a-weeping. (1)

shloka_text:
एवमुक्ता तु वैदेही राक्षसीभिर्मनस्विनी।
उवाच परमत्रस्ता बाष्पगद्गदया गिरा ॥ २ ॥
explanation: Greatly alarmed when threatened thus by the ogresses, Sītā, a princess of the Videha territory, of firm resolve, for her part, spoke as follows in a voice choked with tears: (2)

shloka_text:
न मानुषी राक्षसस्य भार्या भवितुमर्हति।
कामं खादत मां सर्वां न करिष्यामि वो वचः ॥ ३ ॥
explanation: “A female human being is not fit to become the wife of an ogre. Devour me all, if you will; I shall never follow your counsel.” (3)

shloka_text:
सा राक्षसीमध्यगता सीता सुरसुतोपमा।
न शर्म लेभे शोकार्ता रावणेनेव भर्त्सिता ॥ ४ ॥
explanation: Surrounded by ogresses, stricken with grief, as it were, due to her having been reproached by Rāvaṇa, the aforesaid Sītā, who resembled the daughter of a god, did not find rest. (4)

shloka_text:
वेपते स्माधिकं सीता विशन्तीवांगमात्मनः।
वने यूथपरिभ्रष्टा मृगी कोकैरिवार्दिता ॥ ५ ॥
explanation: Shrinking into her own person, as it were, through fear, Sītā shook violently as a doe which has strayed away from its herd and is tormented by wolves in a forest. (5)

shloka_text:
सा त्वशोकस्य विपुलां शाखामालम्ब्य पुष्पिताम्।
चिन्तयामास शोकेन भर्तारं भग्नमानसा ॥ ६ ॥
explanation: Laying hold of a big bough of an Aśoka tree, which was rich in blossom, frustrated as she was in mind through grief, Sītā, for her part, thought of her lord. (6)

shloka_text:
सा स्नापयन्ती विपुलौ स्तनौ नेत्रजलस्तवैः।
चिन्तयन्ती न शोकस्य तदन्तमधिगच्छति ॥ ७ ॥
explanation: Bathing her large breasts with the streams of her tears and brooding over her miserable plight, she saw no end to her grief at that moment. (7)

shloka_text:
सा वेपमाना पतिता प्रवाते कदली यथा।
राक्षसीनां भयत्रस्ता विवर्णवदनाभवत् ॥ ८ ॥
explanation: Shaking like a plantain tree exposed to a stormy wind, seized as she was with the fear of the ogresses, Sītā looked palefaced. (8)

shloka_text:
तस्याः सा दीर्घबहुला वेपन्त्याः सीतया तदा।
ददृशे कम्पिता वेणी व्यालीव परिसर्पती ॥ ९ ॥
explanation: That swinging braid of Sītā, long and thick, while she was shaking from head to foot, looked like a gliding serpent at that time. (9)

shloka_text:
सा निःश्वसन्ती शोकार्ता कोपोपहतचेतना।
आर्ता व्यसृजदशृणि मैथिली विललाप च ॥ १० ॥
हा रामेति च दुःखार्ता हा पुनर्लक्ष्मणेति च।
हा श्वश्रूर्मम कौसल्ये हा सुमित्रेति भामिनी ॥ ११ ॥
explanation: Drawing deep audible breaths, miserable and stricken with grief as she was, that lovely young lady, the princess of Mithilā, whose understanding had been clouded through anger and who was afflicted with agony, began to shed tears and wailed—“O Rāma,” and again, “O Lakṣmaṇa, O Kausalyā, my mother-in-law, O Sumitrā ! (10-11)

shloka_text:
लोकप्रवादः सत्योऽयं पण्डितैः समुदाहृतः।
अकाले दुर्लभो मृत्युः स्त्रिया वा पुरुषस्य वा ॥ १२ ॥
यत्राहमाभिः क्रूराभी राक्षसीभिरिहार्दिता।
जीवामि हीना रामेण मुहूर्तमपि दुःखिता ॥ १३ ॥
explanation: “There is this popular saying uttered by the wise that the death of a woman or of a man is difficult to occur before time inasmuch as, even though I am tormented by these fierce ogresses here and stand separated from Śrī Rāma, and afflicted, I am able to survive even for a while. (12-13)

shloka_text:
एषाल्पपुण्या कृपणा विनशिष्याम्यनाथवत्।
समुद्रमध्ये नौः पूर्णा वायुवेगैरिवाहता ॥ १४ ॥
explanation: “Of poor merit and wretched that I am, I shall perish like a forlorn creature, even as a bark fully loaded and buffeted by the blasts of a tempest would flounder in the ocean. (14)

shloka_text:
भर्तारं तमपश्यन्ती राक्षसीवशमागता।
सीदामि खलु शोकेन कूलं तोयहतं यथा ॥ १५ ॥
explanation: “Unable to see my celebrated husband and fallen into the clutches of ogresses, I am wasting away through grief even as a river bank undermined by the current. (15)

shloka_text:
तं पद्मदलपत्राक्षं सिंहविक्रान्तगामिनम्।
धन्याः पश्यन्ति मे नाथं कृतज्ञं प्रियवादिनम् ॥ १६ ॥
explanation: “Only the fortunate are able to look on my aforesaid lord, who has eyes resembling the petals of an expanded lotus and walks with the gait of a lion, who is alive to the services rendered to him and speaks kind words to all. (16)

shloka_text:
सर्वथा तेन हीनाया रामेण विदितात्मना।
तीक्ष्णं विषमिवास्वाद्य दुर्लभं मम जीवनम् ॥ १७ ॥
explanation: “My life, now that I have been separated from the aforesaid Śrī Rāma, a knower of the Self, is hard to sustain even as for one who has swallowed a deadly poison. (17)

shloka_text:
कीदृशं तु महापापं मया देहान्तरे कृतम्।
तेनेदं प्राप्यते घोरं महादुःखं सुदारुणम् ॥ १८ ॥
explanation: “What kind of heinous sin was actually perpetrated by me in another body in a previous existence? Due to that, this terrible and most cruel major sorrow is being experienced by me. (18)

shloka_text:
जीवितं त्यक्तुमिच्छामि शोकेन महता वृता।
राक्षसीभिश्च रक्षन्त्या रामो नासाद्यते मया ॥ १९ ॥
explanation: “Beset that I am with this intense grief, I long to give up the ghost; for Śrī Rāma can never be reached by me so long as I am being guarded by the ogresses. (19)

shloka_text:
धिगस्तु खलु मानुष्यं धिगस्तु परवश्यताम्।
न शक्यं यत् परित्यक्तुमात्मच्छन्देन जीवितम् ॥ २० ॥
explanation: “Shame indeed be upon the human state and shame be upon dependence on others, due to which it is not possible for me even to yield up life of my own free will!” (20)

Making up her mind not to submit to the advances of Rāvaṇa even on pain of death, when menaced by the ogresses, and indulging in speculation as to why Śrī Rāma was not turning up to rescue her, Sītā wails in various ways

shloka_text:
प्रसक्ताश्रुमुखी त्वेवं ब्रुवती जनकात्मजा।
अधोगतमुखी बाला विलप्तुमुपचक्रमे ॥ १ ॥
उन्मत्तेव प्रमत्तेव भ्रान्तचित्तेव शोचती।
उपावृत्ता किशोरीव विचेष्टन्ती महीतले ॥ २ ॥
explanation: While speaking as aforesaid and grieving, tears rolling down her face, her head bent low, as though she were possessed, distracted or bewildered in mind, and wallowing on the earth's surface like a colt which rolls habitually about in order to shake off its fatigue, the youthful daughter of Janaka for her part began to wail as follows: (1-2)

shloka_text:
राघवस्य प्रमत्तस्य रक्षसा कामरूपिणा।
रावणेन प्रमथ्याहमानीता क्रोशती बलात् ॥ ३ ॥
explanation: “Though living under the protection of Śrī Rāma, a scion of Raghu, who having been lured away from my presence by Mārīca, had grown heedless about me, I was forcibly borne away, screaming after being overpowered by the ogre, Rāvaṇa, who is able to change his form at will. (3)

shloka_text:
राक्षसीवशमापन्ना भर्त्स्यमाना च दारुणम्।
चिन्तयन्ती सुदुःखार्ता नाहं जीवितुमुत्सहे ॥ ४ ॥
explanation: “Fallen that I am into the clutches of ogresses and am being ruthlessly threatened by them, and remain constantly brooding and sore stricken with sorrow, I dare not survive any longer. (4)

shloka_text:
नहि मे जीवितेनार्थो नैवार्थेन च भूषणैः।
वसन्त्या राक्षसीमध्ये विना रामं महारथम् ॥ ५ ॥
explanation: “I have no use whatsoever for life, nor even for riches, nor for jewels, as long as I am living in the midst of ogresses apart from Śrī Rāma, a great chariot-warrior. (5)

shloka_text:
अश्मसारमिदं नूनमथवाप्यजरामरम्।
हृदयं मम येनेदं न दुःखेन विशीर्यते ॥ ६ ॥
explanation: “This heart of mine is surely like iron or * SUNDARAKĀṆḌA * 131 proof against age and death in that it does not get riven even through agony. (6)

shloka_text:
धिङ्मामनार्यामसतीं याहं तेन विना कृता।
मुहूर्तमपि जीवामि जीवितं पापजीविका ॥ ७ ॥
explanation: “Woe be to me, ignoble and vile that I am, inasmuch as I preserve my life even for a while, though separated from him and leading as I do a sinful existence. (7)

shloka_text:
चरणेनापि सव्वेन न स्पृशेयं निशाचरम्।
रावणं किं पुनरहं कामयेयं विगर्हितम् ॥ ८ ॥
explanation: “I would not touch the ogre Rāvaṇa even with my left foot, much less love the despicable fellow. (8)

shloka_text:
प्रत्याख्यानं न जानाति नात्मानं नात्मनः कुलम्।
यो नृशंसस्वभावेन मां प्रार्थयितुमिच्छति ॥ ९ ॥
explanation: “He does not heed my refusal, nor does he cognize himself, nor his own race. Due to his cruel nature, on the other hand, he seeks to win me over. (9)

shloka_text:
छिन्ना भिन्ना प्रभिन्ना वा दीप्ता वाग्रौ प्रदीपिता।
रावणं नोपतिष्ठेयं किं प्रलापेन वशिचरम् ॥ १० ॥
explanation: “I would not betake myself to Rāvaṇa even if I am transfixed, cut asunder, hacked to pieces, roasted in fire or burnt. What shall be gained by your raving for so long? (10)

shloka_text:
ख्यातः प्राज्ञः कृतज्ञश्च सानुक्रोशश्च राघवः।
सद्वृत्तो निरनुक्रोशः शङ्के मद्भाग्यसंक्षयात् ॥ ११ ॥
राक्षसानां जनस्थाने सहस्राणि चतुर्दश।
एकेनैव निरस्तानि स मां किं नाभिपद्यते ॥ १२ ॥
explanation: “I fear Śrī Rāma, a scion of Raghu, who was well-known as a wise man, alive to the services rendered to him, nay, merciful and a man of excellent morals, has become pitiless due to complete loss of my good fortune. Otherwise, why does he, by whom alone as many as fourteen thousand ogres were killed in Janasthāna, not come to me? (11-12)

shloka_text:
निरुद्धा रावणेनाहमल्पवीर्येण रक्षसा।
समर्थः खलु मे भर्ता रावणं हन्तुमाहवे ॥ १३ ॥
explanation: “What a pity that I have been detained by Rāvaṇa, an ogre of poor strength, although my husband is surely able to kill Rāvaṇa in combat. (13)

shloka_text:
विराधो दण्डकारण्ये येन राक्षसपुंगवः।
रणे रामेण निहतः स मां किं नाभिपद्यते ॥ १४ ॥
explanation: “Why does Śrī Rāma, by whom Virādha, the foremost of ogres, was slain in the Daṇḍaka forest, not run up to me? (14)

shloka_text:
कामं मध्ये समुद्रस्य लङ्केयं दुष्प्रधर्षणा।
न तु राघवबाणानां गतिरोधो भविष्यति ॥ १५ ॥
explanation: “Granted that, situated as it is in mid-ocean, this Laṅkā is difficult to storm, but the flight of the arrows of Śrī Rāma, however, can meet with no obstruction here. (15)

shloka_text:
किं नु तत् कारणं येन रामो दृढपराक्रमः।
रक्षसापहतां भार्यामिष्टां यो नाभिपद्यते ॥ १६ ॥
explanation: “What on earth could be the reason why Śrī Rāma of unyielding prowess does not run to the rescue of his beloved wife, borne away by an ogre? (16)

shloka_text:
इहस्थां मां न जानीते शङ्के लक्ष्मणपूर्वजः।
जानन्नपि स तेजस्वी धर्षणां मर्षयिष्यति ॥ १७ ॥
explanation: “I fear that Śrī Rāma, an elder brother of Lakṣmaṇa, does not know me to be here. Knowing that I am here, will he be able to put up with the outrage, all powerful and mighty that he is? (17)

shloka_text:
हृतेति मां योऽधिगत्य राघवाय निवेदयेत्।
गृध्रराजोऽपि स रणे रावणेन निपातितः ॥ १८ ॥
explanation: “That king of vultures too, who having come to know that Rāvaṇa had borne me away, could have reported the matter to Śrī Rāma, a scion of Raghu, but was killed by Rāvaṇa in an encounter. (18)

shloka_text:
कृतं कर्म महत् तेन मां तथाभ्यवपद्यता।
तिष्ठता रावणवधे वृद्धेनापि जटायुषा ॥ १९ ॥
explanation: “A prodigious feat was accomplished by the aforesaid Jatāyu, who though old, strove to get rid of Rāvaṇa in order to rescue me at the moment. (19)

shloka_text:
यदि मामिह जानीयाद् वर्तमानां हि राघवः।
अद्य बाणैरभिकृद्भः कुर्याल्लोकमराक्षसम् ॥ २० ॥
explanation: “If Śrī Rāma really knew me to be present here, he would in fury rid the world of ogres with his shafts today. (20)

shloka_text:
निर्दहेच्च पुरीं लङ्कां निर्दहेच्च महोदधिम्।
रावणस्य च नीचस्य कीर्तिं नाम च नाशयेत् ॥ २१ ॥
explanation: “Nay, he would reduce the city of Laṅkā to ashes and burn up the ocean. He would also blot out the fame as well as the name of the despicable Rāvaṇa. (21)

shloka_text:
ततो निहतनाथानां राक्षसीनां गृहे गृहे।
यथाहमेवं रुदती तथा भूयो न संशयः ॥ २२ ॥
explanation: “Then, even as I stand weeping thus, more so would be heard in every house wails of the ogresses, whose lords would have been slain: there is no doubt about it. (22)

shloka_text:
अन्विष्य रक्षसां लङ्कां कुर्याद् रामः सलक्ष्मणः।
नहि ताभ्यां रिपुर्दृष्टो मुहूर्तमपि जीवति ॥ २३ ॥
explanation: “Having searched out Laṅkā, he with Lakṣmaṇa will encompass the destruction of ogres. An enemy seen by them would not survive even for a while. (23)

shloka_text:
चिताधूमाकुलपथा गृध्रमण्डलमण्डिता।
अचिरेणैव कालेन श्मशानसदृशी भवेत् ॥ २४ ॥
explanation: “With its streets obscured by the smoke of funeral piles and graced with wreaths of vultures, Laṅkā will at no distant date look like a crematorium. (24)

shloka_text:
अचिरेणैव कालेन प्राप्स्याम्येनं मनोरथम्।
दुष्प्रस्थानोऽयमाभाति सर्वेषां वो विपर्ययः ॥ २५ ॥
explanation: “I shall at no distant time attain the object of my desire; for this evil conduct of you all in the shape of my abduction and oppression means your annihilation. (25)

shloka_text:
यादृशानि तु दृश्यन्ते लङ्कायामशुभानि तु।
अचिरेणैव कालेन भविष्यति हतप्रभा ॥ २६ ॥
explanation: “The type of ill-omens, which are actually seen here in Laṅkā lead one to conclude that the city will at no distant date be shorn of its splendour. (26)

shloka_text:
नूनं लङ्का हते पापे रावणे राक्षसाधिपे।
शोषमेष्यति दुर्धर्षा प्रमदा विधवा यथा ॥ २७ ॥
explanation: “Surely when the sinful Rāvaṇa, the suzerain ruler of ogres, is slain, Laṅkā, which appears difficult to storm now, will wither up like a young widow. (27)

shloka_text:
पुण्योत्सवसमृद्धा च नष्टभर्त्री सराक्षसा।
भविष्यति पुरी लङ्का नष्टभर्त्री यथांगना ॥ २८ ॥
explanation: “Abounding in festive ceremonies at present, the city of Laṅkā, when its ruler is dead and gone with the ogres inhabiting it, will look like a widow. (28)

shloka_text:
नूनं राक्षसकन्यानां रुदतीनां गृहे गृहे।
श्रोष्यामि नचिरादेव दुःखार्तानामिह ध्वनिम् ॥ २९ ॥
explanation: “I shall assuredly hear before long the cry of distress of ogres maids stricken with sorrow and weeping in every dwelling here. (29)

shloka_text:
सान्धकारा हतद्योता हतराक्षसपुंगवा।
भविष्यति पुरी लङ्का निर्दग्धा रामसायकैः ॥ ३० ॥
यदि नाम स शूरो मां रामो रक्तान्तलोचनः।
जातीयाद् वर्तमानां यां राक्षसस्य निवेशने ॥ ३१ ॥
explanation: “Consumed by Śrī Rāma’s shafts, Laṅkā, with its principal ogres slain and its splendour dissipated, will look gloomy, if only that heroic Śrī Rāma, the corners of whose eyes are red, comes to know of my being present in the abode of Rāvaṇa. (30-31)

shloka_text:
अनेन तु नृशंसेन रावणेनाधमेन मे।
समयो यस्तु निर्दिष्टस्तस्य कालोऽयमागतः ॥ ३२ ॥
explanation: “The expiry of that time-limit of twelve months which was actually fixed by this cruel and vile Rāvaṇa for my death, has well-nigh arrived, as it is coming only two months hence. (32)

shloka_text:
स च मे विहितो मृत्युरस्मिन् दुष्टेन वर्तते।
अकार्यं ये न जानन्ति नैर्ऋताः पापकारिणः ॥ ३३ ॥
explanation: “Again, the aforesaid death of mine has * SUNDARAKĀṆḌA * 133 been ordained in the near future by the wicked fellow in the presence of these sinful ogresses, who have no idea of what should not be perpetrated. (33)

shloka_text:
अधर्मात् तु महोत्पातो भविष्यति हि साम्प्रतम् ।
नैते धर्मं विजानन्ति राक्षसाः पिशिताशनाः ॥ ३४ ॥
explanation: “A great calamity indeed will presently follow from the injustice which is being done to me. These flesh-eating ogres, however, attach no value to virtue. (34)

shloka_text:
ध्रुवं मां प्रातराशार्थं राक्षसः कल्पयिष्यति ।
साहं कथं करिष्यामि तं विना प्रियदर्शनम् ॥ ३५ ॥
explanation: “The ogre will undoubtedly cut me into slices for his morning repast. As such what shall I do in the absence of Śrī Rāma of pleasing aspect? (35)

shloka_text:
रामं रक्तान्तनयनमपश्यन्ती सुदुःखिता ।
क्षिप्रं वैवस्वतं देवं पश्येयं पतिना विना ॥ ३६ ॥
explanation: “Unable to see Śrī Rāma, the corners of whose eyes are red, and therefore sore distressed, I shall soon see God Yama (the god of death, son of the sun-god) in the absence of my husband. (36)

shloka_text:
नाजानाज्जीवतीं रामः स मां भरतपूर्वजः ।
जानन्ती तु न कुर्यातां नोर्व्यां हि परिमार्गणम् ॥ ३७ ॥
explanation: “Śrī Rāma, that elder brother of Bharata, does not know me to be living, nor does Lakṣmaṇa. Had they known it, it cannot be imagined that they would not prosecute their search all over the globe. (37)

shloka_text:
नूनं ममैव शोकेन स वीरो लक्ष्मणाग्रजः ।
देवलोकमितो यातस्त्यक्त्वा देहं महीतले ॥ ३८ ॥
explanation: “Leaving his body on the earth's surface precisely through grief caused by separation from me, that gallant elder brother of Lakṣmaṇa has surely departed to the heavenly world from this globe. (38)

shloka_text:
धन्या देवाः सगन्धर्वाः सिद्धाश्च परमर्षयः ।
मम पश्यन्ति ये वीरं रामं राजीवलोचनम् ॥ ३९ ॥
explanation: “Happy in heaven are the gods as well as the Gandharvas, the Siddhas and the eminent Ṛṣis, who are able to look on my husband, the heroic Śrī Rāma of lotus-like eyes. (39)

shloka_text:
अथवा नहि तस्यार्थो धर्मकामस्य धीमतः ।
मया रामस्य राजर्षेर्भार्यया परमात्मनः ॥ ४० ॥
explanation: “Or, that royal sage, the sagacious Śrī Rāma, who seeks religious merit alone and has become one with the Supreme Spirit, has no longer any use for me, his wife. (40)

shloka_text:
दृश्यमाने भवेत् प्रीतिः सौहृदं नास्त्यदृश्यतः ।
नाशयन्ति कृतघ्नास्तु न रामो नाशयिष्यति ॥ ४१ ॥
explanation: “Love sticks to one remaining before one's eyes while it no longer exists for one who is out of sight. But the ungrateful alone spurn love; Śrī Rāma would never do so. (41)

shloka_text:
किं वा मयगुणाः केचित् किं वा भाग्यक्षयो हि मे ।
या हि सीता वराहेण हीना रामेण भामिनी ॥ ४२ ॥
explanation: “Or, are there any shortcomings in me or perhaps it is loss of fortune in my case due to which, I, Sītā, a young lady, deserving his protection, stand separated from Śrī Rāma, who is worthy of excellent possessions. (42)

shloka_text:
श्रेयो मे जीवितान्मर्तुं विहीनाया महात्मना ।
रामादकिलष्टचारित्राच्छूराच्छत्रुनिर्बर्हणात् ॥ ४३ ॥
explanation: “Death is preferable to life for me, who stand disunited from the high-souled and heroic Śrī Rāma, who is unwearied in maintaining his character and who is capable of exterminating his foes. (43)

shloka_text:
अथवा न्यस्तशस्त्रौ तौ वने मूलफलाशनौ ।
भ्रातरो हि नरश्रेष्ठौ चरन्तौ वनगोचरौ ॥ ४४ ॥
explanation: “Or, those two brothers, Śrī Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, the foremost of men, roaming, as they do, in the forest as dwellers of the forest and living on roots and fruits alone have actually given up their arms and taken a vow of non-violence. (44)

shloka_text:
अथवा राक्षसेन्द्रेण रावणेन दुरात्मना ।
छद्मना घातितौ शूरौ भ्रातरो रामलक्ष्मणौ ॥ ४५ ॥
explanation: 134 * VĀLMĪKI-RĀMĀYAṆA * “Or, the two gallant brothers, Śrī Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, have been caused to be killed through some trick by the evil-minded Rāvaṇa, the lord of ogres. (45)

shloka_text:
साहमेवंविधे काले मर्तुमिच्छामि सर्वतः ।
न च मे विहितो मृत्युरस्मिन् दुःखेऽतिवर्तति ॥ ४६ ॥
explanation: “Situated as I am, I wish to die by all means at such a juncture; my death, however, is not ordained even in my present extreme agony. (46)

shloka_text:
धन्याः खलु महात्मानो मुनयः सत्यसम्मताः ।
जितात्मानो महाभागा येषां न स्तः प्रियाप्रिये ॥ ४७ ॥
explanation: “Happy indeed are the magnanimous and highly blessed hermits by whom the highest Reality has been fully recognized as their very Self and who have subdued the self and in whose eyes the pleasing and the displeasing do not exist. (47)

shloka_text:
प्रियान्न सम्भवेद् दुःखमप्रियादधिकं भवेत् ।
ताभ्यां हि ते वियुज्यन्ते नमस्तेषां महात्मनाम् ॥ ४८ ॥
explanation: “To them sorrow does not follow from the pleasing, being snatched away, nor does it grow intense through the displeasing being met with, inasmuch as they are rid of joy and sorrow. Hail to those high-souled ones! (48)

shloka_text:
साहं त्यक्ता प्रियेणैव रामेण विदितात्मना ।
प्राणांस्त्यक्ष्यामि पापस्य रावणस्य गता वशम् ॥ ४९ ॥
explanation: “Situated as I am, I, who have been forsaken by my beloved Śrī Rāma himself, a knower of the Self, and I, who have fallen into the clutches of the sinful Rāvaṇa, shall give up the ghost.” (49)

Risen from sleep, an ogress, Trijāṭā by name, speaks to her companions intimidating Sītā, of a dream she saw only a few minutes before revealing the triumph of Śrī Rāma and the discomfiture of Rāvaṇa, and stops them from molesting Sītā. Pressed by them, she relates the dream to them and also speaks of the omens portending the triumph of Sītā

shloka_text:
इत्युक्ताः सीतया घोरं राक्षस्य क्रोधमूर्च्छिताः ।
काश्चिज्जग्मुस्तदाख्यातुं रावणस्य दुरात्मनः ॥ १ ॥
explanation: Distracted through anger when told by Sītā of her violent intention, some ogresses proceeded to communicate it to the evil-minded Rāvaṇa. (1)

shloka_text:
ततः सीतामुपागम्य राक्षस्यो भीमदर्शनाः ।
पुनः परुषमेकार्थमनर्थार्थमथाब्रुवन् ॥ २ ॥
explanation: Approaching Sītā, the ogresses of hideous aspect then spoke to her again the following harsh words, which harped on the same point and spelt disaster to them alone: (2)

shloka_text:
अद्येदानीं तवानार्ये सीते पापविनिश्चये ।
राक्षस्यो भक्षयिष्यन्ति मांसमेतद् यथासुखम् ॥ ३ ॥
explanation: “O wretched Sītā of sinful resolve, the ogresses will feast at pleasure on this flesh of yours this very moment today.” (3)

shloka_text:
सीतां ताभिरनार्याभिर्दृष्ट्वा संतर्जितां तदा ।
राक्षसी त्रिजटा वृद्धा प्रबुद्धा वाक्यमब्रवीत् ॥ ४ ॥
explanation: * SUNDARAKĀṆḌA * 135 Seeing Sītā intimidated as above by those vile women at that moment, an aged ogress, Trijāṭā, who had just woken up from sleep, spoke as follows: (4)

shloka_text:
आत्मानं खादतानार्या न सीतां भक्षयिष्यथ।
जनकस्य सुतामिष्टां स्नुषां दशरथस्य च ॥५॥
explanation: “Devour yourselves, O wretches if you will; you will not be able to feast on Sītā, Janaka’s daughter and beloved daughter-in-law of Daśaratha. (5)

shloka_text:
स्वप्नो ह्यद्य मया दृष्टो दारुणो रोमहर्षणः।
राक्षसानामभावाय भर्तुरस्या भवाय च ॥६॥
explanation: “A horrible dream, which makes my hair stand on end, has actually been seen by me today pointing to the annihilation of ogres and to the well-being of her husband.” (6)

shloka_text:
एवमुक्तास्त्रिजटया राक्षस्यः क्रोधमूर्च्छिताः।
सर्वा एवाब्रुवन् भीतास्त्रिजटां तामिदं वचः ॥७॥
explanation: Seized with fright when spoken to as aforesaid by Trijāṭā, all the ogresses, who were distracted through anger only a minute before, spoke as follows to the aforesaid Trijāṭā: (7)

shloka_text:
कथयस्व त्वया दृष्टः स्वप्नोऽयं कीदृशो निशि।
तासां श्रुत्वा तु वचनं राक्षसीनां मुखोद्गतम् ॥८॥
उवाच वचनं काले त्रिजटा स्वप्नसंश्रितम्।
गजदन्तमयीं दिव्यां शिबिकामन्तरिक्षगाम् ॥९॥
युक्तां वाजिसहस्रेण स्वयमास्थाय राघवः।
शुक्लमाल्याम्बरधरो लक्ष्मणेन समागतः ॥१०॥
explanation: “Speak out what kind of dream was seen by you this night.” Hearing the request that had escaped from the lips of the ogresses, Trijāṭā for her part made the following answer bearing on the dream seen by her during the morning wee-hours : “Mounting a celestial palanquin made of ivory and coursing through the airspace, nay, drawn by a thousand horses, Śrī Rāma himself, clad in a white raiment and wearing a white garland, has duly come here with Lakṣmaṇa. (8—10)

shloka_text:
स्वप्ने चाद्य मया दृष्टा सीता शुक्लाम्बरावृता।
सागरेण परिक्षिप्तं श्वेतपर्वतमास्थिता ॥११॥
explanation: “Clad in white robes, Sītā, too, was seen by me in the dream today perched on a white mountain surrounded by sea. (11)

shloka_text:
कृष्यमाणः स्त्रिया मुण्डो दृष्टः कृष्णाम्बरः पुनः ।
रथेन खुरयुक्तेन रक्तमाल्यानुलेपनः ॥ २४ ॥
explanation: "He was seen in a dream once more with a shaven head and robed in black, wearing a red garland and smeared with red sandal-paste and being pulled by a woman on a chariot drawn by asses. (24)

shloka_text:
पिबंस्तैलं हसन्त्यन् भ्रान्तचित्ताकुलेन्द्रियः ।
गर्दभेन ययौ शीघ्रं दक्षिणां दिशमास्थितः ॥ २५ ॥
explanation: "Quaffing oil, laughing and dancing, his mind confused and senses obscured, he sped on the back of an ass in a southerly direction. (25)

shloka_text:
पुनरेव मया दृष्टो रावणो राक्षसेश्वरः ।
पतितोऽवाक्सिरा भूमौ गर्दभाद् भयमोहितः ॥ २६ ॥
explanation: "Rāvaṇa, the lord of ogres, was again seen by me fallen headlong from the back of the ass, confused through fear. (26)

shloka_text:
सहसोत्थाय सम्भ्रान्तो भयार्तो मदविह्वलः ।
उन्मत्तरूपो दिग्वासा दुर्वाक्यं प्रलपन् बहु ॥ २७ ॥
explanation: "Leaping up suddenly, utterly bewildered, terror-stricken, overpowered with intoxication, looking like a madman, and sky-clad, he was seen uttering many abusive words. (27)

shloka_text:
दुर्गन्धं दुःसहं घोरं तिमिरं नरकोपमम् ।
मलपङ्कं प्रविश्याशु मग्रस्तत्र स रावणः ॥ २८ ॥
explanation: "Entering a fearful gloom, resembling hell itself, emitting a foul smell difficult to bear, nay, full of filth and mire, the aforesaid Rāvaṇa soon disappeared into it. (28)

shloka_text:
रावणस्य सुताः सर्वे मुण्डास्तैलसमुक्षिताः ।
वराहेण दशग्रीवः शिशुमारेण चेन्द्रजित् ॥ ३१ ॥
उष्ट्रेण कुम्भकर्णश्च प्रयातो दक्षिणां दिशम् ।
एकस्तत्र मया दृष्टः श्वेतच्छत्रो विभीषणः ॥ ३२ ॥
शुक्लमाल्याम्बरधरः शुक्लगन्धानुलेपनः ।
शङ्खदुन्दुभिनिर्घोषैर्नृसगीतैरलंकृतः ॥ ३३ ॥
आरुह्य शैलसंकाशं मेघस्तनितनिःस्वनम् ।
चतुर्दन्तं गजं दिव्यमास्ते तत्र विभीषणः ॥ ३४ ॥
चतुर्भिः सचिवैः सार्धं वैहायसमुपस्थितः ॥ ३५ ॥
explanation: "All the sons of Rāvaṇa too were seen by me with shaven heads and bathed in oil. Nay, Rāvaṇa, the ten-headed monster, departed in a southerly direction on the back of a boar, his eldest son Meghanāda (the conqueror of Indra) too on the back of a dolphin and Kumbhakarṇa on the back of a camel. In that dream Vibhīṣaṇa, Rāvaṇa's youngest brother, alone was seen by me shaded with a white canopy, dressed in white and wearing a white garland, nay, smeared with white sandal-paste. Hailed with blasts of conch-shells and the beating of kettledrums as well as with dances and songs, Vibhīṣaṇa stood there in the air mounted on a four-tusked celestial elephant closely resembling a hill and trumpeting like thunder, with four ministers. (31—35)

shloka_text:
समाजश्च महान् वृत्तो गीतवादित्रनिःस्वनः ।
पिबतां रक्तमाल्यानां रक्षसां रक्तवाससाम् ॥ ३६ ॥
explanation: "A large assemblage, distinguished by the sound of vocal and instrumental music, of ogres, clad in red and adorned with red garlands and drinking oil, had also collected. (36)

shloka_text:
लङ्का चेयं पुरी रम्या सवाजिरथकुञ्जरा ।
सागरे पतिता दृष्टा भग्नगोपुरतोरणा ॥ ३७ ॥
explanation: "Nay, this enchanting city of Laṅkā, horses, chariots and elephants and all, was seen by me fallen into the sea, its gateways and arches shattered. (37)

shloka_text:
लङ्का दृष्टा मया स्वप्ने रावणेनाभिरक्षिता ।
दग्धा रामस्य दूतेन वानरेण तरस्विना ॥ ३८ ॥
explanation: "Though protected on all sides by Rāvaṇa, Laṅkā was further seen by me in a different dream burnt up by an agile monkey, acting as an envoy of Śrī Rāma. (38)

shloka_text:
पीत्वा तैलं प्रमत्ताश्च प्रहसन्त्यो महास्वनाः ।
लङ्कायां भस्मरूक्षायां सर्वां राक्षसयोषितः ॥ ३९ ॥
explanation: "All the ogresses in Laṅkā, now arid with ashes, were seen drunk with oil and laughing heartily with great noise. (39)

shloka_text:
कुम्भकर्णादयश्चेमे सर्वे राक्षसपुंगवाः ।
रक्तं निवसनं गृह्य प्रविष्टा गोमयहुदम् ॥ ४० ॥
explanation: "Putting on a red attire of inferior quality, all these jewels among the ogres, Kumbhakarṇa and others, disappeared into a pool of cowdung. (40)

shloka_text:
अपगच्छत पश्यध्वं सीतामाप्नोति राघवः ।
घातयेत् परमामर्षी युष्मान् सार्धं हि राक्षसैः ॥ ४१ ॥
explanation: "Therefore, get away from this place and watch how Śrī Rāma, a scion of Raghu, recovers Sītā. Supremely intolerant by nature, he will undoubtedly kill you all alongwith the ogres. (41)

shloka_text:
प्रियां बहुमतां भार्या वनवासमनुव्रताम् ।
भर्त्सितां तर्जितां वापि नानुमंस्यति राघवः ॥ ४२ ॥
explanation: "Śrī Rāma, a scion of Raghu, would never tolerate his beloved and highly esteemed wife, who had followed him in his exile, to be reproached or threatened by you. (42)

shloka_text:
तदलं क्रूरवाक्यैश्च सान्त्वमेवाभिधीयताम् ।
अभियाचाम वैदेहीमेतद्वि मम रोचते ॥ ४३ ॥
explanation: "Therefore, have done with cruel words and let conciliatory words alone be spoken to her. Let us crave her forgiveness; for, this alone appeals to me. (43)

shloka_text:
यस्या होवविधः स्वप्नो दुःखितायाः प्रदृश्यते।
सा दुःखैर्बहुभिर्मुक्ता प्रियं प्राप्नोत्यनुत्तमम् ॥ ४४ ॥
explanation: “Rid of her numerous woes, that wretched lady about whom such a dream has been vividly seen by me will undoubtedly attain her beloved and highest object. (44)

shloka_text:
भर्त्सितामपि याचध्वं राक्षस्यः किं विवक्षया।
राघवाद्भि भयं घोरं राक्षसानामुपस्थितम् ॥ ४५ ॥
explanation: “Beseech her forgiveness, O ogresses, even though she has been menaced by you. What will be gained through your anxiety to discuss the subject any more; for a terrible danger from Śrī Rāma (a scion of Raghu) threatens the ogres. (45)

shloka_text:
प्रणिपातप्रसन्ना हि मैथिली जनकात्मजा।
अलमेषा परित्रातुं राक्षस्यो महतो भयात् ॥ ४६ ॥
explanation: “Sītā, a princess of Mithilā, daughter of Janaka, will get pleased with prostration alone. She is capable of shielding you from a terrible danger, O ogresses ! (46)

shloka_text:
अपि चास्या विशालाक्ष्या न किंचिदुपलक्षये।
विरूपमपि चांगेषु सुसूक्ष्ममपि लक्षणम् ॥ ४७ ॥
explanation: “Furthermore, I do not notice in the limbs of this large-eyed lady any inauspicious mark, however minute, which may give indication of any mishap to her. (47)

shloka_text:
छायावैगुण्यमात्रं तु शङ्के दुःखमुपस्थितम्।
अदुःखार्हमिमां देवीं वैहायसमुपस्थितम् ॥ ४८ ॥
explanation: “I, for my part, suspect that misfortune has befallen this godlike lady—who does not merit adversity and who mounted an aerial car in the dream seen by me—only in the shape of diminution of splendour occasioned by want of bath, toilet etc. (48)

shloka_text:
अर्थसिद्धिं तु वैदेह्याः पश्याम्यहमुपस्थितम्।
राक्षसेन्द्रविनाशं च विजयं राघवस्य च ॥ ४९ ॥
explanation: “I, for my part, visualize the accomplishment of purpose of Sītā, a princess of the Videha territory to be at hand, as also the destruction of Rāvaṇa, the lord of ogres, and the triumph of Śrī Rāma, a scion of Raghu. (49)

shloka_text:
निमित्तभूतमेतत् तु श्रोतुमस्या महत् प्रियम्।
दृश्यते च स्फुरच्छक्षुः पद्मपत्रमिवायतम् ॥ ५० ॥
explanation: “Nay, her left eye, large as a lotus-petal, is seen throbbing. This is surely a prognostication of her hearing a most pleasing news. (50)

shloka_text:
ईषद्धि हृषितो वास्या दक्षिणाया ह्यदक्षिणः।
अकस्मादेव वैदेह्या बाहुरेकः प्रकम्पते ॥ ५१ ॥
explanation: “Again, slightly thrilled, the left arm alone of this amiable lady, Sītā, a princess of the Videha territory, is palpitating without any visible cause at all. (51)

shloka_text:
करेणुहस्तप्रतिमः सव्यश्चोरुनुत्तमः।
वेपन् कथयतीवास्या राघवं पुरतः स्थितम् ॥ ५२ ॥
explanation: “Her most shapely left thigh, resembling the proboscis of an elephant, which is also pulsating, announces, as it were, the presence of Śrī Rāma, a scion of Raghu, standing in front of her. (52)

shloka_text:
पक्षी च शाखानिलयं प्रविष्टः
पुनः पुनश्चोत्तमसान्तववादी।
सुस्वागतां वाचमुदीरयाणः
पुनः पुनश्चोदयतीव हृष्टः ॥ ५३ ॥
explanation: “Nay, uttering excellent sweet notes again and again after entering its nest on the branch of a tree, a delighted bird is repeatedly urging Sītā, as it were, to rejoice, uttering, as it did, a note announcing the advent of an auspicious hour.” (53)

shloka_text:
ततः सा हीमती बाला भर्तुर्विजयहर्षिता।
अवोचद् यदि तत् तथ्यं भवेयं शरणं हि वः ॥ ५४ ॥
explanation: Rejoiced at the prospect of her husband's triumph, that shy youthful lady thereupon said, “If that comes out to be true, I shall undoubtedly be your protector.” (54)

The moment Sītā, who was unable to bear the reproaches and threats of the ogresses, endeavours after wailing a good deal to strangle herself to death with the cord used for tying her hair, a propitious omen, never seen before, appears on her person

shloka_text:
सा राक्षसेन्द्रस्य वचो निशम्य
तद् रावणस्याप्रियमप्रियार्ताः।
सीता वितत्रास यथा वनान्ते
सिंहाभिपन्ना गजराजकन्या ॥ १ ॥
explanation: Recalling the aforesaid unpalatable threat of Rāvaṇa, the lord of ogres, the celebrated Sītā, who was already afflicted with separation from her beloved husband, got terrified even as the female calf of a lordly elephant fallen into the clutches of a lion on the edge of a forest. (1)

shloka_text:
सा राक्षसीमध्यगता च भीरु-
वाग्भिर्भूशं रावणतर्जिता च।
कान्तारमध्ये विजने विसृष्टा
बालेव कन्या विललाप सीता ॥ २ ॥
explanation: Encircled by the ogresses and repeatedly intimidated with threats by Rāvaṇa, that timid lady, Sītā, began to wail as follows like a young girl abandoned in the heart of a lonely and thick forest: (2)

shloka_text:
सत्यं बतेदं प्रवदन्ति लोके
नाकालमृत्युर्भवतीति सन्तः।
यत्राहमेवं परिभर्त्स्यमाना
जीवामि यस्मात् क्षणमप्यपुण्या ॥ ३ ॥
explanation: "Truly do the wise affirm that death does not come in the world before the appointed hour, since I, devoid of merit that I am, survive even for a moment, though being reproached unsparingly in this way. (3)

shloka_text:
सुखाद् विहीनं बहुदुःखपूर्ण-
मिदं तु नूनं हृदयं स्थिरं मे।
विदीर्यते यन्न सहस्रधाद्य
वत्राहृतं शृंगमिवाचलस्य ॥ ४ ॥
explanation: "Though bereft of joy and full of great agony, my heart must be hard indeed in that it does not break into a thousand pieces this day like the crest of a mountain struck by lightning. (4)

shloka_text:
नैवास्ति नूनं मम दोषमत्र
वध्याहमस्याप्रियदर्शनस्य ।
भावं न चास्याहमनुप्रदातु-
मलं द्विजो मन्त्रमिवाद्विजाय ॥ ५ ॥
explanation: "Surely no blame whatsoever will attach to me if I give up the ghost at this juncture; for, I stand sentenced to death at the hands of this ogre of odious appearance. In any case, I am unable voluntarily to bestow my affection on him any more than a member of the twice-born classes would impart Vedic knowledge to one not belonging to the twice-born classes. (5)

shloka_text:
तस्मिन्ननागच्छति लोकनाथे
गर्भस्थजन्तोरिव शल्यकृन्तः।
नूनं ममांगान्यचिरादनार्यः
शस्त्रैः शितैश्चेत्स्यति राक्षसेन्द्रः ॥ ६ ॥
explanation: "Even before Śrī Rāma, that ruler of the world, arrives here, the vile Rāvaṇa, the lord of ogres, will as surely cut my limbs to pieces in no time with his sharpened weapons even as a surgeon would cut the limbs of a lifeless foetus in order to facilitate its extraction from the womb under extraordinary circumstances when other contrivances to force it out prove abortive. (6)

shloka_text:
दुःखं बतेदं ननु दुःखिताया
मासौ चिरायाभिगमिष्यतो द्वौ।
बद्धस्य वध्यस्य यथा निशान्ते
राजोपरोधादिव तस्करस्य ॥ ७ ॥
explanation: 140 * VĀLMĪKI-RĀMĀYAṆA * “Alas, it is painful indeed that two months (on the expiry of which I am going to be killed by Rāvaṇa) will before long slip away past me, afflicted for long, even as the night at the end of which a thief, placed in fetters under the detention orders of a king is to be executed, passes away in his cell. (7)

shloka_text:
हा राम हा लक्ष्मण हा सुमित्रे
हा राममातः सह मे जनन्यः।
एषा विपद्याम्यहमल्पभाग्या
महाणवे नौरिव मूढवाता ॥ ८ ॥
explanation: “O Rāma, O Lakṣmaṇa, O Sumitrā, O Kausalyā (Śrī Rāma’s mother) and alongwith these my own mothers too, I, a woman of scanty fortune, am going to perish like a bark caught in a whirlwind in mid-ocean. (8)

shloka_text:
तरस्विनौ धारयता मृगस्य
सत्त्वेन रूपं मनुजेन्द्रपुत्री।
नूनं विशस्तौ मम कारणात् तौ
सिंहर्षभौ द्वाविव वैद्युतेन ॥ ९ ॥
explanation: “Like a pair of excellent lions killed by a stroke of lightning, those two agile princes (Śrī Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa) were undoubtedly killed on my account by the being who had assumed the guise of a deer. (9)

shloka_text:
नूनं स कालो मृगरूपधारी
मामल्पभाग्यां लुलुभे तदानीम्।
यत्रार्यपुत्री विससर्जं मूढा
रामानुजं लक्ष्मणपूर्वजं च ॥ १० ॥
explanation: “It was surely the Time-Spirit, who, having assumed the form of a deer, beguiled me, a woman of scanty fortune that I am, at that time and to whom I, a stupid woman, despatched the two sons of my father-in-law, Lakṣmaṇa, a younger brother of Śrī Rāma, and Śrī Rāma, the eldest brother of Lakṣmaṇa. (10)

shloka_text:
हा राम सत्यव्रत दीर्घबाहो
हा पूर्णचन्द्रप्रतिमानवक्र।
हा जीवलोकस्य हितः प्रियश्च
वध्यां न मां वेत्सि हि राक्षसानाम् ॥ ११ ॥
explanation: “O Śrī Rāma of unfailing vows and long arms, whose countenance resembles the full moon, you, who are friendly to and beloved of the world of living beings, do not actually know me to have been sentenced to death by the king of ogres. (11)

shloka_text:
अनन्यदेवत्वमियं क्षमा च
भूमौ च शय्या नियमश्च धर्मे।
पतिव्रतात्वं विफलं ममेदं
कृतं कृतघ्नेष्विव मानुषाणाम् ॥ १२ ॥
explanation: “My devotion to a single deity in the form of my husband and this forbearance, nay, my reposing on the ground, and my observing rules of righteousness and loyalty to my husband—all this has proved futile like the service rendered by human beings to ungrateful men. (12)

shloka_text:
मोघो हि धर्मश्चरितो ममायं
तथैकपत्नीत्वमिदं निरर्थकम्।
या त्वां न पश्यामि कृशा विवर्णा
हीना त्वया संगमने निराशा ॥ १३ ॥
explanation: “Only in vain has this virtue been practised by me and this exclusive devotion of mine to my husband has also proved futile in that I do not behold you and, separated from you, have grown pale and emaciated and lost all hope of being re-united with you. (13)

shloka_text:
पितुर्निदेशं नियमेन कृत्वा
वनान्निवृत्तश्चरितव्रतश्च ।
स्त्रीभिस्तु मन्ये विपुलेक्षणाभिः
संरस्यसे वीतभयः कृतार्थः ॥ १४ ॥
explanation: “When, having carried out the behest of your father according to rules and completed your vow of fourteen years of ascetic life, you return from the forest, rid of all fear and accomplished of purpose, you for your part will, I believe, revel with many large-eyed women after marrying them. (14)

shloka_text:
अहं तु राम त्वयि जातकामा
चिरं विनाशाय निबद्धभावा।
मोघं चरित्वाथ तपो व्रतं च
त्यक्ष्यामि धिग्जीवितमल्पभाग्याम् ॥ १५ ॥
explanation: * SUNDARAKĀṆḌA * 141 “Having practised austerities and observed holy vows for nothing (as they did not prove effective in reuniting me with you), I for myself, O Śrī Rāma, in whom was aroused a longing for you and whose affection has been fastened in you for long to my mortal agony, I shall presently give up the ghost now. Woe to me of scanty fortune! (15)

shloka_text:
संजीवितं क्षिप्रमहं त्यजेयं
विषेण शस्त्रेण शितेन वापि।
विषस्य दाता न तु मेऽस्ति कश्चि-
च्छस्त्रस्य वा वेश्मनि राक्षसस्य ॥ १६ ॥
explanation: “I would shortly part with my life through poison or even by means of a sharpened weapon. In the abode of Rāvaṇa, an ogre, however, there is none to give me poison or a weapon.” (16)

shloka_text:
शोकाभितप्ता बहुधा विचिन्त्य
सीताथ वेणीग्रथनं गृहीत्वा।
उद्धृदध्य वेण्युदग्रथनेन शीघ्र-
महं गमिष्यामि यमस्य मूलम् ॥ १७ ॥
explanation: Reflecting on various lines and then seizing the string that tied her hair, Sītā, who was tormented with grief, now thought within herself: “Tying my neck with the fillet that ties my braid, I shall proceed to the presence of Yama.” (17)

shloka_text:
उपस्थिता सा मृदुसर्वगात्री
शाखां गृहीत्वा च नगस्य तस्य।
तस्यास्तु रामं परिचिन्तयन्त्या
रामानुजं स्वं च कुलं शुभांगधाः ॥ १८ ॥
तस्या विशोकानि तदा बहूनि
धैर्याजितानि प्रवराणि लोके।
प्रादुर्निमित्तानि तदा बभूवुः
पुरापि सिद्धान्युपलक्षितानि ॥ १९ ॥
explanation: Taking hold of a branch of the aforesaid Śiṁśapā tree, that lady, who was delicate of all limbs, stood near that tree. While that lady of charming limbs was thinking deeply of Śrī Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa as also of her own royal House, many omens—which were well-known in the world as dispellers of grief and restoring confidence, and which had been found by her even before as predictive of success, presently appeared on her person. (18-19)
The omens described. Concluding them to be auspicious, from the thrill that ran through her body at their sight, Sītā experiences great joy

shloka_text:
तथागतां तां व्यथितामनिन्दितां
व्यतीतहर्षां परिदीनमानसाम्।
शुभां निमित्तानि शुभानि भेजिरे
नरं श्रिया जुष्टमिवोपसेविनः ॥ १ ॥
explanation: Like willing attendants flocking round a man favoured by the goddess of fortune, auspicious omens appeared on the person of the aforesaid blessed lady, who, though beyond reproach, was nevertheless agonized, utterly bereft of joy and sore distressed in mind, and had reached the Śiṁśapā tree as aforesaid. (1)

shloka_text:
तस्याः शुभं वाममरालपक्षम्-
राज्यावृतं कृष्णविशालशुक्लम्।
प्रास्पन्दतैकं नयनं सुकेश्या
मीनाहतं पद्ममिवाभिताम्नम् ॥ २ ॥
explanation: 142 * VĀLMĪKI-RĀMĀYAṆA * The charming left eye alone, of that lady of lovely locks—which was screened with rows of slanting eyelashes, was dark in the middle, large and white all round and coppery at the edge—began repeatedly to throb like a lotus struck gently by a fish. (2)

shloka_text:
भुजश्च चार्वञ्चितवृत्तपीनः
परार्धकालागुरुचन्दनार्हः ।
अनुत्तेनमायुषितः प्रियेण
चिरेण वामः समवेपताशु ॥ ३ ॥
explanation: Her charming, graceful, rounded and fleshy left arm too, which deserved to be painted with excellent black aloe and sandalwood paste and had been used for long before this as a pillow by her most excellent darling, Śrī Rāma, at once began to palpitate. (3)

shloka_text:
गजेन्द्रहस्तप्रतिमश्च पीन-
स्तयोर्द्वयोः संहतयोस्तु जातः ।
प्रस्पन्दमानः पुनरूरुस्य
रामं पुरस्तात् स्थितमाचचक्षे ॥ ४ ॥
explanation: Again, of her well-knit thighs, the left one, which was fleshy and beautiful, nay, which resembled the proboscis of a lordly elephant and was visibly throbbing—announced, as it were, the presence of Śrī Rāma standing in front of her. (4)

shloka_text:
शुभं पुनर्हमसमानवर्ण-
मीषद्रजोध्यस्तमिवातुलाक्ष्याः ।
वासः स्थितायाः शिखराग्रदन्त्याः
किंचित् परिश्रंसत चारुगात्र्याः ॥ ५ ॥
explanation: Moreover, the covering of Sītā standing there, of matchless eyes and charming limbs, whose teeth resembled the ends of the seeds of a pomegranate—which was of golden hue and was slightly soiled, as it were, with dust-slipped a bit from her person in a way which augered well for her. (5)

shloka_text:
एतेर्निमित्तैरपरैश्च सुभूः
संचोदिता प्रागपि साधुसिद्धैः ।
वातातपक्लान्तमिव प्रणष्टं
वर्षेण बीजं प्रतिसंजहर्ष ॥ ६ ॥
explanation: Reassured by these and other omens as well, which had come out perfectly true even before, Sītā, of shapely eyelashes, greatly rejoiced even as a seed blighted by the wind and the sun comes back of life through a shower. (6)

shloka_text:
तस्याः पुनर्बिम्बफलोपमोष्टं
स्वक्षिभुकेशान्तमरालपक्षम् ।
वक्त्रं बभासे सितशुक्लदंष्ट्रं
राहोर्मुखाच्चन्द्र इव प्रमुक्तः ॥ ७ ॥
explanation: Again, her countenance with its lips resembling a ripe Bimba fruit in colour and its beautiful eyes, shapely brows, lovely locks, curved eyelashes and set white teeth shone like the full moon released from the mouth of the demon Rāhu. (7)

shloka_text:
सा वीतशोका व्यपनीततन्द्रा
शान्तज्वरा हर्षविबुद्धसत्त्वा ।
अशोभतार्या वदनेन शुक्ले
शीतांशुना रात्रिरिवोदितेन ॥ ८ ॥
explanation: Completely rid of grief, her exhaustion fully relieved, her fever allayed and her mind illumined through joy, the noble lady Sītā looked charming with her countenance as a night with the moon having risen during the bright fortnight. (8)
Weighing the pros and cons of comforting Sītā or remaining mum, now that he had come to know everything about Sītā at first hand, Hanumān decides upon the former course at the psychological moment

shloka_text:
हनुमानपि विक्रान्तः सर्वं शुश्राव तत्त्वतः।
सीतायास्त्रिजटायाश्च राक्षसीनां च तर्जितम् ॥ १ ॥
explanation: The valiant Hanumān too correctly heard everything including the lamentation of Sītā, the dream of Trijāṭā and the threats of the ogresses. (1)

shloka_text:
अवेक्षमाणस्तां देवीं देवतामिव नन्दने।
ततो बहुविधां चिन्तां चिन्तयामास वानरः ॥ २ ॥
explanation: Looking intently on that lady, who resembled a heavenly being in the Nandana grove (forming part of Indra's paradise), Hanumān thereupon indulged in speculation of various kinds. (2)

shloka_text:
यां कपीनां सहस्राणि सुबहून्ययुतानि च।
दिक्षु सर्वासु मार्गन्ते सेयमासादिता मया ॥ ३ ॥
explanation: He said to himself: 'The lady found by me here is the same Sītā whom many thousands, nay, myriads of monkeys have been seeking in all the quarters. (3)

shloka_text:
चारेण तु सुयुक्तेन शत्रोः शक्तिमवेक्षता।
गूढेन चरता तावदवेक्षितमिदं मया ॥ ४ ॥
explanation: 'By me, thoughtfully appointed by my master as a spy and moving about incognito in my attempt to ascertain the enemy's strength, for my part, the following information has been gathered. (4)

shloka_text:
राक्षसानां विशेषश्च पुरी चेयं निरीक्षिता।
राक्षसाधिपतेरस्य प्रभावो रावणस्य च ॥ ५ ॥
explanation: 'The relative position in regard to power and resources of the ogres per se as well as the topography of this city of Laṅkā as also the glory of this Rāvaṇa, the suzerain lord of ogres, has been scrutinized by me. (5)

shloka_text:
यथा तस्याप्रमेयस्य सर्वसत्त्वदयावतः।
समाश्वासयितुं भार्या पतिदर्शनकांक्षिणीम् ॥ ६ ॥
explanation: 'It is opportune for me duly to comfort the spouse, longing to see her husband, of Śrī Rāma, who is immeasurably great and full of compassion for all beings. (6)

shloka_text:
अहमाश्वासयाम्येनां पूर्णचन्द्रनिभाननाम्।
अदृष्टदुःखां दुःखस्य न ह्यन्तमधिगच्छतीम् ॥ ७ ॥
explanation: 'I shall presently console this lady, whose countenance resembles the full moon, who had never experienced sorrow before and yet who is not reaching the end of her suffering. (7)

shloka_text:
यदि ह्यहं सतीमेनां शोकोपहतचेतनाम्।
अनाश्वास्य गमिष्यामि दोषवद् गमनं भवेत् ॥ ८ ॥
explanation: 'If I actually return without reassuring this virtuous lady, whose understanding has been clouded by grief, my departure will be regarded as blameworthy. (8)

shloka_text:
गते हि मयि तत्रेयं राजपुत्री यशस्विनी।
परित्राणमपश्यन्ती जानकी जीवितं त्यजेत् ॥ ९ ॥
explanation: 'Perceiving no means of deliverance from her calamity, when I have actually left for Kīskindhā without meeting her, this illustrious princess, the daughter of Janaka, may yield up her life. (9)

shloka_text:
यथा च स महाबाहुः पूर्णचन्द्रनिभाननः।
समाश्वासयितुं न्याय्यः सीतादर्शनलालसः ॥ १० ॥
explanation: 'Even as the long-armed Śrī Rāma, whose countenance resembles the full moon, and who is equally eager to behold Sītā, deserves to be comforted with the tidings of Sītā, and Sītā too deserves to be comforted with the news of Śrī Rāma. (10)

shloka_text:
निशाचरीणां प्रत्यक्षमक्षमं चाभिभाषितम्।
कथं नु खलु कर्तव्यमिदं कृच्छ्रगतो ह्यहम् ॥ ११ ॥
explanation: 'To speak to her within the sight of the ogresses is, however, not advisable. How, I wonder, can this be actually done? I am really placed in a dilemma. (11)

shloka_text:
अनेन रात्रिशेषेण यदि नाश्वास्यते मया।
सर्वथा नास्ति संदेहः परित्यक्ष्यति जीवितम् ॥ १२ ॥
explanation: 'If by the end of this night she is not restored to confidence by me, she will by all means give up the ghost: there is no doubt about it. (12)

shloka_text:
रामस्तु यदि पृच्छेन्मां किं मां सीताब्रवीद् वचः।
किमहं तं प्रतिब्रूयामसम्भाष्य सुमध्यमाम् ॥ १३ ॥
explanation: 'If Śrī Rāma for his part inquires of me as to what message Sītā gave to me, what reply shall I give to him without having spoken to Sītā of slender waist? (13)

shloka_text:
सीतासंदेशरहितं मामितस्त्वरया गतम्।
निर्दहदपि काकुत्स्थः क्रोधतीव्रेण चक्षुषा ॥ १४ ॥
explanation: 'Śrī Rāma, a scion of Kakutstha, may even consume me with his glance, violent through anger, if I return from this place in haste without taking any message from Sītā. (14)

shloka_text:
यदि वोद्योजयिष्यामि भर्तारं रामकारणात्।
व्यर्थमागमनं तस्य ससैन्यस्य भविष्यति ॥ १५ ॥
explanation: 'Even if I prevail on my master Sugriva to exert himself in the cause of Śrī Rāma, his expedition to Laṅkā with an army will go in vain in that Sītā will have given up the ghost long before his arrival. (15)

shloka_text:
अन्तरं त्वहमासाद्य राक्षसीनामवस्थितः।
शनैराश्वासयाम्यद्य संतापबहुलामिमाम् ॥ १६ ॥
explanation: 'Therefore, snatching some suitable opportunity when the ogresses are inattentive, even though stationed in the midst of the ogresses, I shall this very day slowly console Sītā, who is full of agony. (16)

shloka_text:
अहं ह्यतितनुश्चैव वानरश्च विशेषतः।
वाचं चोदाहरिष्यामि मानुषीमिह संस्कृतम् ॥ १७ ॥
explanation: 'I am indeed not only exceedingly small in size but am a monkey to boot. I shall, however, speak on this occasion the Sanskrit language as spoken by humans. (17)

shloka_text:
यदि वाचं प्रदास्यामि द्विजातिरिव संस्कृतम्।
रावणं मन्यमाना मां सीता भीता भविष्यति ॥ १८ ॥
explanation: 'But If I utter the Sanskrit language like a Brāhmaṇa, Sītā will get frightened thinking me to be Rāvaṇa. (18)

shloka_text:
अवश्यमेव वक्तव्यं मानुषं वाक्यमर्थवत्।
मया सान्त्वयितुं शक्या नान्यथेयमनिन्दिता ॥ १९ ॥
explanation: 'The human language alone as spoken near about Ayodhyā, which will convey my meaning to her, needs must be used by me. This irreproachable lady cannot otherwise be restored to confidence. (19)

shloka_text:
सेयमालोक्य मे रूपं जानकी भाषितं तथा।
रक्षोभिस्त्रासिता पूर्वं भूयस्त्रासमुपैष्यति ॥ २० ॥
explanation: 'Beholding my monkey form and hearing my human speech, however, this celebrated daughter of Janaka, already terrorized by the ogres, will give way to fear all the more. (20)

shloka_text:
ततो जातपरित्रासा शब्दं कुर्यान्मनस्विनी।
जानाना मां विशालाक्षी रावणं कामरूपिणम् ॥ २१ ॥
explanation: 'Seized with terror knowing me to be Rāvaṇa, who is able to change his form at will, the sensitive and large-eyed lady will then raise a cry. (21)

shloka_text:
सीतया च कृते शब्दे सहसा राक्षसीगणः।
नानाप्रहरणो घोरः समेयादन्तकोपमः ॥ २२ ॥
explanation: 'Nay, on a cry being raised by Sītā, the whole host of ogresses, armed with various weapons and terrible as Death, will flock together all at once. (22)

shloka_text:
ततो मां सम्परिक्षिप्य सर्वतो विकृताननाः।
वधे च ग्रहणे चैव कुर्युर्यन्तं महाबलाः ॥ २३ ॥
explanation: 'Surrounding me from all sides, the ogresses of loathsome appearance and endowed with extraordinary might will make an effort to kill or capture me. (23)

shloka_text:
तं मां शाखाः प्रशाखाश्च स्कन्धांश्चोत्तमशाखिनाम्।
दृष्ट्वा च परिधावन्तं भवेयुः परिशङ्किताः ॥ २४ ॥
explanation: ‘Again, they will get alarmed to see me as such leaping on the boughs and branches as well as on the trunks of the tallest trees. (24)

shloka_text:
मम रूपं च सम्प्रेक्ष्य वने विचरतो महत्।
राक्षस्यो भयवित्रस्ता भवेयुर्विकृतस्वराः ॥ २५ ॥
explanation: ‘Nay, sore stricken with terror to perceive my gigantic form even as I move about in the forest, the ogresses will begin to scream in terror. (25)

shloka_text:
ततः कुर्युः समाह्वानं राक्षस्यो रक्षसामपि।
राक्षसेन्द्रनियुक्तानां राक्षसेन्द्रनिवेशने ॥ २६ ॥
explanation: ‘The ogresses will then summon to their aid the ogres too posted on duty by Rāvaṇa, the lord of ogres, at his own palace. (26)

shloka_text:
ते शूलशरनिस्त्रिंशविविधायुधपाणयः।
आपतेयुर्विमर्देऽस्मिन् वेगेनोद्वेगकारणात् ॥ २७ ॥
explanation: ‘Due to excitement in this commotion they will rush with impetuosity taking darts, arrows, swords and various other weapons in hand. (27)

shloka_text:
संरुद्धस्तैस्तु परितो विधमे राक्षसं बलम्।
शक्नुयां न तु सम्प्राप्तुं परं पारं महोदधेः ॥ २८ ॥
explanation: ‘Surrounded on all sides by them, I can no doubt exterminate the army of ogres; but I shall not in that case be able to reach the other end of the ocean. (28)

shloka_text:
मां वा गृह्णीयुरावृत्य बहवः शीघ्रकारिणः।
स्यादियं चागृहीतार्था मम च ग्रहणं भवेत् ॥ २९ ॥
explanation: ‘Or, it is also possible that surrounding me, many agile ogres may capture me. In that case Sītā will remain unacquainted with my mission and my capture too will be effected. (29)

shloka_text:
हिंसाभिरुचयो हिंस्युरिमां वा जनकात्मजाम्।
विपन्नं स्यात् ततः कार्यं रामसुग्रीवयोरिदम् ॥ ३० ॥
explanation: ‘Alternatively, the ogres, who take delight in bloodshed, may dispose of this daughter of Janaka. The present object of Śrī Rāma and Sugrīva will in that case be defeated. (30)

shloka_text:
उद्देशे नष्टमार्गेऽस्मिन् राक्षसैः परिवारिते।
सागरेण परिक्षिप्ते गुप्ते वसति जानकी ॥ ३१ ॥
explanation: ‘Sītā, Janaka’s daughter, lives in this obscure sea-girt region, whose approaches are unknown and which is surrounded by ogres. (31)

shloka_text:
विशस्ते वा गृहीते वा रक्षोभिर्मयि संयुगे।
नान्यं पश्यामि रामस्य सहायं कार्यसाधने ॥ ३२ ॥
explanation: ‘In the event of my being either killed or captured by the ogres in an encounter, I do not find anyone else who can assist Śrī Rāma in accomplishing this task of seeing Sītā and conveying her message to Śrī Rāma. (32)

shloka_text:
विमृशंश्च न पश्यामि यो हते मयि वानरः।
शतयोजनविस्तीर्णं लङ्कयेत महोदधिम् ॥ ३३ ॥
explanation: ‘Even on taxing my brain I do not see any monkey who should be able, when I am dead, to leap across the vast sea a hundred Yojanas (eight-hundred miles) wide. (33)

shloka_text:
कामं हन्तुं समर्थोऽस्मि सहस्राण्यपि रक्षसाम्।
न तु शक्ष्याम्यहं प्राप्तुं परं पारं महोदधेः ॥ ३४ ॥
explanation: ‘Although I am capable of killing thousands of ogres, I shall not, however, be able to reach the other end of the ocean due to exhaustion caused by the combat. (34)

shloka_text:
असत्यानि च युद्धानि संशयो मे न रोचते।
कश्च निःसंशयं कार्यं कुर्यात् प्राज्ञः ससंशयम् ॥ ३५ ॥
explanation: ‘Conflicts are always dubious and uncertainty does not find favour with me. And what wise man would embark on a dubious undertaking without demur? (35)

shloka_text:
एष दोषो महान् हि स्यान्मम सीताभिभाषणे।
प्राणत्यागश्च वैदेह्या भवेदनभिभाषणे ॥ ३६ ॥
explanation: ‘Indeed this will constitute a great error on my part if I openly talk with Sītā. And the death by her own self of Sītā, a princess of the Videha territory, will follow if I do not talk to her. (36)

shloka_text:
भूताश्चार्था विरुध्यन्ति देशकालविरोधिताः ।
विकल्पं दूतमासाद्य तमः सूर्योदये यथा ॥ ३७ ॥
explanation: 'Even as darkness disappears at sunrise, objects which are all but accomplished are completely lost at the hands of a timid or thoughtless messenger when they are set in opposition to time and place. (37)

shloka_text:
अर्थानर्थान्तरे बुद्धिर्निश्चितानि न शोभते ।
घातयन्ति हि कार्याणि दूताः पण्डितमानिनः ॥ ३८ ॥
explanation: 'Even a decision duly arrived at by a ruler in consultation with his ministers regarding what should be done and what should be refrained from, does not yield good results when implemented by a thoughtless messenger. Indeed messengers fancying themselves clever but really not so, bring to nought all undertakings on such occasions. (38)

shloka_text:
न विनश्येत् कथं कार्यं वैक्लव्यं न कथं मम ।
लङ्घनं च समुद्रस्य कथं नु न वृथा भवेत् ॥ ३९ ॥
explanation: 'How should I act to ensure that the purpose may not be frustrated? How should I guard against thoughtlessness? And how, I wonder, should I ensure that my leaping across the sea does not go in vain? (39)

shloka_text:
कथं नु खलु वाक्यं मे शृणुयान्नोद्विजेत च ।
इति संचिन्त्य हनुमांश्चकार मतिमान् मतिम् ॥ ४० ॥
explanation: 'How indeed should I ensure that Sītā listens to my speech and does not get perturbed?' Pondering thus, the wise Hanumān made the following resolve: (40)

shloka_text:
राममक्लिष्टकर्माणं सुबन्धुमनुकीर्तयन् ।
नैनामुद्देजयिष्यामि तद्वन्धुगतचेतनाम् ॥ ४१ ॥
explanation: 'Singing the praises of her praiseworthy spouse, Śrī Rāma of unwearied action, I shall take care not to frighten her, her mind being absorbed in her aforesaid lord. (41)

shloka_text:
इक्ष्वाकूणां वरिष्ठस्य रामस्य विदितात्मनः ।
शुभानि धर्मयुक्तानि वचनानि समर्पयन् ॥ ४२ ॥
श्रावयिष्यामि सर्वाणि मधुरां प्रव्रुवन् गिरम् ।
श्रद्धास्यति यथा सीता तथा सर्वं समादधे ॥ ४३ ॥
explanation: 'Delivering to her the beautiful message, conformable to righteousness, of Śrī Rāma, the foremost of the Ikṣwākus and a knower of the Self, I shall convey it fully, uttering sweet words, and shall make everything so intelligible that Sītā will give credence to it.' (42-43)

shloka_text:
इति स बहुविधं महाप्रभावो
जगतिपतेः प्रमदामवेक्षमाणः ।
मधुरमवितथं जगाद वाक्यं
द्रुमविटपान्तरमास्थितो हनुमान् ॥ ४४ ॥
explanation: Addressing himself to the young wife of Śrī Rāma and remaining seated in the midst of the boughs of the tree occupied by him, the celebrated Hanumān, who was possessed of great valour, made the following variously-worded sweet and truthful speech. (44)

Transported with joy to hear the story commencing from the birth of Śrī Rāma and ending with Hanumān’s espying Sītā, narrated in a human tongue by Hanumān, remaining perched on the Śimśapā tree and casting her eyes all round, Sītā catches sight of Hanumān sitting on a bough of the same Śimśapā tree beneath which she stood

shloka_text:
एवं बहुविधां चिन्तां चिन्तयित्वा महामतिः।
संश्रवे मधुरं वाक्यं वैदेह्या व्याजहार ह॥ १॥
explanation: Having indulged in speculation of various kinds as aforesaid, Hanumān who was endowed with extraordinary intelligence, they say, made the following sweet speech within the hearing of Sītā: (1)

shloka_text:
राजा दशरथो नाम रथकुञ्जरवाजिमान्।
पुण्यशीलो महाकीर्तिरिक्ष्वाकूणां महायशाः॥ २॥
explanation: “In the line of the Ikṣwākus there was a highly illustrious and greatly renowned king named Daśaratha, who was given to meritorious deeds and owned excellent chariots, elephants and horses. (2)

shloka_text:
राजर्षीणां गुणश्रेष्ठस्तपसा चर्षिभिः समः।
चक्रवर्तिकुले जातः पुरंदरसमो बले॥ ३॥
explanation: “Born in a line of universal monarchs, he was the foremost of royal sages in point of virtues, vied with seers in asceticism and was a compeer of Indra, the ruler of gods, in might. (3)

shloka_text:
अहिंसारतिरक्षुद्रो घृणी सत्यपराक्रमः।
मुख्यस्येक्ष्वाकुवंशस्य लक्ष्मीवाँल्लक्ष्मिवर्धनः॥ ४॥
पार्थिवव्यञ्जनैर्युक्तः पृथुश्रीः पार्थिवर्षभः।
पृथिव्यां चतुरन्तायां विश्रुतः सुखदः सुखी॥ ५॥
explanation: “That jewel among monarchs took delight in harmlessness, was magnanimous, compassionate and distinguished by unfailing prowess. He enhanced the glory of the already distinguished line of Ikṣwāku, was full of prosperity, adorned with all the bodily marks, distinguishing a ruler of the earth, was endowed with a vast splendour and well-known all over the earth bounded by the four seas in the four quarters, and was not only happy himself but conferred happiness on others too. (4-5)

shloka_text:
तस्य पुत्रः प्रियो ज्येष्ठस्ताराधिपनिभाननः।
रामो नाम विशेषज्ञः श्रेष्ठः सर्वधनुष्मताम्॥ ६॥
explanation: “His favourite eldest son, whose countenance resembled the full moon, nay, who was skilled in archery and the foremost of all bowmen, was known by the name of Rāma. (6)

shloka_text:
रक्षिता स्वस्य वृत्तस्य स्वजनस्यापि रक्षिता।
रक्षिता जीवलोकस्य धर्मस्य च परंतपः॥ ७॥
explanation: “Śrī Rāma, the scourge of his foes, was a zealous upholder of his own character, the protector also of his own people, nay the protector of the whole world of living beings and the defender of righteousness. (7)

shloka_text:
तस्य सत्याभिसंधस्य वृद्धस्य वचनात् पितुः।
सभार्यः सह च भ्रात्रा वीरः प्रव्रजितो वनम्॥ ८॥
explanation: “In deference to the plighted word (given to his own stepmother) of his aforesaid father, who was aged and true to his promise, the hero, accompanied by his consort and his younger brother, Lakṣmaṇa, proceeded in exile to the forest. (8)

shloka_text:
तेन तत्र महारण्ये मृगयां परिधावता।
राक्षसा निहताः शूरा बहवः कामरूपिणः॥ ९॥
explanation: “By him, while chasing game in that vast forest, were slain many gallant ogres, able to change their form at will. (9)

shloka_text:
जनस्थानवधं श्रुत्वा निहतौ खरदूषणौ।
ततस्त्वमर्षापहता जानकी रावणेन तु ॥ १० ॥
वञ्चयित्वा वने रामं मृगरूपेण मायया।
स मार्गमाणस्तां देवीं रामः सीतामनिन्दिताम् ॥ ११ ॥
आससाद वने मित्रं सुग्रीवं नाम वानरम्।
ततः स वालिनं हत्वा रामः परपुरंजयः ॥ १२ ॥
आयच्छत् कपिराज्यं तु सुग्रीवाय महात्मने।
सुग्रीवेणाभिसंदिष्टा हरयः कामरूपिणः ॥ १३ ॥
दिक्षु सर्वासु तां देवीं विचिन्वन्तः सहस्रशः।
अहं सम्पातिवचनाच्छतयोजनमायतम् ॥ १४ ॥
तस्या हेतोविंशालाक्ष्याः समुद्रं वेगवान् प्लुतः।
यथारूपां यथावर्णां यथालक्ष्मवतीं च ताम् ॥ १५ ॥
अश्लोषं राघवस्याहं सेयमासादिता मया।
विररामेवमुक्त्वा स वाचं वानरपुंगवः ॥ १६ ॥
explanation: "Having put Śrī Rāma off the scent in the forest through one disguised as a deer by recourse to a conjuring trick on hearing of the destruction of Janasthāna (a part of the Daṇḍaka forest inhabited by ogres) as well as of the death of his younger half-brothers, Khara and Dūṣaṇa, Sītā, Janaka's daughter, for her part was then borne away in indignation by Rāvaṇa. While searching for that godlike and irreproachable lady, Sītā, he found in the forest a friend in a monkey named Sugrīva. Having made short work of Vāli, Sugrīva's elder brother, Śrī Rāma, capable of conquering hostile cities, for his part thereupon bestowed the kingship of monkeys on the high-souled Sugrīva. Commanded by Sugrīva, monkeys, capable of changing their form at will, set out in thousands in all the four quarters, searching for that godlike lady, Sītā. Full of impetuosity I took a leap across the sea (streching between the island of Laṅkā and the mainland and), extending to a distance of a hundred Yojanas (or eight hundred miles) at the instance of Sampātī, the king of birds and the elder brother of Jaṭāyu, for the sake of that large-eyed lady. She has been found by me here endowed with a comeliness, complexion and bodily marks similar to those of which I had heard from the mouth of Śrī Rāma, a scion of Raghu." Having delivered the aforesaid speech, that bull among monkeys fell silent. (10—16)

shloka_text:
जानकी चापि तच्छ्रुत्वा विस्मयं परमं गता।
ततः सा वक्रकेशान्ता सुकेशी केशसंवृतम्।
उन्म्य वदनं भीरुः शिशपामन्ववैक्षत ॥ १७ ॥
explanation: Sītā, Janaka's daughter, herself was struck with supreme wonder to hear that speech. Raising her face screened with dishevelled hair, that timid lady with charming curly locks thereupon looked up into the Śīṃśapā tree on which Hanumān was perched. (17)

shloka_text:
निशम्य सीता वचनं कपेश्च
दिशश्च सर्वाः प्रदिशश्च वीक्ष्य।
स्वयं प्रहर्षं परमं जगाम
सर्वात्मना राममनुस्मरन्ती ॥ १८ ॥
explanation: Hearing the monkey's speech and looking inquiringly into all the four quarters as well as into the "intermediate points, Sītā experienced supreme rapture thinking all the time of Śrī Rāma with all her being. (18)

shloka_text:
सा तिर्यगूर्ध्वं च तथा ह्यधस्ता-
निरीक्षमाणा तमचिन्त्यबुद्धिम्।
ददर्श पिंगाधिपतेरमात्यं
वातात्मजं सूर्यमिवोदयस्थम् ॥ १९ ॥
explanation: Glancing from side to side as well as up and down, she espied the aforesaid Hanumān, son of the wind-god, of inconceivable intelligence, a minister of Sugrīva, the suzerain ruler of monkeys, and resembling the sun risen on the eastern sky. (19)

Imagining Hanumān to have been seen in a dream, though actually perceived by her, and believing the sight of a monkey in a dream to be ominous, Sītā becomes anxious about the welfare of Śrī Rāma and others. Then concluding him on other grounds to have been seen in her waking hours, she prays to Brahmā and other gods that the statement of Hanumān may come out to be true

shloka_text:
ततः शाखान्तरे लीनं दृष्ट्वा चलितमानसा।
वेष्टितार्जुनवस्त्रं तं विद्युत्संघातपिंगलम् ॥ १ ॥
explanation: Then, beholding Hanumān, clad in white and tawny like a series of flashes of lightning, concealed under cover of boughs, Sītā felt disturbed in mind. (1)

shloka_text:
सा ददर्श कपिं तत्र प्रश्रितं प्रियवादिनम्।
फुल्लाशोकोत्कराभासं तप्तचामीकरेक्षणम् ॥ २ ॥
explanation: She noticed there a monkey, meek and kind in speech, shining like a cluster of expanded Aśoka flowers and with eyes bright as refined gold. (2)

shloka_text:
साथ दृष्ट्वा हरिश्रेष्ठं विनीतवदवस्थितम्।
मैथिली चिन्तयामास विस्मयं परमं गता ॥ ३ ॥
explanation: Struck with extreme wonder to see Hanumān, the foremost of monkeys, sitting in a humble posture, the aforesaid princess of Mithilā now reflected as follows: (3)

shloka_text:
अहो भीममिदं सत्त्वं वानरस्य दुरासदम्।
दुर्निरीक्ष्यमिदं मत्वा पुनरेव मुमोह सा ॥ ४ ॥
explanation: 'Ah, how terrible is this being of the monkey family!' Nay, regarding it as difficult to approach and hideous to behold, she fainted once more suspecting it to be illusory. (4)

shloka_text:
विललाप भूशं सीता करुणं भयमोहिता।
राम रामेति दुःखार्ता लक्ष्मणेति च भामिनी ॥ ५ ॥
explanation: Distracted with fear and stricken with agony, the lovely Sītā piteously cried again and again: "Rāma ! O Rāma ! O Lakṣmaṇa !" (5)

shloka_text:
रुरोद सहसा सीता मन्दमन्दस्वरा सती।
साथ दृष्ट्वा हरिवरं विनीतवदुपागतम्।
मैथिली चिन्तयामास स्वप्नोऽयमिति भामिनी ॥ ६ ॥
explanation: Nay, the virtuous Sītā fell a-sobbing all at once in faint accents. Seeing Hanumān, the foremost of monkeys, come near in a humble mien in the meantime, the lovely Sītā thought that it must be a dream (6)

shloka_text:
सा वीक्षमाणा पृथुभुग्रवक्त्रं
शाखामृगेन्द्रस्य यथोक्तकारम्।
ददर्श पिंगप्रवरं महार्ह
वातात्मजं बुद्धिमतां वरिष्ठम् ॥ ७ ॥
explanation: Looking round, in order to make sure that the ogresses were not looking at her or at the monkey, she beheld Hanumān, son of the wind-god, a jewel among the monkeys, adored even by the great, the foremost of the wise, who was obedient to Sugrīva (the ruler of monkeys) and who had big jaws, one of which had been broken by means of the thunderbolt hurled by Indra to arrest his progress towards the sun to devour the solar orb. (7)

shloka_text:
सा तं समीक्ष्यैव भूशं विपन्ना
गतासुकल्पेव बभूव सीता।
चिरेण संज्ञां प्रतिलभ्य चैवं
विचिन्तयामास विशालनेत्रा ॥ ८ ॥
explanation: Getting utterly unconscious at the very sight of Hanumān, the aforesaid Sītā became like one lifeless. Nay, regaining consciousness after a long time, the large-eyed lady began to reflect as follows : (8)

shloka_text:
स्वप्नो मयायं विकृतोऽद्य दृष्टः
शास्त्रामृगः शास्त्रगणैर्निषिद्धः ।
स्वस्त्यस्तु रामाय सलक्ष्मणाय
तथा पितुर्मे जनकस्य राज्ञः ॥ ९ ॥
explanation: 'This hideous dream has been seen by me today. The vision of a monkey has been condemned by the scriptures. May good luck attend on Śrī Rāma with Lakṣmaṇa as well as on my father, King Janaka. (9)

shloka_text:
स्वप्नो हि नायं नहि मेऽस्ति निद्रा
शोकेन दुःखेन च पीडितायाः ।
सुखं हि मे नास्ति यतो विहीना
तेनेन्दुपूर्णप्रतिमाननेन ॥ १० ॥
explanation: 'Surely this cannot be a dream; for sleep does not come to me, stricken as I am with grief and sorrow. Nor indeed is there any joy for me, separated as I am from that prince whose countenance resembles the full moon (10)

shloka_text:
रामेति रामेति सदैव बुद्ध्या
विचिन्त्य वाचा ब्रुवती तमेव ।
तस्यानुरूपं च कथां तदर्था-
मेवं प्रपश्यामि तथा शृणोमि ॥ ११ ॥
