explanation: 'Pondering with my mind at all times on the concept conveyed by the word 'Rāma' and speaking of the same Rāma with my tongue, I hear as well a talk corresponding to the same thought and likewise visualize the talk heard by me in conformity with the same theme. (11)

shloka_text:
अहं हि तस्याद्य मनोभवेन
सम्पीडिता तद्गतसर्वभावा ।
विचिन्तयन्ती सततं तमेव
तथैव पश्यामि तथा शृणोमि ॥ १२ ॥
explanation: 'Constantly thinking as I do of him alone, tormented as I am by a longing for him, my whole affection being fastened on him, I likewise behold him and hear of him alone. (12)

shloka_text:
मनोरथः स्यादिति चिन्तयामि
तथापि बुद्ध्यापि वितर्कयामि ।
किं कारणं तस्य हि नास्ति रूपं
सुव्यक्तरूपश्च वदत्ययं माम् ॥ १३ ॥
explanation: 'I speculate that what I am seeing may be a mere image; yet I reflect with my mind as to what can be the cause of this apparition; for a conceptual image has no concrete form, while this monkey appearing before me has a distinct form and is also talking to me. (13)

shloka_text:
नमोऽस्तु वाचस्पतये सवत्रिणे
स्वयम्भुवे चैव हुताशनाय ।
अनेन चोक्तं यदिदं ममाग्रतो
वनौकसा तच्च तथास्तु नान्यथा ॥ १४ ॥
explanation: 'Let my salutation be to Sage Brhaspati (the master of speech) alongwith Indra (who is armed with a thunderbolt), to Brahmā (the self-born creator) as well as to the god of fire (the deity presiding over the organ of speech) ! May all that which has been uttered now in my presence by this monkey (lit., a denizen of the forest) prove true and not otherwise.' (14)

Keen to hear of Sītā's identity from her own lips, even though he had identified her, Hanumān inquires of her whether she was a goddess or anyone else and asks her to disclose her identity in case she was Sītā. In reply to this query Sītā narrates to him her whole life-story ending with her abduction by Rāvaṇa and tells him how Rāvaṇa was going to kill her two months later, and how in the event of her not being delivered from his clutches before that, she has resolved to end her life by herself

shloka_text:
सोऽवतीर्य द्रुमात् तस्माद् विद्रुमप्रतिमाननः।
विनीतवेषः कृपणः प्रणिपत्योपसूत्य च ॥ १ ॥
तामब्रवीन्महातेजा हनूमान् मारुतात्मजः।
शिरस्यञ्जलिमाधाय सीतां मधुरया गिरा ॥ २ ॥
explanation: Slipping down from the aforesaid Śiṁśapā tree, bowing down and approaching Sītā, nay, placing his folded hands on his head, Hanumān, son of the wind-god, whose face resembled coral in hue, who was attired in a humble guise, was endowed with extraordinary energy and appeared distressed at the sight of Sītā's sad plight, spoke to her as follows in gentle tones: (1-2)

shloka_text:
का नु पद्मपलाशाक्षि क्लिष्टकौशेयवासिनि।
द्रुमस्य शाखामालम्ब्य तिष्ठसि त्वमनिन्दिते ॥ ३ ॥
explanation: "Who are you, O irreproachable lady with eyes resembling a lotus petal and clad in a worn silken garment, who stand holding a branch of this tree? (3)

shloka_text:
किमर्थं तव नेत्राभ्यां वारि स्त्रवति शोकजम्।
पुण्डरीकपलाशाभ्यां विप्रकीर्णमिवोदकम् ॥ ४ ॥
explanation: "Wherefore are tears born of grief trickling from your eyes like drops of water falling from a pair of lotus leaves? (4)

shloka_text:
सुराणामसुराणां च नागगन्धर्वरक्षसाम्।
यक्षाणां किंनराणां च का त्वं भवसि शोभने ॥ ५ ॥
explanation: "Who are you among the gods and demons, the Nāgas, Gandharvas and ogres, the Yakṣas or the Kinnaras, O charming one? (5)

shloka_text:
का त्वं भवसि रुद्राणां मरुतां वा वरानने।
वसूनां वा वरारोहे देवता प्रतिभासि मे ॥ ६ ॥
explanation: "Who are you among the eleven Rudras (the gods of destruction), the forty-nine wind-gods and the eight Vasus, O lady of exquisite features? For, to me you appear to be a goddess, a lady of excellent limbs! (6)

shloka_text:
किं नु चन्द्रमसा हीना पतिता विबुधालयात्।
रोहिणी ज्योतिषां श्रेष्ठा श्रेष्ठा सर्वगुणाधिकार् ॥ ७ ॥
explanation: "Or, are you Rohini, the foremost of lunar mansions and superior in all excellent virtues, separated from the moon and fallen from heaven, the abode of celestials? (7)

shloka_text:
कोपाद् वा यदि वा मोहाद् भर्तारमसितेक्षणे।
वसिष्ठं कोपयित्वा त्वं वासि कल्याणंरुन्धती ॥ ८ ॥
explanation: "Or, are you, O dark-eyed one, the blessed Arundhati, fallen from the heavenly world on having angered your husband, Sage Vasiṣṭha, through resentment or error? (8)

shloka_text:
को नु पुत्रः पिता भ्राता भर्ता वा ते सुमध्यमे।
अस्माल्लोकादमुं लोकं गतं त्वमनुशोचसि ॥ ९ ॥
explanation: "Who is it, your son, father, brother or husband, O lady with slender waist, for whom, departed from this world, to the other you are grieving? (9)

shloka_text:
रोदनादतिनिःश्वासाद् भूमिसंस्पर्शनादपि।
न त्वां देवीमहं मन्ये राज्ञः संज्ञावधारणात् ॥ १० ॥
explanation: “From your crying, drawing deep and audible breaths, touching the ground and taking the name of a king, I do not consider you to be a goddess. (10)

shloka_text:
व्यञ्जनानि हि ते यानि लक्षणानि च लक्षये।
महिषी भूमिपालस्य राजकन्या च मे मता ॥ ११ ॥
explanation: “Indeed, on the strength of the limbs of your body as well as from the marks on your person which I perceive, you are believed by me to be the consort of a ruler of the earth and the daughter of a king. (11)

shloka_text:
रावणेन जनस्थानाद् बलात् प्रमथिता यदि।
सीता त्वमसि भद्रं ते तन्ममाचक्ष्व पृच्छतः ॥ १२ ॥
explanation: “If you are Sītā, stolen away forcibly by Rāvaṇa from Janasthāna, kindly reveal it to me, who am inquisitive about it. May prosperity attend on you! (12)

shloka_text:
यथा हि तव वै दैन्यं रूपं चाप्यतिमानुषम्।
तपसा चान्वितो वेषस्त्वं राममहिषी ध्रुवम् ॥ १३ ॥
explanation: “Indeed, the sad plight, the ethereal beauty and the garb marked with asceticism, the like of which are seen in you, lead me to conclude that you are undoubtedly the consort of Śrī Rāma.” (13)

shloka_text:
सा तस्य वचनं श्रुत्वा रामकीर्तनहर्षिता।
उवाच वाक्यं वैदेही हनूमन्तं दुमाश्रितम् ॥ १४ ॥
explanation: Delighted at the mention of Śrī Rāma on hearing the utterance of the monkey, that princess of the Videha territory spoke as follows to Hanumān standing beneath the tree: (14)

shloka_text:
पृथिव्यां राजसिंहानां मुख्यस्य विदितात्मनः।
स्नुषा दशरथस्याहं शत्रुसैन्यप्रणाशिनः ॥ १५ ॥
explanation: “I am daughter-in-law of Daśaratha, the foremost of lions among kings on earth, who is a knower of the Self and the exterminator of hostile forces. (15)

shloka_text:
दुहिता जनकस्याहं वैदेहस्य महात्मनः।
सीतेति नाम्ना चोक्ताहं भार्या रामस्य धीमतः ॥ १६ ॥
explanation: “Nay, I am a daughter of the high-souled King Janaka, ruler of the Videha territory, and the consort of the wise Śrī Rāma, and I am called by the name of Sītā. (16)

shloka_text:
समा द्वादश तत्राहं राघवस्य निवेशने।
भुञ्जाना मानुषान् भोगान् सर्वकामसमृद्धिनी ॥ १७ ॥
explanation: “Enjoying human luxuries and endowed with an abundance of all enjoyments, I dwelt in the well-known abode of Śrī Rāma, a scion of Raghu, for twelve years. (17)

shloka_text:
ततस्त्रयोदशे वर्षे राज्ये चेश्वाकुनन्दनम्।
अभिषेचयितुं राजा सोपाध्यायः प्रचक्रमे ॥ १८ ॥
explanation: “Then in the thirteenth year the king with his preceptor Sage Vasiṣṭha proceeded to install Śrī Rāma, the delight of the Ikṣwākus, on the throne as Prince Regent. (18)

shloka_text:
तस्मिन् सम्भ्रियमाणे तु राघवस्याभिषेचने।
कैकेयी नाम भर्तारमिदं वचनमब्रवीत् ॥ १९ ॥
explanation: “While preparations for the said installation as Prince Regent of Śrī Rāma, a scion of Raghu, were being carried on, Kaikeyi (a stepmother of Śrī Rāma), they say, spoke as follows to her husband: (19)

shloka_text:
न पिबेयं न खादेयं प्रत्यहं मम भोजनम्।
एष मे जीवितस्यान्तो रामो यद्यभिषिच्यते ॥ २० ॥
explanation: “I shall no longer drink nor partake of my repast from day to day. Nay, this installation will prove to be the end of my existence if Rāma is installed on the throne. (20)

shloka_text:
यत् तदुक्तं त्वया वाक्यं प्रीत्या नृपतिसत्तम।
तच्चेन्न वितथं कार्यं वनं गच्छतु राघवः ॥ २१ ॥
explanation: “If that well-known pledge which was lovingly given by you, O jewel among the protectors of men, is not going to be dishonoured, let Rāma, a scion of Raghu, proceed to the forest.” (21)

shloka_text:
स राजा सत्यवाग् देव्या वरदानमनुस्मरन्।
मुमोह वचनं श्रुत्वा कैकेय्याः क्रूरमप्रियम् ॥ २२ ॥
explanation: * SUNDARAKĀṆḌA * 153 “Recalling the dual boon granted by him long before in favour of the queen Kaikeyi, the aforesaid king, who was true to his word, fainted on hearing the cruel and unpalatable demand of Kaikeyi. (22)

shloka_text:
ततस्तं स्थविरो राजा सत्यधर्मं व्यवस्थितः।
ज्येष्ठं यशस्विनं पुत्रं रुदन् राज्यमयाचत ॥ २३ ॥
explanation: “Then on regaining consciousness the aged king, who stood firmly by the vow of truthfulness, begged the sovereignty of Ayodhyā, in favour of Bharata, of his aforesaid eldest and illustrious son, Śrī Rāma. (23)

shloka_text:
स पितुर्वचनं श्रीमानभिषेकात् परं प्रियम्।
मनसा पूर्वमासाद्य वाचा प्रतिगृहीतवान् ॥ २४ ॥
explanation: “Having bowed first with his mind to the command of his father, which was dearer to him than his own installation on the throne as Prince Regent, the glorious Śrī Rāma accepted it with his words. (24)

shloka_text:
दद्यात्र प्रतिगृहीयात् सत्यं ब्रूयात्र चानृतम्।
अपि जीवितहेतोर्हि रामः सत्यपराक्रमः ॥ २५ ॥
explanation: “Śrī Rāma of unfailing prowess would only give and not accept gifts. He would speak the truth and never utter a falsehood even for his life. (25)

shloka_text:
स विहायोत्तरीयाणि महाहाणि महायशाः।
विसृज्य मनसा राज्यं जनन्यै मां समादिशत् ॥ २६ ॥
explanation: “Casting off his costly upper garments and renouncing the kingdom with his mind, that highly illustrious prince gave me into his mother's keeping. (26)

shloka_text:
साहं तस्याग्रतस्तूर्णं प्रस्थिता वनचारिणी।
नहि मे तेन हीनाया वासः स्वर्गेऽपि रोचते ॥ २७ ॥
explanation: “Resolved to range in the forest with my husband, I, however, immediately marched to the forest in front of him; for living apart from him even in heaven would not find favour with me. (27)

shloka_text:
प्रागेव तु महाभागः सौमित्रिर्मित्रनन्दनः।
पूर्वजस्यानुयात्रार्थं कुशचीररलंकृतः ॥ २८ ॥
explanation: “Clad in robes of Kuśa grass and tattered clothes, the highly fortunate Lakṣmaṇa (son of Sumitrā) too, the delight of his friends, got ready to accompany his eldest brother even before me. (28)

shloka_text:
ते वयं भर्तुरादेशं बहुमान्य दृढव्रताः।
प्रविष्टाः स्म पुरादृष्टं वनं गम्भीरदर्शनम् ॥ २९ ॥
explanation: “Highly respecting the command of our lord, and steadfast in our vows, we the aforesaid three penetrated deep into the forest, which had never been seen by us before and which was dreadful to look at. (29)

shloka_text:
वसतो दण्डकारण्ये तस्याहममितौजसः।
रक्षसापहता भार्या रावणेन दुरात्मना ॥ ३० ॥
explanation: “The consort of the aforesaid prince, who is endowed with immense strength, I was borne away, while the latter was sojourning in the Daṇḍaka forest, by the evil-minded ogre, Rāvaṇa. (30)

shloka_text:
द्वौ मासौ तेन मे कालो जीवितानुग्रहः कृतः।
ऊर्ध्वं द्वाभ्यां तु मासाभ्यां ततस्त्यक्ष्यामि जीवितम् ॥ ३१ ॥
explanation: “A period of two months has been allowed to me by him to live on sufferance. After the said two months, however, I shall give up the ghost.” (31)

Inferring from the suitable reply to his queries received from Sītā and the trust reposed in him by the latter, Hanumān reveals to her the role of an envoy allotted to him by Śrī Rāma and repeat the inquiries made by the two brothers about her welfare. Taking him to be Rāvaṇa disguised as a monkey, Sītā, on the other hand, reproaches him when the latter approaches her in order to bow down at her feet. In order to allay her fears, Hanumān for his part discloses to her his reality as a minister of Sugrīva as well as requests her to give credence to his words

shloka_text:
तस्यास्तद् वचनं श्रुत्वा हनूमान् हरिपुंगवः।
दुःखाद् दुःखाभिभूतायाः सान्त्वमुत्तरमब्रवीत् ॥ १ ॥
explanation: Hearing the aforesaid speech of Sītā, who was overwhelmed with sorrow after sorrow, Hanumān, the foremost of monkeys, uttered the following reassuring reply : (1)

shloka_text:
अहं रामस्य संदेशाद् देवि दूतस्तवागतः।
वैदेहि कुशली रामः स त्वां कौशलमब्रवीत् ॥ २ ॥
explanation: "I have sought your presence, O godlike lady, as an envoy carrying a message sent by Śrī Rāma. Śrī Rāma, O princess of the Videha territory, is doing well. He has communicated his own welfare to you. (2)

shloka_text:
यो ब्राह्ममस्त्रं वेदांश्च वेद वेदविदां वरः।
स त्वां दाशरथी रामो देवि कौशलमब्रवीत् ॥ ३ ॥
explanation: "Nay, Śrī Rāma, the celebrated son of Daśaratha, and the foremost of the knowers of Veda, who knows the use of the mystic missile presided over by Brahmā, the creator, as well as the import of the Vedas, O godlike lady, has also inquired of you about your own welfare. (3)

shloka_text:
लक्ष्मणश्च महातेजा भर्तुस्तेऽनुचरः प्रियः।
कृतवाञ्छोकसंतप्तः शिरसा तेऽभिवादनम् ॥ ४ ॥
explanation: "Endowed with extraordinary energy, Lakṣamaṇa too, a beloved servant of your husband, has saluted you with his head bent low, tormented as he is with grief." (4)

shloka_text:
सा तयोः कुशलं देवी निशम्य नरसिंहयोः।
प्रतिसंहृष्टसर्वांगी हनूमन्तमथाब्रवीत् ॥ ५ ॥
explanation: Thrilled all over her body to hear about the welfare of those two lions among men, that godlike lady now replied as follows to Hanumān : (5)

shloka_text:
कल्याणी बत गाथेयं लौकिकी प्रतिभाति मा।
एति जीवन्तमानन्दो नरं वर्षशतादपि ॥ ६ ॥
explanation: "Ah, the following popular adage that 'joy comes to a surviving man, even though it be at the end of a hundred years', appears true to me." (6)

shloka_text:
तयोः समागमे तस्मिन् प्रीतिरुत्पादिताद्भूता।
परस्परेण चालापं विश्वस्तौ तौ प्रचक्रतुः ॥ ७ ॥
explanation: Consequent on that meeting of Hanumān and Sītā, a strange delight came over them. And restored to confidence, the two began to converse with one another. (7)

shloka_text:
तस्यास्तद् वचनं श्रुत्वा हनूमान् मारुतात्मजः।
सीतायाः शोकतस्रायाः समीपमुपचक्रमे ॥ ८ ॥
explanation: Hearing the aforesaid reply of Sītā, who was stricken with grief, Hanumān, son of the wind-god, endeavoured to draw nearer to her. (8)

shloka_text:
यथा यथा समीपं स हनूमानुपसर्पति।
तथा तथा रावणं सा तं सीता परिशङ्कृते ॥ ९ ॥
explanation: The nearer did the celebrated Hanumān draw to her, the more did that Sītā suspect him to be Rāvaṇa. (9)

shloka_text:
अहो धिग् धिक्कृतमिदं कथितं हि यदस्य मे।
रूपान्तरमुपागम्य स एवायं हि रावणः ॥ १० ॥
explanation: She said to herself : 'Oh, shame ! What a pity that I held all this converse with him. Indeed, he is the same Rāvaṇa, who has come here assuming another guise.' (10)

shloka_text:
तामशोकस्य शाखां तु विमुक्त्वा शोककर्षिता।
तस्यामेवानवद्याङ्गी धरण्यां समुपाविशत् ॥ ११ ॥
explanation: Letting go that branch of the Aśoka tree, Sītā, for her part, of faultless limbs, sank down on that very spot on which she stood, exhausted as she was from grief. (11)

shloka_text:
अवन्दत महाबाहुस्ततस्तां जनकात्मजाम्।
सा चैनं भयसंत्रस्ता भूयो नैनमुदैक्षत ॥ १२ ॥
explanation: Thereupon Hanumān of mighty arms saluted the aforesaid daughter of Janaka. Sore stricken as she was with fear, Sītā, however, no longer raised her eyes to him. (12)

shloka_text:
तं दृष्ट्वा वन्दमानं च सीता शशिनिभानना।
अब्रवीद् दीर्घमुच्छ्रुस्य वानरं मधुरस्वरा ॥ १३ ॥
explanation: Drawing a deep audible breath on seeing him while bowing down to her, Sītā, however, whose countenance resembled the full moon, spoke to Hanumān in sweet accents as follows : (13)

shloka_text:
मायां प्रविष्टो मायावी यदि त्वं रावणः स्वयम्।
उत्पादयसि मे भूयः संतापं तत्र शोभनम् ॥ १४ ॥
explanation: "If you are Rāvaṇa himself, given to conjuring tricks and, having entered a deceitful form, are causing agony to me once more, it is not good. (14)

shloka_text:
स्वं परित्यज्य रूपं यः परिव्राजकरूपवान्।
जनस्थाने मया दृष्टस्त्वं स एव हि रावणः ॥ १५ ॥
explanation: "Surely you are the same Rāvaṇa, who, having assumed the guise of a vagrant recluse, abandoning your native form, were seen by me in Janasthāna. (15)

shloka_text:
उपवासकृशां दीनां कामरूप निशाचर।
संतापयसि मां भूयः संतापं तत्र शोभनम् ॥ १६ ॥
explanation: "It is not right, O ranger of the night, able to change form at will, that you should once more torment me, emaciated through fasting and miserable as I am. (16)

shloka_text:
अथवा नैतदेवं हि यन्मया परिशङ्कितम्।
मनसो हि मम प्रीतिरुत्पन्ना तव दर्शनात् ॥ १७ ॥
explanation: "Or, that which is feared by me may not at all be true; for delight has sprung up in my heart at your sight. (17)

shloka_text:
यदि रामस्य दूतस्त्वमागतो भद्रमस्तु ते।
पृच्छामि त्वां हरिश्रेष्ठ प्रिया रामकथा हि मे ॥ १८ ॥
explanation: "If, on the other hand, you have really come as a messenger of Śrī Rāma, may good betide you. In that case I make inquiries of you about Śrī Rāma; for talk about Śrī Rāma is pleasing to me, O jewel among the monkeys ! (18)

shloka_text:
गुणान् रामस्य कथय प्रियस्य मम वानर।
चित्तं हरसि मे सौम्य नदीकूलं यथा रयः ॥ १९ ॥
explanation: "Recount the virtues of my beloved Śrī Rāma, O gentle monkey ! Even as the current of a river wears away its bank, you are luring my mind with the prospect of delighting me with the news of Śrī Rāma. (19)

shloka_text:
अहो स्वप्नस्य सुखता याहमेव चिराहता।
प्रेषितं नाम पश्यामि राघवेण वनौकसम् ॥ २० ॥
explanation: "Oh the sweetness of the dream presented to me, in which the selfsame I, who was borne away by Rāvaṇa long since, see with my own eyes a monkey sent by Śrī Rāma, a scion of Raghu ! (20)

shloka_text:
स्वप्नेऽपि यद्यहं वीरं राघवं सहलक्ष्मणम्।
पश्येयं नावसीदेयं स्वप्नोऽपि मम मत्सरी ॥ २१ ॥
explanation: "If I could see the heroic Śrī Rāma accompanied by Lakṣmaṇa, even in a dream, I would not feel disheartened; but even a dream is proving niggardly in my case. (21)

shloka_text:
नाहं स्वप्नमिमं मन्ये स्वप्ने दृष्ट्वा हि वानरम्।
न शक्योऽभ्युदयः प्राप्तुं प्राप्तश्चाभ्युदयो मम ॥ २२ ॥
explanation: "I do not believe this to be a dream; for good fortune cannot be attained on seeing a 156 * VĀLMĪKI-RĀMĀYAṆA * monkey in a dream; while placidity of mind, which is a harbinger of good fortune, has been attained by me. (22)

shloka_text:
किं नु स्याच्चित्तमोहोऽयं भवेद् वातगतिस्त्वयम्।
उन्मादजो विकारो वा स्यादयं मृगतृष्णिका ॥ २३ ॥
explanation: “Can this meeting of mine with a monkey be a delusion of my mind? Or, it may be a delusion caused by my being possessed by a ghost (clothed with an aerial body). Or, again, it may be a malady born of insanity or it may only be an optic illusion. (23)

shloka_text:
अथवा नायमुन्मादो मोहोऽप्युन्मादलक्षणः।
सम्बुद्धे चाहमात्मानमिमं चापि वनौकसम् ॥ २४ ॥
explanation: “Or this may not be a case of insanity, nor even delusion showing symptoms similar to those of insanity; for I am conscious of my own self as well as of this monkey.” (24)

shloka_text:
इत्येवं बहुधा सीता सम्प्रधार्य बलाबलम्।
रक्षसां कामरूपत्वान्मेने तं राक्षसाधिपम् ॥ २५ ॥
explanation: Having thus duly considered in many ways the strength of ogres and the weakness of monkeys, who cannot be expected to leap across a vast sea, and also considering the fact that the ogres are able to change their form at will, Sītā concluded Hanumān to be Rāvaṇa, the suzerain ruler of ogres. (25)

shloka_text:
एतां बुद्धिं तदा कृत्वा सीता सा तनुमध्यमा।
न प्रतियोजहाराथ वानरं जनकात्मजा ॥ २६ ॥
explanation: Having arrived at this conclusion at that time, that lady of slender waist, Sītā, Janaka's daughter, did not speak any more to the monkey, Hanumān. (26)

shloka_text:
सीताया निश्चितं बुद्ध्वा हनुमान् मारुतात्मजः।
श्रोत्रानुकूलैर्वचनेस्तदा तां सम्प्रहर्षयन् ॥ २७ ॥
explanation: Coming to know the decision of Sītā, Hanumān, sprung from the loins of the wind-god, spoke as follows bringing excessive joy to her with his words, which were delightful to the ear: (27)

shloka_text:
आदित्य इव तेजस्वी लोककान्तः शशी यथा।
राजा सर्वस्य लोकस्य देवो वैश्रवणो यथा ॥ २८ ॥
explanation: “Glorious as the sun, nay, beloved of the world as the moon, Śrī Rāma brings delight to the entire universe by bestowing riches and food grains on all as the god Kubera, son of Sage Viśravā. (28)

shloka_text:
विक्रमेणोपपन्नश्च यथा विष्णुर्महायशाः।
सत्यवादी मधुरवाग् देवो वाचस्पतिर्यथा ॥ २९ ॥
explanation: “He is endowed with prowess like the highly illustrious Lord Viṣṇu and utters truthful and sweet words like the celestial sage Bṛhaspati. (29)

shloka_text:
रूपवान् सुभगः श्रीमान् कंदर्प इव मूर्तिमान्।
स्थानक्रोधे प्रहर्ता च श्रेष्ठो लोके महारथः ॥ ३० ॥
explanation: “He is rich in comeliness, graceful and full of splendour as Love-incarnate. He punishes only him who deserves anger and is the foremost chariot-warrior in the world. (30)

shloka_text:
बाहुच्छायामवष्टब्धो यस्य लोको महात्मनः।
अपक्रम्याश्रमपदान्मृगरूपेण राघवम् ॥ ३१ ॥
शून्ये येनापनीतासि तस्य द्रक्ष्यसि तत्फलम्।
अचिराद् रावणं संख्ये यो वधिष्यति वीर्यवान् ॥ ३२ ॥
क्रोधप्रमुक्तैरिषुभिर्जलद्भिरिव पावकैः।
तेनाहं प्रेषितो दूतस्त्वत्सकाशमिहागतः ॥ ३३ ॥
explanation: “The whole world depends on the protection of the arms of that exalted soul. You will see for yourself the consequence of the sinful act of Rāvaṇa, by whom you were borne away in a state of utter desolation after diverting Śrī Rāma, a scion of Raghu, from the site of his hermitage through an ogre disguised as a deer. I have sought your presence here as an envoy despatched by that powerful prince, who will before long kill Rāvaṇa in a combat with his shafts, resembling blazing flames and shot in anger. (31—33)

shloka_text:
त्वद्वियोगेन दुःखार्तः स त्वां कौशलमब्रवीत्।
लक्ष्मणश्च महातेजाः सुमित्रानन्दवर्धनः ॥ ३४ ॥
अभिवाद्य महाबाहुः स त्वां कौशलमब्रवीत्।
रामस्य च सखा देवि सुग्रीवो नाम वानरः ॥ ३५ ॥
राजा वानरमुख्यानां स त्वां कौशलमब्रवीत्।
नित्यं स्मरति ते रामः ससुग्रीवः सलक्ष्मणः ॥ ३६ ॥
explanation: * SUNDARAKĀṆḌA * 157 “Stricken with agony caused by separation from you, he has made inquiries of you about your welfare. Greeting you, the mighty-armed and celebrated Lakṣmaṇa, the enhancer of Sumitrā’s joy, who is endowed with extraordinary energy, has also made inquiries of you about your welfare. Śrī Rāma’s friend, the celebrated monkey, named Sugrīva, the ruler of the foremost of monkeys, has also made inquiries of you about your welfare, O godlike lady! Śrī Rāma, along with Sugrīva and Lakṣmaṇa, always remember you. (34—36)

shloka_text:
दिष्ट्या जीवसि वैदेहि राक्षसीवशमागता।
नचिराद् द्रक्ष्यसे रामं लक्ष्मणं च महारथम् ॥ ३७ ॥
मध्ये वानरकोटीनां सुग्रीवं चामितौजसम्।
अहं सुग्रीवसचिवो हनुमान् नाम वानरः ॥ ३८ ॥
explanation: “By good luck, O princess of the Videha territory, you survive, though fallen into the clutches of ogresses. Before long you will see Śrī Rāma and the great chariot-warrior, Lakṣmaṇa, as also Sugrīva of immeasurable strength in the midst of crores of other monkeys. I am a monkey named Hanumān, a minister of Sugrīva. (37-38)

shloka_text:
प्रविष्टो नगरीं लङ्कां लङ्कयित्वा महोदधिम्।
कृत्वा मूर्ध्नि पदन्यासं रावणस्य दुरात्मनः ॥ ३९ ॥
explanation: “Having leapt across the vast sea dividing the mainland from Laṅkā, I penetrated deep into the city of Laṅkā, setting my foot, as it were, on the head of the evil-minded Rāvaṇa. (39)

shloka_text:
त्वां द्रष्टुमुपयातोऽहं समाश्रित्य पराक्रमम्।
नाहमस्मि तथा देवि यथा मामवगच्छसि।
विशङ्का त्यज्यतामेषा श्रद्धत्स्व वदतो मम ॥ ४० ॥
explanation: “Relying on my own prowess I have come to see you. I am not what you suppose me to be, O godlike lady! Let this misgiving be shaken off and, pray, believe my words as I speak.” (40)

Questioned by Sītā, who was anxious to ascertain the bonafides of the monkey, Hanumān, after cataloguing the marks on the person of Śrī Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, narrates his own life-story from his birth onwards including his role as a minister of Sugrīva, and ending with his seeing of Sītā Hearing the aforesaid story of Śrī Rāma from the lips of Hanumān, the foremost of monkeys, Sītā, a princess of the Videha territory, for her part spoke the following reassuring words in sweet accents: (1)

shloka_text:
तां तु रामकथां श्रुत्वा वैदेही वानरर्षभात्।
उवाच वचनं सान्त्वमिदं मधुरया गिरा ॥ १ ॥
क्व ते रामेण संसर्गः कथं जानासि लक्ष्मणम्।
वानराणां नराणां च कथमासीत् समागमः ॥ २ ॥
explanation: “Where did your contact with Śrī Rāma come about and how do you know Lakṣmaṇa? And how did a meeting take place between monkeys and human beings? (2)

shloka_text:
यानि रामस्य चिह्नानि लक्ष्मणस्य च वानर।
तानि भूयः समाचक्ष्व न मां शोकः समाविशेत् ॥ ३ ॥
explanation: 158 * VĀLMĪKI-RĀMĀYAṆA * “Describe in detail once more those distinctive marks which exist on the person of Śrī Rāma as well as on that of Lakṣmaṇa, O Hanumān, so that grief may not take possession of me. (3)

shloka_text:
कीदृशं तस्य संस्थानं रूपं तस्य च कीदृशम्।
कथमूरु कथं बाहू लक्ष्मणस्य च शंस मे ॥ ४ ॥
explanation: “Tell me what the shape and form of Śrī Rāma as well as of Lakṣmaṇa are like. What are their thighs and arms like?” (4)

shloka_text:
एवमुक्तस्तु वैदेह्या हनुमान् मारुतात्मजः।
ततो रामं यथातत्त्वमाख्यातुमुपचक्रमे ॥ ५ ॥
explanation: Questioned thus by Sītā, Hanumān, sprung from the loins of the wind-god, for his part forthwith proceeded to describe Śrī Rāma in accordance with facts as follows: (5)

shloka_text:
जानन्ती बत दिष्ट्या मां वैदेहि परिपृच्छसि।
भर्तुः कमलपत्राक्षि संस्थानं लक्ष्मणस्य च ॥ ६ ॥
explanation: He said: “Luckily enough for me, O princess of the Videha territory, whose eyes resemble a lotus petal, you inquire in detail of me about the disposition of limbs of your husband as well as of Lakṣmaṇa, even though knowing them. (6)

shloka_text:
यानि रामस्य चिह्नानि लक्ष्मणस्य च यानि वै।
लक्षितानि विशालाक्षि वदतः शृणु तानि मे ॥ ७ ॥
explanation: “Hear from me even as I speak, O large-eyed lady, of those distinctive marks which have been actually noticed by me on the person of Śrī Rāma as well as on that of Lakṣmaṇa. (7)

shloka_text:
रामः कमलपत्राक्षः पूर्णचन्द्रनिभाननः।
रूपदाक्षिण्यसम्पन्नः प्रसूतो जनकात्मजे ॥ ८ ॥
explanation: “Śrī Rāma has eyes resembling a lotus petal; his countenance resembles the full moon, O daughter of Janaka ! He is richly endowed with charm and generosity from his birth. (8)

shloka_text:
तेजसाऽऽदित्यसंकाशः क्षमया पृथिवीसमः।
बृहस्पतिसमो बुद्ध्या यशसा वासवोपमः ॥ ९ ॥
explanation: “He vies with the sun in effulgence, with the earth in forbearance, with sage Bṛhaspati, the preceptor of gods, in intelligence and with Indra in renown. (9)

shloka_text:
रक्षिता जीवलोकस्य स्वजनस्य च रक्षिता।
रक्षिता स्वस्य वृत्तस्य धर्मस्य च परंतपः ॥ १० ॥
explanation: “He is a protector of the entire world of living beings as well as of his own people. Nay, he guards his own character and is a vindicator of virtue and the scourge of his enemies. (10)

shloka_text:
रामो भामिनि लोकस्य चातुर्वर्ण्यस्य रक्षिता।
मर्यादानां च लोकस्य कर्ता कारयिता च सः ॥ ११ ॥
explanation: “Śrī Rāma, O lovely lady, is a protector of the world and the preserver of the four grades of society. Nay, as the Creator and Protector of the universe, he has fixed the bounds of propriety to be observed by the people and has inspired the Ṛṣis and others to do so. (11)

shloka_text:
अचिष्मानर्चितोऽत्यर्थं ब्रह्मचर्यव्रते स्थितः।
साधूनामुपकारज्ञः प्रचारज्ञश्च कर्मणाम् ॥ १२ ॥
explanation: “He is full of splendour and is greatly adored by all and is steadfast in his vow of chastity. He is keenly alive to the services of holy men and knows how to popularize right actions. (12)

shloka_text:
राजनीत्यां विनीतश्च ब्राह्मणानामुपासकः।
ज्ञानवान् शीलसम्पन्नो विनीतश्च परंतपः ॥ १३ ॥
explanation: “He is well-versed in politics and a worshipper of Brāhmaṇas, is full of wisdom and richly endowed with amiability, has subdued his passions and is the torment of his foes. (13)

shloka_text:
यजुर्वेदविनीतश्च वेदविद्भिः सुपूजितः।
धनुर्वेदे च वेदे च वेदाङ्गेषु च निष्ठितः ॥ १४ ॥
explanation: “He is well-versed in Yajurveda and is highly respected by the knowers of Veda. He is highly proficient in the science of archery as well as in the Vedas as also in the sciences auxiliary to the Vedas. (14)

shloka_text:
विपुलांसो महाबाहुः कम्बुग्रीवः शुभाननः।
गूढजत्रुः सुताम्राक्षो रामो नाम जनैः श्रुतः ॥ १५ ॥
explanation: “He has broad shoulders, mighty-arms, a conch-shaped neck, a charming countenance and coppery eyes; he has his clavicle concealed behind muscles and is known by the people by the name of Rāma. (15)

shloka_text:
दुन्दुभिस्वननिर्घोषः स्निग्धवर्णः प्रतापवान्।
समश्च सुविभक्ताङ्गो वर्णं श्यामं समाश्रितः ॥ १६ ॥
explanation: “He has a voice deep like the sound of a kettledrum and a glossy skin, is full of glory, square-built and of well-proportioned limbs and is endowed with a dark-brown complexion. (16)

shloka_text:
त्रिस्थिरस्त्रिप्रलम्बश्च त्रिसमस्त्रिषु चोन्नतः।
त्रिताम्रस्त्रिषु च स्निग्धो गम्भीरस्त्रिषु नित्यशः ॥ १७ ॥
त्रिवलीमांस्त्यवनतश्चतुर्व्यङ्गस्त्रिशीर्षवान्।
चतुष्कलश्चतुर्लेखश्चतुष्कष्कुश्रुतः समः ॥ १८ ॥
चतुर्दशसमद्वन्द्वश्चतुर्दृष्टश्चतुर्गतिः।
महोऽहहनुनासश्च पञ्चस्निग्धोऽष्टवंशवान् ॥ १९ ॥
explanation: He is ever stiff in three limbs$^{1}$ (viz., the breast, wrist and fist), long in three$^{2}$ (viz., the eyebrows, arms and the scrotum), uniform in three$^{3}$ (viz., his locks, testicles and knees), elevated in three$^{4}$ (viz., the breast, the rim of the navel and the abdomen), coppery in three$^{5}$ (viz., the rims of his eyes, nails and the palms as well as the soles), soft in three$^{6}$ (viz., the end of the membrum virile, the lines on his soles and the hair), and deep in three$^{7}$ (viz., the voice, gait and the navel). He has three folds (in the skin of his neck and belly), is depressed at three places (viz., the middle of his soles, the lines on his soles, and the nipples), undersized at four places$^{8}$ (viz., the neck, membrum virile, the back and the shanks), endowed with three$^{9}$ spirals in the hair of his head, four lines at the root of his thumbs$^{10}$ (indicating his knowledge of all the four Vedas) and four lines$^{11}$ on his forehead (indicating longevity), is four cubits high, and has four pairs of limbs (viz., the cheeks, arms, shanks and knees) equally matched.$^{12}$ He has fourteen other pairs of limbs (viz., the eyebrows, nostrils, eyes, ears, the lips, nipples, elbows, wrists, the knees, the testicles, the loins, the hands, the feet and the thighs equally matched.$^{13}$ The four large teeth at both the ends of his upper and the lower jaws are very sharp.$^{14}$ He walks in four different gaits resembling those of a lion, a tiger, an elephant and a bull$^{15}$, is endowed with excellent lips, chin and nose, five glossy limbs, viz., the hair, eyes, teeth, skin and soles and eight long limbs, viz., the arms, the fingers and the toes, the eyes and the ears, the nose, the backbone and the body. (17—19)

shloka_text:
सत्यधर्मतः श्रीमान् संग्रहानुग्रहे रतः।
देशकालविभागज्ञः सर्वलोकप्रियवदः ॥ २१ ॥
explanation: “He is devoted to truth and righteousness and glorious and remains intent on accumulating wealth and power and showering favour on the people. He knows the right use of time and place and speaks kindly to all people. (21)

shloka_text:
भ्राता चास्य च वैमात्रः सौमित्रिरमितप्रभः।
अनुरागेण रूपेण गुणैश्चापि तथाविधः ॥ २२ ॥
explanation: “His brother, Lakṣmaṇa, son of Sumitrā, too, of immeasurable splendour, is a replica of Śrī Rāma in affection, charm and excellences. (22)

shloka_text:
तयोरन्योन्यसम्भाषाद् भूशं प्रीतिरजायत।
तत्र तौ कीर्तिसम्पन्नौ हरीश्वरनरेश्वरी ॥ ३३ ॥
परस्परकृताश्वासौ कथया पूर्ववृत्तया।
तं ततः सान्त्वयामास सुग्रीवं लक्ष्मणाग्रजः ॥ ३४ ॥
स्त्रीहेतोर्वालिना भ्रात्रा निरस्तं पुरतेजसा।
ततस्त्वन्नाशजं शोकं रामस्याक्लिष्टकर्मणः ॥ ३५ ॥
लक्ष्मणो वानरेन्द्राय सुग्रीवाय न्यवेदयत्।
स श्रुत्वा वानरेन्द्रस्तु लक्ष्मणेनेरितं वचः ॥ ३६ ॥
तदासीन्निष्प्रभोऽत्यर्थं ग्रहग्रस्त इवांशुमान्।
ततस्त्वदात्रशोभीनि रक्षसा ह्रियमाणया ॥ ३७ ॥
यान्याभरणजालानि पातितानि महीतले।
तानि सर्वाणि रामाय आनीय हरियूथपाः ॥ ३८ ॥
संहृष्टा दर्शयामासुर्गतिं तु न विदुस्तव।
तानि रामाय दत्तानि मयैवोपहतानि च ॥ ३९ ॥
स्वन्वन्त्यवकीर्णानि तस्मिन् विहतचेतसि।
तान्यङ्के दर्शनीयानि कृत्वा बहुविधं तदा ॥ ४० ॥
तेन देवप्रकाशेन देवेन परिदेवितम्।
पश्यतस्तानि रुदतस्ताम्यतश्च पुनः पुनः ॥ ४१ ॥
प्रादीपयद् दाशरथेस्तदा शोकहुताशनम् ॥ ४२ ॥
explanation: “As a sequel to their holding talks with one another, a great amity sprang up between them—Śrī Rāma and Sugrīva. On that occasion those illustrious personage, the lord of monkeys and the ruler of men, felt mutually comforted by narrating their respective past history. Śrī Rāma (the eldest brother of Lakṣmaṇa) then consoled Sugrīva, who had been banished for the sake of his wife, Rūmā, who had been wrested from him by his elder brother, Vāli, who was endowed with extraordinary energy. Thereupon Lakṣmaṇa spoke to Sugrīva, the lord of monkeys, about the grief caused to Śrī Rāma of unwearied action by your (Sītā's) loss. “Hearing the words uttered by Lakṣmaṇa, the aforesaid lord of monkeys for his part looked extremely lustreless on that occasion like the sun overshadowed by the planet Rāhu. Fetching all those sets of jewels which adorned your limbs and which had been dropped on the earth's surface by you while being carried away by the ogre Rāvaṇa, the leaders of monkey-hordes, greatly delighted, showed them to Śrī Rāma. They, however, did not know your whereabouts. The jewels, which were handed over at that time to Śrī Rāma while he had completely lost his consciousness due to excessive grief, had fallen with a tinkling sound and got scattered, and had been brought in the first instance when they had actually fallen on the ground, by me alone. Clasping those jewels, worth beholding as they were, to his bosom, that adorable prince, who is a manifestation of the Deity, wailed in many ways. Even as he looked on them, he wept and pined for you again and again; the lamentation of Śrī Rāma, son of Daśaratha, highly inflamed the fire of our grief at that time. (33—42)

shloka_text:
शायितं च चिरं तेन दुःखार्तेन महात्मना।
मयापि विविधैर्वाक्यैः कृच्छ्रादुत्थापितः पुनः ॥ ४३ ॥
explanation: “Stricken with agony, that exalted soul lay down senseless on the ground for a long time and was then roused by me by means of various cheering expressions with difficulty. (43)

shloka_text:
तानि दृष्ट्वा महाहाणि दर्शयित्वा मुहुर्मुहुः।
राघवः सहसौमित्रिः सुग्रीवे संन्यवेशयत् ॥ ४४ ॥
explanation: “Having examined those valuable jewels, they showed them again and again to one another, and Śrī Rāma, together with Lakṣmaṇa, deposited them with Sugrīva. (44)

shloka_text:
स तवादर्शनादार्ये राघवः परितप्यते।
महता ज्वलता नित्यमग्निनेवाग्निपर्वतः ॥ ४५ ॥
explanation: “That scion of Raghu feels sore distressed at your loss even as the 162 * VĀLMĪKI-RĀMĀYAṆA * mountain* reputed to be the seat of the fire of universal destruction is ever burning with a mighty blazing fire, O noble lady! (45)

shloka_text:
त्वत्कृते तमनिद्रा च शोकश्चिन्ता च राघवम्।
तापयन्ति महात्मानमग्न्यगारमिवाग्रयः ॥ ४६ ॥
explanation: “On account of you, sleeplessness, grief and anxiety too consume the high-souled Śrī Rāma (a scion of Raghu), even as the three sacred fires keep a fire-sanctuary heated. (46)

shloka_text:
तवादर्शनशोकेन राघवः परिचाल्यते।
महता भूमिकम्पेन महानिव शिलोच्चयः ॥ ४७ ॥
explanation: “Śrī Rāma, a scion of Raghu, has been shaken by grief caused by your absence in the same way as a large mountain is rocked by a violent earthquake. (47)

shloka_text:
काननानि सुरम्याणि नदीप्रस्वणानि च।
चरन् न रतिमाप्नोति त्वामपश्यन् नृपात्मजे ॥ ४८ ॥
explanation: “Unable to see you, O princess, Śrī Rāma finds no delight even while ranging highly charming woodlands and by the side of streams and cascades. (48)

shloka_text:
स त्वां मनुजशार्दूलः क्षिप्रं प्राप्यति राघवः।
समित्रबान्धवं हत्वा रावणं जनकात्मजे ॥ ४९ ॥
explanation: “Making short work of Rāvaṇa with his near and dear ones, O daughter of Janaka, the celebrated Śrī Rāma, a scion of Raghu, a veritable tiger among men, will soon recover you. (49)

shloka_text:
सहितौ रामसुग्रीवावुभावकुरुतां तदा।
समयं वालिनं हन्तुं तव चान्वेषणं प्रति ॥ ५० ॥
explanation: “United together in this way, both Śrī Rāma and Sugrīva then arrived at a mutual understanding to get rid of Vāli and to institute a search for you. (50)

shloka_text:
ततस्ताभ्यां कुमाराभ्यां वीराभ्यां स हरीश्वरः।
किष्किन्धां समुपागम्य वाली युद्धे निपातितः ॥ ५१ ॥
explanation: “On their reaching Kiṣkindhā together, the aforesaid Vāli, the ruler of monkeys, was then killed in combat by those two gallant princes. (51)

shloka_text:
ततो निहत्य तरसा रामो वालिनमाहवे।
सर्वक्षहरिसङ्कानां सुग्रीवमकरोत् पतिम् ॥ ५२ ॥
explanation: “Having struck down Vāli by his prowess in fight, Śrī Rāma thereupon crowned Sugrīva king of all the hordes of bears and monkeys. (52)

shloka_text:
रामसुग्रीवयोरैक्यं देव्येवं समजायत।
हनुमन्तं च मां विद्धि तयोर्दूतमुपागतम् ॥ ५३ ॥
explanation: “In this way, O godlike lady, did the alliance of Śrī Rāma and Sugrīva come about. And know me to be Hanumān arrived here as their envoy. (53)

shloka_text:
स्वं राज्यं प्राप्य सुग्रीवः स्वानानीय महाकपीन्।
त्वदर्थं प्रेषयामास दिशो दश महाबलान् ॥ ५४ ॥
explanation: “Having regained his lost sovereignty and calling together the great monkeys owing allegiance to him, and endowed with extraordinary might, Sugrīva despatched them in all the ten directions (viz., the four quarters, the four intermediate points, the higher and the lower regions). (54)

shloka_text:
आदिष्टा वानरेन्द्रेण सुग्रीवेण महौजसः।
अद्रिराजप्रतीकाशाः सर्वतः प्रस्थिता महीम् ॥ ५५ ॥
explanation: “Commanded by Sugrīva, the lord of monkeys, monkeys possessed of extraordinary vigour and looking like so many lordly mountains, sallied forth in all directions on the earth. (55)

shloka_text:
ततस्ते मार्गमाणा वै सुग्रीववचनातुराः।
चरन्ति वसुधां कृत्स्नां वयमन्ये च वानराः ॥ ५६ ॥
explanation: “Searching for you, afraid as we were of violating the command of Sugrīva, we as well as other monkeys have been actually trotting the entire globe. (56)

shloka_text:
अङ्गदो नाम लक्ष्मीवान् वालिसूनुर्महाबलः।
प्रस्थितः कपिशादूलस्त्रिभागबलसंवृतः ॥ ५७ ॥
explanation: “The glorious son of Vāli, Aṅgada by name, who is endowed with extraordinary might and is a veritable tiger among monkeys, set out accompanied by one-third of the Vānara army. (57)

shloka_text:
तेषां नो विप्रणष्टानां विंध्ये पर्वतसत्तमे।
भृशं शोकपरीतानामहोरात्रगणा गताः ॥ ५८ ॥
explanation: “A number of days and nights rolled past us, overwhelmed as we were with grief, having got lost on the Vindhyan range, the foremost of mountains. (58)

shloka_text:
ते वयं कार्यनैराश्यात् कालस्यातिक्रमेण च।
भयाच्च कपिराजस्य प्राणांस्त्यक्तुमुपस्थिताः ॥ ५९ ॥
explanation: “Due to despondency in the matter of accomplishing our purpose and in fear of the lord of monkeys, the time-limit for return having expired, we got ready to give up the ghost. (59)

shloka_text:
विचित्य गिरिदुर्गाणि नदीप्रस्वणानि च।
अनासाद्य पदं देव्याः प्राणांस्त्यक्तुं व्यवस्थिताः ॥ ६० ॥
explanation: “Having not been able to find out any trace of Your Majesty, even on scouring mountain fastnesses as also river banks and regions surrounding cascades, we stood resolved to yield our lives. (60)

shloka_text:
ततस्तस्य गिरेर्मूर्ध्वं वयं प्रायमुपास्महे।
दृष्ट्वा प्रायोपविष्टांश्च सर्वान् वानरपुङ्गवान् ॥ ६१ ॥
भृशं शोकार्णवे मग्नः पर्यदेवयदङ्गदः।
तव नाशं च वैदेहि वालिनश्च तथा वधम् ॥ ६२ ॥
प्रायोपवेशमस्माकं मरणं च जटायुषः।
तेषां नः स्वामिसंदेशान्निराशानां मुमूर्षताम् ॥ ६३ ॥
कार्यहेतोरिहायातः शकुनिर्वीर्यवान् महान्।
गृध्रराजस्य सोदर्यः सम्पातिर्नाम गृध्रराट् ॥ ६४ ॥
explanation: “We then sat down to fast till death on the summit of that Vindhyan mountain. Plunged deep into an ocean of grief on seeing all the foremost of monkeys resolved upon fasting till death, Prince Aṅgada began to bewail your untraceability, O princess of the Videha territory, as also the destruction of Vāli, his own father, and our resolution to die of hunger as well as the death of Jaṭāyu. “For helping our cause (under the dispensation of Providence), now that we had lost all hope of carrying out the behest of our master, Sugriva, and longed to die, there appeared on the spot a gigantic and powerful bird, the king of vultures, Sampāti by name, the uterine elder brother of Jaṭāyu, also a king of vultures. (61—64)

shloka_text:
श्रुत्वा भ्रातृवधं कोपादिदं वचनमब्रवीत्।
यवीयान् केन मे भ्राता हतः क्व च निपातितः ॥ ६५ ॥
एतदाख्यातुमिच्छामि भवद्भिर्वानरोत्तमाः।
अङ्गदोऽकथयत् तस्य जनस्थाने महद्वधम् ॥ ६६ ॥
रक्षसा भीमरूपेण त्वामुद्दिश्य यथार्थतः।
जटायोस्तु वधं श्रुत्वा दुःखितः सोऽरुणात्मजः ॥ ६७ ॥
explanation: “Hearing of the destruction of his younger brother, Jaṭāyu, he spoke in anguish as follows : ‘I wish to hear it narrated by you, O jewels among monkeys, by whom my younger brother was killed and where he was struck down.’ Thereupon Aṅgada truly related to him how that great soul was killed by an ogre of terrible form on account of you (Sītā), whom Jaṭāyu was trying to rescue from that monster’s clutches. That son of Aruṇa, Sampāti, for his part felt distressed to hear of Jaṭāyu’s killing. (65—67)

shloka_text:
त्वामाह स वरारोहे वसन्तीं रावणालये।
तस्य तद् वचनं श्रुत्वा सम्पातेः प्रीतिवर्धनम् ॥ ६८ ॥
अङ्गदप्रमुखाः सर्वे ततः प्रस्थापिता वयम्।
विन्ध्यादुत्थाय सम्प्राप्ताः सागरस्यान्तमुत्तमम् ॥ ६९ ॥
explanation: “Nay, he spoke of you as dwelling in the abode of Rāvaṇa, O lady of excellent limbs ! Hearing the aforesaid report of Sampāti, which intensified our joy, and departing from the aforesaid Vindhyan mountain, as urged by Sampāti, we all duly reached the excellent seashore, with Aṅgada as our leader. (68-69)

shloka_text:
त्वदृशने कृतोत्साहा हृष्टाः पुष्टाः प्लवङ्गमाः।
अङ्गदप्रमुखाः सर्वे वेलोपान्तमुपागताः ॥ ७० ॥
explanation: 164 * VĀLMĪKI-RĀMĀYAṆA * “Feeling happy and strong, resolved as they were to discover you, all the monkeys headed by Aṅgada then arrived near the seashore. (70)

shloka_text:
चिन्तां जग्मुः पुनर्भीमां त्वद्दर्शनसमुत्सुकाः ।
अथाहं हरिसैन्यस्य सागरं दृश्य सीदतः ॥ ७१ ॥
व्यवधूय भयं तीव्रं योजनानां शतं प्लुतः ।
लङ्का चापि मया रात्रौ प्रविष्टा राक्षसाकुला ॥ ७२ ॥
explanation: “The monkeys, however, who were very keen to find you, fell a prey to a terrible anxiety at the sight of the sea. Dispelling the acute fear of the monkey army, which was sinking into despondency on beholding the sea, I forthwith leapt across a distance of one hundred Yojanas (or eight hundred miles). Nay, Laṅkā too, which is crowded with ogres, was duly penetrated into by me at night. (71-72)

shloka_text:
रावणश्च मया दृष्टस्त्वं च शोकनिपीडिता ।
एतत् ते सर्वमाख्यातं यथावृत्तमनिन्दिते ॥ ७३ ॥
explanation: “Rāvaṇa also was beheld by me as well as you, who are sore stricken with grief. All this has been narrated to you by me in accordance with facts, O irreproachable lady ! (73)

shloka_text:
अभिभाषस्व मां देवि दूतो दाशरथेरहम् ।
तन्मां रामकृतोद्गोगं त्वन्निमित्तमिहागतम् ॥ ७४ ॥
सुग्रीवसचिवं देवि बुद्ध्यस्व पवनात्मजम् ।
कुशली तव काकुत्स्थः सर्वशस्त्रभृतां वरः ॥ ७५ ॥
explanation: “Speak to me, O godlike lady; I am a messenger of Śrī Rāma, son of Daśaratha. Therefore, know me, O godlike lady, to be Hanumān, son of the wind-god, a minister of Sugrīva, arrived here for your sake, having exerted in the cause of Śrī Rāma. All is well with your lord, Śrī Rāma, a scion of Kakutstha, the foremost of all wielders of weapons. (74-75)

shloka_text:
गुरोराराधने युक्तो लक्ष्मणः शुभलक्षणः ।
तस्य वीर्यवतो देवि भर्तुस्तव हिते रतः ॥ ७६ ॥
explanation: “So is Lakṣmaṇa, who remains ever engaged in propitiating his eldest brother and is endowed with auspicious bodily marks, nay, is devoted to the well-being of your aforesaid powerful husband, O godlike lady ! (76)

shloka_text:
अहमेकस्तु सम्प्राप्तः सुग्रीववचनादिह ।
मयेयमसहायेन चरता कामरूपिणा ॥ ७७ ॥
दक्षिणा दिगनुक्रान्ता त्वन्मार्गविचयैषिणा ।
दिष्ट्याहं हरिसैन्यानां त्वन्नाशमनुशोचताम् ॥ ७८ ॥
अपनेष्यामि संतापं तवाधिगमशासनात् ।
दिष्ट्या हि न मम व्यर्थं सागरस्येह लङ्कनम् ॥ ७९ ॥
explanation: “I, for my part, have arrived here alone in obedience to the command of Sugrīva. This southern quarter has been scoured by me, moving all alone, capable as I am of changing my form at will and keen as I was to find out your whereabouts. By good luck I shall be able to dispel the agony of the monkey hordes who are bewailing your loss by telling them your discovery. Luckily enough, my leaping across the sea on this occasion will not go in vain. (77—79)

shloka_text:
प्राप्यायमहमिदं देवि त्वद्दर्शनकृतं यशः ।
राघवश्च महावीर्यः क्षिप्रं त्वामभिपत्स्यते ॥ ८० ॥
सपुत्रबान्धवं हत्वा रावणं राक्षसाधिपम् ।
माल्यवान् नाम वैदेहि गिरीणामुत्तमो गिरिः ॥ ८१ ॥
ततो गच्छति गोकर्णं पर्वतं केसरी हरिः ।
स च देवर्षिभिर्दिष्टः पिता मम महाकपिः ।
तीर्थे नदीपतेः पुण्ये शम्बसादनमुद्धरन् ॥ ८२ ॥
explanation: “I shall win, O godlike lady, this renown of having discovered you. Nay, having killed Rāvaṇa, the suzerain lord of ogres, with his sons and kinsfolk, Śrī Rāma, a scion of Raghu, will soon meet you. There is a mountain, Mālyavān by name, which is the foremost of mountains, O princess of the Videha territory ! From that mountain, which constituted the abode of Keśarī, the monkey Keśarī repaired to the Gokarṇa mountain. Enjoined by celestial sages, the aforesaid mighty monkey, who is my father, killed Sambasādana (a demon of that name, who oppressed the people on the seaside) on that sacred spot on the seashore. (80—82)

shloka_text:
यस्याहं हरिणः क्षेत्रे जातो वातेन मैथिलि।
हनुमानिति विख्यातो लोके स्वेनैव कर्मणा ॥ ८३ ॥
explanation: “Begotten by the wind-god, O princess of Mithilā, through the consort of that monkey, I am called Hanumān and known all over the world for my own exploits. (83)

shloka_text:
विश्वासार्थं तु वैदेहि भर्तुरुक्ता मया गुणाः।
अचिरात् त्वामितो देवि राघवो नयिता ध्रुवम् ॥ ८४ ॥
explanation: “Indeed to inspire you with confidence, O princess of the Videha territory, the excellences of your lord have been recounted by me. Before long, O godlike lady, will Śrī Rāma, a scion of Raghu, take you without doubt from this place.” (84)

shloka_text:
एवं विश्वासिता सीता हेतुभिः शोककशिता।
उपपत्रैरभिज्ञानैर्दूतं तमधिगच्छति ॥ ८५ ॥
अतुलं च गता हर्षं प्रहर्षेण तु जानकी।
नेत्राभ्यां वक्रपक्षाभ्यां मुमोचानन्दजं जलम् ॥ ८६ ॥
explanation: Reassured thus by cogent proofs and the identification marks described by Hanumān, Sītā, who was emaciated through grief, believed him to be a messenger of her husband and was moved to incomparable joy. Nay, due to excessive joy the daughter of Janaka shed tears of joy from her eyes fringed with curved lashes. (85-86)

shloka_text:
चारु तद् वदनं तस्यास्ताम्रशुक्लायतेक्षणम्।
अशोभत विशालाक्ष्या राहुमुक्त इवोडुराट् ॥ ८७ ॥
explanation: The charming countenance of that large- eyed lady with coppery, white and big eyes shone at that time like the moon (lit., the lord of stars), disengaged from the hold of Rāhu. (87)

shloka_text:
हनुमन्तं कपिं व्यक्तं मन्यते नान्यथेति सा।
अथोवाच हनुमांस्तामुत्तरं प्रियदर्शनाम् ॥ ८८ ॥
explanation: She now thought Hanumān unmistakably to be a monkey, and not otherwise. Hanumān now addressed the following excellent words to Sītā of pleasing aspect: (88)

shloka_text:
एतत् ते सर्वमाख्यातं समाश्वसिहि मैथिलि।
किं करोमि कथं वा ते रोचते प्रतियाम्यहम् ॥ ८९ ॥
explanation: “Everything that I wished to say has thus been told by me. Be reassured, O princess of Mithilā! What more can I do for you and what would please you? I should like to return if you allow me to go. (89)

shloka_text:
हतेऽसुरे संयति शम्बसादने
कपिप्रवीरेण महर्षिचोदनात्।
ततोऽस्मि वायुप्रभवो हि मैथिलि
प्रभावतस्तत्प्रतिमश्च वानरः ॥ ९० ॥
explanation: “After the demon Sambasādana had been killed in combat by Kesari, a distinguished hero among the monkeys, at the command of an eminent sage, I was then born of the loins of the wind-god, O princess of Mithilā, and am a monkey equal to him in might.” (90)

Hanumān delivers Śrī Rāma’s signet ring to Sītā in order to strengthen her confidence in him. Applauding Hanumān, Sītā, who was rejoiced to receive the token, inquires about the health of Śrī Rāma and others. In order to appease the lady, who felt indignant at the thought that Śrī Rāma did not care to come to her rescue so far, which led her to suspect that he had ceased to love her, Hanumān attributes his non-appearance to his ignorance about her whereabouts. Describing Śrī Rāma’s desolation in order to betoken his excessive love for her, he consoles her with the assurance that Śrī Rāma is sparing no pains to rescue her from her confinement

shloka_text:
भूय एव महातेजा हनुमान् पवनात्मजः।
अब्रवीत् प्रश्नितं वाक्यं सीताप्रत्ययकारणात्॥ १॥
explanation: In order to inspire confidence in Sītā, Hanumān, son of the wind-god, who was endowed with extraordinary energy, once more addressed the following courteous words to her : (1)

shloka_text:
वानरोऽहं महाभागे दूतो रामस्य धीमतः।
रामनामाङ्कितं चेदं पश्य देव्यङ्गुलीयकम्॥ २॥
प्रत्ययार्थं तवानीतं तेन दत्तं महात्मना।
समाश्वसिहि भद्रं ते क्षीणदुःखफला ह्यसि॥ ३॥
explanation: “I am a monkey and a messenger of the wise Śrī Rāma, O highly blessed one! Also behold, O godlike lady, this ring marked with the name of Śrī Rāma, handed over by that exalted soul and brought by me to gain your confidence. Be reassured, may good betide you. The fruit of your past deeds which you have been reaping in the form suffering all these days has certainly come to an end.” (2-3)

shloka_text:
गृहीत्वा प्रेक्षमाणा सा भर्तुः करविभूषितम्।
भर्तारमिव सम्प्राप्तं जानकी मुदिताभवत्॥ ४॥
explanation: Taking the jewel which had adorned so long the hand of her lord and gazing on it, as though her own husband had duly arrived in the form of that ring, Sītā, Janaka’s daughter, felt rejoiced. (4)

shloka_text:
चारु तद् वदनं तस्यास्ताम्रशुक्लायतेक्षणम्।
बभूव हर्षोदग्रं च राहुमुक्त इवोडुराट्॥ ५॥
explanation: Her charming countenance with large coppery and white eyes bloomed with joy and shone like the moon (lit., the lord of stars) released by Rāhu. (5)

shloka_text:
ततः सा हीमती बाला भर्तुः संदेशहर्षिता।
परितुष्टा प्रियं कृत्वा प्रशंशंस महाकपिम्॥ ६॥
explanation: Treating Hanumān with regard, that youthful lady, who was delighted to receive the message of her lord, felt so very happy to see the token of her husband and fully satisfied, then paid a tribute to the great monkey in the following words : (6)

shloka_text:
विक्रान्तस्त्वं समर्थस्त्वं प्राज्ञस्त्वं वानरोत्तम।
येनेदं राक्षसपदं त्वयैकेन प्रधर्षितम्॥ ७॥
explanation: “You are valiant, you are full of address and you are learned, a jewel among the monkeys, in that this abode of ogres has been assailed by you alone. (7)

shloka_text:
शतयोजनविस्तीर्णः सागरो मकरालयः।
विक्रमश्लाघनीयेन क्रमता गोष्पदीकृतः॥ ८॥
explanation: “Nay, the sea which extends to a distance of one hundred Yojanas (or eight hundred miles) and is an abode of alligators, * SUNDARAKĀṆḌA * 167 has been treated by you like the impression of a cow's hoof on the soil while crossing it, laudable as you are for your prowess. (8)

shloka_text:
नहि त्वां प्राकृतं मन्ये वानरं वानरर्षभ।
यस्य ते नास्ति संत्रासो रावणादपि सम्भ्रमः ॥ ९ ॥
explanation: “Surely, I do not look upon you as an ordinary monkey, O jewel among monkeys, in that there exists no fear nor any awe even for Rāvaṇa in your mind. (9)

shloka_text:
अहंसे च कपिश्रेष्ठ मया समभिभाषितुम्।
यद्यसि प्रेषितस्तेन रामेण विदितात्मना ॥ १० ॥
explanation: “Nay, you deserve to be talked with by me, O jewel among monkeys, if you have been sent by the celebrated Śrī Rāma, a knower of the Self. (10)

shloka_text:
प्रेषयिष्यति दुर्धर्षो रामो नह्यपरीक्षितम्।
पराक्रममविज्ञाय मत्सकाशं विशेषतः ॥ ११ ॥
explanation: “Surely Śrī Rāma, who is difficult to overpower, would not send to my presence in particular an untried hand without fully ascertaining the latter's prowess. (11)

shloka_text:
दिष्ट्या च कुशली रामो धर्मात्मा सत्यसंगरः।
लक्ष्मणश्च महातेजाः सुमित्रानन्दवर्धनः ॥ १२ ॥
explanation: “Nay, luckily enough for me Śrī Rāma, whose mind is given to piety and who is unfailing in his promise, is doing well, as also Lakṣmaṇa, who is endowed with extraordinary energy and enhances the joy of Sumitrā, his mother. (12)

shloka_text:
कुशली यदि काकुत्स्थः किं न सागरमेखलाम्।
महीं दहति कोपेन युगान्ताग्निरिवोत्थितः ॥ १३ ॥
explanation: “If Śrī Rāma, a scion of Kakutstha, is well, wherefore does he not consume with his wrath the earth encircled by the oceans, as the fire of universal destruction would. (13)

shloka_text:
अथवा शक्तिमन्तौ तौ सुराणामपि निग्रहे।
ममैव तु न दुःखानामस्ति मन्ये विपर्ययः ॥ १४ ॥
explanation: “Nay, the two princes are able to subdue even gods. But I believe the end of my sufferings has not yet arrived. (14)

shloka_text:
कच्चिन्न व्यथते रामः कच्चिन्न परितप्यते।
उत्तराणि च कार्याणि कुरुते पुरुषोत्तमः ॥ १५ ॥
explanation: “I hope Śrī Rāma does not feel afflicted nor does he suffer agony. Does that ideal man discharge his duties relating to the future? (15)

shloka_text:
कच्चिन्न दीनः सम्भ्रान्तः कार्येषु च न मुह्यति।
कच्चिन्न पुरुषकार्याणि कुरुते नृपतेः सुतः ॥ १६ ॥
explanation: “I hope the prince does not feel helpless or nervous and does not get perplexed in the matter of his duties? Does he perform his human duties? (16)

shloka_text:
द्विविधं त्रिविधोपायमुपायमपि सेवते।
विजिगीषुः सुहृत् कच्चिन्नमित्रेषु च परंतपः ॥ १७ ॥
explanation: “I hope, acting as a friend towards his allies, Śrī Rāma, the scourge of his foes, pursues in relation to them the twofold policy of conciliation and gift and, desirous of victory, follows the threefold policy of gift, chastisement and sowing seeds of dissension with regard to his enemies. (17)

shloka_text:
कच्चिन्नमित्राणि लभतेऽमित्रैश्चाप्यभिगम्यते।
कच्चिन्न कल्याणमित्रश्च मित्रैश्चापि पुरस्कृतः ॥ १८ ॥
explanation: “I hope he is able to gain friends and is sought for help and protection even by enemies. Are his friends well-disposed towards him and is he esteemed by his friends? (18)

shloka_text:
कच्चिदाशास्ति देवानां प्रसादं पार्थिवात्मजः।
कच्चिन्न पुरुषकारं च दैवं च प्रतिपद्यते ॥ १९ ॥
explanation: “Does the prince ever seek the favour of gods? And does he fall back upon personal effort as well as on Providence for the success of his undertakings? (19)

shloka_text:
कच्चिन्न विगतस्तेहो विवासान्मयि राघवः।
कच्चिन्नां व्यसनादस्मान्मोक्षयिष्यति राघवः ॥ २० ॥
explanation: “I hope Śrī Rāma has not become completely devoid of love towards me as a result of my living in an alien land. Will Śrī Rāma, a scion of Raghu, deliver me from this calamity? (20)

shloka_text:
सुखानामुचितो नित्यमसुखानामनुचितः ।
दुःखमुत्तरमासाद्य कच्चिद् रामो न सीदति ॥ २१ ॥
explanation: “I hope Śrī Rāma, who is ever deserving of delights and is undeserving of woes, has not sunk into despondency on meeting with the greatest misfortune of his life in the form of my loss? (21)

shloka_text:
कौसल्यायास्तथा कच्चित् सुमित्रायास्तथैव च ।
अभीक्षणं श्रूयते कच्चित् कुशलं भरतस्य च ॥ २२ ॥
explanation: “I hope news about the welfare of Kausalyā and likewise of Sumitrā as well as of Bharata is frequently brought to his ears. (22)

shloka_text:
मन्त्रिमित्तेन मानार्हः कच्चिच्छोकेन राघवः ।
कच्चिन्नान्यमना रामः कच्चिन्नां तारयिष्यति ॥ २३ ॥
explanation: “Does Śrī Rāma, who is deserving of honour, feel stricken with grief occasioned by my absence? I hope he has not become indifferent to me. And will he rescue me? (23)

shloka_text:
कच्चिदक्षौहिणीं भीमां भरतो भ्रातृवत्सलः ।
ध्वजिनीं मन्त्रिभिर्गुमां प्रेषयिष्यति मत्कृते ॥ २४ ॥
explanation: “Will Bharata, who is fond of his brother, send out for my sake a formidable army, consisting of one Akṣauhiṇī, protected by ministers? (24)

shloka_text:
वानराधिपतिः श्रीमान् सुग्रीवः कच्चिदेष्यति ।
मत्कृते हरिभिर्वीरैर्वृतो दन्तनखायुधैः ॥ २५ ॥
explanation: “Will the glorious Sugrīva, the suzerain lord of monkeys, come to my succour, followed by gallant monkeys using their teeth and nails for weapons? (25)

shloka_text:
कच्चिच्छलक्ष्मणः शूरः सुमित्रानन्दवर्धनः ।
अस्त्रविच्छरजालेन राक्षसान् विधमिष्यति ॥ २६ ॥
explanation: “Nay, will the heroic Lakṣmaṇa, who enhances the joy of Sumitrā, his mother, and is skilled in the use of mystic missiles, exterminate the ogres with his volley of arrows? (26)

shloka_text:
रौद्रेण कच्चिदस्त्रेण रामेण निहतं रणे ।
द्रक्ष्याम्यल्पेन कालेन रावणं ससुहृज्जनम् ॥ २७ ॥
explanation: “I hope I shall see Rāvaṇa killed at no distant date with his near and dear ones in combat by Śrī Rāma with an infallible and devastating missile? (27)

shloka_text:
कच्चिन्न तद्धेमसमानवर्णं
तस्याननं पद्मसमानगन्धि ।
मया विना शुष्यति शोकदीनं
जलक्षये पद्ममिवातपेन ॥ २८ ॥
explanation: “I hope that golden countenance of his, melancholy with grief and fragrant like a lotus, has not withered like a lotus blasted under the sun when the water in a pond has dried up. (28)

shloka_text:
धर्मापदेशात् त्यजतः स्वरान्यं
मां चाप्यरण्यं नयतः पदातेः ।
नासीद् यथा यस्य न भीनं शोकः
कच्चित् स धैर्यं हृदये करोति ॥ २९ ॥
explanation: “I hope Śrī Rāma, whom neither fear nor grief could flinch from his purpose, when he renounced his sovereignty in the name of righteousness and led me on foot to the forest, still retains firmness in his heart. (29)

shloka_text:
न चास्य माता न पिता न चान्यः
स्नेहाद् विशिष्टोऽस्ति मया समो वा ।
तावद्ध्यहं दूत जिजीविषेयं
यावत् प्रवृत्तिं शृणुयां प्रियस्य ॥ ३० ॥
explanation: “No one, not even his own mother, Kausalyā, or his father, Emperor Daśaratha, or any other relation, has had the privilege of receiving as abundant affection from Śrī Rāma as he has bestowed on me, not to speak of anyone getting more than me. I too wish to survive only so long as I continue to hear the news of my beloved lord.” (30)

shloka_text:
इतीव देवी वचनं महार्थ
तं वानरेन्द्रं मधुरार्थमुक्त्वा ।
श्रोतुं पुनस्तस्य वचोऽभिरामं
रामार्थयुक्तं विराम रामा ॥ ३१ ॥
explanation: Having addressed these words of sweet content and full of great import to that leader of monkeys, Hanumān, the charming lady * SUNDARAKĀṆḌA * 169 became silent in order to be able to hear more of Hanumān's delightful speech dealing with the theme of Śrī Rāma. (31)

shloka_text:
सीताया वचनं श्रुत्वा मारुतिभीमविक्रमः।
शिरस्यञ्जलिमाधाय वाक्यमुत्तरमब्रवीत् ॥ ३२ ॥
explanation: Placing his folded hands on his head as a token of submission on hearing the reply of Sītā, Hanumān, son of the wind-god, of redoubtable prowess made the following excellent submission: (32)

shloka_text:
न त्वामिहस्थां जानीते रामः कमललोचनः।
तेन त्वां नानयत्याशु शचीमिव पुरंदरः ॥ ३३ ॥
explanation: "The lotus-eyed Śrī Rāma does not know you to be here. Therefore, he does not take you back soon as did Indra (the destroyer of strongholds) rescue his own consort, Śaci, borne away by the demon Anuhṛada. (33)

shloka_text:
श्रुत्वैव च वचो मह्यं क्षिप्रमेष्यति राघवः।
चमूं प्रकर्षन् महतीं हर्षृक्षगणसंयुताम् ॥ ३४ ॥
explanation: "Leading a huge army consisting of monkeys and bears, Śrī Rāma, a scion of Raghu, will instantly come here merely on hearing my report. (34)

shloka_text:
विष्टम्भयित्वा बाणौघैरक्षोभ्यं वरुणालयम्।
करिष्यति पुरीं लङ्कां काकुत्स्थः शान्तराक्षसाम् ॥ ३५ ॥
explanation: "Filling the sea (lit., the abode of Varuṇa) through and through with volleys of shafts, even though it cannot even be shaken by others, Śrī Rāma, a scion of Kakutstha, will rid the city of Laṅkā of ogres. (35)

shloka_text:
तत्र यद्यन्तरा मृत्युर्देवा महासुराः।
स्थास्यन्ति पथि रामस्य स तानपि वधिष्यति ॥ ३६ ॥
explanation: "On that occasion if Death, gods or even mighty demons stand in the way of Śrī Rāma, he would destroy them too. (36)

shloka_text:
तवादर्शनजेनार्ये शोकेन परिपूरितः।
न शर्म लभते रामः सिंहादित इव द्विपः ॥ ३७ ॥
explanation: "Filled with grief born of your absence, O noble lady, Śrī Rāma does not find rest any more than an elephant wounded by a lion. (37)

shloka_text:
मन्दरेण च ते देवि शपे मूलफलेन च।
मलयेन च विन्ध्येन मेरुणा ददुरेण च ॥ ३८ ॥
यथा सुनयनं वल्गु बिम्बोष्टं चारुकुण्डलम्।
मुखं द्रक्ष्यसि रामस्य पूर्णचन्द्रमिवोदितम् ॥ ३९ ॥
explanation: "Nay, I swear to you by the Mandara and Malaya, Vindhya, Sumeru and Dardura mountains, constituting the abode of monkeys, as well as by roots and fruits which serve as our food, O godlike lady, that you will soon behold the charming countenance of Śrī Rāma, resembling the risen full moon, with beautiful eyes, lips like a ripe Bimba fruit and lovely earrings. (38-39)

shloka_text:
क्षिप्रं द्रक्ष्यसि वैदेहि रामं प्रस्ववणे गिरौ।
शतक्रतुमिवासीनं नागपृष्ठस्य मूर्धनि ॥ ४० ॥
explanation: "You will shortly see Śrī Rāma perched on the Prasravaṇa mountain like Indra (who is believed to have performed a hundred horse-sacrifices in his previous existences as a condition precedent for being born as Indra) seated on the back of Airāvata (the chief of elephants), O princess of the Videha territory! (40)

shloka_text:
न मांसं राघवो भुङ्क्ते न चैव मधु सेवते।
वन्यं सुविहितं नित्यं भक्तमश्राति पञ्चमम् ॥ ४१ ॥
explanation: "Śrī Rāma, a scion of Raghu, does not take meat nor honey. He partakes everyday of wild fruits and boiled (wild) rice, fully sanctioned for an ascetic, in the evening (the fifth* period of the day). (41)

shloka_text:
नैव दंशान् न मशकान् न कीटान् न सरीसृपान्।
राघवोऽपनयेद् गात्रात् त्वद्गतेनान्तरात्मना ॥ ४२ ॥
explanation: "Śrī Rāma is no longer able to drive away gnats or mosquitoes, insects or even reptiles from his body, his mind being fixed on you. (42)

shloka_text:
नित्यं ध्यानपरो रामो नित्यं शोकपरायणः ।
नान्यच्चिन्तयते किंचित् स तु कामवशं गतः ॥ ४३ ॥
explanation: “Śrī Rāma is ever given to contemplation and ever given over to grief. He for his part does not think of anything else, other than you fallen as he is under the sway of love. (43)

shloka_text:
अनिद्रः सततं रामः सुसोऽपि च नरोत्तमः ।
सीतेति मधुरां वाणीं व्याहरन् प्रतिबुध्यते ॥ ४४ ॥
explanation: “Śrī Rāma remains ever awake. Even when asleep, that jewel among men starts up, uttering the name of Sītā in sweet accents. (44)

shloka_text:
दृष्ट्वा फलं वा पुष्पं वा यच्चान्यत् स्त्रीमनोहरम् ।
बहुशो हा प्रियेत्येवं श्वसंस्त्वामभिभाषते ॥ ४५ ॥
explanation: “Heaving a sigh on beholding a fruit or flower or whatever else is likely to captivate the mind of women, he often calls on you, saying ‘Ah, darling !’ (45)

Sītā, who was distressed to hear of Śrī Rāma’s excessive grief caused by his separation from her, implores Hanumān to bring Śrī Rāma at once to her. Hanumān, who could not bear to see Sītā’s sad plight, offers to carry her on his back to the presence of Śrī Rāma and girds up his loins to do so. In order to inspire confidence in Sītā, who doubts his capacity to do it looking to his small size, Hanumān assumes a gigantic form; Sītā, however, declines to go with him and urges Hanumān to bring Śrī Rāma to her

shloka_text:
अमृतं विषसम्पृक्तं त्वया वानर भाषितम्।
यच्च नान्यमना रामो यच्च शोकपरायणः ॥ २ ॥
explanation: “What has been said by you, O Hanumān, viz., that Śrī Rāma does not give his mind to any other thing than me and that he is given over to grief, is nectar mixed with poison. (2)

shloka_text:
ऐश्वर्ये वा सुविस्तीर्णे व्यसने वा सुदारुणे।
रज्ज्वेव पुरुषं बद्ध्वा कृतान्तः परिकर्षति ॥ ३ ॥
explanation: “Tying a man with a cord, as it were, Death snatches away a man, no matter whether he is rolling in very extensive fortune or sunk in terrible adversity. (3)

shloka_text:
विधिर्नूनमसंहार्यः प्राणिनां प्लवगोत्तम।
सौमित्रिं मां च रामं च व्यसनैः पश्य मोहितान् ॥ ४ ॥
explanation: “Inevitable indeed is the destiny of living beings, O jewel among monkeys! For example, look at Lakṣmaṇa, son of Sumitrā, Śrī Rāma and myself distracted by woes. (4)

shloka_text:
शोकस्यास्य कथं पारं राघवोऽधिगमिष्यति।
प्लवमानः परिक्रान्तो हतनीः सागरे यथा ॥ ५ ॥
explanation: “How will Śrī Rāma, a scion of Raghu, reach the end of this ocean of grief any more than a powerful man who has suffered a shipwreck and is swimming in a sea? (5)

shloka_text:
राक्षसानां वधं कृत्वा सूदयित्वा च रावणम्।
लङ्कामुन्मथितां कृत्वा कदा द्रक्ष्यति मां पतिः ॥ ६ ॥
explanation: “When will my lord, Śrī Rāma, see me after compassing the destruction of ogres, killing Rāvaṇa and laying Laṅkā waste? (6)

shloka_text:
स वाच्यः संत्वरस्वेति यावदेव न पूर्यते।
अयं संवत्सरः कालस्तावद्भि मम जीवितम् ॥ ७ ॥
explanation: “He should be asked to act with great haste; for my life is going to last only till the current period of twelve months is not complete. (7)

shloka_text:
वर्तते दशमो मासो द्वौ तु शेषौ प्लवङ्गम।
रावणेन नृशंसेन समयो यः कृतो मम ॥ ८ ॥
explanation: “This is the close of the tenth month and two months still remain, O Hanumān, out of the time-limit of twelve months that has been fixed by the merciless Rāvaṇa for my survival. (8)

shloka_text:
विभीषणेन च भ्रात्रा मम निर्यातनं प्रति।
अनुनीतः प्रयत्नेन न च तत् कुरुते मतिम् ॥ ९ ॥
explanation: “Nay, Rāvaṇa was perseveringly entreated by his younger brother, Vibhīṣaṇa, for my restoration to Śrī Rāma; but the former does not feel inclined to do it. (9)

shloka_text:
मम प्रतिप्रदानं हि रावणस्य न रोचते।
रावणं मार्गते संख्ये मृत्युः कालवशंगतम् ॥ १० ॥
explanation: “My restoration does not find favour with Rāvaṇa; for Death lies in wait for him in combat, fallen as he is in the clutches of the Time-Spirit (an embodiment of the destructive principle). (10)

shloka_text:
ज्येष्ठा कन्या कला नाम विभीषणसुता कपे।
तया ममैतदाख्यातं मात्रा प्रहितया स्वयम् ॥ ११ ॥
explanation: “The eldest daughter born of Vibhīṣaṇa is called by the name of Kalā, O Hanumān! This was reported to me by Kalā herself when she was sent to me by her mother. (11)

shloka_text:
अविन्ध्यो नाम मेधावी विद्वान् राक्षसपुङ्गवः।
धृतिमाञ्छीलवान् वृद्धो रावणस्य सुसम्मतः ॥ १२ ॥
explanation: “There is a jewel among the ogres, Avindhya by name, who is intelligent and learned, full of fortitude and rich in amiable disposition, aged and highly respected by Rāvaṇa. (12)

shloka_text:
रामात् क्षयमनुप्राप्तं रक्षसां प्रत्यचोदयत्।
न च तस्य स दुष्टात्मा शृणोति वचनं हितम् ॥ १३ ॥
explanation: “He forewarned Rāvaṇa of the imminent destruction of ogres at the hands of Śrī Rāma if he did not restore me; but the evil-minded fellow did not heed his salutary advice. (13)

shloka_text:
आशंसेयं हरिश्रेष्ठ क्षिप्रं मां प्राप्यते पतिः।
अन्तरात्मा हि मे शुद्धस्तस्मिंश्च बहवो गुणाः ॥ १४ ॥
explanation: “I hope, O jewel among monkeys, that my lord will regain me soon; for my heart is 172 * VĀLMĪKI-RĀMĀYAṆA * pure and the virtues existing in him are numerous. (14)

shloka_text:
उत्साहः पौरुषं सत्त्वमानुशंस्य कृतज्ञता।
विक्रमश्च प्रभावश्च सन्ति वानर राघवे ॥ १५ ॥
explanation: “Perseverance, manliness, courage, absence of cruelty, gratitude, prowess and energy figure in Śrī Rāma, a scion of Raghu, O Hanumān ! (15)

shloka_text:
चतुर्दश सहस्राणि राक्षसानां जघान यः।
जनस्थाने विना भ्रात्रा शत्रुः कस्तस्य नोद्भिजेत् ॥ १६ ॥
explanation: “What enemy would not tremble before him, who slew as many as fourteen thousand ogres in Janasthāna, unaided by his younger brother, Lakṣmaṇa? (16)

shloka_text:
न स शक्यस्तुलयितुं व्यसनैः पुरुषर्षभः।
अहं तस्यानुभावज्ञा शक्रस्येव पुलोमजा ॥ १७ ॥
explanation: “That jewel among men cannot be shaken by woes (which are no match for him). I know his might even as Śaci (sprung from the loins of the demon Pulomā) knows the might of her husband, Indra. (17)

shloka_text:
शरजालांशुमान् शूरः कपे रामदिवाकरः।
शत्रुरक्षोमयं तोयमुपशोषं नयिष्यति ॥ १८ ॥
explanation: “The valiant Śrī Rāma, who is like the sun with his shafts for rays, O Hanumān, will surely dry up the water in the form of the hostile ogres.” (18)

shloka_text:
इति संजल्पमानां तां रामार्थे शोककर्षिताम्।
अश्रुसम्पूर्णवदनामुवाच हनुमान् कपिः ॥ १९ ॥
explanation: To Sītā, who was speaking volubly as aforesaid, nay, who had been emaciated through grief on account of her separation from Śrī Rāma, her face bathed in tears, Hanumān submitted as follows : (19)

shloka_text:
श्रुत्वैव च वचो मह्यं क्षिप्रमेष्यति राघवः।
चमूं प्रकर्षन् महतीं हर्षुक्षगणसंकुलाम् ॥ २० ॥
explanation: “Leading a huge army, full of monkeys and bears, Śrī Rāma will surely hasten to Laṅkā the moment he hears my report. (20)

shloka_text:
अथवा मोचयिष्यामि त्वामद्यैव सराक्षसात्।
अस्माद् दुःखादुपारोह मम पृष्ठमनिन्दिते ॥ २१ ॥
explanation: “Or, I myself shall deliver you from this calamity caused by the ogre Rāvaṇa this very day. Please climb up my back, O irreproachable lady ! (21)

shloka_text:
त्वां तु पृष्ठगतां कृत्वा संतरिष्यामि सागरम्।
शक्तिरस्ति हि मे वोढुं लङ्कामपि सरावणाम् ॥ २२ ॥
explanation: “I shall easily leap across the sea even after placing you on my back; for I can carry on my back the whole of Laṅkā, Rāvaṇa and all. (22)

shloka_text:
अहं प्रस्वणस्थाय राघवायाद्य मैथिलि।
प्रापयिष्यामि शक्राय हव्यं हुतमिवानलः ॥ २३ ॥
explanation: “I shall transport you this very day, O princess of Mithila, to Śrī Rāma, a scion of Raghu, staying on Mount Prasravaṇa, even as the sacred fire conveys the oblations thrown into it to Indra for whom they are intended. (23)

shloka_text:
द्रक्ष्यस्यद्यैव वैदेहि राघवं सहलक्ष्मणम्।
व्यवसायसमायुक्तं विष्णुं दैत्यवधे यथा ॥ २४ ॥
त्वदर्शनकृतोत्साहमाश्रमस्थं महाबलम्।
पुरंदरमिवासीनं नगराजस्य मूर्धनि ॥ २५ ॥
explanation: “You will see this very day Śrī Rāma, accompanied by Lakṣmaṇa—Śrī Rāma, who in his determination to exterminate the ogres resembles Lord Viṣṇu, full of determination to destroy the demons, is endowed with extraordinary might and resolved to see you and remains seated in his hermitage even as Indra (the destroyer of strongholds) on the summit of Mount Meru, the king of mountains, O Sītā ! (24-25)

shloka_text:
पृष्ठमारोह मे देवि मा विकाङ्क्षस्व शोभने।
योगमन्विच्छ रामेण शशाङ्केनेव रोहिणी ॥ २६ ॥
explanation: “Mount on my back, O godlike lady ! Do not show reluctance, O charming one! Seek to be united with Śrī Rāma even as Rohiṇī* is with the deity presiding over * A consort of the moon-god, presiding over a constellation of the same name. * SUNDARAKĀṆḌA * 173 the moon (marked with the figure of a hare). (26)

shloka_text:
कथयन्तीव शशिना संगमिष्यसि रोहिणी।
मत्पृष्टमधिरोह त्वं तराकाशं महार्णवम् ॥ २७ ॥
explanation: “You will be united with Śrī Rāma as Rohiṇī with the moon-god, the very moment, as it were, you say that you wish to be so united. Pray, climb up my back and reach beyond the vast sea through space the very next moment, as it were. (27)

shloka_text:
नहि मे सम्प्रयातस्य त्वामितो नयतोऽङ्गुने।
अनुगन्तुं गतिं शक्ताः सर्वे लङ्कानिवासिनः ॥ २८ ॥
explanation: “Surely all the dwellers in Laṅkā will not be able to follow my speed even as I depart from this place bearing you on my back, O fair one! (28)

shloka_text:
यथैवाहमिह प्राप्तस्तथैवाहमसंशयम्।
यास्यामि पश्य वैदेहि त्वामुद्यम्य विहायसम् ॥ २९ ॥
explanation: “Lo, bearing you on my back, O princess of the Videha territory, I shall undoubtedly return through airspace precisely as I came here.” (29)

shloka_text:
मैथिली तु हरिश्रेष्ठाच्छ्रुत्वा वचनमद्भुतम्।
हर्षविस्मितसर्वाङ्गी हनुमन्तमथाब्रवीत् ॥ ३० ॥
हनुमन् दूरमध्वानं कथं मां नेतुमिच्छसि।
तदेव खलु ते मन्ये कपित्वं हरियूथप ॥ ३१ ॥
explanation: Thrilled all over with joy to hear the aforesaid wonderful proposal from Hanumān, the foremost of monkeys, Sītā, a princess of Mithilā, for her part forthwith replied as follows to Hanumān: “How do you intend to take me, O Hanumān, to such a long distance from this place? Indeed, I look upon the aforesaid proposal of yours to be precisely monkey-like, O leader of monkey hordes! (30-31)

shloka_text:
कथं चाल्पशरीरस्त्वं मामितो नेतुमिच्छसि।
सकाशं मानवेन्द्रस्य भर्तुर्मे प्लवगर्षभ ॥ ३२ ॥
explanation: “How do you intend to take me from this place, diminutive of form that you are, to the presence of my royal husband, O jewel among monkeys?” (32)

shloka_text:
सीतायास्तु वचः श्रुत्वा हनुमान् मारुतात्मजः।
चिन्तयामास लक्ष्मीवान् नवं परिभवं कृतम् ॥ ३३ ॥
explanation: Hearing the query of Sītā, the glorious Hanuman, son of the wind-god, thought it to be the first affront of its kind offered to him. (33)

shloka_text:
न मे जानाति सत्त्वं वा प्रभावं वासितेक्षणा।
तस्मात् पश्यतु वैदेही यद् रूपं मम कामतः ॥ ३४ ॥
explanation: He said to himself: ‘The dark-eyed lady does not know my strength nor my power. Let the princess of the Videha territory, therefore, behold the form that I can assume at will.’ (34)

shloka_text:
इति संचिन्त्य हनुमांस्तदा प्लवगसत्तमः।
दर्शयामास सीतायाः स्वरूपमरिमर्दनः ॥ ३५ ॥
explanation: Thinking thus, Hanumān, the foremost of monkeys and the destroyer of his enemies, revealed his form to Sītā on that occasion. (35)

shloka_text:
स तस्मात् पादपाद् धीमानाप्लुत्य प्लवगर्षभः।
ततो वर्धितुमारेभे सीताप्रत्ययकारणात् ॥ ३६ ॥
explanation: Leaping down from that tree (beneath which she stood), that wise leader of monkeys then began to grow in size in order to inspire confidence in Sītā. (36)

shloka_text:
मेरुमन्दरसंकाशो बभौ दीमानलप्रभः।
अग्रतो व्यवतस्थे च सीताया वानरर्षभः ॥ ३७ ॥
explanation: Hanumān, the foremost of monkeys, looked like Mount Meru or Mount Mandāra and stood in front of Sītā, shining brightly like a blazing fire. (37)

shloka_text:
हरिः पर्वतसंकाशस्ताम्रवक्त्रो महाबलः।
वज्रदंष्ट्रनखो भीमो वैदेहीमिदमब्रवीत् ॥ ३८ ॥
explanation: The redoubtable Hanumān, who resembled a mountain and had a coppery countenance with adamantine teeth and nails and was endowed with extraordinary might, submitted as follows to Sītā, a princess of the Videha Kingdom: (38)

shloka_text:
सपर्वतवनोद्देशां साट्टप्राकारतोरणाम्।
लङ्कामिमां सनाथां वा नयितुं शक्तिरस्ति मे ॥ ३९ ॥
explanation: 174 * VĀLMĪKI-RĀMĀYAṆA * “There is capacity in me to carry this entire city of Laṅkā including its hills and woodlands as well as its market-places, defensive walls and arches, with its very lord, Rāvaṇa. (39)

shloka_text:
तदवस्थाप्यतां बुद्धिरलं देवि विकाङ्क्षया।
विशोकं कुरु वैदेहि राघवं सहलक्ष्मणम् ॥ ४० ॥
explanation: “Therefore, let your mind be settled, O godlike lady, and have done with hesitation. Rid Śrī Rāma, a scion of Raghu, alongwith Lakṣmaṇa, of grief, O princess of the Videha territory!” (40)

shloka_text:
तं दृष्ट्वाचलसंकाशमुवाच जनकात्मजा।
पद्मपत्रविशालाक्षी मारुतस्यौरसं सुतम् ॥ ४१ ॥
explanation: Finding Hanumān of the size of a mountain, Sītā, daughter of Janaka, who had eyes big as the petals of a lotus, replied as follows to the son of the wind-god: (41)

shloka_text:
तव सत्त्वं बलं चैव विजानामि महाकपे।
वायोरिव गतिश्रापि तेजश्चाग्नेरिवाद्भुतम् ॥ ४२ ॥
explanation: “I know full well your courage and strength, O mighty Hanumān! Your speed is like that of the wind, while your marvellous brilliance too is like that of fire itself. (42)

shloka_text:
प्राकृतोऽन्यः कथं चेमां भूमिमागन्तुमर्हति।
उदधेरप्रमेयस्य पारं वानरयूथप ॥ ४३ ॥
explanation: “How could any other ordinary monkey actually reach this land beyond the vast sea, O leader of hordes of monkeys? (43)

shloka_text:
जानामि गमने शक्तिं नयने चापि ते मम।
अवश्यं सम्प्रधार्याशु कार्यसिद्धिरिवात्मनः ॥ ४४ ॥
explanation: “I know your power of locomotion as well as your ability to carry me on your back. The accomplishment of my object too must, however, be determined at once even as yours. (44)

shloka_text:
अयुक्तं तु कपिश्रेष्ठ मया गन्तुं त्वया सह।
वायुवेगसवेगस्य वेगो मां मोहयेत् तव ॥ ४५ ॥
explanation: “My going with you, however, O jewel among monkeys, is not proper. Your speed, which is equal to that of the wind, may render me unconscious. (45)

shloka_text:
धृतव्रतो राजसुतो महात्मा
तवैव लाभाय कृतप्रयत्नः ॥ ४६ ॥
explanation: “Suffering extreme agony caused by separation from you and calling on you alone by the name of Sītā, that magnanimous prince, who has undertaken sacred vows, is solely engaged in efforts for your recovery.” (46)

shloka_text:
अहमाकाशमासक्ता उपर्युपरि सागरम्।
प्रपतेयं हि ते पृष्ठाद् भूयो वेगेन गच्छतः ॥ ४६ ॥
explanation: “Besides, stuck to space, even as you sweep with speed all over the sea, I may actually tumble down from your back. (46)

shloka_text:
सा रामसंकीर्तनवीतशोका
रामस्य शोकेन समानशोका ।
शरन्मुखेनाम्बुदशेषचन्द्रा
निशेव वैदेहसुता बभूव ॥ ४७ ॥
explanation: That daughter of Janaka, a ruler of the Videha territory, whose grief (over the imagined apathy of Śrī Rāma) was now completely gone at the detailed description of the condition of Śrī Rāma, yet who felt equally grieved on hearing of Śrī Rāma’s grief—resembled a night, partly bright and partly dark, at the commencement of autumn with the moon obscured by the remnants of clouds. (47)

shloka_text:
पतिता सागरे चाहं तिमिनक्रशषाकुले।
भवेयमाशु विवशा यादसामन्नमुत्तमम् ॥ ४७ ॥
explanation: “Nay, fallen insensible into the sea, teeming with sharks, crocodiles and giant fish, I may become the excellent food of aquatic creatures. (47)

shloka_text:
न च शक्ष्ये त्वया सार्धं गन्तुं शत्रुविनाशन।
कलत्रवति संदेहस्त्वयि स्यादप्यसंशयम् ॥ ४८ ॥
explanation: “For other reasons too, O destroyer of foes, I shall not be able to go with you. Suspicion of the ogres will undoubtedly fall on you as you will go with a lady on your back. (48)

shloka_text:
ह्रियमाणां तु मां दृष्ट्वा राक्षसा भीमविक्रमाः।
अनुगच्छेयुरादिष्टा रावणेन दुरात्मना ॥ ४९ ॥
explanation: “Enjoined by the evil-minded Rāvaṇa, ogres of terrible prowess will surely pursue you on seeing me being borne away by you. (49)

shloka_text:
तैस्त्वं परिवृतः शूरैः शूलमुद्रपाणिभिः।
भवेत्स्वं संशयं प्राप्तो मया वीर कलत्रवान् ॥ ५० ॥
explanation: “Surrounded by the heroic ogres carrying darts and clubs in their hands, and accompanied by a lady i.e., myself, you will fall into danger. (50)

shloka_text:
सायुधा बहवो व्योमि राक्षसास्त्वं निरायुधः।
कथं शक्ष्यसि संयुतुं मां चैव परिरक्षितुम् ॥ ५१ ॥
explanation: “There will be numerous ogres equipped with arms in space; how then will you be able to fight them, as also protect me, unarmed that you are? (51)

shloka_text:
युध्यमानस्य रक्षोभिस्ततस्तैः क्रूरकर्मभिः।
प्रपतेयं हि ते पृष्ठाद् भयार्ता कपिसत्तम ॥ ५२ ॥
explanation: * SUNDARAKĀṆḌA * 175 “Stricken with fear, O jewel among monkeys, I may then fall down from your back while you are contending with those ogres of cruel deeds. (52)

shloka_text:
अथ रक्षांसि भीमानि महान्ति बलवन्ति च।
कथंचित् साम्पराये त्वां जयेयुः कपिसत्तम ॥५३॥
अथवा युध्यमानस्य पतेयं विमुखस्य ते।
पतितां च गृहीत्वा मां नयेयुः पापराक्षसाः ॥५४॥
explanation: “In case the ogres, who are terrible, huge and mighty, are somehow able to overcome you in conflict, or if I slip when you have turned your eyes away from me while fighting with them, the sinful ogres may bear me away, laying hold on me when fallen. (53-54)

shloka_text:
मां वा हरेयुस्त्वद्भस्ताद् विशसेयुरथापि वा।
अनवस्थौ हि दृश्येते युद्धे जयपराजयौ ॥५५॥
explanation: “Or, they may wrest me from your grasp or even kill me afterwards; for victory and defeat in combat are said to be uncertain. (55)

shloka_text:
अहं वापि विपद्येयं रक्षोभिरभितर्जिता।
त्वत्प्रयत्नो हरिश्रेष्ठं भवेन्निष्फल एव तु ॥५६॥
explanation: “Or, I may even die when intimidated by the ogres. Your endeavour to take me to the presence of Śrī Rāma may in that case prove utterly futile, O jewel among monkeys! (56)

shloka_text:
कामं त्वमपि पर्याप्तो निहन्तुं सर्वराक्षसान्।
राघवस्य यशो हीयेत् त्वया शस्तैस्तु राक्षसैः ॥५७॥
explanation: “Even though you are able to kill all the ogres, the fame of Śrī Rāma, a scion of Raghu, may suffer diminution because of the ogres having been killed by you. (57)

shloka_text:
अथवाऽऽदाय रक्षांसि न्यसेयुः संवृते हि माम्।
यत्र ते नाभिजानीयुर्हरयो नापि राघवः ॥५८॥
explanation: “Or, bearing me away, the ogres may actually lodge me in a secret place, where neither those monkeys nor Śrī Rāma, a scion of Raghu, may know anything about me. (58)

shloka_text:
आरम्भस्तु मदर्थोऽयं ततस्तव निरर्थकः।
त्वया हि सह रामस्य महानागमने गुणः ॥५९॥
explanation: “This adventure of yours undertaken on my account will then prove to be in vain. A great advantage indeed lies in Śrī Rāma’s advent with you. (59)

shloka_text:
मयि जीवितमायत्तं राघवस्यामितौजसः।
भ्रातृणां च महाबाहो तव राजकुलस्य च ॥६०॥
explanation: “The life of Śrī Rāma, who is endowed with immeasurable strength, as well as of his three younger brothers, as also of your king, Sugrīva and his family is dependent on me, O mighty-armed monkey! (60)

shloka_text:
तौ निराशौ मदर्थं च शोकसंतापकशितौ।
सह सर्वक्षहरिभिस्त्यक्ष्यतः प्राणसंग्रहम् ॥६१॥
explanation: “Despondent and emaciated through grief and agony on my account, the two princes, Śrī Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, will give up their hold on life alongwith all the bears and monkeys. (61)

shloka_text:
भर्तुर्भक्तिं पुरस्कृत्य रामादन्यस्य वानर।
नाहं स्पृष्टं स्वतो गात्रमिच्छेदं वानरोत्तम ॥६२॥
explanation: “Keeping as I do devotion to my lord in the forefront, O Hanumān, I do not wish to touch of my own free will the body of anyone other than Śrī Rāma, O jewel among monkeys! (62)

shloka_text:
यदहं गात्रसंस्पर्शं रावणस्य गता बलात्।
अनीशा किं करिष्यामि विनाथा विवशा सती ॥६३॥
explanation: “That I was forced into contact with Rāvaṇa was because, being helpless, without a protector and having lost control of myself, I could not do anything. (63)

shloka_text:
यदि रामो दशग्रीवमिह हत्वा सराक्षसम्।
मामितो गृह्य गच्छेत तत् तस्य सदृशं भवेत् ॥६४॥
explanation: “If, having killed Rāvaṇa alongwith the other ogres on this soil, and recovering me, Śrī Rāma departs from this place, that would be worthy of him. (64)

shloka_text:
न देवगन्धर्वभुजङ्गराक्षसा
