shloka_text:
तस्य सीता हता भार्या रावणेन दुरात्मना।
तस्याः सकाशं दूतोऽहं गमिष्ये रामशासनात् ॥ २६ ॥
explanation: “His consort, Sītā, was borne away by the evil-minded Rāvaṇa. At the behest of Śrī Rāma I am going to seek her presence as a messenger. (26)

shloka_text:
कर्तुमर्हसि रामस्य साहाय्यं विषये सती।
अथवा मैथिलीं दृष्ट्वा रामं चाक्लिष्टकारिणम् ॥ २७ ॥
आगमिष्यामि ते वक्त्रं सत्यं प्रतिशृणोमि ते।
एवमुक्ता मया सा तु सुरसा कामरूपिणी ॥ २८ ॥
अब्रवीन्नातिवर्तेत कश्चिदेष वरो मम।
एवमुक्तः सुरसया दशयोजनमायतः ॥ २९ ॥
ततोऽर्धगुणविस्तारो बभूवाहं क्षणेन तु।
मत्प्रमाणाधिकं चैव व्यादितं तु मुखं तया ॥ ३० ॥
explanation: “Living as you do in the dominion of Śrī Rāma, you ought to render assistance to him. Or, having seen the daughter of Janaka and having reported to Śrī Rāma of unwearied action, I shall seek your mouth : I truthfully promise this to you. Assured thus by me, the said Surasā for her part, who was able to change her form at will, replied, ‘None can dare escape me: this is the boon granted in my favour.’ Threatened thus by Surasā, I, for my part, who was ten Yojanas (or eighty miles) in extent, grew half as much in size in a trice. Her mouth too was distended by her to a size greater than mine. (27—30)

shloka_text:
तद् दृष्ट्वा व्यादितं त्वास्यं ह्रस्वं हाकरवं पुनः।
तस्मिन् मुहूर्ते च पुनर्बभूवाङ्मुखसम्मितः ॥ ३१ ॥
explanation: Perceiving her mouth wide open, I then assumed a dwarfish form, nay, the same moment I further reduced myself to the size of a human thumb. (31)

shloka_text:
अभिपत्याशु तद्वक्त्रं निर्गतोऽहं ततः क्षणात्।
अब्रवीत् सुरसा देवी स्वेन रूपेण मां पुनः ॥ ३२ ॥
explanation: “Having entered her mouth quickly, I came out of it instantly. Appearing in her native form, the goddess Surasā further said to me : (32)

shloka_text:
अर्थसिद्धौ हरिश्रेष्ठ गच्छ सौम्य यथासुखम्।
समानय च वैदेहीं राघवेण महात्मना ॥ ३३ ॥
explanation: * SUNDARAKĀṆḌA * 253 “Proceed now, O gentle one, according to your pleasure for accomplishing your purpose, O jewel among the monkeys, and re-unite the princess of the Videha territory with the high-souled Śrī Rāma, a scion of Raghu. (33)

shloka_text:
सुखी भव महाबाहो प्रीतास्मि तव वानर।
ततोऽहं साधुसाध्वीति सर्वभूतैः प्रशंसितः ॥ ३४ ॥
explanation: “Be happy, O mighty-armed monkey! I am pleased with you.’ Thereupon I was applauded by all beings, who said: ‘Well done! Bravo!!’ (34)

shloka_text:
ततोऽन्तरिक्षं विपुलं प्लुतोऽहं गरुडो यथा।
छाया मे निगृहीता च न च पश्यामि किंचन ॥ ३५ ॥
explanation: “Then I sprang into the vast space like Garuḍa (the king of birds, the carrier of Lord Viṣṇu). In the meantime my shadow was held fast; yet I perceived nothing. (35)

shloka_text:
सोऽहं विगतवेगस्तु दिशो दश विलोकयन्।
न किंचित् तत्र पश्यामि येन मे विहता गतिः ॥ ३६ ॥
explanation: “My speed having been arrested thereby, I surveyed all the ten directions; yet I could not discover there the object by which my course had been stayed. (36)

shloka_text:
अथ मे बुद्धिरुत्पन्ना किंनाम गमने मम।
ईदृशो विघ्न उत्पन्नो रूपमत्र न दृश्यते ॥ ३७ ॥
explanation: “Then the thought came to me: ‘How I wonder such an obstacle has appeared in my journey, although no concrete form is to be discerned here?’ (37)

shloka_text:
अधोभागे तु मे दृष्टिः शोचतः पतिता तदा।
तत्राद्राक्षमहं भीमां राक्षसीं सलिलेशयाम् ॥ ३८ ॥
explanation: “While I was brooding thus, my eye presently fell downward. There I espied a terrible ogress lying on water. (38)

shloka_text:
प्रहस्य च महानादमुक्तोऽहं भीमया तया।
अवस्थितमसम्भ्रान्तमिदं वाक्यमशोभनम् ॥ ३९ ॥
explanation: “Heartily laughing on seeing me motionless, yet undaunted, that dreadful woman accosted me with a loud cry in the following inauspicious words : (39)

shloka_text:
क्वासि गन्ता महाकाय क्षुधिताया ममेप्सितः।
भक्षः प्रीणय मे देहं चिरमाहारवर्जितम् ॥ ४० ॥
explanation: “Whither are you bound, O gigantic monkey? You are my coveted food, hungry as I am. Pray, gratify my person, which has remained without sustenance for a long period.’ (40)

shloka_text:
बाढमित्येव तां वाणीं प्रत्यगृह्णामहं ततः।
आस्यप्रमाणादधिकं तस्याः कायमपूरयम् ॥ ४१ ॥
explanation: “Saying ‘Amen,’ I actually bowed to that command of hers and then expanded my body to a size larger than the capacity of her mouth. (41)

shloka_text:
तस्याश्चास्यं महद् भीमं वर्धते मम भक्षणे।
न तु मां सा नु बुबुधे मम वा विकृतं कृतम् ॥ ४२ ॥
explanation: “Her huge and dreadful mouth too began to grow in order to devour me. She, however, neither recognized me nor did she perceive the transformation subsequently gone through by me in the shape of a minute form. (42)

shloka_text:
ततोऽहं विपुलं रूपं संक्षिप्य निमिषान्तरात्।
तस्या हृदयमादाय प्रपतामि नभःस्थलम् ॥ ४३ ॥
explanation: Having contracted my gigantic form in the twinkling of an eye, and extracting her heart, I forthwith sprang in the vault of heaven. (43)

shloka_text:
सा विसृष्टभुजा भीमा पपात लवणाम्भसि।
मया पर्वतसंकाशा निकृत्तहृदया सती ॥ ४४ ॥
explanation: “Her heart having been cut off, that terrible woman, who looked much like a mountain, dropped into the salty water, her arms paralysed. (44)

shloka_text:
शृणोमि खगतानां च वाचः सौम्या महात्मनाम्।
राक्षसी सिंहिका भीमा क्षिप्रं हनुमता हता ॥ ४५ ॥
explanation: “I heard at that moment the delightful words of exalted souls standing in the sky: ‘The terrible ogress, Sirhika, has been dispatched in no time by Hanumān.’ (45)

shloka_text:
दक्षिणं तीरमुदधेलङ्का यत्र गता पुरी।
अस्तं दिनकरे याते रक्षसां निलयं पुरीम् ॥ ४७ ॥
प्रविष्टोऽहमविज्ञातो रक्षोभिर्भीमविक्रमैः।
तत्र प्रविशतश्चापि कल्पान्तघनसप्रभा ॥ ४८ ॥
अङ्गहासं विमुञ्चन्ती नारी काप्युत्थिता पुरः।
जिघांसन्तीं ततस्तां तु ज्वलदग्निशिरोरुहाम् ॥ ४९ ॥
सव्यमुष्टिप्रहारेण पराजित्य सुभैरवाम्।
प्रदोषकाले प्रविशं भीतयाहं तयोदितः ॥ ५० ॥
explanation: “Calling to mind once more my errand in the shape of Sītā’s discovery, which had been delayed, after having killed her, and traversing a long distance, I sighted the southern shore of the sea, graced with mountains, where stood the city of Laṅkā. The sun having set, I penetrated, unnoticed by ogres of terrible prowess, deep into the city constituting the abode of ogres. Even while I was making good my entry into the city, a certain woman possessing the hue of a cloud, appearing at the end of a world cycle, rose in front of me, bursting into a horse-laugh. Having vanquished with a stroke of my left fist that exceedingly dreadful woman, whose locks resembled a flaming fire, and who sought to kill me, I for my part then compassed my entry at eventide, spoken to by her, afraid as she was, in the following words: (46—50)

shloka_text:
अहं लङ्कापुरी वीर निजिता विक्रमेण ते।
यस्मात् तस्माद् विजेतासि सर्वरक्षांस्यशेषतः ॥ ५१ ॥
explanation: “I am the city of Laṅkā (incarnate), O hero! Since I have been vanquished by you by dint of prowess, you will conquer all the ogres in their entirety.” (51)

shloka_text:
प्रीतिमत्सूपविष्टेषु वानरेषु महात्मसु।
तं ततः प्रतिसंहृष्टः प्रीतियुक्तं महाकपिम् ॥२॥
जाम्बवान् कार्यवृत्तान्तमपृच्छदनिलात्मजम्।
कथं दृष्टा त्वया देवी कथं वा तत्र वर्तते ॥३॥
explanation: The high-souled monkeys being joyfully and comfortably seated, Jāmbavān, who felt highly rejoiced, now enquired of that great monkey, Hanumān, who was also The glorious Aṅgada sat there encircled by numerous monkeys even like Indra, the lord of gods, waited upon by gods in heaven. (52)

shloka_text:
तत्राहं सर्वरात्रं तु विचरञ्जनकात्मजाम्।
रावणान्तःपुरगतो न चापश्यं सुमध्यमाम् ॥ ५२ ॥
explanation: “Though ranging over Laṅkā all through the night, I did not find Janaka’s daughter of slender waist even though I penetrated into the gynaecium of Rāvaṇa.” (52)

shloka_text:
हनुमता कीर्तिमता यशस्विना
तथाङ्गदेनाङ्गदनद्बाहुना ।
मुदा तदाध्यासितमुन्नतं मह-
न्महीधराग्रं ज्वलितं श्रियाभवत् ॥५३॥
explanation: Full of joy at that time, the glorious Hanumān as well as the illustrious Aṅgada, who had his arms adorned with a pair of armlets, the lofty and huge mountain peak stood illumined with splendour. (53)

shloka_text:
ततः सीतामपश्यंस्तु रावणस्य निवेशने।
शोकसागरमासाद्य न पारमुपलक्षये ॥ ५३ ॥
explanation: “Not finding Sītā even in the abode of Rāvaṇa and thus facing an ocean of grief, I did not perceive its end. (53)

shloka_text:
शोचता च मया दृष्टं प्राकारेणाभिसंवृतम्।
काञ्चनेन विकृष्टेन गृहोपवनमुत्तमम् ॥ ५४ ॥
explanation: “Even while I was brooding, an excellent pleasance enclosed on all sides by a lofty wall of gold was seen by me. (54)

shloka_text:
सप्राकारमवप्लुत्थ पश्यामि बहुपादपम्।
अशोकवनिकामध्ये शिशपापादपो महान् ॥ ५५ ॥
explanation: “Having leapt across the enclosure, I as such saw a grove consisting of numerous trees. In the midst of that grove of Aśoka trees, there stood a huge Śiṁśapā (Aśoka) tree. (55)

shloka_text:
तमारुह्य च पश्यामि काञ्चनं कदलीवनम्।
अदूराच्छिशपावृक्षात् पश्यामि वरवर्णिनीम् ॥ ५६ ॥
श्यामां कमलपत्राक्षीमुपवासकृशाननाम्।
तदेकवासःसंवीतां रजोध्वस्तशिरोरुहाम् ॥ ५७ ॥
शोकसंतापदीनाङ्गीं सीतां भर्तृहिते स्थिताम्।
राक्षसीभिर्विरूपाभिः क्रूराभिरभिसंवृताम् ॥ ५८ ॥
मांसशोणितभक्ष्याभिर्व्याघ्रीभिर्हरिणीं यथा।
सा मया राक्षसीमध्ये तर्ज्यमाना मुहुर्मुहुः ॥ ५९ ॥
एकवेणीधरा दीना भर्तृचिन्तापरायणा।
भूमिशय्या विवर्णाङ्गी पद्मिनीव हिमागमे ॥ ६० ॥
रावणाद् विनिवृत्तार्था मर्तव्ये कृतनिश्चया।
कथंचिन्मृगशावाक्षी तूर्णमासादिता मया ॥ ६१ ॥
explanation: “Ascending it, I sighted a golden thicket of plantain trees. Not far from the Śiṁśapā tree, I beheld the youthful Sītā of excellent complexion with eyes resembling lotus petals and a face emaciated through fasting, her hair soiled with dust and her limbs afflicted through grief and agony, clad in a single piece of cloth which she had on her person while being borne away by Rāvaṇa over Kiṣkindhā, devoted to the good of her lord and surrounded on all sides by ugly and cruel ogresses living on flesh and blood even as a doe encircled by tigresses. The lady, who had eyes like those of a fawn, * SUNDARAKĀṆḌA * 255 was somehow quickly found by me miserable in the midst of ogresses, intimidated as she was by them again and again, wearing a single pleat as a mark of desolation, given to the thought of her lord, having the bare ground for her bed, pale-limbed like a lotus plant at the advent of winter, nay, deprived of the object of her desire viz., the service of Śrī Rāma, because of Rāvaṇa and resolved upon dying. (56—61)

shloka_text:
ताँ दृष्ट्वा तादृशीं नारीं रामपत्नी यशस्विनीम्।
तत्रैव शिंशपावृक्षे पश्यन्नहमवस्थितः ॥ ६२ ॥
explanation: “Perceiving that illustrious lady, the consort of Śrī Rāma, in such a condition, I remained perched on the same Śīṁśapā tree, looking at her. (62)

shloka_text:
ततो हलहलाशब्दं काञ्चीनपुरमिश्रितम्।
शृणोम्यधिकगम्भीरं रावणस्य निवेशने ॥ ६३ ॥
explanation: “Then I heard in the abode of Rāvaṇa an unusually deep sound of hallooing, mixed with the jingling of girdles and anklets. (63)

shloka_text:
ततोऽहं परमोद्विग्नः स्वरूपं प्रत्यसंहरम्।
अहं च शिंशपावृक्षे पक्षीव गहने स्थितः ॥ ६४ ॥
explanation: “Feeling supremely anxious, I thereupon contracted my form and remained crouched like a bird on the Śīṁśapā tree thick with foliage. (64)

shloka_text:
ततो रावणदाराश्च रावणश्च महाबलः।
तं देशमनुसम्प्रासो यत्र सीताभवत् स्थिता ॥ ६५ ॥
explanation: “Then arrived the consorts of Rāvaṇa as well as Rāvaṇa himself, who is endowed, with extraordinary might, in that place where Sītā was ensconced. (65)

shloka_text:
तं दृष्ट्वाथ वरारोहा सीता रक्षोगणेश्वरम्।
संकुच्योरु स्तनौ पीनौ बाहुभ्यां परिरभ्य च ॥ ६६ ॥
explanation: “Seeing that lord of ogre hordes, Sītā of lovely hips sat compressing her thighs and enclosing her high breasts with her arms. (66)

shloka_text:
वित्रस्तां परमोद्विग्नां वीक्ष्यमाणामितस्ततः।
त्राणं कञ्चिदपश्यन्तीं वेपमानां तपस्विनीम् ॥ ६७ ॥
तामुवाच दशग्रीवः सीतां परमदुःखिताम्।
अवाकुशिराः प्रपतितो बहुमन्यस्व मामिति ॥ ६८ ॥
explanation: “Fallen flat at her feet, head downward, Rāvaṇa, the ten-headed monster, said to the aforesaid Sītā, who felt greatly frightened and highly confused, and was glancing round in the hope of finding an asylum, but, finding no saviour, was trembling helpless and supremely distressed as she was; ‘Pray, regard me with favour. (67-68)

shloka_text:
एतच्छ्रुत्वा वचस्तस्य रावणस्य दुरात्मनः।
उवाच परमकृद्वा सीता वचनमुत्तमम् ॥ ७० ॥
explanation: “Highly incensed to hear this request of that evil-minded Rāvaṇa, Sītā made the following excellent reply : (70)

shloka_text:
राक्षसाधम रामस्य भार्याममिततेजसः।
इक्ष्वाकुवंशनाथस्य स्तुषां दशरथस्य च ॥ ७१ ॥
अवाच्यं वदतो जिह्वा कथं न पतिता तव।
किंस्विद्वीर्यं तवानार्यं यो मां भर्तुरसंनिधौ ॥ ७२ ॥
अपहत्यागतः पाप तेनादृष्टो महात्मना।
न त्वं रामस्य सदृशो दास्येऽप्यस्य न युज्यसे ॥ ७३ ॥
explanation: “How did your tongue not fall off, O vile ogre, even as you made a proposal which should not be made to the consort of Śrī Rāma, who is endowed with immeasurable strength and daughter-in-law of Emperor Daśaratha, the protector of Ikṣwāku’s line? Of what account is your valour, O ignoble soul, when you came away abducting me stealthily, in the absence of my lord and unperceived by that exalted soul, O sinful one? You are not equal in any respect to Śrī Rāma; nay, you are not fit even to be his slave. (71—73)

shloka_text:
मैथिलीं हन्तुमारब्धः स्त्रीभिर्हाहाकृतं तदा।
स्त्रीणां मध्यात् समुत्पत्य तस्य भार्या दुरात्मनः ॥ ७६ ॥
वरा मन्दोदरी नाम तया स प्रतिषेधितः।
उक्तश्च मधुरां वाणीं तया स मदनार्दितः ॥ ७७ ॥
explanation: “Śrī Rāma, a scion of Raghu, is invincible, truthful of speech, valiant and a lover of war.” Spoken to in these harsh words by Sītā (the daughter of Janaka), Rāvaṇa (the ten-headed monster) blazed up all of a sudden with wrath even like a fire deposited in a funeral pile. Rolling his cruel eyes and raising his right fist, he proceeded to strike the princess of Mithilā. An alarm was then raised by the women. Springing up from their midst, the excellent wife of that evil-minded fellow, Mandodari by name, ran to him. By her he was restrained. Nay, the fellow, who was smitten with love, was spoken to by her in sweet words as follows : (74—77)

shloka_text:
सीतया तव किं कार्यं महेन्द्रसमविक्रम।
मया सह रमस्वाद्य मद्विशिष्टा न जानकी ॥ ७८ ॥
explanation: “What purpose of yours will be served by Sītā, O lord, You, who are equal in prowess to the mighty Indra? Pray, revel with me today; Sītā, the daughter of Janaka, is in no way superior to me. (78)

shloka_text:
देवगन्धर्वकन्याभिर्यक्षकन्याभिरेव च।
सार्धं प्रभो रमस्वेति सीतया किं करिष्यसि ॥ ७९ ॥
explanation: “Nay, sport with the daughters of gods and Gandharvas (celestial musicians) as well as with those of Yakṣas, my lord! You have nothing to do with Sītā.” (79)

shloka_text:
ततस्ताभिः समेताभिर्नारीभिः स महाबलः।
उत्थाप्य सहसा नीतो भवनं स्वं निशाचरः ॥ ८० ॥
explanation: “Having been raised up by those women collectively, that ranger of the night, who was endowed with extraordinary might, was then abruptly conducted back to his residence. (80)

shloka_text:
याते तस्मिन् दशग्रीवे राक्षस्यो विकृताननाः।
सीतां निर्भर्त्सयामासुर्वाक्यैः क्रूरैः सुदारुणैः ॥ ८१ ॥
explanation: “The aforesaid Rāvaṇa (the ten-headed monster) having left, the ogresses with ugly faces, who had been posted there to guard Sītā, threatened her in cruel and very sharp terms. (81)

shloka_text:
तृणवद् भाषितं तासां गणयामास जानकी।
गर्जितं च तथा तासां सीतां प्राप्य निरर्थकम् ॥ ८२ ॥
explanation: “The daughter of Janaka, Sītā, however, accounted their effusion worth no more than straw. Their thundering too was likewise lost on Sītā. (82)

shloka_text:
वृथा गर्जितनिश्चेष्टा राक्षस्यः पिशिताशनाः।
रावणाय शशंसुस्ताः सीताव्यवसितं महत् ॥ ८३ ॥
explanation: “The flesh-eating ogresses, who had become motionless due to their thundering having proved abortive, made known to Rāvaṇa the mighty resolve of Sītā to die rather than to submit to him. (83)

shloka_text:
ततस्ताः सहिताः सर्वा विहताशा निरुद्यमाः।
परिक्लिश्य समस्तास्ता निद्रावशमुपागताः ॥ ८४ ॥
explanation: “Having given up all effort to persuade Sītā to submit to Rāvaṇa, now that their hopes had been frustrated, nay, feeling vexed, they were all collectively as well as individually overpowered by sleep. (84)

shloka_text:
तासु चैव प्रसुप्तासु सीता भर्तृहिते रता।
विलप्य करुणं दीना प्रशुशोच सुदुःखिता ॥ ८५ ॥
explanation: “Wailing piteously, when they had all fallen fast asleep, Sītā, who was devoted to the good of her husband, deeply lamented, miserable and sore distressed as she was. (85)

shloka_text:
तासां मध्यात् समुत्थाय त्रिजटा वाक्यमब्रवीत्।
आत्मानं खादत क्षिप्रं न सीतामसितेक्षणाम् ॥ ८६ ॥
जनकस्यात्मजां साध्वीं स्त्रुषां दशरथस्य च।
स्वप्नो ह्यद्य मया दृष्टो दारुणो रोमहर्षणः ॥ ८७ ॥
रक्षसां च विनाशाय भर्तुरस्या जयाय च।
अलमस्मान् परित्रातुं राघवाद् राक्षसीगणम् ॥ ८८ ॥
explanation: “Rising up from their midst, Trijāta spoke as follows : ‘Sooner feed on yourselves than on the dark-eyed Sītā, daughter of Janaka * SUNDARAKĀṆḌA * 257 and a virtuous daughter-in-law of Emperor Daśaratha. In fact, a fearful dream has been seen by me, which makes my hair stand on end and presages the destruction of ogres and the triumph of her lord. She alone is competent to protect us, the entire host of ogresses from the wrath of Rāma, the scion of Raghu. (86—88)

shloka_text:
अभियाचाम वैदेहीमेतद्वि मम रोचते।
यदि होवविधः स्वप्नो दुःखितायाः प्रदृश्यते ॥ ८९ ॥
सा दुःखैर्विविधैर्मुक्ता सुखमाप्नोत्यनुत्तमम्।
प्रणिपातप्रसन्ना हि मैथिली जनकात्मजा ॥ ९० ॥
explanation: “Let us, therefore, solicit the grace of Sītā, a princess of the Videha territory; for this alone finds favour with me. For, if such a dream is vividly seen about an afflicted lady, she is freed from woes of various kinds and attains unsurpassed felicity. Sītā, daughter of Janaka, will surely be propitiated through mere prostration at her feet. (89-90)

shloka_text:
अलमेषा परित्रातुं राक्षस्यो महतो भयात्।
ततः सा हीमती बाला भर्तुर्विजयहर्षिता ॥ ९१ ॥
अवोचद् यदि तत् तथ्यं भवेयं शरणं हि वः।
तां चाहं तादृशीं दृष्ट्वा सीताया दारुणां दशाम् ॥ ९२ ॥
चिन्तयामास विश्रान्तो न च मे निर्वृतं मनः।
सम्भाषणार्थं च मया जानक्याश्चिन्तितो विधिः ॥ ९३ ॥
explanation: “She alone is competent to deliver the ogresses from the great peril.” Hanumān rejoiced at the prospect of her lord’s triumph on hearing of the dream related to her by Trijāṭā, that youthful lady, Sītā, who was full of modesty, thereupon said, ‘If the dream seen by Trijāṭā comes out to be true, I shall surely afford protection to you all.’ Witnessing such a hard plight of Sītā, I, who had taken some rest in the meantime became thoughtful; my mind, however, was not at rest. A method was also contrived by me to enter into conversation with the daughter of Janaka. (91—93)

shloka_text:
इक्ष्वाकुकुलवंशस्तु स्तुतो मम पुरस्कृतः।
श्रुत्वा तु गदितां वाचं राजर्षिगणभूषिताम् ॥ ९४ ॥
प्रत्यभाषत मां देवी बाष्पैः पिहितलोचना।
कस्त्वं केन कथं चेह प्राप्तो वानरपुङ्गव ॥ ९५ ॥
explanation: “The pedigree of the House of Ikṣwākus, which was placed in the forefront by all even in the past began to be extolled by me. Hearing the speech uttered by me, which was enriched with the praises of a royal sage viz., King Daśaratha, the godlike lady, Sītā, for her part, spoke in return to me as follows, her eyes full of tears: “Who are you? Dispatched by whom and how have you arrived here, O bull among monkeys?” (94-95)

shloka_text:
का च रामेण ते प्रीतिस्तन्मे शंसितुमर्हसि।
तस्यास्तद् वचनं श्रुत्वा अहमप्यबुवं वचः ॥ ९६ ॥
explanation: “Nay, what kind of love is cherished by you for Śrī Rāma? You ought to relate all that to me.” Hearing her aforesaid questionnaire, I too made the following reply: (96)

shloka_text:
देवि रामस्य भर्तुस्ते सहायो भीमविक्रमः।
सुग्रीवो नाम विक्रान्तो वानरेन्द्रो महाबलः ॥ ९७ ॥
explanation: “There is a valiant ally of terrific prowess of your lord, Sugriva by name, the valiant ruler of monkeys, who is endowed with extraordinary might, O godlike lady! (97)

shloka_text:
तस्य मां विद्धि भूत्यं त्वं हनुमन्तमिहागतम्।
भर्त्रा सम्प्रहितस्तुभ्यं रामेणाक्लिष्टकर्मणा ॥ ९८ ॥
explanation: “Know me to be his servant, Hanumān by name, arrived here. I have been duly dispatched by your husband, Śrī Rāma, of unwearied action. (98)

shloka_text:
यदि चेत्त्वं तु मां दर्पात्राभिनन्दसि गर्विते।
द्विमासानन्तरं सीते पास्यामि रुधिरं तव ॥ ६९ ॥
explanation: “If, however, you do not welcome me through vanity. O proud Sītā, I shall drink your blood after two months.’ (99)

shloka_text:
इदं तु पुरुषव्याघ्रः श्रीमान् दाशरथिः स्वयम्।
अङ्गुलीयमभिज्ञानमदात् तुभ्यं यशस्विनि ॥ ९९ ॥
explanation: “Nay, the glorious Śrī Rāma, son of Daśaratha, a tiger among men, has personally handed over as a token this ring for you, O illustrious lady! (99)

shloka_text:
तदिच्छामि त्वयाज्ञसं देवि किं करवाण्यहम्।
रामलक्ष्मणयोः पार्श्वं नयामि त्वां किमुत्तरम् ॥ १०० ॥
explanation: “Therefore, I seek your command, 258 * VĀLMĪKI-RĀMĀYAṆA * O godlike lady, as to what I should do. I can carry you, if you so please, to the presence of Śrī Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa. What is your response? (100)

shloka_text:
एतच्छ्रुत्वा विदित्वा च सीता जनकनन्दिनी।
आह रावणमुत्पाट्य राघवो मां नयत्विति ॥ १०१ ॥
explanation: “Hearing this and knowing the truth, Sītā, the delight of Janaka, replied, ‘Let Śrī Rāma, a scion of Raghu, take me back after destroying Rāvaṇa.’ (101)

shloka_text:
प्रणम्य शिरसा देवीमहमार्यामनिन्दिताम्।
राघवस्य मनोह्लादमभिज्ञानमयाचिषम् ॥ १०२ ॥
explanation: “Having respectfully saluted the godlike noble and irreproachable lady, Sītā, with my head bent low, I asked her for a token which should bring delight to the mind of Śrī Rāma, a scion of Raghu. (102)

shloka_text:
अथ मामब्रवीत् सीता गृह्यतामयमुत्तमः।
मणिर्येन महाबाहू रामस्त्वां बहु मन्यते ॥ १०३ ॥
explanation: “Sītā thereupon said to me, ‘Let this excellent jewel be taken by you, for which the mighty-armed Śrī Rāma will hold you in great esteem.’ (103)

shloka_text:
इत्युक्त्वा तु वरारोहा मणिप्रवरमुत्तमम्।
प्रायच्छत् परमोद्विग्ना वाचा मां संदिदेश ह ॥ १०४ ॥
explanation: “Saying so, Sītā (a lady with lovely limbs), for her part, delivered to me an excellent jewel (the foremost of jewels) for the head and, feeling highly upset, further related to me in so many words one or two incidents known to Śrī Rāma alone. (104)

shloka_text:
ततस्तस्यै प्रणम्याहं राजपुत्र्यै समाहितः।
प्रदक्षिणं परिक्राममिहाभ्युद्गतमानसः ॥ १०५ ॥
explanation: “Having respectfully bowed down to that princess, I thereupon then devoutly went clockwise round her with a mind intent upon returning to this place. (105)

shloka_text:
उत्तरं पुनरेवाह निश्चित्य मनसा तदा।
हनुमन् मम वृत्तान्तं वक्तुमर्हसि राघवे ॥ १०६ ॥
explanation: “Having deliberated with her mind, she then once more addressed the following to me: ‘You ought to relate my story to Śrī Rāma, a scion of Raghu, O Hanumān !’ (106)

shloka_text:
यथा श्रुत्वैव नचिरात् तावुभौ रामलक्ष्मणौ।
सुग्रीवसहितौ वीरावुपेयातां तथा कुरु ॥ १०७ ॥
explanation: “ ‘Nay, act in such a way that immediately on hearing my story both those heroes, Śrī Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, may turn up before long alongwith Sugriva. (107)

shloka_text:
यदन्यथा भवेदेतद् द्वौ मासौ जीवितं मम।
न मां द्रक्ष्यति काकुत्स्थो प्रिये साहमनाथवत् ॥ १०८ ॥
explanation: “ ‘If this proves to be otherwise, my life is to continue only for a month (two fortnights*). If Śrī Rāma does not appear within this period I, as such, shall have to die like one without a protector and Śrī Rāma, a scion of Kakutstha, will no longer be able to see me.’ (108)

shloka_text:
तच्छ्रुत्वा करुणं वाक्यं क्रोधो मामभ्यवर्तत।
उत्तरं च मया दृष्टं कार्यशेषमनन्तरम् ॥ १०९ ॥
explanation: “When I heard that pathetic appeal, anger took possession of me and what remained to be done by me next was forthwith envisaged by me. (109)

shloka_text:
ततोऽवर्धत मे कायस्तदा पर्वतसंनिभः।
युद्धाकाङ्क्षी वनं तस्य विनाशयितुमारभे ॥ ११० ॥
explanation: “My body then began to expand and presently grew to the size of a mountain. Seeking a combat, I forthwith proceeded to devastate the pleasure-grove of Rāvaṇa. (110)

shloka_text:
तद् भयं वनखण्डं तु भ्रान्तत्रस्तमृगद्विजम्।
प्रतिबुद्ध्य निरीक्षन्ते राक्षस्यो विकृताननाः ॥ १११ ॥
explanation: “Waking up from slumber, the ugly faced ogresses beheld that part of the grove laid waste and its beasts and birds bewildered and panic-striken. (111)

shloka_text:
मां च दृष्ट्वा वने तस्मिन् समागम्य ततस्ततः।
ताः समभ्यागताः क्षिप्रं रावणायाचचक्षिरे ॥ ११२ ॥
explanation: “Nay, meeting together from every side on seeing me in the grove, they collectively reported the matter to Rāvaṇa without delay in the following words : (112)

shloka_text:
राजन् वनमिदं दुर्गं तव भग्नं दुरात्मना।
वानरेण ह्यविज्ञाय तव वीर्यं महाबल ॥ ११३ ॥
explanation: “This grove of yours, which is difficult of access, has been destroyed by an evil-minded monkey, who surely does not fully know your power, O king, endowed with extraordinary might ! (113)

shloka_text:
तस्य दुर्बुद्धिता राजंस्तव विप्रियकारिणः।
वधमाज्ञापय क्षिप्रं यथासौ न पुनर्वजेत् ॥ ११४ ॥
explanation: “This is no doubt his perversity, O king ! Pray, therefore, order his death instantly since he has given offence to you lest he should run away unpunished.’ (114)

shloka_text:
तच्छ्रुत्वा राक्षसेन्द्रेण विसृष्टा बहुदुर्जयाः।
राक्षसाः किंकरा नाम रावणस्य मनोऽनुगाः ॥ ११५ ॥
explanation: “On hearing the report, ogres, collectively known as the Kīṅkaras, who were very difficult to conquer and followed the mind of Rāvaṇa, were sent out by the king of ogres. (115)

shloka_text:
तेषामशीतिसाहस्रं शूलमुद्रपाणिनाम्।
मया तस्मिन् वनोद्देशे परिघेण निषूदितम् ॥ ११६ ॥
explanation: “Eighty thousand of them, darts and clubs in hand, were exterminated by me in that part of the grove with an iron bar. (116)

shloka_text:
तेषां तु हतशिष्टा ये ते गता लघुविक्रमाः।
निहतं च मया सैन्यं रावणायाचचक्षिरे ॥ ११७ ॥
explanation: “Taking quick strides, those few for their part, who had survived, went and broke the news to Rāvaṇa of the army having been wiped out by me. (117)

shloka_text:
ततो मे बुद्धिरुत्पन्ना चैत्यप्रासादमुत्तमम्।
तत्रस्थान् राक्षसान् हत्वा शतं स्तम्भेन वै पुनः ॥ ११८ ॥
ललामभूतो लङ्काया मया विध्वंसितो रुषा।
ततः प्रहस्तस्य सुतं जम्बुमालिनमादिशत् ॥ ११९ ॥
राक्षसैर्बहुभिः सार्धं घोररूपैर्भयानकैः।
तमहं बलसम्पन्नं राक्षसं रणकोविदम् ॥ १२० ॥
परिघेणातिघोरेण सूदयामि सहानुगम्।
तच्छ्रुत्वा राक्षसेन्द्रस्तु मन्त्रिपुत्रान् महाबलान् ॥ १२१ ॥
पदातिबलसम्पन्नान् प्रेषयामास रावणः।
परिघेणैव तान् सर्वान् नयामि यमसादनम् ॥ १२२ ॥
explanation: “Next it struck my mind to demolish the excellent edifice of a sanctuary sacred to the tutelary deity of the ogres. After killing a hundred ogres garrisoned there, the sanctuary, which was the very ornament of Laṅkā, was then utterly destroyed by me in anger with a pillar of the same structure. Thereupon Rāvaṇa dispatched Jambumāli, son of Prahasta, alongwith numerous frightful ogres of grim aspect. I killed that mighty ogres, though he was skilled in warfare, alongwith his followers with a most formidable iron bar. Hearing of it, Rāvaṇa, the ruler of ogres, dispatched the sons of his minister, who were endowed with extraordinary might, and were strengthened by a regiment of infantry. I, however, sent them to the abode of Death with the iron bar itself. (118—122)

shloka_text:
मन्त्रिपुत्रान् हतान् श्रुत्वा समरे लघुविक्रमान्।
पञ्च सेनाग्रान् शूरान् प्रेषयामास रावणः ॥ १२३ ॥
explanation: “Hearing of the minister’s sons, who were quick in exhibiting their valour in combat, having been killed, Rāvaṇa dispatched five heroic generals. (123)

shloka_text:
तानहं सहसैन्यान् वै सर्वानेवाभ्यसूदयम्।
ततः पुनर्दशग्रीवः पुत्रमक्षं महाबलम् ॥ १२४ ॥
बहुभी राक्षसैः सार्धं प्रेषयामास संयुगे।
तं तु मन्दोदरीपुत्रं कुमारं रणपण्डितम् ॥ १२५ ॥
सहसा खं समुद्यन्तं पादयोश्च गृहीतवान्।
तमासीनं शतगुणं भ्रामयित्वा व्यपेषयम् ॥ १२६ ॥
explanation: “I, however, destroyed them all alongwith their troops. Thereupon Rāvaṇa, the ten-headed monster, sent to the field of battle his son, Akṣa, who was endowed with extraordinary might, alongwith many other ogres. I, however, suddenly caught by the 260 * VĀLMĪKI-RĀMĀYAṆA * feet the aforesaid prince, son of Mandodari, who was a past master in warfare and was springing in the sky. Nay, whirling him round a hundred times as soon as he was down, I crushed him.” (124—126)

shloka_text:
तमक्षमागतं भर्गं निशम्य स दशाननः।
ततश्चेन्द्रजितं नाम द्वितीयं रावणः सुतम् ॥ १२७ ॥
व्यादिदेश सुसंक्रुद्धो बलिनं युद्धदुर्मदम्।
तच्चाप्यहं बलं सर्वं तं च राक्षसपुङ्गवम् ॥ १२८ ॥
नष्टौजसं रणे कृत्वा परं हर्षमुपागतः।
महतापि महाबाहुः प्रत्ययेन महाबलः ॥ १२९ ॥
प्रहितो रावणेनैष सह वीरैर्मदोद्भूतैः।
सोऽविषहं हि मां बुद्ध्वा स्वसैन्यं चावमर्दितम् ॥ १३० ॥
ब्रह्मणोऽस्त्रेण स तु मां प्रबद्ध्वा चातिवेगिनः।
रज्जुभिश्चापि बध्नन्ति ततो मां तत्र राक्षसाः ॥ १३१ ॥
explanation: “Highly enraged to hear of the celebrated Prince Akṣa having been killed as soon as arrived, that ten-headed monster, Rāvaṇa, thereupon dispatched his other mighty son, Indrajit by name, fierce in combat, with a large army. Having crushed in combat the spirit of that entire force as well as of that bull among ogres, I experienced supreme felicity. Alongwith heroes who were insolent with arrogance, this mighty-armed prince, who was endowed with extraordinary might, had been sent by Rāvaṇa with great confidence. Perceiving his army crushed and consequently realizing me to be irresistible, Indrajit for his part made me captive by means of a missile presided over by Brahmā (the creator) and, having bound me, handed me over to the ogres. Ogres full of excessive agility then began to bind me further with cords on that spot. (127—131)

shloka_text:
रावणस्य समीपं च गृहीत्वा मामुपागमन्।
दृष्ट्वा सम्भाषितश्चाहं रावणेन दुरात्मना ॥ १३२ ॥
पृष्टश्च लङ्कागमनं राक्षसानां च तं वधम्।
तत्सर्वं च रणे तत्र सीतार्थमुपजल्पितम् ॥ १३३ ॥
explanation: “Holding me by the hand, they sought the presence of Rāvaṇa. On seeing me, I was spoken to by the evil-minded Rāvaṇa and questioned about the motive of my visit to Laṅkā and my said destruction of the ogres. ‘All that was done by me in combat for the sake of Sītā !’ was the reply made by me. (132-133)

shloka_text:
तस्यास्तु दर्शनाकाङ्क्षी प्राप्तस्त्वद्भवनं विभो।
मारुतस्यौरसः पुत्रो वानरो हनुमानहम् ॥ १३४ ॥
explanation: I continued: “I am a monkey, Hanumān, an offspring of the wind-god, arrived in your palace with a longing to see Sītā. (134)

shloka_text:
रामदूतं च मां विद्धि सुग्रीवसचिवं कपिम्।
सोऽहं दौत्येन रामस्य त्वत्सकाशमिहागतः ॥ १३५ ॥
explanation: “Further know me to be a monkey, envoy of Śrī Rāma and a minister of Sugrīva. As such I have sought your presence here in the capacity of a messenger of Śrī Rāma. (135)

shloka_text:
शृणु चापि समादेशं यदहं प्रब्रवीमि ते।
राक्षसेश हरीशस्त्वां वाक्यमाह समाहितम् ॥ १३६ ॥
explanation: “I hereby deliver to you, O lord of ogres, the friendly message which Sugrīva, the lord of monkeys, has sent to you. Pray, listen to his advice too. (136)

shloka_text:
सुग्रीवश्च महाभागः स त्वां कौशलमब्रवीत्।
धर्मार्थकामसहितं हितं पथ्यमुवाच ह ॥ १३७ ॥
explanation: “Nay, the celebrated and highly blessed Sugrīva has inquired after your welfare and has tendered this friendly and salutary advice, which is in consonance with righteousness, your worldly interests and enjoyment too. (137)

shloka_text:
वसतो ऋष्यमुके मे पर्वते विपुलदुमे।
राघवो रणविक्रान्तो मित्रत्वं समुपागतः ॥ १३८ ॥
explanation: “While I was sojourning on the Ṛṣyamūka mountain, covered with numerous trees, Śrī Rāma, a scion of Raghu, who is valiant in combat, entered into an alliance with me. (138)

shloka_text:
तेन मे कथितं राजन् भार्या मे रक्षसा हता।
तत्र साहाय्यहेतोर्मे समयं कर्तुमर्हसि ॥ १३९ ॥
explanation: “The following exhortation was * SUNDARAKĀṆḌA * 261 addressed by him, O king, to me: 'My consort has been borne away by an ogre. You ought to give me your pledge to render help in her recovery.' (139)

shloka_text:
वालिना हृतराज्येन सुग्रीवेण सह प्रभुः।
चक्रेऽग्निसाक्षिकं सख्यं राघवः सहलक्ष्मणः ॥ १४० ॥
explanation: 'The powerful Śrī Rāma, who was accompanied by his younger brother, Lakṣmaṇa, solemnized his alliance with me (Sugriva), who had been robbed of my sovereignty by Vāli (my elder brother), in the presence of fire as a witness. (140)

shloka_text:
तेन वालिनमाहत्य शरेणैकेन संयुगे।
वानराणां महाराजः कृतः सम्प्लवतां प्रभुः ॥ १४१ ॥
explanation: 'After killing Vāli with a single arrow on the field of battle, I (Sugriva), the lord of monkeys, was crowned by him suzerain lord of all monkeys. (141)

shloka_text:
तस्य साहाय्यमस्माभिः कार्यं सर्वात्मना त्विह।
तेन प्रस्थापितस्तुभ्यं समीपमिह धर्मतः ॥ १४२ ॥
explanation: 'Help must be rendered to him by us with all our being in this life: with this end in view an envoy has been dispatched by me (Sugriva) to your presence in Laṅkā in accordance with the principles of righteousness. (142)

shloka_text:
क्षिप्रमानीयतां सीता दीयतां राघवस्य च।
यावन्न हरयो वीरा विधमन्ति बलं तव ॥ १४३ ॥
explanation: 'Let Sītā be brought and restored to Śrī Rāma, a scion of Raghu, before the monkey heroes exterminate your forces. (143)

shloka_text:
वानराणां प्रभावोऽयं न केन विदितः पुरा।
देवतानां सकाशं च ये गच्छन्ति निमन्त्रिताः ॥ १४४ ॥
explanation: 'To whom is this glory of the monkeys not already known, who seek the presence even of gods only when invited by the latter for help?' (144)

shloka_text:
इति वानरराजस्वामाहेत्यभिहितो मया।
मामैक्षत ततो रुष्टश्चक्षुषा प्रदहन्निव ॥ १४५ ॥
explanation: 'Sugriva, the ruler of monkeys, has sent the foregoing message to you.' 'Provoked to anger when spoken to in these words by me, Rāvaṇa presently looked at me as though he was going to reduce me to ashes by his very gaze. (145)

shloka_text:
तेन वध्योऽहमाज्ञसो रक्षसा रौद्रकर्मणा।
मत्प्रभावमविज्ञाय रावणेन दुरात्मना ॥ १४६ ॥
explanation: 'I was ordered to be put to death by that ogre of violent deeds, the evil-minded Rāvaṇa, who did not know my glory in the shape of my immunity from death. (146)

shloka_text:
ततो विभीषणो नाम तस्य भ्राता महामतिः।
तेन राक्षसराजश्च याचितो मम कारणात् ॥ १४७ ॥
explanation: 'His younger brother, Vibhīṣaṇa by name, who is endowed with great sagacity, was also present there. By him was Rāvaṇa (the ruler of ogres) solicited on my behalf in the following words: (147)

shloka_text:
नैवं राक्षसशार्दूल त्यज्यतामेष निश्चयः।
राजशास्त्रव्यपेतो हि मार्गः संलक्ष्यते त्वया ॥ १४८ ॥
explanation: 'No such attempt should at all be made, O tiger among the ogres! Let this resolve be abandoned by you. A course which is repugnant to the code governing the conduct of kings is being envisaged by you. (148)

shloka_text:
दूतवध्या न दृष्टा हि राजशास्त्रेषु राक्षस।
दूतेन वेदितव्यं च यथाभिहितवादिना ॥ १४९ ॥
explanation: 'The killing of an envoy is surely not approved of in the codes governing the conduct of rulers, O ogre! The message of his master must be delivered by an envoy, who simply reiterates what he has been told by his master. (149)

shloka_text:
सुमहत्यपराधेऽपि दूतस्यातुलविक्रम।
विरूपकरणं दृष्टं न वधोऽस्ति हि शास्त्रतः ॥ १५० ॥
explanation: 'Even in the event of a very grave offence committed by an envoy, O brother endowed with incomparable prowess, mutilation alone, and not death, has been approved in the scriptures.' (150)

shloka_text:
विभीषणेनैवमुक्तो रावणः संदिदेश तान्।
राक्षसानेतदेवाद्य लाङ्गुलं दह्यतामिति ॥ १५१ ॥
explanation: 262 * VĀLMĪKI-RĀMĀYAṆA * “Exhorted in these words by Vibhīṣaṇa, Rāvaṇa commanded those ogres present by his side as follows : ‘Let the tail alone of the monkey be burnt now.’ (151)

shloka_text:
ततस्तस्य वचः श्रुत्वा मम पुच्छं समन्ततः ।
वेष्टितं शणवल्कैश्च पट्टैः कार्पासकैस्तथा ॥ १५२ ॥
explanation: “On hearing his command, my tail was forthwith wrapped all over in the bark of hemp as well as in rags of silk and cotton. (152)

shloka_text:
राक्षसाः सिद्धसंनाहास्ततस्ते चण्डविक्रमाः ।
तदादीप्यन्त मे पुच्छं हनन्तः काष्ठमुष्टिभिः ॥ १५३ ॥
explanation: “Having wrapped my tail as above, those ogres of terrible prowess then set fire to my aforementioned tail, striking me with their wooden staffs and fists. (153)

shloka_text:
बद्धस्य बहुभिः पाशैर्यन्त्रितस्य च राक्षसैः ।
न मे पीडाभवत् काचिद् दिदृक्षोर्नगरी दिवा ॥ १५४ ॥
explanation: “No pain was experienced by me even though I was bound with many cords and wrapped in rags, since I was eager to survey Laṅkā by the day. (154)

shloka_text:
ततस्ते राक्षसाः शूरा बद्धं मामग्निसंवृतम् ।
अघोषयन् राजमार्गे नगरद्वारमागताः ॥ १५५ ॥
explanation: “Arrived at the city gate, those gallant ogres made me publicly known in the principal streets, bound by cords and my tail enveloped in flames. (155)

shloka_text:
ततोऽहं सुमहद्रूपं संक्षिप्य पुनरात्मनः ।
विमोचयित्वा तं बन्धं प्रकृतिस्थः स्थितः पुनः ॥ १५६ ॥
explanation: “Having contracted my gigantic form once more and thereby unfastened my bonds, I stood in my native form again. (156)

shloka_text:
आयसं परिघं गृह्य तानि रक्षांस्यसूदयम् ।
ततस्तत्रगरद्वारं वेगेन प्लुतवानहम् ॥ १५७ ॥
explanation: “Seizing an iron bar I made short work of those ogres. Then with agility I leapt up that city gate. (157)

shloka_text:
पुच्छेन च प्रदीप्तेन तां पुरीं साङ्गोपुराम् ।
दहाम्यहमसम्भ्रान्तो युगान्ताग्निरिव प्रजाः ॥ १५८ ॥
explanation: “Nay, with my tail inflamed I set fire to that city with its attics and gates without getting confused, even as the fire of universal destruction would burn all created beings. (158)

shloka_text:
विनष्टा जानकी व्यक्तं न ह्यदग्धः प्रदृश्यते ।
लङ्कायाः कश्चिदुद्देशः सर्वा भस्मीकृता पुरी ॥ १५९ ॥
explanation: “ ‘Evidently Sītā, daughter of Janaka, has also perished, since no part of Laṅkā is seen unburnt—the whole city stands reduced to ashes. (159)

shloka_text:
दहता च मया लङ्कां दग्धा सीता न संशयः ।
रामस्य च महत्कार्यं मयेदं विफलीकृतम् ॥ १६० ॥
explanation: “ ‘Even while I was setting fire to Laṅkā, Sītā too has been burnt; there is no doubt about it. Nay, this great purpose of Śrī Rāma has thereby been defeated by me.’ (160)

shloka_text:
इति शोकसमाविष्टश्चिन्तामहमुपागतः ।
ततोऽहं वाचमश्रौषं चारणानां शुभाक्षराम् ॥ १६१ ॥
जानकी न च दग्धेति विस्मयोदन्तभाषिणाम् ।
ततो मे बुद्धिरुत्पन्ना श्रुत्वा तामद्भुतां गिरम् ॥ १६२ ॥
explanation: “Thoroughly possessed by grief, I began to reflect as above. In the meantime I heard the propitious utterance of Cāraṇas (celestial bards), who were narrating a tale of wonder, saying that Janaka’s daughter had not been burnt. When I heard that wondrous speech, the following thought presently occurred to me : (161-162)

shloka_text:
अदग्धा जानकीत्येव निमित्तैश्चोपलक्षितम् ।
दीप्यमाने तु लाङ्गूले न मां दहति पावकः ॥ १६३ ॥
explanation: “ ‘Sītā, daughter of Janaka, has surely escaped being burnt. Nay, this is indicated by the following good omens too. In the first place even though my tail is burning, the fire does not burn me. (163)

shloka_text:
हृदयं च प्रहृष्टं मे वाताः सुरभिगन्धिनः ।
तैर्निमित्तैश्च दृष्टार्थैः कारणैश्च महागुणैः ॥ १६४ ॥
ऋषिवाक्यैश्च दृष्टार्थैरभवं हृष्टमानसः ।
पुनर्दृष्टा च वैदेही विसृष्टश्च तया पुनः ॥ १६५ ॥
explanation: “ ‘My heart too feels extremely rejoiced * SUNDARAKĀṆḌA * 263 and the breezes are laden with sweet odour.' On account of the aforesaid good omens, whose welcome results had been witnessed by me on many an occasion in the past, nay, for very potent reasons such as the glory of Śrī Rāma and Sītā's exclusive devotion to her husband, which led me to conclude that Sītā was alive as also on the strength of the words of the Cāraṇas, who could see everything, which were based on perceived facts, I felt rejoiced in my mind.' Nay, Sītā, a princess of the Videha territory, was seen by me once more and I was granted leave by her again. (164-165)

shloka_text:
ततः पर्वतमासाद्य तत्रारिष्टमहं पुनः।
प्रतिप्लवनमारेभे युष्महर्शनकाङ्क्षया ॥ १६६ ॥
explanation: "Having reached the Ariṣṭa mountain there in Laṅkā, I then proceeded to leap back from that mountain with a longing to see you all. (166)

shloka_text:
ततः श्वसनचन्द्रार्कसिद्धगन्धर्वसेवितम्।
पन्थानमहामाक्रम्य भवतो दृष्टवानिह ॥ १६७ ॥
explanation: "Following the path frequented by the wind, the moon, the sun, the Siddhas and the Gandharvas, I have found you all here. (167)

shloka_text:
राघवस्य प्रसादेन भवतां चैव तेजसा।
सुग्रीवस्य च कार्यार्थं मया सर्वमनुष्ठितम् ॥ १६८ ॥
explanation: "Everything has been accomplished by me through the grace of Śrī Rāma as well as through your boisterous energy, as also for achieving the purpose of King Sugriva. (168)

shloka_text:
एतत् सर्वं मया तत्र यथावदुपपादितम्।
तत्र यत्र कृतं शेषं तत् सर्वं क्रियतामिति ॥ १६९ ॥
explanation: "All this has been duly carried out by me in Laṅkā. Let all that which could not be done there and still remains to be done, be accomplished by you." (169)

Picturing to his fellow monkeys the said plight of Sītā, and feeling that it behoved them all to see Śrī Rāma only after recovering Sītā from Laṅkā, nay, recounting the past heroic exploits of Jāmbavān and others, Hanumān incites them all to have recourse to the arbitrament of war

shloka_text:
एतदाख्याय तत् सर्वं हनुमान् मारुतात्मजः।
भूयः समुपचक्राम वचनं वक्तुमुत्तरम् ॥ १ ॥
explanation: Having narrated all this story to the monkeys assembled there, Hanumān (sprung from the loins of the wind-god) once more proceeded to make his further statement as follows : (1)

shloka_text:
सफलो राघवोद्योगः सुग्रीवस्य च सम्भ्रमः।
शीलमासाद्य सीताया मम च प्रीणितं मनः ॥ २ ॥
explanation: "Fruitful is the endeavour of Śrī Rāma, a scion of Raghu, and the perseverance of Sugriva. Nay, my mind is gratified to witness the chastity of Sītā. (2)

shloka_text:
आर्यायाः सदृशं शीलं सीतायाः प्लवगर्षभाः।
तपसा धारयेल्लोकान् क्रुद्धा वा निर्दहेदपि ॥ ३ ॥
explanation: "The conduct of Sītā is worthy of that noble lady, O jewels among monkeys. She can sustain all the worlds by virtue of her 264 * VĀLMĪKI-RĀMĀYAṆA * asceticism, as also, if enraged, she can reduce them all to ashes. (3)

shloka_text:
सर्वथातिप्रकृष्टोऽसौ रावणो राक्षसेश्वरः।
यस्य तां स्पृशतो गात्रं तपसा न विनाशितम् ॥ ४ ॥
explanation: “That ruler of ogres, Rāvaṇa too, is very rich in asceticism in everyway, in that his body was not destroyed by her askesis even while he laid hands on Sītā. (4)

shloka_text:
न तदग्निशिखा कुर्यात् संस्पृष्टा पाणिना सती।
जनकस्य सुता कुर्याद् यत् क्रोधकलुषीकृता ॥ ५ ॥
explanation: “Even a flame, when fully touched with one's hand, is incapable of doing that harm which Janaka's daughter would if stirred by anger. (5)

shloka_text:
जाम्बवत्प्रमुखान् सर्वाननुज्ञाप्य महाकपीन्।
अस्मिन्नेवंगते कार्ये भवतां च निवेदिते।
न्याय्यं स्म सह वैदेह्या द्रष्टुं तौ पार्थिवात्मजौ ॥ ६ ॥
explanation: “This work of mine in the shape of Sītā's discovery, which has thus been crowned with success, having been reported to you all, it behoves us to raid the pleasance of Rāvaṇa and after recovering Sītā forcibly from the clutches of Rāvaṇa to see those two princes, Śrī Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, alongwith Sītā, a princess of the Videha territory, after taking leave of all the great monkeys headed by Jāmbavān. (6)

shloka_text:
अहमेकोऽपि पर्याप्तः सराक्षसगणां पुरीम्।
तां लङ्कां तरसा हन्तुं रावणं च महाबलम् ॥ ७ ॥
किं पुनः सहितो वीरैर्बलवद्भिः कृतात्मभिः।
कृतास्त्रैः प्लवगैः शक्तैर्भवद्विविजयैषिभिः ॥ ८ ॥
explanation: “Even single handed, I am capable of destroying with my prowess that city of Laṅkā with its host of ogres, and killing Rāvaṇa, who is endowed with extraordinary might, much more so when accompanied by you—heroic, mighty and powerful, monkeys, disciplined of mind, skilled in the use of missiles and eager for victory. (7-8)

shloka_text:
अहं तु रावणं युद्धे ससैन्यं सपुरःसरम्।
सहपुत्रं वधिष्यामि सहोदरयुतं युधि ॥ ९ ॥
explanation: “I, for my part, shall destroy in an encounter on the field of battle Rāvaṇa with his army, those marching before him, his sons and his brothers. (9)

shloka_text:
ब्राह्ममस्त्रं च रौद्रं च वायव्यं वारुणं तथा।
यदि शक्रजितोऽस्त्राणि दुर्निरीक्ष्याणि संयुगे।
तान्यहं निहनिष्यामि विधमिष्यामि राक्षसान् ॥ १० ॥
explanation: “Even though the missiles employed by Indrajit (Rāvaṇa's eldest son) are e.g., those presided over by Brahmā (the creator) and Rudra (the god of destruction) and Vayu (the wind-god) and Varuṇa (the god of water) difficult even to discern on the battlefield, I shall repulse them as well as exterminate the ogres. (10)

shloka_text:
भवतामभ्यनुज्ञातो विक्रमो मे रुणद्धि तम्।
मयातुला विसृष्टा हि शैलवृष्टिर्निरन्तरा ॥ ११ ॥
देवानपि रणे हन्यात् किं पुनस्तान् निशाचरान्।
भवतामननुज्ञातो विक्रमो मे रुणद्धि माम् ॥ १२ ॥
सागरोऽप्यतियाद् वेलां मन्दरः प्रचलेदपि।
न जाम्बवन्तं समरे कम्पयेदरिवाहिनी ॥ १३ ॥
explanation: “If approved by you, my prowess will frustrate him; for an incessant and unequalled shower of rocks discharged by me on the field of battle is enough to destroy even gods, much more so those rangers of the night. So long as it is not approved by you, I keep my vehemence under check. Even the sea may overflow its shores; even Mount Mandāra may move from its position; but no hostile army shall be able to stagger Jāmbavān in combat. (11—13)

shloka_text:
सर्वराक्षससङ्कानां राक्षसा ये च पूर्वजाः।
अलमेकोऽपि नाशाय वीरो वालिसुतः कपिः ॥ १४ ॥
explanation: “The heroic Aṅgada, son of Vāli, alone is equal to the destruction of all Rakṣasa hosts, nay, even of the ogres who were their progenitors. (14)

shloka_text:
प्लवगस्योरुवेगेन नीलस्य च महात्मनः।
मन्दरोऽप्यवशीर्येत किं पुनर्युधि राक्षसाः ॥ १५ ॥
explanation: “Even Mount Mandāra would be shattered in an encounter by the rapid * SUNDARAKĀṆḌA * 265 movement of the thighs of the high-minded monkey, Nila, much more so the ogres. (15)

shloka_text:
सदेवासुरयक्षेषु गन्धर्वैरगपक्षिषु।
मैन्दस्य प्रतियोद्धारं शंसत द्विविदस्य वा ॥ १६ ॥
explanation: “Point out to me a warrior among the demons and Yakṣas including the gods, as well as among the Gandharvas, serpents and birds, who can contend as an equal with Mainda or Dwivida. (16)

shloka_text:
अश्विपुत्रौ महावेगावेतौ प्लवगसत्तमै।
एतयोः प्रतियोद्धारं न पश्यामि रणाजिरे ॥ १७ ॥
explanation: “These two sons of the Aświnikumāras, are endowed with great impetuosity and are the foremost among monkeys. I do not find any match for them on the field of battle. (17)

shloka_text:
मयैव निहता लङ्का दग्धा भस्मीकृता पुरी।
राजमार्गेषु सर्वेषु नाम विश्रावितं मया ॥ १८ ॥
explanation: “By me alone was Laṅkā, the ogress presiding over Laṅkā, laid low and the city set to fire and reduced to ashes. Nay, in all the principal streets the name of Śrī Rāma and others was proclaimed by me as follows: (18)

shloka_text:
जयत्यतिबलो रामो लक्ष्मणश्च महाबलः।
राजा जयति सुग्रीवो राघवेणाभिपालितः ॥ १९ ॥
explanation: “Victorious is Śrī Rāma of exceeding might, as also Lakṣmaṇa, who is endowed with extraordinary might! Victorious is King Sugrīva, who is protected on all sides by Śrī Rāma (a scion of Raghu)! (19)

shloka_text:
अहं कोसलराजस्य दासः पवनसम्भवः।
हनुमानिति सर्वत्र नाम विश्रावितं मया ॥ २० ॥
explanation: “I am Hanumān, a servant of Śrī Rāma, ruler of the kingdom of Kośala, and son of the wind-god.” In this way the name of Śrī Rāma and others was proclaimed by me everywhere. (20)

shloka_text:
अशोकवनिकामध्ये रावणस्य दुरात्मनः।
अधस्ताच्छंशपामूले साध्वी करुणमास्थिता ॥ २१ ॥
राक्षसीभिः परिवृता शोकसंतापकशिता।
मेघरेखापरिवृता चन्द्ररेखेव निष्प्रभा ॥ २२ ॥
explanation: “The virtuous lady Sītā abides in a pitiable condition on the ground at the foot of a Śrīśapā tree in the heart of a grove of Aśoka trees, belonging to the evil-minded Rāvaṇa, surrounded by ogresses, nay, emaciated through grief and agony and bereft of splendour like a digit of the moon veiled by the strip of a cloud. (21-22)

shloka_text:
अचिन्तयन्ती वैदेही रावणं बलदर्पितम्।
पतिव्रता च सुश्रोणी अवष्टब्धा च जानकी ॥ २३ ॥
explanation: “Caring little for Rāvaṇa, who is proud of his might, Sītā of charming limbs, a princess of the Videha territory, who has taken a vow of fidelity to her lord, has been placed under restraint. (23)

shloka_text:
अनुरक्ता हि वैदेही रामे सर्वात्मना शुभा।
अनन्यचित्ता रामेण पौलोमीव पुरन्दरे ॥ २४ ॥
explanation: “Devoted to Śrī Rāma with her whole being, the blessed Sītā, a princess of the Videha territory, has set her mind exclusively on Śrī Rāma even as Śaci (daughter of the demon Pulomā) on Indra. (24)

shloka_text:
तदेकवासःसंवीता रजोध्वस्ता तथैव च।
सा मया राक्षसीमध्ये तर्ज्यमाना मुहुर्मुहुः ॥ २५ ॥
राक्षसीभिर्विरूपाभिर्दृष्टा हि प्रमदावने।
एकवेणीधरा दीना भर्तृचिन्तापरायणा ॥ २६ ॥
explanation: “Clad in a single piece of cloth, which she had on her person even while being borne away by Rāvaṇa, and likewise soiled with dust, she was actually seen by me in a wretched condition in the midst of ogresses in a pleasance, wearing a single braid, absorbed in the thought of her husband and being threatened again and again by mis-shapen ogresses. (25-26)

shloka_text:
अधःशय्या विवर्णाङ्गी पद्मिनीव हिमोदये।
रावणाद् विनिवृत्तार्था मर्तव्यकृतनिश्चया ॥ २७ ॥
explanation: “She stretches herself on the bare ground, has grown pale of body like a lotus plant at the dawn of winter, has utterly refused to have anything to do with Rāvaṇa 266 * VĀLMĪKI-RĀMĀYAṆA * and is determined to die rather than submit to Rāvaṇa. (27)

shloka_text:
कथंचिन्मृगशावाक्षी विश्वासमुपपादिता।
ततः सम्भाषिता चैव सर्वमर्थं प्रकाशिता ॥ २८ ॥
explanation: “Somehow the lady with eyes like those of a fawn was inspired with confidence. She was then talked to and apprised of the whole truth. (28)

shloka_text:
रामसुग्रीवसख्यं च श्रुत्वा प्रीतिमुपागता।
नियतः समुदाचारो भक्तिर्भर्तिरि चोत्तमा ॥ २९ ॥
explanation: “Hearing of the alliance between Śrī Rāma and Sugriva, she experienced joy. Constant is her chastity and supreme is her devotion to her lord. (29)

shloka_text:
यत्र हन्ति दशग्रीवं स महात्मा दशाननः।
निमित्तमात्रं रामस्तु वधे तस्य भविष्यति ॥ ३० ॥
explanation: “Since Sītā does not kill Rāvaṇa by subjecting him to a curse, it is evident that the aforesaid Rāvaṇa is very powerful by virtue of his asceticism. Nevertheless as the great sin incurred by him through the abduction of Sītā has filled his cup of sin to the brim, Śrī Rāma will serve only as an instrument for his death. (30)

shloka_text:
सा प्रकृत्यैव तन्वङ्गी तद्वियोगाच्च कशिता।
प्रतिपत्पाठशीलस्य विद्येव तनुतां गता ॥ ३१ ॥
explanation: “Frail-bodied by her very nature, Sītā has been further reduced through separation from her Lord and has grown thin like the learning of a scholar continuing his studies even on the first day of a lunar fortnight (which must be observed as a complete holiday by students). (31)

shloka_text:
एवमास्ते महाभागा सीता शोकपरायणा।
यदत्र प्रतिकर्तव्यं तत् सर्वमुपकल्प्यताम् ॥ ३२ ॥
explanation: “In this way the highly blessed Sītā remains given over to grief. Let all that be devised which requires to be done by way of a remedy in this behalf.” (32)

Feeling encouraged by the tributes paid to his valour by his fellow monkeys, Prince Aṅgada undertakes to exterminate the entire ogre race including Rāvaṇa and bring back Sītā from Laṅkā. Jāmbavān, however, who is more sagacious and practical-minded, discourages him by recourse to potent counter-arguments

shloka_text:
कृतास्त्रैः प्लवगैः शक्तैर्भवद्विविजयैषिभिः।
वायुसूनोर्बलेनैव दग्धा लङ्केति नः श्रुतम् ॥ ७ ॥
explanation: Hearing the aforesaid narration of Hanumān, Aṅgada (son of Vāli) spoke as follows: “The two mighty monkeys, Mainda and Dwivida (sons of the Aświnikumāras, the twin born physicians of gods), who are endowed with great impetuosity, fell a prey to great vanity due to haughtiness caused by a boon granted in their favour by Brahmā (the grandfather of the entire creation). In order to do honour to the Aświnikumāras, Brahmā (the grandfather of the whole universe) actually bestowed on these two monkeys (Mainda and Dwivida) on a former occasion the incomparable boon in the shape of incapability of being slain by anyone. Having completely routed the mighty army of the gods, the two heroes, who were intoxicated with pride occasioned by this rare boon and were endowed with extraordinary might, quaffed the drink of immortality. Highly enraged, these two alone are actually able to destroy Laṅkā with its horses, chariots and elephants, let alone all the other monkeys. Even single-handed I am capable of destroying with my might the aforesaid city of Laṅkā with its hosts of ogres and killing Rāvaṇa, who is endowed with extraordinary might, much more so when accompanied by you, heroic, mighty and powerful monkeys, disciplined of mind, skilled in the use of missiles and eager for victory. It has just been heard by us that Laṅkā was burnt by the very might of Hanumān (son of the wind-god). (1—7)

shloka_text:
दृष्टा देवी न चानीता इति तत्र निवेदितुम्।
न युक्तमिव पश्यामि भवद्विः ख्यातपौरुषैः ॥ ८ ॥
explanation: “I do not deem it fit to be reported there at Kiṣkindhā by you, whose virility is well-known, that the godlike lady Sītā has been discovered but not recovered. (8)

shloka_text:
नहि वः प्लवने कश्चिन्नापि कश्चित् पराक्रमे।
तुल्यः सामरदैत्येषु लोकेषु हरिसत्तमाः ॥ ९ ॥
explanation: “None among the inhabitants of all the worlds, including gods and demons, is your match in leaping or in valour, O jewels among the monkeys! (9)

shloka_text:
जित्वा लङ्कां सरक्षौघां हत्वा तं रावणं रणे।
सीतामादाय गच्छामः सिद्धार्था हृष्टमानसाः ॥ १० ॥
explanation: “Conquering Laṅkā with its hosts of ogres, and killing the notorious Rāvaṇa in an encounter, and taking Sītā back, we should all return to Kiṣkindhā, accomplished of purpose and rejoiced at heart. (10)

shloka_text:
तेष्वेवं हतवीरेषु राक्षसेषु हनूमता।
किमन्यदत्र कर्तव्यं गृहीत्वा याम जानकीम् ॥ ११ ॥
explanation: “When the valiant among the ogres have thus been killed by Hanumān, what else remains to be done at this hour? Let us, therefore, return taking the daughter of Janaka with us. (11)

shloka_text:
रामलक्ष्मणयोर्मध्ये न्यस्याम जनकात्मजाम्।
किं व्यलीकैस्तु तान् सर्वान् वानरान् वानरर्षभान् ॥ १२ ॥
explanation: “Let us take and place the daughter of Janaka between Śrī Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa. What shall we gain by unnecessarily burdening the monkeys assembled at Kiṣkindhā, who are all jewels among monkeys, with hardships involved in leaping across the sea? (12)

shloka_text:
वयमेव हि गत्वा तान् हत्वा राक्षसपुङ्गवान्।
राघवं द्रष्टुमर्हामः सुग्रीवं सहलक्ष्मणम् ॥ १३ ॥
explanation: “Going to Laṅkā and making short work of those jewels among ogres, we ourselves should actually see Śrī Rāma (a scion of Raghu), accompanied by Lakṣmaṇa, as well as Sugriva.” (13)

shloka_text:
तमेवं कृतसंकल्पं जाम्बवान् हरिसत्तमः।
उवाच परमप्रीतो वाक्यमर्थवदर्थवित् ॥ १४ ॥
explanation: To Aṅgada, who had resolved as above, Jāmbavān, the foremost of monkeys and bears, who knew the truth, and felt highly pleased, made the following significant reply: (14)

shloka_text:
नैषा बुद्धिर्महाबुद्धे यद् ब्रवीषि महाकपे।
विचेतुं वयमाज्ञा दक्षिणां दिशमुत्तमाम् ॥ १५ ॥
नानेतुं कपिराजेन नैव रामेण धीमता।
कथंचिन्निर्जितां सीतामस्माभिर्नाभिरोचयेत् ॥ १६ ॥
राघवो नृपशार्दूलः कुलं व्यपदिशन् स्वकम्।
प्रतिज्ञाय स्वयं राजा सीताविजयमग्रतः ॥ १७ ॥
सर्वेषां कपिमुख्यानां कथं मिथ्या करिष्यति।
विफलं कर्म च कृतं भवेत् तुष्टिनं तस्य च ॥ १८ ॥
वृथा च दर्शितं वीर्यं भवेद् वानरपुङ्गवाः।
तस्माद् गच्छाम वै सर्वे यत्र रामः सलक्ष्मणः।
सुग्रीवश्च महातेजाः कार्यस्यास्य निवेदने ॥ १९ ॥
explanation: "What you say, O mighty monkey of great understanding, is not wisdom. We were enjoined only to explore the excellent southern quarter, and not to bring back Sītā either by Sugrīva, the ruler of monkeys, or by the sagacious Śrī Rāma. In the name of his own race Śrī Rāma, a scion of Raghu, a veritable tiger among kings, may not like Sītā having anyhow been won by us. Having taken a vow before all the leading monkeys that he would win back Sītā himself, how will he falsify his vow? The work accomplished by Hanumān will then have been rendered fruitless nor will his pleasure be won and the valour exhibited in winning back Sītā will also prove infructuous, O bulls among monkeys! Therefore, in order to report this achievement of Hanumān, let us all actually return to where Śrī Rāma, accompanied by Lakṣmaṇa, and Sugrīva, who is endowed with extraordinary energy, are. (15—19)

shloka_text:
न तावदेशा मतिरक्षमा नो
यथा भवान् पश्यति राजपुत्र।
यथा तु रामस्य मतिर्निविष्टा
तथा भवान् पश्यतु कार्यसिद्धिम् ॥ २० ॥
explanation: "This suggestion of yours, the way in which you are thinking, O prince, is not at all such as we may not be able to carry out. But devise you the means to accomplish our purpose according to the decision arrived at by Śrī Rāma." (20)

Set out from the Mahendra mountain in the direction of Kiṣkindhā, the monkeys halt at Madhuvana, a grove guarded by the monkey Dadhimukha, and most beloved of Sugrīva, which falls on their way. When the monkeys began to enjoy the fruits of the grove with the permission of Prince Aṅgada, Dadhimukha, comes in their way and is lacerated with their claws and teeth

shloka_text:
ततो जाम्बवतो वाक्यमगृह्णन्त वनौकसः।
अङ्गदप्रमुखा वीरा हनुमांश्च महाकपिः ॥ १ ॥
explanation: The heroic monkeys headed by Aṅgada, as well as the great monkey, Hanumān, thereupon accepted the advice of Jāmbavān. (1)

shloka_text:
सभान्यमानं भूतैस्तमात्मवन्तं महाबलम्।
हनुमन्तं महावेगं वहन्त इव दृष्टिभिः ॥ ४ ॥
राघवे चार्थनिर्वृत्तिं कर्तुं च परमं यशः।
समाधाय समृद्धार्थाः कर्मसिद्धिभिरुन्नताः ॥ ५ ॥
explanation: Having made up their mind to accomplish the purpose of Śrī Rāma, a scion of Raghu, and to bring the highest renown to him, and leaping from the aforesaid summit of the Mahendra mountain, all the jewels among monkeys—who were gigantic like the Meru and Mandāra mountains and resembled lordly elephants in rut, and were endowed with extraordinary might, nay, who were accomplished of purpose and felt exalted due to successes in their undertakings, leapt forward in the direction of Kīskindhā, full of joy, with Hanumān (son of the wind-god) at their head, covering the space, as it were, nay, bearing the celebrated, self-possessed and exceptionally mighty Hanumān, who was endowed with great impetuosity and was being honoured by heavenly beings by their gazes, as it were. (2—5)

shloka_text:
प्रियाख्यानोन्मुखाः सर्वे सर्वे युद्धाभिनन्दिनः।
सर्वे रामप्रतीकारे निश्चितार्था मनस्विनः ॥ ६ ॥
explanation: All were keen to break the pleasant tidings; all hailed war and all were determined to assist Śrī Rāma in subduing Rāvaṇa, and were high-minded. (6)

shloka_text:
प्लवमानाः खमाप्लुत्य ततस्ते काननौकसः।
नन्दनोपममासेदुर्वनं द्रुमशतायुतम् ॥ ७ ॥
explanation: Bounding into the air, the aforesaid monkeys arrived, leaping at a grove full of hundreds of trees and vying with the Nandana grove in paradise. (7)

shloka_text:
यत् तन्मधुवनं नाम सुग्रीवस्याभिरक्षितम्।
अधृष्यं सर्वभूतानां सर्वभूतमनोहरम् ॥ ८ ॥
यद् रक्षति महावीरः सदा दधिमुखः कपिः।
मातुलः कपिमुखस्य सुग्रीवस्य महात्मनः ॥ ९ ॥
ते तद् वनमुपागम्य बभूवुः परमोत्कटाः।
वानरा वानरेन्द्रस्य मनःकान्तं महावनम् ॥ १० ॥
explanation: Those monkeys felt supremely eager to partake of the honey etc., in which the grove abounded or reaching that grove, Madhuvana by name, belonging to Sugrīva, which was an extensive grove protected on all sides, and as such inviolable for all created beings, nay, which captivated the soul of all created beings, which was constantly guarded by the exceptionally gallant monkey, Dadhimukha, maternal uncle of the high-souled Sugrīva, the foremost of monkeys, and which was pleasing to the mind, O Sugrīva, the ruler of monkeys. (8—10)

shloka_text:
ततस्ते वानरा हृष्टा दृष्ट्वा मधुवनं महत्।
कुमारमभ्ययाचन्तं मधूनि मधुपिङ्गलाः ॥ ११ ॥
explanation: Rejoiced to see the extensive Madhuvana, the aforesaid monkeys, who were reddish brown as honey, thereupon asked Prince Aṅgada for permission to taste the honey. (11)

shloka_text:
ततः कुमारस्तान् वृद्धाञ्जाम्बवत्प्रमुखान् कपीन्।
अनुमान्य ददौ तेषां निसर्गं मधुभक्षणे ॥ १२ ॥
explanation: Securing the consent of those elderly monkeys headed by Jāmbavān, the prince then granted them permission to partake of the honey. (12)

shloka_text:
ते निसृष्टाः कुमारेण धीमता वालिसूनुना।
हरयः समपद्यन्तं द्रुमान् मधुकराकुलान् ॥ १३ ॥
explanation: Authorized by the sagacious Prince Aṅgada (son of Vāli), those monkeys approached the trees swarming with bees. (13)

shloka_text:
भक्षयन्तः सुगन्धीनि मूलानि च फलानि च।
जग्मुः प्रहर्षं ते सर्वे बभूवुश्च मदोत्कटाः ॥ १४ ॥
explanation: Feasting on the fragrant roots and fruits too, they all experienced great joy and got excited through drink. (14)

shloka_text:
ततश्चानुमताः सर्वे सुसंहृष्टा वनौकसः।
मुदिताश्च ततस्ते च प्रनृत्यन्ति ततस्ततः ॥ १५ ॥
explanation: Having been granted permission by Aṅgada to partake of the honey, all the 270 * VĀLMĪKI-RĀMĀYAṆA * monkeys now felt extremely delighted. Nay, feeling rejoiced, they then began to dance merrily here and there. (15)

shloka_text:
गायन्ति केचित् प्रहसन्ति केचि-
वृत्त्यन्ति केचित् प्रणमन्ति केचित्।
पतन्ति केचित् प्रचरन्ति केचित्
प्लवन्ति केचित् प्रलपन्ति केचित् ॥ १६ ॥
explanation: While some sang, others laughed to their heart's content, still others danced, while many more meekly bowed down. Again, some fell down, others moved quickly, still others bounded and some more raved. (16)

shloka_text:
परस्परं केचिदुपाश्रयन्ति
परस्परं केचिदतिब्रुवन्ति।
दुमाद् दुमं केचिदभिद्रवन्ति
क्षितौ नगाग्रात्रिपतन्ति केचित् ॥ १७ ॥
explanation: Some leaned against one another, others disputed with one another, still others ran from one tree to another while many more jumped to the ground from tree-tops. (17)

shloka_text:
महीतलात् केचिदुदीर्णवेगा
महादुमाग्राण्यभिसम्पतन्ति ।
गायन्तमन्यः प्रहसन्नुपैति
हसन्तमन्यः प्ररुदन्नुपैति ॥ १८ ॥
explanation: Some with increased impetuosity flew to the top of gigantic trees from the earth's surface. While one was singing, another approached him laughing to his heart's content; and while one was laughing, another went up to him weeping bitterly. (18)

shloka_text:
तुदन्तमन्यः प्रणदन्नुपैति
समाकुलं तत् कपिसैन्यमासीत्।
न चात्र कश्चिन्न बभूव मत्तो
न चात्र कश्चिन्न बभूव दूतः ॥ १९ ॥
explanation: While one was pinching another, a third approached the former roaring. In short, greatly excited was that entire army of monkeys. None in that army was not drunk; and none in that army was not haughty. (19)

shloka_text:
ततो वनं तत् परिभक्ष्यमाणं
दुमांश्च विध्वंसितपत्रपुष्पान्।
समीक्ष्य कोपाद् दधिवक्त्रनामा
निवारयामास कपिः कपीस्तान् ॥ २० ॥
explanation: Perceiving that grove being wrecked and the trees stripped off their leaves and blossom, the monkey named Dadhimukha (who had been placed in charge of the grove by King Sugriva) angrily checked the aforesaid monkeys. (20)

shloka_text:
स तैः प्रवृद्धैः परिभत्स्यमानो
वनस्य गोप्ता हरिवृद्धवीरः।
चकार भूयो मतिमुग्रतेजा
वनस्य रक्षां प्रति वानरेभ्यः ॥ २१ ॥
explanation: While being upbraided by those arrogant monkeys, that elderly hero among the monkeys, who guarded the grove, and was endowed with terrific energy, further contemplated the means of protecting the grove against the monkeys. (21)

shloka_text:
उवाच कांश्चित् परुषाण्यभीत-
मसक्तमन्यांश्च तलैर्जघान।
समेत्य कैश्चित् कलहं चकार
तथैव साम्नोपजगाम कांश्चित् ॥ २२ ॥
explanation: He dauntlessly spoke harsh words to some, while others he smote immediately with his palms; coming at close quarters with others, he wrangled with them, while still others he approached with soothing words. (22)

shloka_text:
स तैर्मदादप्रतिवार्यवेगै-
र्बलाच्च तेन प्रतिवार्यमाणैः।
प्रधर्षणे त्यक्तभयैः समेत्य
प्रकृष्यते चाप्यनवेक्ष्य दोषम् ॥ २३ ॥
explanation: Dadhimukha began to be dragged violently by those monkeys, who were being forcibly checked by him even though their vehemence had become irresistible due to their inebriety, nay, who had cast away all fear and who had joined together, taking no account of the guilt involved in assaulting a servant of the king. (23)

shloka_text:
नखैस्तुदन्तो दशनैर्दशान्त-
स्तलैश्च पादैश्च समापयन्तः।
मदात् कपिं ते कपयः समन्ता-
न्महावनं निर्विषयं च चक्रुः ॥ २४ ॥
explanation: Scratching Dadhimukha with their claws, biting him with their teeth and taking the life out of him, as it were, with their slaps and kicks in their drunkenness, the aforesaid monkeys divested that extensive grove on all sides of all its edibles in the shape of fruits, honey and roots etc. (24)

Having entered Madhuvana and partaken of honey, as permitted by Hanumān, and singing and dancing like drunken people, the monkeys were forbidden by those guarding the grove and they belaboured the latter. Repulsed by them, the guards reported the matter to their leader, Dadhimukha, who appeared on the scene with his entourage and on remonstrating with the monkeys was thrashed by Aṅgada, who dashed him to the ground. The guards headed by Dadhimukha then move en masse to Kiṣkindhā to report the matter to Sugrīva and bow down at the latter's feet

shloka_text:
तानुवाच हरिश्रेष्ठो हनुमान् वानरर्षभः।
अव्यग्रमनसो यूयं मधु सेवत वानराः ॥ १ ॥
explanation: Hanumān, the foremost of monkeys and a veritable jewel among them, spoke to them as follows: "With an undisturbed mind enjoy you the honey, O monkeys!" (1)

shloka_text:
अहमावर्जयिष्यामि युष्माकं परिपन्थिनः।
श्रुत्वा हनुमतो वाक्यं हरीणां प्रवरोऽङ्गदः ॥ २ ॥
प्रत्युवाच प्रसन्नात्मा पिबन्तु हरयो मधु।
अवश्यं कृतकार्यस्य वाक्यं हनुमतो मया ॥ ३ ॥
अकार्यमपि कर्तव्यं किमङ्गं पुनरीदृशम्।
अङ्गदस्य मुखाच्छ्रुत्वा वचनं वानरर्षभाः ॥ ४ ॥
साधु साध्विति संहृष्टा वानराः प्रत्यपूजयन्।
पूजयित्वाङ्गदं सर्वे वानरा वानरर्षभम् ॥ ५ ॥
जग्मुर्मधुवनं यत्र नदीवेग इव दुमम्।
ते प्रविष्टा मधुवनं पालानाक्रम्य शक्तितः ॥ ६ ॥
अतिसर्गाच्च पटवो दृष्ट्वा श्रुत्वा च मैथिलीम्।
पपुः सर्वे मधु तदा रसवत् फलमाददुः ॥ ७ ॥
explanation: "I shall ward off those who hinder you." Delighted at heart to hear the exhortation of Hanumān, Aṅgada, the most eminent of monkeys, echoed his words as follows: "Let the monkeys drink honey. The direction of Hanumān, who has accomplished his errand, must be followed by me even if it is not worth following, much more an advice of this type which is worth following, O dear ones!" Highly rejoiced to hear the compliment coming from the lips of Aṅgada, the monkeys, who were the foremost of their class, approved it, saying "Excellent! Bravo!!" Applauding Aṅgada, the foremost of monkeys, all the monkeys proceeded once more to the site where Madhuvana was, even as the strong 272 * VĀLMĪKI-RĀMĀYAṆA * current of a river would rush towards a tree standing on its bank. Having penetrated deep into Madhuvana after overpowering the guards by dint of their superior might, all the monkeys—who felt exceptionally strong due to the permission granted by Aṅgada to enjoy the produce of the grove and because Hanumān had seen Sītā, princess of Mithilā, and others had heard of her being present in Laṅkā, drank honey on that happy occasion and gathered the delicious fruits to enjoy them. (2—7)

shloka_text:
उत्पत्य च ततः सर्वे वनपालान् समागतान्।
ते ताडयन्तः शतशः सक्ता मधुवने तदा ॥ ८ ॥
explanation: Jumping up and thrashing the guards of the grove, who had come together to hinder them, all the monkeys then became engaged in hundreds in gathering the fruit etc., in Madhuvana on that occasion. (8)

shloka_text:
मधूनि द्रोणमात्राणि बाहुभिः परिगृह्य ते।
पिबन्ति कपयः केचित् सङ्कुशस्तत्र हृष्टवत् ॥ ९ ॥
explanation: Holding with their arms honeycombs weighing a Droṇa (approx. 30 Kg.) each, some monkeys in that grove quaffed the honey in groups to their heart's content. (9)

shloka_text:
घ्नन्ति स्म सहिताः सर्वे भक्षयन्ति तथापरे।
केचित् पीत्वापविध्यन्ति मधूनि मधुपिङ्गलाः ॥ १० ॥
explanation: All the monkeys, who were reddish brown like honey, broke the honeycombs together, while others partook of the honey contained in those combs, while still others threw away the combs after drinking the honey. (10)

shloka_text:
मधूच्छिष्टेन केचिच्च जघ्नुरन्योन्यमुक्तटाः।
अपरे वृक्षमूलेषु शाखा गृह्य व्यवस्थिताः ॥ ११ ॥
explanation: Others, who were intoxicated, pelted one another with balls of wax, while still others stood rooted at the foot of trees, seizing the boughs. (11)

shloka_text:
अत्यर्थं च मदग्लानाः पर्णान्यास्तीर्यं शेरते।
उन्मत्तवेगाः प्लवगा मधुमत्ताश्च हृष्टवत् ॥ १२ ॥
explanation: Feeling utterly languid through inebriety, monkeys, who were drunk with honey and possessed the impetuosity of a madman, lay down, full of joy, spreading leaves on the ground. (12)

shloka_text:
क्षिपन्त्यपि तथान्योन्यं स्वलन्ति च तथापरे।
केचित् क्ष्वेडान् प्रकुर्वन्ति केचित् कूजन्ति हृष्टवत् ॥ १३ ॥
explanation: Others, likewise, insulted one another, while others stumbled down. Some roared like lions, while others, full of joy, whistled like birds. (13)

shloka_text:
हरयो मधुना मत्ताः केचित् सुमा महीतले।
धृष्टाः केचिद्वसन्त्यन्ये केचित् कुर्वन्ति चेतरत् ॥ १४ ॥
explanation: Drunk with honey, some monkeys lay down to repose on the earth's surface, while other impudent monkeys laughed, while still others did the reverse, i.e., wept. (14)

shloka_text:
कृत्वा केचिद् वदन्त्यन्ये केचिद् बुध्यन्ति चेतरत्।
येऽप्यत्र मधुपालाः स्युः प्रेष्या दधिमुखस्य तु ॥ १५ ॥
explanation: Having done one thing, some monkeys pretended to have done something else, while still others construed their acts in a different way. (15)

shloka_text:
तेऽपि तैर्वानरैर्भीमैः प्रतिषिद्धा दिशो गताः।
जानुभिश्च प्रघृष्टाश्च देवमार्गं च दर्शिताः ॥ १६ ॥
explanation: Hindered in their duty by those terrible monkeys, even the aforesaid servants of Dadhimukha, who for their part guarded the honey in this grove, fled in all directions. Nay, they were dragged by their knees and, further seized by their feet, were tossed up in the air. (16)

shloka_text:
अब्रुवन् परमोद्विग्ना गत्वा दधिमुखं वचः।
हनुमता दत्तवैरर्हतं मधुवनं बलात्।
वयं च जानुभिर्घृष्टा देवमार्गं च दर्शिताः ॥ १७ ॥
explanation: Approaching Dadhimukha, greatly alarmed as they were, they submitted as follows : “Madhuvana has been forcibly laid waste by the monkeys, who had been granted by Hanumān, the privilege to enjoy the fruits etc., of the grove. Nay, we too * SUNDARAKĀṆḌA * 273 were dragged by the knees and, seized by the feet, tossed up in the air.” (17)

shloka_text:
तदा दधिमुखः क्रुद्धो वनपस्तत्र वानरः।
हतं मधुवनं श्रुत्वा सान्त्वयामास तान् हरीन् ॥ १८ ॥
एतागच्छत गच्छामो वानरानतिदर्पितान्।
बलेनावारयिष्यामि प्रभुञ्जानान् मधूतम् ॥ १९ ॥
explanation: Incensed to hear of Madhuvana having been devastated by the monkeys, Dadhimukha, whose duty it was to guard the grove, consoled the reporting monkeys on that occasion as follows : “Come along, come away; let us approach the highly arrogant monkeys. I shall forcibly ward off the monkeys feasting on the excellent honey.” (18-19)

shloka_text:
श्रुत्वा दधिमुखस्येदं वचनं वानरर्षभाः।
पुनर्वीरा मधुवनं तेनैव सहिता ययुः ॥ २० ॥
explanation: Hearing this assurance of Dadhimukha, the aforesaid heroic jewels among monkeys retraced their steps to Madhuvana, accompanied by Dadhimukha himself. (20)

shloka_text:
मध्ये चैषां दधिमुखः सुप्रगृह्य महातरम्।
समभ्यधावन् वेगेन सर्वे ते च प्लवंगमाः ॥ २१ ॥
explanation: Nay, uprooting and firmly seizing a huge tree, Dadhimukha took up his position in their midst. And all the aforesaid monkeys ran with all speed in the direction of Madhuvana. (21)

shloka_text:
ते शिलाः पादपांश्चैव पाषाणानपि वानराः।
गृहीत्वाभ्यागमन् क्रुद्धा यत्र ते कपिकुञ्जराः ॥ २२ ॥
explanation: Seizing rocks and trees as well as slabs of stone, those monkeys arrived, full of rage, at the place where those elephants among monkeys were. (22)

shloka_text:
बलात्रिवारयन्तश्च आसेदुर्हरयो हरीन्।
संदष्टौष्ठपुटाः क्रुद्धा भर्त्सयन्तो मुहुर्मुहुः ॥ २३ ॥
explanation: Forcibly hindering the monkeys, nay, biting their lips in rage and threatening them again and again, the monkeys came near them. (23)

shloka_text:
अथ दृष्ट्वा दधिमुखं क्रुद्धं वानरपुङ्गवाः।
अभ्यधावन्त वेगेन हनुमत्प्रमुखास्तदा ॥ २४ ॥
explanation: Seeing Dadhimukha enraged, the aforesaid bulls among monkeys, headed by Hanumān, forthwith ran with all speed to meet them on that occasion. (24)

shloka_text:
सवृक्षं तं महाबाहुमापतन्तं महाबलम्।
वेगवन्तं विजग्राह बाहुभ्यां कुपितोऽङ्गदः ॥ २५ ॥
explanation: Full of rage, Aṅgada clasped tightly by his arms the mighty-armed Dadhimukha, who was endowed with extraordinary might and was rushing with all speed, tree in hand. (25)

shloka_text:
मदान्धो न कृपां चक्रे आर्यकोऽयं ममेति सः।
अथैनं निष्पिषाशु वेगेन वसुधातले ॥ २६ ॥
explanation: Blinded with intoxication, he did not show any mercy to him on the score of his being his granduncle. Nay, causing him at once to fall down, he began to rub him against the ground with vehemence. (26)

shloka_text:
स भगबाहूरुमुखो विह्वलः शोणितोक्षितः।
प्रमुमोह महावीरो मुहूर्तं कपिकुञ्जरः ॥ २७ ॥
explanation: Having completely lost control over himself, nay, bathed in blood, his arms, thighs and face broken, that elephant among monkeys, an eminent hero, fainted away for a moment. (27)

shloka_text:
स कर्थचिद् विमुक्तस्तैर्वानरैर्वानरर्षभः।
उवाचैकान्तमागत्य स्वान् भृत्यान् समुपागतान् ॥ २८ ॥
explanation: Withdrawing to a secluded corner when let go somehow by those monkeys, that jewel among monkeys spoke as follows to his subordinates, who had come very near: (28)

shloka_text:
एतागच्छत गच्छामो भर्ता नो यत्र वानरः।
सुग्रीवो विपुलग्रीवः सह रामेण तिष्ठति ॥ २९ ॥
explanation: “Come along, come away; we shall proceed to where the thick-necked monkey, Sugriva, our master, is staying with Śrī Rāma. (29)

shloka_text:
सर्वं चैवाङ्गदे दोषं श्रावयिष्याम पार्थिवे।
अमर्षी वचनं श्रुत्वा घातयिष्यति वानरान् ॥ ३० ॥
explanation: “Nay, we shall make known to the king 274 * VĀLMĪKI-RĀMĀYAṆA * all the misconduct of Aṅgada. Full of indignation he will cause the offending monkeys to be put to death on hearing our complaint. (30)

shloka_text:
इष्टं मधुवनं ह्येतत् सुग्रीवस्य महात्मनः ।
पितृपैतामहं दिव्यं देवैरपि दुरासदम् ॥ ३१ ॥
explanation: “For, this wonderful Madhuvana, which has been inherited by him from his forefathers and is difficult to approach even for gods, is dear to the high-souled Sugriva. (31)

shloka_text:
स वानरानिमान् सर्वान् मधुलुब्धान् गतायुषः ।
घातयिष्यति दण्डेन सुग्रीवः ससुहृज्जनान् ॥ ३२ ॥
explanation: “The celebrated Sugriva will cause to be killed by way of punishment all these monkeys—avid for honey, whose sands of life have already run out—alongwith their near and dear ones. (32)

shloka_text:
वध्या ह्येते दुरात्मानो नृपाज्ञापरिपन्थिनः ।
अमर्षप्रभवो रोषः सफलो मे भविष्यति ॥ ३३ ॥
explanation: “These evil-minded monkeys, deserve to be killed because they have flouted the royal command. Born of indignation, my wrath will bear fruit only then.” (33)

shloka_text:
एवमुक्त्वा दधिमुखो वनपालान् महाबलः ।
जगाम सहसोत्पत्य वनपालैः समन्वितः ॥ ३४ ॥
explanation: Having spoken as aforesaid to the guards of the grove, and springing up all at once, Dadhimukha, who was endowed with extraordinary might, departed for Kīṣkindhā, duly accompanied by the guards of the grove. (34)

shloka_text:
निमेषान्तरमात्रेण स हि प्राप्तो वनालयः ।
सहस्रांशुसुतो धीमान् सुग्रीवो यत्र वानरः ॥ ३५ ॥
explanation: In the mere twinkling of an eye the aforesaid monkey actually reached the place where the sagacious monkey, Sugriva, son of the sun god, was. (35)

shloka_text:
रामं च लक्ष्मणं चैव दृष्ट्वा सुग्रीवमेव च ।
समप्रतिष्ठां जगतीमाकाशान्निपपात ह ॥ ३६ ॥
explanation: Beholding from a distance Śrī Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa too, as well as Sugriva, he descended to a level ground from the airspace: so the tradition goes. (36)

shloka_text:
स निपत्य महावीरः सर्वैस्तैः परिवारितः ।
हरिर्दधिमुखः पालैः पालानां परमेश्वरः ॥ ३७ ॥
स दीनवदनो भूत्वा कृत्वा शिरसि चाञ्जलिम् ।
सुग्रीवस्याशु तौ मूर्ध्ना चरणौ प्रत्यपीडयत् ॥ ३८ ॥
explanation: Coming down, surrounded by all the aforesaid guards, nay, wearing a miserable aspect and placing his joined palms over his head, that monkey, Dadhimukha, the paramount leader of those guards, who was a great hero, forthwith pressed the well-known feet of Sugriva with his head. (37-38)

Having heard from the mouth of Dadhimukha the story of Madhuvana having been laid waste by the monkeys, Sugrīva concludes from the jubilation of the monkeys that Sītā has been traced out. Comforting Dadhimukha, he asks him to send Aṅgada and others without delay

shloka_text:
ततो मूर्ध्ना निपतितं वानरं वानरर्षभः ।
दृष्ट्वैवोद्विग्रहदयो वाक्यमेतदुवाच ह ॥ १ ॥
explanation: Feeling anxious at heart on seeing the monkey Dadhimukha fallen flat with his head touching the ground, Sugrīva, the foremost of monkeys, forthwith spoke as follows: so it is said: (1)

shloka_text:
उत्तिष्ठोत्तिष्ठ कस्मात् त्वं पादयोः पतितो मम ।
अभयं ते प्रदास्यामि सत्यमेवाभिधीयताम् ॥ २ ॥
explanation: “Stand up, rise! Why are you lying prostrate at my feet? I shall grant you immunity from all fear: let the bare truth be spoken. (2)

shloka_text:
किं सम्भ्रमाद्भितं कृत्स्नं ब्रूहि यद् वक्तुमर्हसि ।
कच्चिन्मधुवने स्वस्ति श्रोतुमिच्छामि वानर ॥ ३ ॥
explanation: “Through whose fear have you come? Speak out that which is wholly conducive to our interest, since you are free to speak anything you like. I hope all is well with Madhuvana. I wish to hear everything from you, O monkey!” (3)

shloka_text:
स समाश्वासितस्तेन सुग्रीवेण महात्मना ।
उत्थाय स महाप्राज्ञो वाक्यं दधिमुखोऽब्रवीत् ॥ ४ ॥
explanation: Getting up when fully comforted in the foregoing words by the aforesaid Sugrīva, who had a lofty mind, that highly sagacious monkey, Dadhimukha, spoke as follows: (4)

shloka_text:
नैवक्षरजसा राजन् न त्वया न च वालिना ।
वनं निसृष्टपूर्वं ते नाशितं तत्तु वानरैः ॥ ५ ॥
explanation: “That grove Madhuvana, which had never before suffered either by your father Ṛkṣarāja or by yourself or even by your elder brother and predecessor, Vāli, to be freely enjoyed by anyone, has been actually laid waste by the monkeys, O king! (5)

shloka_text:
न्यवारयमहं सर्वान् सहैर्भिर्वनचारिभिः ।
अचिन्तयित्वा मां हृष्टा भक्षयन्ति पिबन्ति च ॥ ६ ॥
explanation: “Alongwith these monkey-guards, I checked them all; disregarding me, however, they merrily continued to feast on the fruits and drink the honey. (6)

shloka_text:
एभिः प्रधर्षणायां च वारितं वनपालकैः ।
मामप्यचिन्तयन् देव भक्षयन्ति वनौकसः ॥ ७ ॥
explanation: “On the depredation being commenced by them, resistance was offered by the guards of the grove; but disregarding even me, O lord, the monkeys continued to eat and drink the produce of the grove. (7)

shloka_text:
शिष्टमत्रापविध्यन्ति भक्षयन्ति तथापरे ।
निवार्यमाणास्ते सर्वे भृकुटिं दर्शयन्ति हि ॥ ८ ॥
explanation: “Some monkeys not only partook of the honey but they threw away what remained in the honeycomb. While being checked they all actually frowned at us. (8)

shloka_text:
इमे हि संरब्धतरास्तदा तैः सम्प्रधर्षिताः ।
निवार्यन्ते वनात् तस्मात् क्रुद्धैर्वानरपुङ्गवैः ॥ ९ ॥
explanation: “When these guards got more enraged, they were actually assaulted by the intruders. Nay, they were driven away from that grove by the excited leaders of monkeys. (9)

shloka_text:
ततस्तैर्बहुभिर्वीरैर्वानरैर्वानरर्षभाः ।
संरक्तनयनैः क्रोधाद्भ्रयः सम्प्रधर्षिताः ॥ १० ॥
explanation: “The monkeys guarding the grove, who 276 * VĀLMĪKI-RĀMĀYAṆA * are veritable jewels among monkeys, were then assaulted by those numerous heroic monkeys with eyes blood-red through anger. (10)

shloka_text:
पाणिभिर्निहताः केचित् केचिन्जानुभिराहताः ।
प्रकृष्टाश्च तदा कामं देवमार्गं च दर्शिताः ॥ ११ ॥
explanation: “Some of these were struck with their hands, others with their knees and then dragged at will and flung in the air. (11)

shloka_text:
एवमेते हताः शूरास्त्वयि तिष्ठति भर्तरि ।
कृत्स्नं मधुवनं चैव प्रकामं तैश्च भक्ष्यते ॥ १२ ॥
explanation: “In this way these valiant monkeys have been thrashed, while you, their master, continue to rule. Nay, the entire Madhuvana has been wrecked by them according to their free will.” (12)

shloka_text:
एवं विज्ञाप्यमानं तं सुग्रीवं वानरर्षभम् ।
अपृच्छत् तं महाप्राज्ञो लक्ष्मणः परवीरहा ॥ १३ ॥
explanation: The highly sagacious Lakṣmaṇa, the destroyer of hostile warriors, interrogated as follows that jewel among monkeys, the celebrated Sugriva, who was being informed as above: (13)

shloka_text:
किमयं वानरो राजन् वनपः प्रत्युपस्थितः ।
किं चार्थमभिर्निर्दिश्य दुःखितो वाक्यमब्रवीत् ॥ १४ ॥
explanation: “What for has this monkey, who guards your grove arrived in your presence? Nay, concerning what matter has this monkey, full of agony, addressed an appeal to you, O king?” (14)

shloka_text:
एवमुक्तस्तु सुग्रीवो लक्ष्मणेन महात्मना ।
लक्ष्मणं प्रत्युवाचेदं वाक्यं वाक्यविशारदः ॥ १५ ॥
explanation: Questioned thus by the high-souled Lakṣmaṇa, Sugriva, for his part, who was a master of expression, submitted to Lakṣmaṇa as follows: (15)

shloka_text:
आर्य लक्ष्मण सम्प्राह वीरो दधिमुखः कपिः ।
अङ्गदप्रमुखैर्वीरैर्भक्षितं मधु वानरैः ॥ १६ ॥
explanation: “O noble Lakṣmaṇa, the heroic monkey, Dadhimukha, was complaining that the honey and other products of Madhuvana had been consumed by the heroic monkeys with Aṅgada as their leader. (16)

shloka_text:
नैषामकृतकार्याणामीदृशः स्याद् व्यतिक्रमः ।
वनं यदभिपन्नास्ते साधितं कर्म तद् ध्रुवम् ॥ १७ ॥
