explanation: “Such an escapade could not have been indulged in by the monkeys had they not accomplished my purpose. Since they have started wrecking the grove, my work has surely been accomplished by them. (17)

shloka_text:
वारयन्तो भूशं प्राप्ताः पाला जानुभिराहताः ।
तथा न गणितश्चायं कपिर्दधिमुखो बली ॥ १८ ॥
explanation: “The guards of the grove, who were posted there, hindering them again and again were crushed with their knees, nay, this mighty monkey, Dadhimukha, was not taken into account either. (18)

shloka_text:
पतिर्मम वनस्यायमस्माभिः स्थापितः स्वयम् ।
दृष्टा देवी न संदेहो न चान्येन हनूमता ॥ १९ ॥
explanation: “This monkey Dadhimukha was posted by me as a guardian of this grove of mine. The godlike lady, Sītā, has been discovered: there is no doubt about it and she has been seen by Hanumān alone and by none else. (19)

shloka_text:
न हान्यः साधने हेतुः कर्मणोऽस्य हनूमतः ।
कार्यसिद्धिर्हनुमति मतिश्च हरिपुङ्गवे ॥ २० ॥
व्यवसायश्च वीर्यं च श्रुतं चापि प्रतिष्ठितम् ।
जाम्बवान् यत्र नेता स्यादङ्गदश्च महाबलः ॥ २१ ॥
हनूमांश्चाप्यधिष्ठाता न तत्र गतिरन्यथा ।
अङ्गदप्रमुखैर्वीरैर्हतं मधुवनं किल ॥ २२ ॥
विचित्य दक्षिणामाशामागतैर्हरिपुङ्गवैः ।
आगतैश्चाप्रधृष्यं तद्धतं मधुवनं हि तैः ॥ २३ ॥
explanation: “Surely none other than Hanumān is capable of accomplishing this task. The capacity to accomplish a deed as well as intelligence, nay strenuous effort and virility and learning too are firmly endowed in Hanumān, a veritable bull among monkeys. In an army where Jāmbavān as well as Aṅgada, who is endowed with extraordinary might, is the leader, and Hanumān a * SUNDARAKĀṆḌA * 277 counsellor, failure is out of the question. Madhuvana, they say, has been laid waste by the heroic jewels among monkeys, headed by Aṅgada, who have returned after exploring the southern quarter. Nay, the celebrated Madhuvana, which could not be laid violent hands upon by anyone, has actually been devastated by them as soon as they returned from Laṅkā. (20—23)

shloka_text:
धर्षितं च वनं कृत्स्नमुपयुक्तं तु वानरैः।
पातिता वनपालास्ते तदा जानुभिराहताः ॥ २४ ॥
explanation: “The wood was not only laid violent hands upon but was wholly consumed by the monkeys. The aforesaid monkeys guarding the grove were knocked down by them and then rubbed with their knees. (24)

shloka_text:
एतदर्थमयं प्राप्नो वक्तुं मधुरवागिह।
नाम्ना दधिमुखो नाम हरिः प्रख्यातविक्रमः ॥ २५ ॥
explanation: “This monkey, Dadhimukha by name, who is sweet of expression and whose prowess is widely known, came here to report this matter. (25)

shloka_text:
दृष्ट्वा सीता महाबाहो सौमित्रे पश्य तत्त्वतः।
अभिगम्य यथा सर्वे पिबन्ति मधु वानराः ॥ २६ ॥
explanation: “Since reaching Madhuvana, the monkeys are all drinking honey; know it correctly, O mighty-armed son of Sumitrā, that Sītā has been discovered. (26)

shloka_text:
न चाप्यदृष्ट्वा वैदेहीं विश्रुताः पुरुषर्षभ।
वनं दत्तवरं दिव्यं धर्षयेयुर्वनौकसः ॥ २७ ॥
explanation: “Without having found Sītā, a princess of the Videha territory, O jewel among men, the renowned monkeys would not have laid violent hands on the heavenly wood which was bestowed upon one of our ancestors as a boon by the gods.” (27)

shloka_text:
ततः प्रहृष्टो धर्मात्मा लक्ष्मणः सहराघवः।
श्रुत्वा कर्णसुखां वाणीं सुग्रीववदनाच्च्युताम् ॥ २८ ॥
explanation: Lakṣmaṇa, whose mind was set on virtue, alongwith Śrī Rāma, a scion of Raghu, thereupon felt highly rejoiced to hear the aforesaid speech, so agreeable to the ear, which had come from the lips of Sugrīva. (28)

shloka_text:
प्राहृष्यत भृशं रामो लक्ष्मणश्च महायशाः।
श्रुत्वा दधिमुखस्यैवं सुग्रीवस्तु प्रहृष्य च ॥ २९ ॥
वनपालं पुनर्वाक्यं सुग्रीवः प्रत्यभाषत।
प्रीतोऽस्मि सोऽहं यद्भुक्तं वनं तैः कृतकर्मभिः ॥ ३० ॥
explanation: Śrī Rāma as well as the highly illustrious Lakṣmaṇa were filled with ecstatic delight. Nay, feeling excessively delighted to hear the aforesaid report of Dadhimukha, Sugrīva, for his part who was distinguished by his well-built neck, once more addressed the following words to Dadhimukha, the guardian of the wood: “I am gratified to learn that the produce of the grove has been consumed by the monkeys who have accomplished their work. (29-30)

shloka_text:
धर्षितं मर्षणीयं च चेष्टितं कृतकर्मणाम्।
गच्छ शीघ्रं मधुवनं संरक्षस्व त्वमेव हि।
शीघ्रं प्रेषय सर्वास्तान् हनुमत्प्रमुखान् कपीन् ॥ ३१ ॥
explanation: “The violence as well as the vagaries of those who have done their duty must be tolerated by us. Return apace to Madhuvana; nay, you alone must guard it jealously as before. Dispatch without delay all those monkeys with Hanumān at their head. (31)

shloka_text:
इच्छामि शीघ्रं हनुमत्प्रधानान्-
शाखामृगांस्तान् मृगराजदर्पान्।
प्रष्टुं कृतार्थान् सह राघवाभ्यां
श्रोतुं च सीताधिगमे प्रयत्नम् ॥ ३२ ॥
explanation: “With the two scions of Raghu, I immediately wish to talk to those monkeys headed by Hanumān, who having accomplished their purpose, are proud as lions, as well as to hear of their endeavour in the cause of finding out Sītā.” (32)

shloka_text:
प्रीतिस्फीताक्षौ सम्प्रहृष्टौ कुमारौ
दृष्ट्वा सिद्धार्थौ वानराणां च राजा।
अङ्गैः प्रहृष्टैः कार्यसिद्धिं विदित्वा
बाहोरासन्नामतिमात्रं ननन्द ॥ ३३ ॥
explanation: 278 * VĀLMĪKI-RĀMĀYAṆA * Beholding the two princes Śrī Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa extremely delighted with their eyes dilated with joy as though accomplished of purpose, nay, realizing, by his own limbs thrilled with delight that the success of his enterprise was within the reach of his arms, Sugrīva, the ruler of monkeys, experienced the height of felicity. (33)

Returning to Madhuvana as commanded by Sugrīva, and craving the forgiveness of Aṅgada, Dadhimukha submits to the latter that he is urgently summoned by Sugrīva. Set out in the company of Hanumān and others, and approaching Sugrīva, Prince Aṅgada apprises Śrī Rāma, after saluting him, of the discovery of Sītā and other events

shloka_text:
सुग्रीवेणैवमुक्तस्तु हृष्टो दधिमुखः कपिः।
राघवं लक्ष्मणं चैव सुग्रीवं चाभ्यवादयत् ॥ १ ॥
explanation: Feeling rejoiced when commanded thus by Sugrīva, the monkey Dadhimukha, for his part, greeted Śrī Rāma, a scion of Raghu, and Lakṣmaṇa as well as Sugrīva. (1)

shloka_text:
स प्रणम्य च सुग्रीवं राघवौ च महाबलौ।
वानरैः सहितः शूरैर्दिवमेवोत्पपात ह ॥ २ ॥
explanation: Nay, having respectfully bowed down to Sugrīva as well as to Śrī Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, who were endowed with extraordinary might, he alongwith the other monkeys, who had accompanied him, sprang in the airspace again on their way to Madhuvana: so the tradition goes. (2)

shloka_text:
स यथैवागतः पूर्वं तथैव त्वरितं गतः।
निपत्य गगनाद् भूमौ तद् वनं प्रविवेश ह ॥ ३ ॥
explanation: He journeyed back quite as quickly as he had come before, nay, descending from the air to the ground, they say, he penetrated deep into the wood. (3)

shloka_text:
स प्रविष्टो मधुवनं ददर्श हरियूथपान्।
विमदानुद्धतान् सर्वान् मेहमानान् मधूदकम् ॥ ४ ॥
explanation: Having found his way into the interior of Madhuvana, he saw the leaders of monkey hordes, who, though overbearing before, had grown sober since and were all passing as urine, honey transformed after assimilation into water. (4)

shloka_text:
स तानुपागमद् वीरो बद्ध्वा करपुटाञ्जलिम्।
उवाच वचनं श्लक्ष्णमिदं हृष्टवदङ्गदम् ॥ ५ ॥
explanation: The said hero approached them and, joining his palms, addressed Aṅgada the following sweet words like one filled with delight : (5)

shloka_text:
सौम्य रोषो न कर्तव्यो यदेभिः परिवारणम्।
अज्ञानाद् रक्षिभिः क्रोधाद् भवन्तः प्रतिषेधिताः ॥ ६ ॥
explanation: "No resentment should be harboured by you, O gentle one, for the restraint unwittingly imposed on you by these guards, in that you were angrily hindered by them from enjoying the produce of this grove. (6)

shloka_text:
श्रान्तो दूरादनुप्रासो भक्षयस्व स्वकं मधु।
युवराजस्त्वमीशश्च वनस्यास्य महाबल ॥ ७ ॥
explanation: “Come from afar and exhausted as you are, partake of the honey, which is yours in that you are the Crown prince and as such the owner of this wood, O prince! endowed with extraordinary might! (7)

shloka_text:
मौख्यात् पूर्वं कृतो रोषस्तद् भवान् क्षन्तुमर्हति।
यथैव हि पिता तेऽभूत् पूर्वं हरिगणेश्वरः ॥ ८ ॥
तथा त्वमपि सुग्रीवो नान्यस्तु हरिसत्तम।
आख्यातं हि मया गत्वा पितृव्यस्य तवानघ ॥ ९ ॥
इहोपयानं सर्वेषामेतेषां वनचारिणाम्।
भवदागमनं श्रुत्वा सहैर्भिर्वनचारिभिः ॥ १० ॥
प्रहृष्टो न तु रुष्टोऽसौ वनं श्रुत्वा प्रधर्षितम्।
प्रहृष्टो मां पितृव्यस्ते सुग्रीवो वानरेश्वरः ॥ ११ ॥
शीघ्रं प्रेषय सर्वास्तानि ति होवाच पार्थिवः।
श्रुत्वा दधिमुखस्यैतद् वचनं श्लक्ष्णमङ्गदः ॥ १२ ॥
अब्रवीत् तान् हरिश्रेष्ठो वाक्यं वाक्यविशारदः।
शङ्के श्रुतोऽयं वृत्तान्तो रामेण हरियूथपाः ॥ १३ ॥
explanation: “You ought to pardon us for the wrath which was vented by us earlier due to foolishness. Sugriva is now the lord of monkey hordes precisely in the same way as your father, Vāli, formerly was. You too are the same and none else, O jewel among monkeys! The arrival here of all these monkeys including yourself was actually reported to your uncle by me after going there, O sinless one! He felt greatly rejoiced to hear of your arrival alongwith all these monkeys. He did not get angry even on hearing of the grove having been devastated. Highly pleased, your uncle, King Sugriva, the lord of monkeys, commanded me as follows: “Please send them all without delay.” Hearing the aforesaid refined submission of Dadhimukha, Aṅgada, the foremost of monkeys, who was a master of expression, spoke to them as follows: “I presume this news of our arrival has been heard by Śrī Rāma, O leaders of monkey hordes! (8—13)

shloka_text:
अयं च हर्षादाख्याति तेन जानामि हेतुना।
तत् क्षमं नेह नः स्थातुं कृते कार्ये परंतपाः ॥ १४ ॥
explanation: “I conclude this also from the fact that this monkey, Dadhimukha, is narrating the event joyfully. Hence it does not behove us to tarry here any longer now that our work has been accomplished, O tormentors of foes! (14)

shloka_text:
पीत्वा मधु यथाकामं विक्रान्ता वनचारिणः।
किं शेषं गमनं तत्र सुग्रीवो यत्र वानरः ॥ १५ ॥
explanation: “You, valiant monkeys, have drunk honey to your heart's content. Nothing remains for you to do. It is, therefore, advisable for us to proceed to Kīṣkindhā where the monkey king Sugriva is. (15)

shloka_text:
सर्वे यथा मां वक्ष्यन्ति समेत्य हरिपुङ्गवाः।
तथास्मि कर्ता कर्तव्ये भवद्भिः परवानहम् ॥ १६ ॥
explanation: “I shall act as you all will conjointly ask me, O bulls among monkeys; for I depend on you in the matter of deciding what should be done by me. (16)

shloka_text:
नाज्ञापयितुमीशोऽहं युवराजोऽस्मि यद्यपि।
अयुक्तं कृतकर्माणो यूयं धर्षयितुं बलात् ॥ १७ ॥
explanation: “Even though I am the Crown prince, I am not competent to issue orders to you. Since you have performed your duty, it will be unjustified on my part to play the lord over you by force.” (17)

shloka_text:
ब्रुवतश्चाङ्गदस्यैवं श्रुत्वा वचनमुत्तमम्।
प्रहृष्टमनसो वाक्यमिदमूर्चुर्वनौकसः ॥ १८ ॥
explanation: Greatly delighted at heart to hear the aforesaid excellent speech of Aṅgada, even while he was speaking, the monkeys submitted as follows: (18)

shloka_text:
एवं वक्ष्यति को राजन् प्रभुः सन् वानरर्षभ।
ऐश्वर्यमदमत्तो हि सर्वोऽहमिति मन्यते ॥ १९ ॥
explanation: “Who, O king, while being a master, would speak in this strain, O jewel among monkeys? Drunk with the pride of power, everyone as a rule is self-conceited. (19)

shloka_text:
तव चेदं सुसदृशं वाक्यं नान्यस्य कस्यचित्।
सन्नतिहि तवाख्याति भविष्यच्छुभयोग्यताम् ॥ २० ॥
explanation: “This speech is quite becoming of you and does not become anyone else. Indeed this extreme humility indicates your fitness for further good fortune. (20)

shloka_text:
सर्वे वयमपि प्राप्तास्तत्र गन्तुं कृतक्षणाः।
स यत्र हरिवीराणां सुग्रीवः पतिरव्ययः ॥ २१ ॥
explanation: “We all too have come here eager to proceed to where Sugriva, that imperishable lord of monkey-heroes, is. (21)

shloka_text:
त्वया हानुकेहरिभिर्नैव शक्यं पदात् पदम्।
क्वचिद् गन्तुं हरिश्रेष्ठं ब्रूमः सत्यमिदं तु ते ॥ २२ ॥
explanation: “It is surely not at all possible for us monkeys to advance even one step from where we stand in any direction, unless commanded by you, O jewel among monkeys : we tell you this quite correctly.” (22)

shloka_text:
एवं तु वदतां तेषामङ्गदः प्रत्यभाषत।
साधु गच्छाम इत्युक्त्वा खमुत्पेतुर्महाबलाः ॥ २३ ॥
explanation: While they were speaking thus, Aṅgada for his part replied, “All right !” Saying : “Let us move !”, the monkeys, who were all endowed with extraordinary might, sprang in the air. (23)

shloka_text:
उत्पतन्तमनुत्पेतुः सर्वे ते हरियूथपाः।
कृत्वा ऽऽकाशं निराकाशं यन्त्रोत्क्षिप्ताः इवोपलाः ॥ २४ ॥
explanation: Filling the space, all those leaders of monkey-hordes followed Aṅgada, even as he sprang, like so many stones shot from a catapult (24)

shloka_text:
अङ्गदं पुरतः कृत्वा हनूमन्तं च वानरम्।
तेऽम्बरं सहसोत्पत्य वेगवन्तः प्लवङ्गमाः ॥ २५ ॥
विनदन्तो महानादं घना वातेरिता यथा।
अङ्गदे समनुप्राप्ते सुग्रीवो वानरेश्वरः ॥ २६ ॥
उवाच शोकसंतप्तं रामं कमललोचनम्।
समाश्वसिहि भद्रं ते दृष्टा देवी न संशयः ॥ २७ ॥
explanation: Springing all of a sudden in the air, placing Aṅgada at their head, as also the monkey, Hanumān, the aforesaid monkeys, full of impetuosity, darted along, thundering like so many clouds propelled by the wind. Aṅgada having arrived near Sugriva, the lord of monkeys, submitted as follows to Śrī Rāma with lotus-like eyes, who was tormented with grief : “Take heart ! May good betide you! The godlike lady, Sītā, has been discovered : there is no doubt about it. (25—27)

shloka_text:
नागन्तुमिह शक्यं तैरतीतसमयैरिह।
अङ्गदस्य प्रहर्षाच्च जानामि शुभदर्शन ॥ २८ ॥
explanation: “It was not possible for them to return here otherwise, the time-limit fixed by me having been exceeded by them long before. I conclude this also from Aṅgada’s ecstatic delight, O prince of charming looks ! (28)

shloka_text:
न मत्सकाशमागच्छेत् कृत्ये हि विनिपातिते।
युवराजो महाबाहुः प्लवतामङ्गदो वरः ॥ २९ ॥
explanation: “Had their design been frustrated, the mighty-armed Crown Prince Aṅgada, the foremost of monkeys, would not have sought my presence in any case. (29)

shloka_text:
यद्यप्यकृतकृत्यानामीदृशः स्यादुपक्रमः।
भवेत् तु दीनवदनो भ्रान्तविप्लुतमानसः ॥ ३० ॥
explanation: “Even though such a conduct may be possible even on the part of those who have not been able to accomplish their purpose, he would have worn a wretched aspect and felt bewildered and disturbed in mind, which he is not. (30)

shloka_text:
पितृपैतामहं चैतत् पूर्वकैरभिरक्षितम्।
न मे मधुवनं हन्याददृष्ट्वा जनकात्मजाम् ॥ ३१ ॥
explanation: “Without seeing Janaka’s daughter, none would have dared to destroy my Madhuvana, which was bequeathed to my father, Rkṣarāja, by my grandfather, Brahmā, and has been protected on all sides by my forbears. (31)

shloka_text:
कौसल्या सुप्रजा राम समाश्वसिहि सुव्रत।
दृष्टा देवी न संदेहो न चान्येन हनूमता ॥ ३२ ॥
explanation: “Kausalyā, your mother, is blessed with * SUNDARAKĀṆḌA * 281 a happy son in you. Be restored to confidence, O Rāma of noble vows! The godlike lady Sītā has been discovered: there is no doubt about it. Nay, she has been traced out by Hanumān and by none else. (32)

shloka_text:
नहान्यः कर्मणो हेतुः साधनेऽस्य हनूमतः।
हनूमतीह सिद्धिश्च मतिश्च मतिसत्तम ॥ ३३ ॥
व्यवसायश्च शौर्यं च श्रुतं चापि प्रतिष्ठितम्।
जाम्बवान् यत्र नेता स्यादङ्गदश्च हरीश्वरः ॥ ३४ ॥
हनूमांश्चाप्यधिष्ठाता न तत्र गतिरन्यथा।
मा भूश्चिन्तासमायुक्तः सम्प्रत्यमितविक्रम ॥ ३५ ॥
यदा हि दर्पितोदग्राः संगताः काननौकसः।
नैषामकृतकार्याणामीदृशः स्यादुपक्रमः ॥ ३६ ॥
explanation: “Surely none else, other than Hanumān, could be confident in accomplishing this task. Nay, the capacity to accomplish a deed as well as intelligence, as also strenuous effort and valour and learning too are firmly embedded in Hanumān, O prince foremost in wisdom! In an army where Jāmbavān as well as Aṅgada, the lord of monkeys, is the leader, and Hanumān a counsellor, failure is out of the question. Do not feel worried any longer. O prince of immeasurable prowess, since the monkeys have come elated with pride. Such conduct would not be possible on the part of those who have not accomplished their task. (33—36)

shloka_text:
वनभङ्गेन जानामि मधूनां भक्षणेन च।
ततः किलकिलाशब्दं शुश्रावासन्नमम्बरे ॥ ३७ ॥
हनूमत्कर्मदूषानां नदतां काननौकसाम्।
किष्किन्धामुपयातानां सिद्धिं कथयतामिव ॥ ३८ ॥
explanation: “From the fact of their having laid waste Madhuvana and enjoyed the honey, I conclude that they are successful.” Presently Sugrīva heard closeby in the sky a cry expressing joy, of monkeys arrived in the vicinity of Kiṣkindhā, roaring and thereby proclaiming their triumph, as it were, proud as they are of the achievements of Hanumān. (37-38)

shloka_text:
ततः श्रुत्वा निनादं तं कपीनां कपिसत्तमः।
आयताञ्चितलाङ्गुलः सोऽभवदृष्टमानसः ॥ ३९ ॥
explanation: Hearing the aforesaid clamour of the monkeys, the celebrated Sugrīva, the foremost of monkeys, now felt delighted at heart and stretched and curled his tail at the end out of joy. (39)

shloka_text:
आजग्मुस्तेऽपि हरयो रामदर्शनकाङ्क्षिणः।
अङ्गदं पुरतः कृत्वा हनूमन्तं च वानरम् ॥ ४० ॥
explanation: Placing Aṅgada as also the monkey Hanumān at their head, all those monkeys too, who were eager to have a look at Śrī Rāma, arrived. (40)

shloka_text:
तेऽङ्गदप्रमुखा वीराः प्रहृष्टाश्च मुदान्विताः।
निपेतुर्हिरिजस्य समीपे राघवस्य च ॥ ४१ ॥
explanation: Filled with joy, nay, thrilled, those heroes, headed by Aṅgada, descended from the airspace close to Sugrīva, the ruler of monkeys, as well as to Śrī Rāma, a scion of Raghu. (41)

shloka_text:
हनूमांश्च महाबाहुः प्रणम्य शिरसा ततः।
नियतामक्षतां देवीं राघवाय न्यवेदयत् ॥ ४२ ॥
explanation: Nay, making respectful obeisance with his head bent low, the mighty-armed Hanumān then reported the godlike lady Sītā to be constant in her devotion to Śrī Rāma and sound in body. (42)

shloka_text:
दृष्ट्वा देवीति हनुमद्वदनादमृतोपमम्।
आकर्ण्य वचनं रामो हर्षमाप सलक्ष्मणः ॥ ४३ ॥
explanation: Śrī Rāma with Lakṣmaṇa experienced delight on hearing the nectar-like news from the lips of Hanumān that the godlike lady had been discovered. (43)

shloka_text:
निश्चितार्थं ततस्तस्मिन् सुग्रीवं पवनात्मजे।
लक्ष्मणः प्रीतिमान् प्रीतं बहुमानादवैक्षत ॥ ४४ ॥
explanation: Full of love, Lakṣmaṇa thereupon regarded with great esteem the joyful Sugrīva, who felt sure about the aforesaid Hanumān (sprung from the loins of the wind-god) having accomplished the object, viz., the discovery of Sītā. (44)

shloka_text:
प्रीत्या च परयोपेतो राघवः परवीरहा।
बहुमानेन महता हनुमन्तमवैक्षत ॥ ४५ ॥
explanation: Full of supreme affection, Śrī Rāma, a sion of Raghu, the destroyer of hostile warriors, too looked on Hanumān with great and high regard. (45)

Asked by Śrī Rāma to tell him the news about Sītā, Hanumān apprises Śrī Rāma of her presence at the foot of a Śimśapā tree in the midst of ogresses and delivers her message after narrating the incidents related by her as a token

shloka_text:
ततः प्रस्वणं शैलं ते गत्वा चित्रकाननम्।
प्रणम्य शिरसा रामं लक्ष्मणं च महाबलम् ॥ १ ॥
युवराजं पुरस्कृत्य सुग्रीवमभिवाद्य च।
प्रवृत्तिमथ सीतायाः प्रवक्तुमुपचक्रमुः ॥ २ ॥
explanation: Then moving to Mount Prasravana, clothed with lovely woods, making obeisance with their heads bent low to Śrī Rāma, and also Lakṣmaṇa, who was endowed with extraordinary might, nay, greeting Sugrīva, and placing Aṅgada, the Crown prince at their head, the monkeys forthwith proceeded to give information regarding Sītā as follows: (1-2)

shloka_text:
रावणान्तःपुरे रोधं राक्षसीभिश्च तर्जनम्।
रामे समनुरागं च यथा च नियमः कृतः ॥ ३ ॥
एतदाख्याय ते सर्वं हरयो रामसंनिधौ।
वैदेहीमक्षतां श्रुत्वा रामस्तूत्तरमब्रवीत् ॥ ४ ॥
explanation: Having related in the presence of Śrī Rāma all this, viz., Sītā's detention in the pleasance of Rāvaṇa, she being threatened by ogresses, her unflinching devotion to Śrī Rāma and how a time limit of a couple of fortnights had been fixed for her survival by Rāvaṇa, the said monkeys kept mum. Hearing of Sītā, a princess of the Videha territory, being alive, Śrī Rāma for his part asked the following question: (3-4)

shloka_text:
क्व सीता वर्तते देवी कथं च मयि वर्तते।
एतन्मे सर्वमाख्यात वैदेही प्रति वानराः ॥ ५ ॥
explanation: "Where does Sītā, the godlike lady, live and how is she disposed towards me? Pray, tell me all this concerning Sītā (a princess of the Videha territory) O monkeys!" (5)

shloka_text:
रामस्य गदितं श्रुत्वा हरयो रामसंनिधौ।
चोदयन्ति हनुमन्तं सीतावृत्तान्तकोविदम् ॥ ६ ॥
explanation: Hearing the command of Śrī Rāma, the monkeys began to urge, in the presence of Śrī Rāma, Hanumān, who knew full well the facts about Sītā, to answer the question of Śrī Rāma. (6)

shloka_text:
दक्षिणस्य समुद्रस्य तीरे वसति दक्षिणे।
तत्र सीता मया दृष्टा रावणान्तःपुरे सती ॥ ११ ॥
त्वयि संन्यस्य जीवन्ती रामा राम मनोरथम्।
दृष्टा मे राक्षसीमध्ये तर्ज्यमाना मुहुर्मुहुः ॥ १२ ॥
राक्षसीभिर्विरूपाभी रक्षिता प्रमदावने।
दुःखमापद्यते देवी त्वया वीर सुखोचिता ॥ १३ ॥
रावणान्तःपुरे रुद्धा राक्षसीभिः सुरक्षिता।
एकवेणीधरा दीना त्वयि चिन्तापरायणा ॥ १४ ॥
explanation: Hearing their request and offering salutations with his head bent low to the southern quarter and thereby to the godlike lady Sītā, Hanumān, an offspring of the wind-god, who knew the art of expression, made the following statement describing how he was able to see Sītā. Having delivered to Śrī Rāma the wonderful golden jewel glowing in its own splendour, Hanumān then submitted with joined palms as follows: “Having leapt across the sea, a hundred Yojanas (or eight hundred miles) wide, I reached its southern shore looking about for Sītā, Janaka’s daughter, with intent to see her. There on the southern shore of the southern sea is situated the city ruled over by the evil-minded Rāvaṇa, known by the name of Laṅkā. The virtuous and lovely Sītā was seen by me living in the pleasancy of Rāvaṇa in that city, having centred her heart on you, O Rāma! Nay, she was seen by me in the midst of ogresses, guarded in a pleasancy by ugly ogresses and being threatened again and again. Detained in the pleasancy of Rāvaṇa and closely guarded by ogresses, the godlike lady, who deserves to live happily with you, O valiant prince, has been reduced to straits. She wears a single pleat of hair (as a mark of desolation), is forlorn and remains absorbed in your thought alone. (7—14)

shloka_text:
अधःशय्या विवर्णाङ्गी पद्मिनीव हिमागमे।
रावणाद् विनिवृत्तार्था मर्तव्यकृतनिश्चया ॥ १५ ॥
explanation: “She stretches herself on the bare ground, is pale of limbs like a lotus plant at the approach of winter, has utterly refused to have anything to do with Rāvaṇa, and is determined to die rather than submit to Rāvaṇa. (15)

shloka_text:
देवी कथंचित् काकुत्स्थ त्वन्मना मार्गिता मया।
इक्ष्वाकुवंशविख्यातिं शनैः कीर्तयतानघ ॥ १६ ॥
सा मया नरशार्दूल शनैर्विश्वासिता तदा।
ततः सम्भाषिता देवी सर्वमर्थं च दर्शिता ॥ १७ ॥
explanation: “The godlike lady, whose mind is set on you, O scion of Kakutstha, was somehow traced out by me. She was then inspired by me, by degrees with confidence, O tiger among men, by gradually recounting the glory of Ikṣwāku’s race. She was later on accosted by me and apprised of all the facts, including your alliance with Sugrīva. (16-17)

shloka_text:
रामसुग्रीवसख्यं च श्रुत्वा हर्षमुपागता।
नियतः समुदाचारो भक्तिश्चास्याः सदा त्वयि ॥ १८ ॥
explanation: “Nay, she experienced delight on hearing of the alliance between you and king Sugrīva. Constant is her morality and abiding is her devotion to you. (18)

shloka_text:
एवं मया महाभाग दृष्टा जनकनन्दिनी।
उग्रेण तपसा युक्ता त्वद्भक्त्या पुरुषर्षभ ॥ १९ ॥
explanation: “In this way, O highly blessed one, was the delight of Janaka, Sītā, found by me, endowed with severe asceticism and devotion to you, O jewel among men! (19)

shloka_text:
अभिज्ञानं च मे दत्तं यथावृत्तं तवान्तिके।
चित्रकूटे महाप्राज्ञ वायसं प्रति राघव ॥ २० ॥
explanation: “The way in which an incident connected with a crow took place in your presence at Citrakūṭa was also related by her by way of a token, O Śrī Rāma, exceptionally sagacious scion of Raghu! (20)

shloka_text:
विज्ञाप्यः पुनरप्येष रामो वायुसुत त्वया।
अखिलेन यथा दृष्टमिति मामाह जानकी ॥ २१ ॥
explanation: “The daughter of Janaka said to me, ‘Śrī Rāma enshrined in my memory, O son of the wind-god, should further be told by you in every detail what has been witnessed by you here. (21)

shloka_text:
अयं चास्मै प्रदातव्यो यत्नात् सुपरिरक्षितः ।
ब्रुवता वचनान्येवं सुग्रीवस्योपशृण्वतः ॥ २२ ॥
explanation: “Nay, this jewel, which has been carefully preserved with diligence, should be handed over to Śrī Rāma after addressing the following words within the hearing of Sugrīva : (22)

shloka_text:
एष चूडामणिः श्रीमान् मया ते यत्नरक्षितः ।
मनःशिलायास्तिलकं तत् स्मरस्वेति चाब्रवीत् ॥ २३ ॥
explanation: “Here is the brilliant jewel for the head associated with you and preserved by me with diligence.’ She further said, ‘Kindly recall that sacred mark on my forehead painted by you with realgar.’ (23)

shloka_text:
एष निर्यातितः श्रीमान् मया ते वारिसम्भवः ।
एवं दृष्ट्वा प्रमोदिष्ये व्यसने त्वामिवानघ ॥ २४ ॥
explanation: “This brilliant jewel found in the waters is hereby being sent by me to you. Gazing on it in my adversity I used to feel highly rejoiced as on seeing you, O sinless prince ! (24)

shloka_text:
जीवितं धारयिष्यामि मासं दशरथात्मज ।
ऊर्ध्वं मासान्न जीवेयं रक्षसां वशमागता ॥ २५ ॥
explanation: “I am going to survive but for a month, O son of Daśaratha ! Fallen that I am into the clutches of ogres, I am not going to survive beyond a month.’ (25)

shloka_text:
इति मामब्रवीत् सीता कृशाङ्गी धर्मचारिणी ।
रावणान्तःपुरे रुद्धा मृगीवोत्फुल्ललोचना ॥ २६ ॥
explanation: “Thus spoke to me Sītā of emaciated limbs, who looked with eyes wide open (through fear) like a doe, was given to the practice of virtue, and had been detained in the pleasance of Rāvaṇa. (26)

shloka_text:
एतदेव मयाऽऽख्यातं सर्वं राघव यद् यथा ।
सर्वथा सागरजले संतारः प्रविधीयताम् ॥ २७ ॥
explanation: “This precisely is the news about Sītā, which has been narrated by me exhaustively and correctly, O scion of Raghu ! A method may now be devised to cross the sea-water at all events.” (27)

shloka_text:
तौ जाताश्वासौ राजपुत्रौ विदित्वा
तच्चाभिज्ञानं राघवाय प्रदाय ।
देव्या चाख्यातं सर्वमेवानुपूर्व्याद्
वाचा सम्पूर्णं वायुपुत्रः शशंस ॥ २८ ॥
explanation: Coming to know that the two princes, Śrī Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, were restored to confidence, and having delivered the aforesaid token to Śrī Rāma, Hanumān, son of the wind-god, reproduced in its entirety in so many words seriatim all that was communicated by the godlike lady. (28)
Pressing to his bosom the jewel for the head sent by Sītā and piteously wailing in many ways, Śrī Rāma urges Hanumān to repeat the message of Sītā

shloka_text:
एवमुक्तो हनुमता रामो दशरथात्मजः।
तं मणिं हृदये कृत्वा रुरोद सहलक्ष्मणः ॥ १ ॥
explanation: Pressing that jewel to his bosom when spoken to as aforesaid by Hanumān, Śrī Rāma, sprung from the loins of Daśaratha, wept with his younger brother, Lakṣmaṇa. (1)

shloka_text:
तं तु दृष्ट्वा मणिश्रेष्ठं राघवः शोककर्षितः।
नेत्राभ्यामश्रुपूर्णाभ्यां सुग्रीवमिदमब्रवीत् ॥ २ ॥
explanation: Beholding that excellent jewel, Śrī Rāma, a scion of Raghu, for his part, who was emaciated through grief born of separation from Sītā, spoke as follows to Sugrīva with eyes full of tears: (2)

shloka_text:
यथैव धेनुः स्ववति स्नेहाद् वत्सस्य वत्सला।
तथा ममापि हृदयं मणिश्रेष्ठस्य दर्शनात् ॥ ३ ॥
explanation: “Even as a cow, who is fond of her calf, begins to distil milk from her teats through excess of affection at the very sight of her calf, so does my heart too melt through the sight of the excellent jewel. (3)

shloka_text:
मणिरत्नमिदं दत्तं वैदेह्याः श्वशुरेण मे।
वधूकाले यथा बद्धमधिकं मूर्ध्नि शोभते ॥ ४ ॥
explanation: “This excellent jewel was presented by my father-in-law King Janaka to Sītā, a princess of the Videha territory, when she had become a bride, and was fastened to her head in such a way as it looked surpassingly charming. (4)

shloka_text:
अयं हि जलसम्भूतो मणिः प्रवरपूजितः।
यज्ञे परमतुष्टेन दत्तः शक्रेण धीमता ॥ ५ ॥
explanation: “This jewel, which was found in the waters and had been adored by the foremost among gods, was actually bestowed on King Janaka by the wise Indra (the ruler of gods), who was highly pleased with the former in the course of a sacrificial performance intended to propitiate him. (5)

shloka_text:
इमं दृष्ट्वा मणिश्रेष्ठं तथा तातस्य दर्शनम्।
अद्यास्यवगतः सौम्य वैदेहस्य तथा विभोः ॥ ६ ॥
explanation: “By seeing this excellent jewel I have indirectly obtained today the sight of my father in whose hands the jewel was placed by Janaka as well as that of the mighty Janaka, the ruler of the Videha territory, in the same way as I have obtained the sight of Sītā herself, O gentle one! (6)

shloka_text:
अयं हि शोभते तस्याः प्रियाया मूर्ध्नि मे मणिः।
अद्यास्य दर्शनेनाहं प्राप्तां तामिव चिन्तये ॥ ७ ॥
explanation: “Indeed, this jewel looked extremely charming on the head of my aforesaid darling. Through its sight today I conceive her to have been recovered. (7)

shloka_text:
किमाह सीता वैदेही ब्रूहि सौम्य पुनः पुनः।
परासुमिव तोयेन सिञ्जन्ती वाक्यवारिणा ॥ ८ ॥
explanation: “Please repeat, O gentle one, again and again, what Sītā, a princess of the Videha territory, said to you, sprinkling me, unconscious as I am, with water in the form of her speech, as it were. (8)

shloka_text:
इतस्तु किं दुःखतरं यदिमं वारिसम्भवम्।
मणिं पश्यामि सौमित्रे वैदेहीमागतां विना ॥ ९ ॥
explanation: Turning to Lakṣmaṇa, “indeed what could be more painful, O son of Sumitrā, than the fact that I behold this jewel, found in the waters, come without Sītā, a princess of the Videha territory? (9)

shloka_text:
चिरं जीवति वैदेही यदि मासं धरिष्यति।
क्षणं वीर न जीवेयं विना तामसितेक्षणम् ॥ १० ॥
explanation: Addressing Hanumān again Śrī Rāma 286 * VĀLMĪKI-RĀMĀYAṆA * said : “Sītā will live long if she survives for a month. I, however, would not survive even for a moment without that dark-eyed lady, O gallant one ! (10)

shloka_text:
नय मामपि तं देशं यत्र दृष्ट्वा मम प्रिया।
न तिष्ठेयं क्षणमपि प्रवृत्तिमुपलभ्य च ॥ ११ ॥
explanation: “Please take me as well to that region where my darling was seen by you. Nay, having received news about her, I cannot tarry even for a moment. (11)

shloka_text:
कथं सा मम सुश्रोणी भीरुभीरुः सती तदा।
भयावहानां घोराणां मध्ये तिष्ठति रक्षसाम् ॥ १२ ॥
explanation: “How does my virtuous consort, Sītā, with charming limbs, who is extremely timid, stay all the time in the midst of violent and frightful ogres? (12)

shloka_text:
शारदस्तिमिरोन्मुक्तो नूनं चन्द्र इवाम्बुदैः।
आवृतो वदनं तस्या न विराजति साम्प्रतम् ॥ १३ ॥
explanation: “Surely her countenance, resembling, as it does, the autumnal moon bereft of its spot, though screened by clouds, does not shine so brightly any more. (13)

shloka_text:
किमाह सीता हनुमंस्तत्त्वतः कथयस्व मे।
एतेन खलु जीविष्ये भेषजेनातुरो यथा ॥ १४ ॥
explanation: “Pray, tell me correctly, O Hanumān, what Sītā said to you. I shall surely survive on the strength of her message even as an ailing man would with the help of medicine. (14)

shloka_text:
मधुरा मधुरालापा किमाह मम भामिनी।
मद्विहीना वरारोहा हनुमन् कथयस्व मे।
दुःखाद् दुःखतरं प्राप्य कथं जीवति जानकी ॥ १५ ॥
explanation: “Please tell me, O Hanumān, what my beloved consort, who has a comely exterior and is sweet of expression, who is endowed with excellent limbs and has been separated from me, said to you. How does the daughter of Janaka survive even on meeting with a misfortune harder than before?” (15)

Hanumān reproduces at length the incident connected with a crow that took place during the sojourn of Sītā with Śrī Rāma at Citrakūṭa, related by her by way of a token, and further describes her piteous lament and the way in which she was comforted by Hanumān

shloka_text:
एवमुक्तस्तु हनुमान् राघवेण महात्मना।
सीताया भाषितं सर्वं न्यवेदयत राघवे ॥ १ ॥
explanation: Urged in the foregoing words by the high-souled Śrī Rāma, a scion of Raghu, Hanumān for his part repeated as follows to Śrī Rāma all that was said by Sītā : (1)

shloka_text:
इदमुक्तवती देवी जानकी पुरुषर्षभ।
पूर्ववृत्तमभिज्ञानं चित्रकूटे यथातथम् ॥ २ ॥
explanation: “The godlike lady Sītā related as follows, even as it had occurred, O jewel among men, an incident that had taken place at Citrakūṭa in the past. (2)

shloka_text:
सुखसुमा त्वया सार्धं जानकी पूर्वमुत्थिता।
वायसः सहसोत्पत्य विददार स्तनान्तरम् ॥ ३ ॥
explanation: “Having slept happily at your side on one occasion, Sītā, daughter of Janaka, got * SUNDARAKĀṆḌA * 287 up before you, when, coming down suddenly, a crow tore the flesh of her breast with its beak. (3)

shloka_text:
पर्यायेण च सुसत्त्वं देव्यङ्के भरताग्रज।
पुनश्च किल पक्षी स देव्या जनयति व्यथा ॥ ४ ॥
explanation: “You then lay asleep on the lap of the godlike lady, O elder brother of Bharata! And once more did that bird actually begin to torment the godlike lady. (4)

shloka_text:
ततः पुनरुपागम्य विददार भूशं किल।
ततस्त्वं बोधितस्तस्याः शोणितेन समुक्षितः ॥ ५ ॥
explanation: “Coming near once more indeed, it forthwith cruelly tore her breast. Bathed in blood that began to flow from her breast, you were awakened then by her. (5)

shloka_text:
वायसेन च तेनैवं सततं बाध्यमानया।
बोधितः किल देव्या त्वं सुखसुमः परंतप ॥ ६ ॥
explanation: “Though lying happily asleep, O tormentor of foes, you were actually awakened by the godlike lady, who was being ceaselessly tormented by that crow as aforesaid. (6)

shloka_text:
तां च दृष्ट्वा महाबाहो दारितां च स्तनान्तरे।
आशीविष इव क्रुद्धस्ततो वाक्यं त्वमूचिवान् ॥ ७ ॥
explanation: “Nay, enraged like a venomous serpent on seeing her lacerated in the breast, O mighty-armed prince, you for your part thereupon put the following question to her : (7)

shloka_text:
नखाग्रैः केन ते भीरु दारितं वै स्तनान्तरम्।
कः क्रीडति सरोषेण पञ्चवक्त्रेण भोगिना ॥ ८ ॥
explanation: “By whom has the flesh of your breast been actually torn with the ends of his nails, O tender one? Who is playing with an angry five-hooded serpent?” (8)

shloka_text:
निरीक्षमाणः सहसा वायसं समुदेक्षथाः।
नखैः सरुधिरैस्तीक्ष्णैस्तामेवाभिमुखं स्थितम् ॥ ९ ॥
explanation: “Casting your eyes around, you suddenly observed a crow with its sharp talons stained with blood, perched just in front of Sītā. (9)

shloka_text:
सुतः किल स शक्रस्य वायसः पततां वरः।
धरान्तरगतः शीघ्रं पवनस्य गतौ समः ॥ १० ॥
explanation: “Indeed, that crow was no other than Jayanta, son of Indra, and was the foremost of birds. Vying as he did with the wind in swift motion, he had his abode in the subterranean regions. (10)

shloka_text:
ततस्तस्मिन् महाबाहो कोपसंवर्तितेक्षणः।
वायसे त्वं व्यधाः क्रूरां मतिं मतिमतां वर ॥ ११ ॥
explanation: “With your eyes rolling through anger, O mighty-armed prince, you then thought of punishing that crow, O jewel among the wise! (11)

shloka_text:
स दर्भसंस्तराद् गृह्य ब्रह्मास्त्रेण न्ययोजयः।
स दीप्त इव कालाग्निर्ज्ज्वालाभिमुखं खगम् ॥ १२ ॥
explanation: “Snatching a blade from your bed of the sacred Kuśa grass, you as such charged it with the potency of a mystic missile presided over by Brahmā, the creator. The blade blazed forth like the flaming fire of universal destruction with its end facing the bird. (12)

shloka_text:
स त्वं प्रदीप्तं चिक्षेप दर्भं तं वायसं प्रति।
ततस्तु वायसं दीप्तः स दर्भोऽनु जगाम ह ॥ १३ ॥
explanation: “You then hurled that blazing blade of the sacred Kuśa grass at the crow. Thereupon that flaming blade of Kuśa grass for its part actually pursued the crow. (13)

shloka_text:
भीतैश्च सम्परित्यक्तः सुरैः सर्वैश्च वायसः।
त्रैल्लोकान् सम्परिक्रम्य त्रातारं नाधिगच्छति ॥ १४ ॥
explanation: “The crow, however, was forsaken by all the gods, who were seized with fear of you, and did not find a protector even after ranging all the three worlds (heaven, earth and the intermediate region). (14)

shloka_text:
किमर्थमस्त्रं रक्षःसु न योजयसि राघव।
न दानवा न गन्धर्वा नासुरा न मरुदृणाः ॥ १९ ॥
तव राम रणे शक्तास्तथा प्रतिसमासितुम्।
तव वीर्यवतः कश्चिन्मयि यद्यस्ति सम्भ्रमः ॥ २० ॥
क्षिप्रं सुनिशितैर्बाणैर्हन्यतां युधि रावणः।
भ्रातुरादेशमाज्ञाय लक्ष्मणो वा परंतपः ॥ २१ ॥
स किमर्थं नरवरो न मां रक्षति राघवः।
शक्तौ तौ पुरुषव्याघ्रौ वाय्वग्निसमतेजसौ ॥ २२ ॥
सुराणामपि दुर्धर्षौ किमर्थं मामुपेक्षतः।
ममैव दुष्कृतं किंचिन्महदस्ति न संशयः ॥ २३ ॥
समर्थौ सहितौ यन्मां न रक्षते परंतपौ।
वैदेह्या वचनं श्रुत्वा करुणं साधुभाषितम् ॥ २४ ॥
पुनरप्यहमायां तामिदं वचनमब्रुवम्।
त्वच्छ्रेकविमुखो रामो देवि सत्येन ते शपे ॥ २५ ॥
explanation: "The crow at long last sought your presence once more at Citrakūṭa, O tamer of foes! Fit as you are to afford protection to those seeking it, you for your part afforded shelter in your mercy to the crow, who sought your protection and had fallen flat on the ground, even though he deserved death, O scion of Kakutstha! You, as such, however, destroyed the right eye of that crow only because it was not possible to render the missile ineffectual, O scion of Raghu! Having saluted you as well as King Daśaratha (in heaven, who had obviously sent him back to Śrī Rāma to seek his forgiveness), the crow for his part, when spared by you, returned forthwith to his abode. Says Sītā: "You are in this way the foremost of those skilled in the use of mystic missiles, full of courage and endowed with an amiable disposition. Wherefore then do you not direct your missiles against the ogres, O scion of Raghu? Neither giants nor Gandharvas (celestial musicians) nor demons nor the troops of wind-gods are able to withstand you in combat any more than that crow, O Rāma! If there exists any regard for me in your mind, powerful as you are, let Rāvaṇa be killed on the field of battle with exceptionally sharp arrows without delay. Or, knowing as he does the behest of his elder brother, why does Lakṣmaṇa, a scion of Raghu, the foremost among men and the scourge of his foes, not come forward to rescue me? Wherefore do those two powerful tigers among men, who vie with the wind-god and the god of fire in energy and are difficult to overcome even for gods, disregard me? No doubt there is some great sin committed by myself due to which Śrī Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, the two scourges of their foes, though powerful and living together, fail to protect me.' Hearing the plaintive and gently-worded invocation of Sītā, I once more addressed the following words to that noble lady: 'I swear to you by my truthfulness that Śrī Rāma has grown indifferent to everything because of grief born of separation from you, O godlike lady! (15—25)

shloka_text:
रामे दुःखाभिभूते च लक्ष्मणः परितप्यते।
कथंचिद् भवती दृष्टा न कालः परिशोचितुम् ॥ २६ ॥
explanation: "Śrī Rāma being overwhelmed with agony, Lakṣmaṇa too is feeling afflicted. Somehow you have been discovered. Hence this is not the time for you to lament. (26)

shloka_text:
अस्मिन् मुहूर्ते दुःखानामन्तं द्रक्ष्यसि भामिनि।
तावुभौ नरशार्दूलौ राजपुत्री परंतपौ ॥ २७ ॥
त्वदर्शनकृतोत्साहौ लङ्कां भस्मीकरिष्यतः।
हत्वा च समरे रौद्रं रावणं सहबान्धवम् ॥ २८ ॥
राघवस्त्वां वरारोहे स्वपुरीं नयिता ध्रुवम्।
यत् तु रामो विजानीयादभिज्ञानमनिन्दिते ॥ २९ ॥
प्रीतिसंजननं तस्य प्रदातुं तत् त्वमर्हसि।
साभिवीक्ष्य दिशः सर्वा वेण्युद्ग्रथनमुत्तमम् ॥ ३० ॥
मुक्त्वा वस्त्राद् ददौ मह्यं मणिमेतं महाबल।
प्रतिगृह्य मणिं दोभ्यां तव हेतो रघुप्रिय ॥ ३१ ॥
शिरसा सम्प्रणम्यैनामहमागमने त्वरे।
गमने च कृतोत्साहमवेक्ष्य वरवर्णिनी ॥ ३२ ॥
विवर्धमानं च हि मामुवाच जनकात्मजा।
अश्रुपूर्णमुखी दीना बाष्पगद्गदभाषिणी ॥ ३३ ॥
explanation: "You will see the end of your woes during this very hour, O lovely lady! Striving * SUNDARAKĀṆḌA * 289 for your sight, both the aforesaid princes, who are tigers among men and the scourge of their foes, will reduce Laṅkā to ashes. Nay, having made short work on the field of battle of the violent Rāvaṇa with his kinsfolk, Śrī Rāma will surely take you back to his city Ayodhyā, O lady of excellent limbs! You, for your part, ought to make over to me a token which Śrī Rāma may easily recognize and which may fully bring delight to him, O irreproachable lady! Surveying all the four quarters and untying from the end of her garment this excellent jewel fit for being strung together with her braid, she handed it over to me, O prince endowed with extraordinary might! Taking the jewel in my hands for being delivered to you, O prince, beloved of the Raghus, and saluting her most respectfully with my head bent low, I was seized with a hurry to return. Nay, perceiving me eager to depart and, therefore, expanding my body to immense proportions, poor Sītā, daughter of Janaka, of excellent complexion, spoke to me in faltering accents, her throat being choked with sobs and her face bathed in tears. (27—33)

shloka_text:
ममोत्पतनसम्भ्रान्ता शोकवेगसमाहता।
मामुवाच ततः सीता सभाग्योऽसि महाकपे ॥ ३४ ॥
यद् द्रक्ष्यसि महाबाहुं रामं कमललोचनम्।
लक्ष्मणं च महाबाहुं देवरं मे यशस्विनम् ॥ ३५ ॥
explanation: “Getting unnerved at the thought of my springing up to cross the ocean and smitten with the vehemence of grief, Sītā then said to me, ‘Fortunate you are, O Hanumān, in that you will be able to see the mighty-armed Śrī Rāma with lotus-like eyes, as also the mighty-armed Lakṣmaṇa, my illustrious brother-in-law.’ (34-35)

shloka_text:
सीतयाप्येवमुक्तोऽहमब्रुवं मैथिलीं तथा।
पृष्ठमारोह मे देवि क्षिप्रं जनकनन्दिनि ॥ ३६ ॥
यावते दर्शयाम्यद्य ससुग्रीवं सलक्ष्मणम्।
राघवं च महाभागे भर्तारमसितेक्षणे ॥ ३७ ॥
explanation: “Spoken to as aforesaid, I likewise said to Sītā, a princess of Mithilā, ‘Get on my back quickly, O godlike lady, the delight of Janaka, and continue there till I show you this very day Śrī Rāma, a scion of Raghu, your spouse, accompanied by Sugrīva and Lakṣmaṇa, O highly blessed lady of dark eyes!’ (36-37)

shloka_text:
साब्रवीन्मां ततो देवी नैष धर्मो महाकपे।
यते पृष्ठं सिषेवेऽहं स्ववशा हरिपुङ्गव ॥ ३८ ॥
explanation: “Thereupon that godlike lady replied to me as follows : ‘It will not be virtuous on my part, O Hanumān, if I get on your back even when I have control over my own self, O bull among monkeys !’ (38)

shloka_text:
पुरा च यदहं वीर स्पृष्टा गात्रेषु रक्षसा।
तत्राहं किं करिष्यामि कालेनोपनिपीडिता ॥ ३९ ॥
explanation: “ ‘Even though I was touched the other day by the ogre Rāvaṇa all over my limbs while being borne away from Janasthāna, O gallant monkey, I could not help it, helpless as I was due to my evil destiny. (39)

shloka_text:
गच्छ त्वं कपिशार्दूल यत्र तौ नृपतेः सुतौ।
इत्येवं सा समाभाष्य भूयः संदेष्टुमास्थिता ॥ ४० ॥
explanation: “ ‘Therefore, proceed you, O tiger among monkeys, to where those two princes, Śrī Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, are.’ Having confidently spoken thus, Sītā proceeded to give the following further message: (40)

shloka_text:
हनुमन् सिंहसंकाशौ तावुभौ रामलक्ष्मणौ।
सुग्रीवं च सहामात्यं सर्वान् ब्रूया अनामयम् ॥ ४१ ॥
explanation: “ ‘Inquire, O Hanumān, on my behalf after the welfare of both the aforesaid lion-like princes, Śrī Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, as also of Sugrīva including his ministers and all the rest. (41)

shloka_text:
यथा च स महाबाहुर्मा तारयति राघवः।
अस्माददुःखाम्बुसरोधात् तत् त्वमाख्यातुमर्हसि ॥ ४२ ॥
explanation: “ ‘You ought to deliver my message in such a way that the celebrated Śrī Rāma of mighty arms may deliver me from this ocean of misery. (42)

shloka_text:
इदं च तीव्रं मम शोकवेगं
रक्षोभिरेभिः परिभर्त्सनं च।
ब्रूयास्तु रामस्य गतः समीपं
शिवश्च तेऽध्वास्तु हरिप्रवीर ॥ ४३ ॥
explanation: “Seeking the presence of Śrī Rāma, O foremost hero among monkeys, speak to him for your part of the poignant vehemence of my grief as also of my being threatened by these ogres. And may your journey be happy!” (43)
Hanumān tells Śrī Rāma, how Sītā expressed her doubt in the first instance about a monkey being able to leap across a vast sea and how her doubt was resolved by him

shloka_text:
अथाहमुत्तरं देव्या पुनरुक्तः ससम्भ्रमम्।
तव स्नेहान्नरव्याघ्रं सौहार्ददनुमान्य च ॥ १ ॥
एवं बहुविधं वाच्यो रामो दाशरथिस्त्वया।
यथा मां प्राप्नुयाच्छ्रीघ्रं हत्वा रावणमाहवे ॥ २ ॥
explanation: “Having shown her regard for me out of native good-heartedness and affection for you, O tiger among men, I, who was in a hurry to depart was then spoken to once more as follows by the godlike lady about the future course of action: ‘Śrī Rāma, son of Daśaratha, should be appealed to by you in many ways so impressively that making short work of Rāvaṇa in combat, he may promptly win me back. (1-2)

shloka_text:
यदि वा मन्यसे वीर वसैकाहमरिंदम।
कस्मिंश्चित् संवृते देशे विश्रान्तः श्वो गमिष्यसि ॥ ३ ॥
explanation: “Or, if you deem fit, O gallant Hanumān, tarry for a day in some covered place, O tamer of foes! Having taken rest, you may leave on the tomorrow. (3)

shloka_text:
मम चाप्यल्पभाग्यायाः सानिध्यात् तव वानर।
अस्य शोकविपाकस्य मुहूर्तं स्याद् विमोक्षणम् ॥ ४ ॥
explanation: “Through your presence, O Hanumān, the termination of my grief, which is a fruit of my sinful deeds, may follow for a while, unfortunate that I am. (4)

shloka_text:
गते हि त्वयि विक्रान्ते पुनरागमनाय वै।
प्राणानामपि संदेहो मम स्यान्नात्र संशयः ॥ ५ ॥
explanation: “When you, O heroic Hanumān, have actually left to come back, there will be danger even to my life; there is no doubt about it. (5)

shloka_text:
तवादर्शनजः शोको भूयो मां परितापयेत्।
दुखाद् दुःखपराभूतां दुर्गतां दुःखभागिनीम् ॥ ६ ॥
explanation: “The grief born of your disappearance from my view will further torment me, who stand discomfited by one woe after another, wretched and doomed to suffering that I am. (6)

shloka_text:
अयं च वीर संदेहस्तिष्ठतीव ममाग्रतः।
सुमहांस्त्वत्सहायेषु हर्षक्षेषु हरीश्वरः॥ ७॥
कथं नु खलु दुष्पारं तरिष्यन्ति महोदधिम्।
तानि हर्षक्षसैन्यानि तौ वा नरवरात्मजौ॥ ८॥
explanation: “Moreover, O valiant chief of monkeys, this very grave doubt precisely stands before me as to how on earth, in spite of the monkeys and bears having you for their helper, all those armies of monkeys and bears or even those two princes, Śrī Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, will actually be able to leap across the ocean, which is so difficult to cross. (7-8)

shloka_text:
त्रयाणामेव भूतानां सागरस्यास्य लङ्कने।
शक्तिः स्याद् वैनतेयस्य वायोर्वा तव चानघ॥ ९॥
explanation: “O sinless Hanumān! the capacity to cross this sea lies in the following three created beings alone, viz., in Garuṇḍa (son of Vinatā), the wind-god and you, O sinless one! (9)

shloka_text:
तदस्मिन् कार्यनिर्योगे वीरैवं दुरतिक्रमे।
किं पश्यसि समाधानं ब्रूहि कार्यविदां वर॥ १०॥
explanation: “Therefore, the accomplishment of this task being so difficult, O gallant monkey, what expedient do you perceive? Speak out, O jewel among those who know how to accomplish an act! (10)

shloka_text:
काममस्य त्वमेवैकः कार्यस्य परिसाधने।
पर्याप्तः परवीरघ्न यशस्यस्ते बलोदयः॥ ११॥
explanation: “Although you are unquestionably capable of accomplishing this task single-handed, O destroyer of hostile warriors, such display of strength on your part will conduce to your own renown. (11)

shloka_text:
बलैः समग्रैर्यदि मां हत्वा रावणमाहवे।
विजयी स्वपुरीं रामो नयेत् तत् स्याद् यशस्करम्॥ १२॥
explanation: “If, making short work of Rāvaṇa in combat in co-operation with all his forces, Śrī Rāma takes me in triumph to his own city, Ayodhyā, that would redound to his glory. (12)

shloka_text:
यथाहं तस्य वीरस्य वनादुपधिना हता।
रक्षसा तद्व्यादेव तथा नाहंति राघवः॥ १३॥
explanation: “Śrī Rāma, a scion of Raghu, ought not to take me back in the same surreptitious way as I was borne away from the forest of Janasthāna by recourse to an artifice by the ogre Rāvaṇa precisely for fear of Śrī Rāma, in his absence. (13)

shloka_text:
बलैस्तु संकुलां कृत्वा लङ्कां परबलार्दनः।
मां नयेद् यदि काकुत्स्थस्तत् तस्य सदृशं भवेत्॥ १४॥
explanation: “If, having overrun Laṅkā with his forces, Śrī Rāma, a scion of Kakutstha, the destroyer of hostile warriors, for his part takes me back to Ayodhyā that would be worthy of him. (14)

shloka_text:
तद् यथा तस्य विक्रान्तमनुरूपं महात्मनः।
भवत्याहवशूरस्य तथा त्वमुपपादयः॥ १५॥
explanation: “Therefore, work out things in such a way that valour worthy of that exalted soul, valiant in combat, may come into play.” (15)

shloka_text:
तदर्थोपहितं वाक्यं प्रश्रितं हेतुसंहितम्।
निशम्याहं ततः शेषं वाक्यमुत्तरमब्रवम्॥ १६॥
explanation: “Hearing the aforesaid appeal of Sītā, which was full of meaning, polite and reasonable, I then made the following concluding submission: (16)

shloka_text:
देवि हर्षक्षसैन्यानामीश्वरः प्लवतां वरः।
सुग्रीवः सत्त्वसम्पन्नस्त्वदर्थं कृतनिश्चयः॥ १७॥
explanation: “Sugriva, the foremost of monkeys and the lord of hordes of monkeys and bears, who is richly endowed with strength, has resolved to rescue you, O godlike lady! (17)

shloka_text:
तस्य विक्रमसम्पन्नाः सत्त्ववन्तो महाबलाः।
मनःसंकल्पसदृशा निदेशे हरयः स्थिताः॥ १८॥
येषां नोपरि नाधस्तान्न तिर्यक् सज्जते गतिः।
न च कर्मसु सीदन्ति महत्त्वमिततेजसः॥ १९॥
explanation: “At his beck and call stand monkeys rich in prowess, full of courage and endowed with extraordinary might, swift as thought and possessed of immense energy, whose movement is not hampered upward or downward, right or left, and who do not lose heart even when faced with great formidable tasks. (18-19)

shloka_text:
असकृत् तैर्महाभागैर्वानरैर्बलसंयुतैः ।
प्रदक्षिणीकृता भूमिर्वायुमार्गानुसारिभिः ॥ २० ॥
explanation: “The earth has been gone round clockwise more than once by those highly blessed and mighty monkeys following the path of the wind. (20)

shloka_text:
मद्विशिष्टाश्च तुल्याश्च सन्ति तत्र वनौकसः ।
मत्तः प्रत्यवरः कश्चिन्नास्ति सुग्रीवसंनिधौ ॥ २१ ॥
explanation: “There are monkeys equal and even superior to me in strength in Kīṣkindhā. There is no monkey inferior to me near about Sugriva. (21)

shloka_text:
अहं तावदिह प्रासः किं पुनस्ते महाबलाः ।
नहि प्रकृष्टाः प्रेष्यन्ते प्रेष्यन्ते हीतरे जनाः ॥ २२ ॥
explanation: “When I have arrived here leaping across the sea, how much more would those monkeys do, endowed as they are with extraordinary might. Under no circumstances are the seniors sent out on errands; the juniors alone are so sent. (22)

shloka_text:
तदलं परितापेन देवि मन्युरपैतु ते ।
एकोत्पातेन ते लङ्कामेष्यन्ति हरियूथपाः ॥ २३ ॥
explanation: “Therefore, have done with agony, O godlike lady ! Let your despondency be over for good. In one bound will the aforesaid leaders of monkey hordes reach Laṅkā. (23)

shloka_text:
मम पृष्ठगतौ तौ च चन्द्रसूर्यविवोदितौ ।
त्वत्सकाशं महाभागे नृसिंहावागमिष्यतः ॥ २४ ॥
explanation: “And perched upon my back will those two lions among men reach your presence, O highly blessed lady, like the moon and the sun risen in the sky. (24)

shloka_text:
अरिघ्नं सिंहसंकाशं क्षिप्रं द्रक्ष्यसि राघवम् ।
लक्ष्मणं च धनुष्मन्तं लङ्काद्वारमुपागतम् ॥ २५ ॥
explanation: “You will soon see Śrī Rāma, a scion of Raghu, the destroyer of his foes, who, resembles a lion, as well as Lakṣmaṇa, armed with an excellent bow, arrived at the very gate of Laṅkā. (25)

shloka_text:
नखदंष्ट्रायुधान् वीरान् सिंहशार्दूलविक्रमान् ।
वानरान् वारणेन्द्राभान् क्षिप्रं द्रक्ष्यसि संगतान् ॥ २६ ॥
explanation: “You will also see gathered here soon the gallant monkeys having nails and teeth for their weapons and endowed with the prowess of lions and tigers, nay, looking like lordly elephants. (26)

shloka_text:
शैलाम्बुदनिकाशानां लङ्कामलयसानुषु ।
नर्दतां कपिमुख्यानां नचिराच्छोष्यसे स्वनम् ॥ २७ ॥
explanation: “You will before long hear the clamour of the foremost of monkeys resembling mountains and clouds and roaring on the peaks of the Trikūṭa mountain in Laṅkā. (27)

shloka_text:
निवृत्तवनवासं च त्वया सार्धमरिंदमम् ।
अभिषिक्तमयोध्यायां क्षिप्रं द्रक्ष्यसि राघवम् ॥ २८ ॥
explanation: “You will also soon see Śrī Rāma, a scion of Raghu, the tamer of his foes, crowned at Ayodhyā with you, his term of exile in the forest just nearing completion.’ (28)

shloka_text:
ततो मया वाग्भिरदीनभाषिणी
शिवाभिरिष्टाभिरभिप्रसादिता ।
उवाह शान्तिं मम मैथिलात्मजा
तवातिशोकेन तथातिपीडिता ॥ २९ ॥
explanation: “Cheered by me with gladdening and agreeable words, Sītā, a princess of Mithilā, who, though sore afflicted with the thought of your excessive grief on her account and who never speaks pitiful words, derived solace in my presence.” (29)

shloka_text:
एतत् तवार्या नृप संयता सा
सीता वचः प्राह विषादपूर्वम्।
एतच्च बुद्ध्वा गदितं यथा त्वं
श्रद्ध्वस्व सीतां कुशलां समग्राम् ॥ ४४ ॥
explanation: “This is the message which that noble and self-restrained lady, Sītā, gave for you with despondency, O protector of men! Nay, pondering this statement of mine in its true perspective, believe Sītā, the foremost of all devoted wives, to be well.” (44)
